author: marcelometal
body:
Four advisories in our lockfiles have fixed releases. RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (crypto-bigint) and RUSTSEC-2026-0385 (ctutils), both of 2026-10-23, report secret-dependent branches in operations meant to run in constant time, and both reach the worker only through janus, the TPM engine behind krun-devices' `tpm` feature. Every crypto-bigint from 0.7.0 to 0.7.8 is yanked, the 0.7.5 locked until now included, so the first commit takes 0.7.10, the newest one that is not, with the ctutils 0.4.6 it requires. RUSTSEC-2026-0194 and RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (quick-xml) reach the guest only through wayland-scanner, a build-time proc-macro over protocol XML shipped inside the wayland crates; the second commit takes wayland-scanner 0.31.11, the first on quick-xml 0.41. Each lock changes in those entries only.

janus's own test suite passes with the new crates on x86_64 Linux, 112 tests as before, and janus type-checks for aarch64-apple-darwin against this lock. The hosted lane's guest Clippy pass is clean, and the guest tests other than limina-init pass, 40 as before; limina-init's tests do not compile for an x86_64 host on either lock. Neither the hosted lane nor this change builds the worker on macOS, so this stays a draft until `cargo xtask build` and `scripts/test-boot.sh debug --test l2_tpm` pass on a developer Mac. rsa's RUSTSEC-2023-0071 has no fix and docs/design/vtpm.md accepts it; zstd's advisories need a libkrun bump.

author: maleadt
body:
Implements the first proposal of #83: in `foreach_range(...; schedule = :steal)`, thieves prefer victims that share their last-level cache, then their NUMA node, and steal from other nodes only once a pass over their own node found nothing. Stacked on #84, whose shared rescue clock this builds on; review only the last two commits.

## Design

- **Topology** comes from Linux sysfs, read once in `Pool()`: the sharing set of each CPU's highest-level unified/data cache, the node CPU lists (ignored when they overlap, as with the emulated NUMA nodes of a Raspberry Pi 5), and node distances. It's only used when every worker's affinity mask is a single CPU of its own, which `Pool()` already reads (Julia ≥ 1.11). Otherwise, on other OSes, on 1.10, or when any file is missing, the order stays cyclic. We read sysfs instead of using SysInfo.jl/Hwloc.jl: SysInfo, which ThreadPinning uses, exposes no cache domains or node distances, and both load Hwloc (~50–250 ms) for every user; the sysfs reads take ~0.6 ms, and only for pinned pools.
- **Victim order**, per worker, immutable in `RangeState`: LLC ∩ node → rest of the node → remote nodes by distance; within a tier, rotated after the worker (remote tiers by the thief's rank within its node, so a node's thieves don't all start on the same remote victim). Victims beyond `p` are skipped.
- **Crossing rule**: thieves repeat local passes while they find work, go remote only after a fruitless local pass, and return to their node right after a remote steal (once its republished remainder is drained). Retiring still requires a full fruitless scan; quarter steals, startup protection and `PROTECTED_PASSES` are unchanged.
- **Proximity is the executing worker's**: a block the caller rescues uses the caller's order (cyclic off the pool), while republished work still goes to the rescued block.
- **Contract**: pin before the first parallel loop, or call `ThreadTeams.shutdown!()` after pinning; documented in the docstring and caveats page. No revalidation, no public API. The static path is unchanged.

Left out after measuring: publishing commands round-robin over nodes (proposal 3's cheap variant) gave no smaller start spread and was slower on desktops; the go-word protocol it would really need is a bigger change.

## Results

Paired ratios, local-first / cyclic, measured in the same process with randomized interleaving (median over 3 processes), with #84 underneath; < 1 is faster. Forced `:steal` `foreach_range`, threads pinned with ThreadPinning.

2× Xeon Gold 6430 (L3 = socket = node), Julia 1.11:

| threads, pinning | axpy 1e5 | axpy 1e6 | axpy 1e7 | stencil 126³ / 128³ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 `:numa` | **0.85** | **0.87** | 0.96 | 1.00 / 1.01 |
| 64 `:cores` | 1.01 | **0.89** | **0.90** | 0.94 / **0.92** |
| 64 `:numa` | **0.87** | **0.87** | **0.89** | **0.79 / 0.82** |
| 32 `:cores` (one node: topology unused) | 1.00–1.05 | | | |

Indices moved across sockets by steals drop from 37–81% (cyclic) to 0–4% on axpy. KernelAbstractions' CPU back-end (JuliaGPU/KernelAbstractions.jl#906) forced to steal follows (0.80–0.88 at `:numa`); its adaptive policy gets 0.72–0.74 on axpy 1e7 at 64 threads, because faster launches keep it under its 50 µs steal threshold.

One node, two L3s (Ryzen 5950X / 9950X, 16 threads): axpy 1e5 0.85 / 0.95, axpy 1e6 1.02 / 0.95; stencils and an imbalanced triangular loop within ±2%. Stolen indices that stay within the CCD: 31% → 89% (5950X, axpy 1e5).

Hosts where topology is unused (96-core Ampere Altra with no shared cache in sysfs, macOS, unpinned): same code as cyclic, no change beyond noise.

Topology detection was checked against `lscpu`/sysfs on a Raspberry Pi 5 (overlapping nodes rejected), Jetson Orin/Xavier/Nano, an Intel laptop, an M1 Mac (cyclic) and the hosts above. Building the orders takes 0.6–1.3 ms at pool start for pinned pools, ~0.03 ms otherwise.

Tests: pure order construction on synthetic topologies (2 nodes × 2 LLCs with `:cores`/`:numa` layouts, sub-NUMA clustering, overlapping nodes, missing caches, `p < nworkers`), the sysfs parser on fake trees, and steal behaviour with installed orders (a thief takes a same-node victim before a remote one, and returns locally after a remote steal); these fail with cyclic order. Full suite on Julia 1.12 (`-t 16,1`) and 1.10 (`-t 8`).

author: vondada
body:
## Root cause (investigated)
- The cost arithmetic is correct. It matches the engine's formulas. For BTC, fees are 0.6% per side (taker) on each leg's value, plus spread and slippage.
- The 327 "costs over risk" trades are in the strategy simulation. The simulation has a cost gate (0.25 R, `strategy_sim.js`) that skips new signals above it; trades recorded before the gate keep their results.
- The forward crypto journal has no such gate. `trading_evidence.js` only checks the stop's price distance (0.1% to 1% of price). With fees near 1.2% round trip, every such journal trade has costs above its risk. The audit sentence "New signals like that are now skipped" was true only for the simulation.

## Change (read only)
- The audit sentence now names which record set the gate covers.
- The deploy audit probe prints, from the owner's own journal:
  - up to five records whose costs exceed their risk, from smallest to largest cost per R, each with the stop distance, risk, every cost, the fee share, the net check and cost per R, all computed from the stored fields;
  - the owner's loss answers (why, worst, best), and the crypto journal's answer on its own line.
- No record is written, no order placed, no model called.

## Checks
- `trading_cost_audit.test.mjs`: 3 of 3, on labelled fixtures derived from the engine's formulas.
- Full Worker suite: 4663 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped, 2 expected TODOs.
- `worker.js`: 1,098,062 bytes, within the 1,100,200 budget.

## Not in this PR
- Adding the journal cost gate. That changes paper trading behavior, so it is a separate PR after the real records are reviewed.

author: sollama58
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"sollama58"} -->
_Requested by **X** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_013BUTnjxhYM62yecj3Xc3V5?thread=cmsg_013BUTnjxhYM62yecj3Xc3V5H5khmmMpRmsMH5PzFqYTmg)_

Full audit 2026-10-27, fix thread T4 (part 1 of 2): DB-2 / MT-10 exam cost, CH-4, BL-1.

## Why
The curator-training run takes about 129 min and grows about 540-610 s a day, so it reaches its 240-minute deadline around 11-07..11-10 (DB-2). #1114's fold-bag cut saved 1% (MT-10). Profiling one fit showed the tree split search was 77% of the time.

## What changed
- `boosting.ts` `growTree`/`bestSplit`: each node's histograms are built in one pass over its rows from a row-major copy of the bins (built once per fit), into one reused slot array per tree (gradient, hessian and count side by side). Columns that cannot split and nodes too small to split are skipped. Each fit bins its two row sets (and the validation vectors) once for all its bags instead of once per bag.
- `forest.ts` passes the same row-major bins.
- Every histogram slot still adds its rows in row order, so every split, threshold and leaf value is unchanged to the bit. No verdict, cutoff or display changes.

## Measured (production rows from the shared 10-27 export, this container)
| fit | before | after | model hash |
|---|---|---|---|
| default boosted recipe, 3 bags, 40,000 rows | 85 s | 57 s (-33%) | identical |
| forest / lambdarank / return / runSize / payoff, 15,000 rows | 2.1 / 6.9 / 6.2 / 11.3 / 7.1 s | 1.8 / 5.1 / 4.4 / 8.4 / 4.8 s | identical |

Expected effect on the run: the exam stage should drop by roughly a quarter to a third (about 7,600 s to about 5,200-5,700 s), which moves the deadline crossing out by several weeks at the current growth. To be confirmed on the next run's `/health/worker` exam time.

## Tests
- `boosting.test.ts`: a reference copy of the old per-feature split search; the new `growTree` must grow the same tree to the bit on 30 random contexts (missing values, constant and all-missing columns, tiny nodes, forest-style node values). Fails on a one-character tie-break change.
- CH-4: `labels.test.ts` near misses on both sides of the 2x bar (1.99x and 1.8x are not wins) and the -50% stop (0.51 holds, 0.50 stops); fails with `WIN_MULTIPLE = 1.8` or a 0.45 stop. `curatedAlerts.test.ts` pins the Rules seat's points-table cutoff through an exported `rulesTableDecision` (a one-word export in `curatedAlerts.ts`); fails with the lane's half-cutoff mutation.
- BL-1: the `trainingRun` challenger test runs on 1,200 synthetic tokens: 22 s against its 60 s cap (was 75 s on 4 cores).

Local checks: core build, typecheck (core, worker), eslint and prettier on changed files, core tests 2,107/2,107, worker tests 1,061/1,061 on a fresh migrated Postgres.

body:
## Summary

In Tangerine, `--text-muted` on a highlighted row (the 12% `--accent-soft` tint over `--bg-panel-elevated`) measures **4.37:1** in dark and **4.38:1** in light. That is below WCAG AA (4.5:1). #3002 fixed this for the picker paths. Four more rows still used muted text on the same tint and panel:

| Rule | Highlighted state |
|---|---|
| `.select-option__description` | `.select-option.is-active` |
| `.composer-dropdown__option-description` | `.composer-dropdown__option:hover` / `:focus-visible` (not disabled) |
| `.composer__schedule-menu-item-description` (send menu: Queue / Steer / Interrupt clauses) | `.composer__schedule-menu-item:hover` / `:focus-visible` (not disabled) |
| `.messaging-surface-picker__context` | `.messaging-surface-picker__list .project-picker__row:hover` / `:focus-visible` / `.is-cursor` |

On a highlighted row, each one now uses `--text-secondary`: still neutral metadata, one step up the text ladder. This matches #3002. The row's one accent stays on the name, per UI-THEME's "selection treatment plus at most one more accent element". Tangerine's `--text-muted` token is unchanged. The comments that said these "stay muted" now give the reason for the lift.

The send-menu description was not in the original list. It has the same pairing, so it is included here.

### Measured (muted at rest on the panel / muted on the tinted row / secondary on the tinted row)

| Theme | panel | row (before) | row (after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| tangerine-dark | 5.21 | **4.37** | 7.44 |
| tangerine-light | 5.17 | **4.38** | 7.36 |
| solarized-dark (lowest non-Tangerine) | 5.89 | 4.95 | 5.35 |

The other color themes measure higher on every surface.

## Tests

`theme-contract.test.tsx` has a new test, "lifts a highlighted option's supporting text off --text-muted in every theme", beside the composer autocomplete floor test. For each menu it:
- reads the panel background (`--bg-panel-elevated`) and the highlight tint (`--accent-soft`) from the CSS
- checks the base ink (`--text-muted`) and the highlighted-row ink (`--text-secondary`)
- measures each ink on the surface it meets, in Tangerine dark and light (4.5 floor) and in every color theme (4.55 floor)

Against main's `app.css`, the new test fails as expected: `.select-option.is-active .select-option__description: expected undefined to be 'text-secondary'`.

## Verification

Sandboxer `sb_0am70mbh2n` at `b6739579b`:
- `setup exit=0`
- `lint exit=0` (55 s)
- focused `theme-contract` + `messaging-surface-picker-row-contract`: 115 passed
- full unit, two shards: shard 1 exit=0 (9886 passed). Shard 2 had 1 failure: `federation-headless.test.ts`, "Headless socket path exceeds 100 bytes; choose a shorter PWRAGENT_HOME". That failure comes from the sandbox's long worktree path and is unrelated to this CSS change.

`apps/desktop/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` runs in PR CI.


## Screenshots

The real `app.css` was rendered in headless Chromium: main's copy for "before", this branch's for "after". Each menu was drawn from its component's markup, using made-up labels. A pointer hover or the keyboard cursor sets the highlighted row.

author: trumpton
body:
Fixes #75.

## What changed

- A repeat has its own time zone (`RepeatZone`, an IANA name such as `Europe/London`). Occurrences are stepped on the clock in that zone, so a 14:00 repeat stays at 14:00 when the clocks change.
- Google sync sends the repeat's zone (`start.timeZone` / `end.timeZone`) with the local time and offset, the same way Google expects a recurring event. Download reads the zone back.
- A wall-clock time that the clocks skip (in spring) moves forward an hour, because Qt returns an invalid time for it.
- Repeat edits move the start and the until date by clock time, not elapsed seconds, so a move across a clock change keeps its clock time.
- The end date of a repeat is taken in the repeat's zone.
- Repeats without a stored zone use this machine's zone.
- One-off appointments are unchanged. They are stored as the instant the form produced, which keeps 14:00 in December even when they were entered in September.

## Base branch

This branch is built on `investigate/open-issues`, which is not merged to `master`. The diff against `master` therefore also includes those commits. The commit for this change is `788f28a`.

## Testing

- Built the app and the bench driver.
- Checked `Appointment` directly against Qt with the real object code: a monthly and a weekly 14:00 London repeat keep 14:00 across 25 October and into December; a 29 March 01:30 occurrence moves to 02:30 BST; the until date stops the repeat.
- New bench scenario `T40` (run with `TZ=Europe/London`): a weekly repeat is listed at 14:00 London time on both sides of 25 October, and Google gets `Europe/London` with `+01:00`.
- Full bench suite: see the results comment on this PR.

author: 8w9ag
body:
openinterp next seed: 3304779326; audit --random seed: 984653572

Scan: `corpus.jsonl`, 512-token windows over 477 docs (199,896 tokens). Unit: L14/N942+ (first experiment on this neuron).

**Verdict: NEEDS_REVISION (confidence 0.73)** — hard negatives 5/11, positive holdouts 5/5, counterfactuals 8/8, lookahead consistency 1/1. Specificity 0.45, sensitivity 1.00, balanced accuracy 0.73, against a token-identity baseline of 0.27. Failed gate: `specificity`.

Hypothesis: a retrospective register dial for plain everyday human-life prose — it accumulates over a passage of ordinary narrative/description of people and their surroundings (children, family, neighbours, homes, gardens, schools, shops, streets, food, errands) and sits near zero or below on technical, abstract, numeric or institutional text (buffers and semaphores, enzymes and substrates, statutes, citation strings, arithmetic drills, code). Inside such a passage it peaks on the short grammatical word that hands over to the next common noun (`the`, `a`, `of`, `in`, `to`, `and`, `or`, `with`, `at`, `by`, `including`, a list comma) and collapses on the noun itself; the build-up is slow, so one everyday phrase is weak while a paragraph of it is strong. Scan max 1.537, with 1,983 of 258,008 tokens above a quarter of peak.

The reviewer's probes confirm the positive side completely and break the gate:

- **All five holdouts fire**, across genres absent from the examples: a ~600-token neighbourhood narrative (1.19), a recipe (0.57), a parent-to-parent chat transcript (0.62), a children's storybook page (0.48), and a personal letter (0.59).
- **Six of eleven hard negatives fire**, and they are exactly the ones where the trigger tokens appear without the supposed class condition. The decisive one is a **metalinguistic paragraph that quotes the trigger-token list itself** — no human-life referents at all — which reads **0.92**. A **telegraphic everyday list** ("Post office. Chemist. School pick-up three o'clock. Corner shop: bread, milk, eggs.") reads **0.97**. A references list reads 0.63, an arithmetic drill 0.54, an institutional housing report dense in `homes`/`children`/`gardens` but as numbers 0.53, and semaphore/buffer prose 0.43.
- **The five that stay quiet** are enzyme kinetics (0.25), a childcare statute (0.28), Python source (0.29), a single short everyday sentence (0.24), and a JSON config (0.21). The single-sentence pass supports the claimed slow build-up, but the telegraphic list does not.
- Eight of eight counterfactuals reproduce, including the three exact-zero controls.

So the peaks are real and the slow accumulation is real, but "everyday human-life prose" is not a gate: the pole responds to the trigger tokens plus an everyday lexicon whether or not the passage is narrative. Text that merely names the tokens fires almost as hard as the examples. Causal metrics are weak: sufficiency 0.42, necessity 0.22.

Explanation scores (judge `external/deepseek-flash`): detection 0.50 (TPR 0.16, FPR 0.16), fuzzing 0.50 (TPR 0.00, FPR 0.00), embedding AUROC 0.50 (499 of 4000 windows active).

Proposer and reviewer were both `external/deepseek-flash[1m]`, so this is a self-review. A revision should drop the genre gate and state the token/lexicon condition the metalinguistic and telegraphic-list probes demonstrate, or fold them in as an explicit second mode.

author: shaullavo
body:
## Quick summary
Bash and other apps can't install the program packages yet: their internal links point at unpublished `0.0.0` versions. This adds a release command that packs base, its families and optionally Git or Python as GitHub release downloads. Each package links to the others, and to the published Waffle runtime, by an exact download URL. A real install from those files is tested before anything is uploaded.

### What it does
- `scripts/program-release.ts` orders the requested families (base → coreutils, findutils, grep, ripgrep, sed; optional git, python), copies each into disposable staging, sets the release version and rewrites every workspace edge and the `waffle` peer to its immutable asset URL. The source checkout is never modified; dirty release sources are refused.
- Reuses PR166's `tools/program-package.ts` admission and tarball readback. No build or Rust producer is duplicated.
- Fails on edges outside the closure, `workspace:`/local-path specs and `0.0.0` pins. Checks every export target, packed relative import, static asset URL and root license; bare runtime imports must be declared.
- Packs a local-URL twin, proves it is byte-identical to the release tarballs apart from those URLs, then runs a real `bun install` of the whole closure from a local HTTP server with the npm registry unreachable. Imports every export and checks every exported guest is the admitted artifact. `--acceptance FILE` runs a consumer program on the install.
- Writes `program-release.json` (source commit/trees, URLs, sizes, SHA-256s, edges, artifact hashes) and `SHA256SUMS`.
- Release URLs are derived from this repository's per-tag GitHub releases. The runtime URL must name the version inside its hash-checked tarball. An existing tag must name exactly the packed commit.
- Child commands run in owned process groups with deadlines. SIGINT/SIGTERM or a timeout retires them before staging is removed.
- `.github/workflows/program-release.yml` (manual dispatch, exact tag checkout): prepares the closure with each family's own `prepare:package`, runs the command and uploads the assets as a workflow artifact. It publishes only when `publish` is set.
- `docs/program-release.md` documents it.
- Normal program CI now selects `scripts/**`, typechecks `scripts/` and runs `scripts/program-release.test.ts`; `ci-paths.test.ts` pins both.

### Validation
- `bun test scripts/program-release.test.ts`: 17 pass. The tests copy PR166's real family sources, run the real pack/install with the actual `waffle-0.0.91.tgz` asset (hash checked), and cover refusals: workspace edge outside the closure, `0.0.0`, local path, missing guest, dirty source, wrong runtime hash, undeclared import, missing export, cycle.
- Review r621 corrections are covered by cheap fixtures:
  - A family whose exports reach none of its admitted guests is refused.
  - Mutable or other-repository runtime URLs are refused, and so is a runtime URL whose version differs from the tarball's package.
  - An existing tag that names a different commit is refused. A missing tag is recorded as `untagged-candidate`, or refused with `--require-tag`.
  - A hung child times out. SIGTERM or SIGINT to the CLI retires the child group and removes staging, with exit codes 143 and 130.
- Strict `tsc` (with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), oxlint and oxfmt pass for `scripts/`.
- Composed with main after #166 (normal merge, no rebase): the 17 release tests, the 20 ci-paths tests, the strict `scripts/` typecheck, `programs:check`, oxlint and oxfmt all pass.
- Real accepted guests, candidate `programs-v0.0.1` (untagged), at `491aa6b`:
  - Inputs: the 23 WASM files and 5 notices from #166's accepted prepared files. All 28 were hash- and size-checked before use and match the manifest; nothing was rebuilt.
  - Edges: only the published 0.0.91 runtime URL and the per-tag family URLs. No `0.0.90`, `workspace:` or local URL remains.
  - Install: npm was unreachable and no overrides were used. All 18 coreutils guests and the find, xargs, grep, sed and rg guests were reached through their exported program descriptors.
  - Acceptance: #166's `tools/family-packed-app.ts` passed all 11 scenarios, 23 programs and 46 executable paths.

Nothing is tagged or published.

author: dbalders
body:
## Summary

New managed GLM and Flash threads browse plugin operation names, then load one typed schema by exact name. The gateway bridge checks the returned namespace/name pair, keeps extension MCP search available, and retains the existing execution and approval checks.

## Why

Unused plugin schemas occupy context needed for the task. A broad lexical search could also omit the requested operation and steer GLM toward an account lookup instead of repository listing. Bounded browsing and exact schema loading address both problems.

## Validation

Current candidate: `c2ba73e658`. Actual native Codex 0.161 and gateway routes `api-glm-5.3` / `api-glm-5.3-flash`.

- Current-head CI test suites passed, including all five server shards and Windows regression tests. Local changed checks: 161 tests plus format, lint, types and unused-code checks passed.
- Both models passed nine fresh trials (11 requested provider calls each) and 20-turn workflows (25 requested operations and 30 checked argument fields each). The workflows include two successful local registry calls and 23 external availability refusals per model; these are not connected external reads. Current-head cohorts recorded 94 + 136 HTTP 200 responses, with no 429s.
- Matched main/current input: Flash **27,207 → 8,393** at startup, **34,617 → 25,165** at turn 20; GLM **27,196 → 8,382**, **34,376 → 25,804**. Model-visible plugin schemas were 143 throughout on main and 0 → 15 on this branch. This plugin-focused fixture excludes separate Harness/skill overhead; final model histories differ.
- Actual-native loopback proof: 18/18 scenarios, both streaming compaction/continuation journeys and 8/8 old/new history replay checks passed without model inference. A normal same-named MCP extension no longer shadows the registered target. Rejected schemas remain absent from model-facing history and compaction.
- **Current strict fidelity failure retained:** the first refreshed Flash approval case inserted a 16-character line into a 2,259-character lookup string. Provider/native arguments match, and the genuine approval produced exactly one correct durable append. This does not establish a source regression. A fixed matched main/current long-text study is being prepared; the other five approval cases and live old/new history refresh remain unrun.
- A separate fresh main control stopped on a repository-list limit of 10 instead of two. That baseline failure is retained; later fresh controls remain unrun. The completed matched main 20-turn workflows and current nine-trial passes remain separate evidence.
- Prior `dceb342fd9` six-case local-plugin approval and live native-history checks passed. Those receipts remain historical, rather than being relabeled as current-head acceptance. Independent Sol reviews and source checks addressed the short-name and same-name retrieval issues. Context/feature probes and a minimal actual-app smoke remain in progress.

## Review Response

Opus raised a possible mixed managed-instance configuration. This is unreachable in the supported product: production [`ServerSettings.layer`](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Harness/blob/dceb342fd9e3be63fcb1402af4425dd3bf048ca9/apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts#L1434) always overlays settings, and [`applyManagedHarnessPolicy`](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Harness/blob/dceb342fd9e3be63fcb1402af4425dd3bf048ca9/apps/server/src/managedPolicy.ts#L407) replaces both model lists and metadata by route before provider creation or rebuild. The driver takes its allowed models from that same effective config; custom IDs do not satisfy its managed-gateway predicate. The reverse case is also excluded: [CodexDriver supplies `allowedModels` only for managed gateways](https://github.com/dbalders/TritonAI-Harness/blob/c2ba73e6589f6010a84d6e05b9d93f8db03eb25d/apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/CodexDriver.ts#L284), so unmanaged instances cannot satisfy the adapter’s nonempty hosted-list predicate. An independent source trace, 30 existing policy/settings tests, and deliberately mixed persisted-input checks confirmed the partition. No extra guard was added for an unsupported direct-construction configuration.

## Risk and Recovery

Native catalogs are fixed per thread; existing flat catalogs retain their prior exposure. Loaded schemas can still accumulate until compaction. Eight native candidates are a bounded retrieval pool, not a guarantee for arbitrary catalog rankings; only the exact registered match is exposed. Older Harness binaries cannot replay the new native search history: rollout requires a compatible reader release first or an explicit unsupported-downgrade boundary.

## Release and Deployment Impact

The gateway service is unchanged. No merge or release is performed. Connected accounts, desktop approval rendering, full-app restart, and Windows remain unverified.

## Upstream Alignment

The adaptation is limited to the managed on-prem transport and reuses native Codex discovery, history, and typed invocation. Other provider routes retain their existing behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused change with regression coverage
- [x] Known actionable local review findings resolved
- [x] No credentials or sensitive logs included
- [ ] Current-head CI and hosted review completed

Implementation: GPT-6.1 Sol via Codex

author: zanderofficial
body:
Closes #196. Part of epic #50.

## Why

After a zoom clear is applied, Syrinx's session worker reads the saved per-site zoom levels and sends them to the window so the + / - controls show the right value (#90, #159, #192). If that read failed after the clear was applied, the clear was still completed in the journal and nothing tried again. The window kept showing levels from before the clear until another zoom event happened to send fresh ones. No data was lost; only what the window shows was stale.

## What changed

- New `crates/syrinx-app/src/session/zoom_levels.rs`: `ZoomLevelsReport` owns reading and sending the levels. A failed read marks the window stale.
- `idle()` in `session.rs` resends on each idle tick while stale. Each failed retry is logged; after four failures in all (the first send plus three retries) it gives up, logs that, and reports the failure to the window. Log lines carry the error only, never a host or address. The retry runs before the tick finishes a pending clear, so a busy database gets a full tick to recover.
- Both paths are covered: the interrupted clear finished by the worker (`finish_pending`) and the clear the owner requests (`clear_site_zooms`, whose own read of the remaining levels now goes through `ZoomLevelsReport::current`). The reviewer found the second path missing in the first commit.
- `Followers` carries the report; `journaled_clear` takes `&mut Followers`. Zoom-clear journaling (#154, #192) is unchanged.
- Only a failed read marks the window stale; a closed window has nothing to resend to.
- A `#[cfg(test)]` counter in the report lets tests make reads fail.

## Tests (synthetic `*.example.test` data)

- `a_levels_read_that_fails_after_the_apply_is_retried_on_a_later_idle_tick`
- `a_levels_read_that_fails_after_a_requested_zoom_clear_is_retried_on_an_idle_tick`
- `a_levels_read_that_keeps_failing_is_retried_a_bounded_number_of_times`

The first and third failed (assertion) with the idle retry disabled, then passed.

## Checks

- `cargo xtask check` passes locally at the head commit.
- Independent opus review (read-only, fresh): one blocking finding (the requested-clear path), fixed and tested in the second commit; nits applied (stale only on read failure, doc wording). Not re-reviewed after the fix. No owner-visible UI changed, so the window was not inspected.

body:
Closes #191.

Add exact-boundary tests that run under `-short` for the snapshot reader record cap and retirement-reserve entry count. The snapshot test stops at a sentinel base decoder, avoiding full record replay. The retirement test uses a count-only fence map, one active generation and pending retirement attempts, with cached byte accounting to avoid encoding or compressing a large checkpoint. Existing reduced checkpoint tests cover replay and retirement.

Mutation proofs, run individually with `-race -short -count=1`:

- `snapshot.go`: changing `len(v.Records) > maxRecords` to `>= maxRecords` makes `TestSnapshotReaderRecordCap/cap+0` fail because it rejects exactly 4,256 records before base decoding. The adjacent 4,255 and 4,257 cases still pass.
- `retention.go`: changing `retirementEntries > maxFenceEntries` to `> maxFenceEntries+1` makes `TestRetirementReserveEntryCap` fail because recovery preflight admits one retirement entry beyond the ceiling.

Both mutants were restored, and the new tests pass against unchanged production code. Only two test files change.

Validation:

- `go test -race -short ./internal/provenance/journal -run 'Test(SnapshotReaderRecordCap|RetirementReserveEntryCap)$' -count=1 -v`: passed.
- `go test -race -short ./internal/provenance/journal -count=1`: passed.
- `go vet ./...`: passed.
- `golangci-lint run`: passed, 0 issues.
- `gofmt` and `git diff --check`: clean.

All Go commands used the required `flock` lock, `GOFLAGS=-p=2`, `GOMEMLIMIT=4GiB`, and Go 1.27.3 toolchain. Package validation, vet and lint also received both database URL variables for localhost:54329.

author: cinquinandy
body:
## Ce que voit la visiteuse

- Les profils **« Vérifiée »** (profil relu par l'équipe) et **« Super maquilleuse »** portent un petit badge sur leurs cartes (recherche, accueil « Mise en avant », pages de zone, blocs sous un texte) et en haut de leur page.
- À pertinence égale, une super maquilleuse passe avant une vérifiée, qui passe avant les autres : un léger bonus de tri, **jamais un filtre**. Il ne passe pas avant « zone indiquée », « coordonnées » ni la distance.
- La page `/classement` a une règle de plus et une section « Les badges … » (ancre `#badges`), avec un lien depuis la page d'un profil.
- Dans l'administration, les descriptions des deux cases disent ce qu'elles font (badge, bonus de tri, Mise en avant, case publique, « relu par l'équipe »).

## Audit (avant le changement)

- **« Super maquilleuse »** : seulement le badge « Pro » de `ResultCard` et des cartes du kit (`ProfileCard`, `ProfileRowCard`) ; rien sur la page d'un profil, rien dans le classement (la page disait « le badge Pro n'avance personne »). Libellé public : « Pro ».
- **« Vérifiée »** : aucun affichage ; seulement la réserve de « Mise en avant » (`featured.ts`). La case est fermée à la lecture publique.
- **« Activité vérifiée »** (SIRET) : cartes et page du profil ; autre badge, inchangé.
- **Classement** : `['-completeness','-updatedAt','slug']` en base, puis rubriques par lieu/distance ; accueil « Les mieux classées », zones et blocs lisent le même annuaire en cache.

## Décisions

- Badge « Pro » remplacé par « Super maquilleuse » ; formule reprise : « posé par l'équipe ».
- Palier `badgeTier` (2 / 1 / 0) calculé une fois dans `readDirectory` (tri stable) et appliqué dans `sectionsByDistance` après distance et pertinence. Le code de tri ne nomme aucune case (test `ranking-transparency`).
- « Vérifiée » est lu à part (règles ouvertes) ; seul le fait `verified: true` sort (carte et page), jamais la date. Aucune nouvelle lecture en cache : tout passe par l'annuaire et la page du profil déjà étiquetés `profils` / `profil:<slug>`.
- Mise en avant : réserve inchangée (« Vérifiée »), super maquilleuses gardées en premier au plafond et poids double dans le tirage navigateur.
- Badge sur la photo (carte en grille, `ResultCard`) ou à cheval sur le bord haut (carte en ligne : photo de 96 px trop petite) : la hauteur de la carte ne change pas.
- Jeu fictif : « Léa Garnier » (`ville-voisine`) super maquilleuse, « Chloé Bertin » (`ville-eloignee`) vérifiée.
- Pas de migration (descriptions seulement) ; `payload-types.ts` régénéré.

## Vérifié

`bun run check`, `typecheck` (hors `PageProps`), `test`, `test:ci-guard`, `names:check`, `build` ; e2e `profile-badges`, `city-search`, `search-distance`, `home-guided-search`, `search-preset` sur banc isolé. Captures 390 et 1440 px (recherche, page de profil).

author: adnerscarpelini
body:
## Resumo

Evita que falhas nas probes descartem pools saudáveis de banco e complementa a cobertura dos gateways com transferência HTTP por sockets reais.

- #116: remove ClearAllPools dos caminhos de falha das probes de Identity e Notifications. Preserva Pooling=false, limites de tempo, dependências e resultados sanitizados. A probe observa saúde sem realizar reset global ou failover.
- #117: acrescenta 12 cenários com os hosts de produção dos dois gateways, invoker padrão e downstream Kestrel controlado em portas efêmeras de loopback, usando HTTP/1.1 real.

## Decisões de design

Correção de produção limitada à remoção das duas chamadas globais. Os testes de pools usam PostgreSQL real e pg_backend_pid para comprovar reutilização da mesma conexão saudável após falhas e recuperação; incluem parada e retomada reais do broker.

Os testes de sockets complementam TestServer: verificam cabeçalhos nomeados por Connection nos dois sentidos, forwarded headers confiáveis, preservação dos corpos, streaming com liberação coordenada dos trechos, 502/504 antes do início e interrupção após resposta parcial, sem acrescentar ProblemDetails. Não adicionam serviços nem infraestrutura de produção.

## QA

QA independente aprovado nas duas issues:

- Arquitetura: 318/318 aprovados em Linux, SDK 10.0.402.
- Integração selecionada: 25/25 aprovados em Windows, incluindo 12 casos novos de sockets, 2 de gateway com Identity, 2 TLS e 9 de isolamento de readiness.
- Regressão adicional: 1/1 aprovada para parada/reinício do PostgreSQL compartilhado, recuperação de readiness HTTP dos dois serviços e login.
- Build completo: zero avisos e erros. Formatação global e diff check aprovados.

Os 12 casos novos usam downstream controlado; a integração com Identity foi verificada pelos testes existentes selecionados. HTTP/2 e cenários adicionais de TLS ficam fora do escopo. A seleção executada não corresponde à suíte completa de integração. Os recursos temporários foram encerrados.

## Documentação

Atualizados docs/development.md e docs/architecture/hosts.md com isolamento das probes, comandos de verificação, cobertura por sockets e limites.

Closes #116
Closes #117

author: robert-velhorst
body:
Repeated numeric input makes LARO's monetary expression retry a failed currency suffix at each digit. A fenced local-model JSON response containing a long whitespace run without a closing fence similarly retries the fence search at each whitespace position. Both slow paths were reproduced against immutable main source (open default CodeQL #46 and #167).

Scan each maximal numeric run once and probe only bounded currency prefixes/suffixes. Preserve original currency-alternative precedence, Unicode decimal/whitespace behavior, raw matches, 80-character context windows and the first-20 result contract. Strip the model's opening JSON fence with an anchored expression and handle a closing fence directly; preserve decoded values and JSON error behavior.

Hosted results at `add55df3feff1db2f23df6cb38a022abb78a18c3`:
- Python 3.15.2: all 12,011 monetary, 12,017 JSON and 31,531 source-passage comparisons agree exactly with the original methods (55,559 total).
- Identical 200,000-digit no-currency input: original exceeds an eight-second child deadline; candidate finishes in about 0.017 seconds.
- Identical 1,000,023-character fenced JSON input: original exceeds the same deadline; candidate finishes in about 0.005 seconds and preserves the complete decoded value. These are observed worker timings, not general performance guarantees.
- The one-million-space source-passage input completes in about 0.006 seconds on both sources. That test does not reproduce #45; the original `_build_source_passages` implementation is retained byte-for-byte. #45 remains open for further triage. No alert dismissal/query exclusion is included.
- All 11 original semantic cases pass unchanged on Python 3.15.2. All 223 unchanged application Python cases also pass on their existing configured Python 3.15.1; latest whole-application-runtime qualification remains separate.
- All 1,023 actual worker source payloads reconcile with the exact Git tree before/after execution. Only `_extract_money` and `_parse_payload` change existing production behavior; all other AST nodes and all 1,018 other baseline payloads are unchanged. Original cases/helpers/fixtures/timeouts/workflows remain unchanged.
- The complete stable/hash-locked Requests graph has 5 distributions and zero unfiltered audit findings. Fresh complete public metadata shows 0 latest-stable gaps for that small graph; this does not qualify the full application/vendor SDK/native graph.

The first candidate also rewrote source passages. Its actual timing did not justify that rewrite, so the original passage implementation was restored without changing any differential/stress case, helper, assertion or deadline. The earlier successful source-bound receipt is retained.

[Actual hosted proof](https://github.com/Robert-Velhorst/000-LARO/actions/runs/40607458717). Snapshot 2026-10-28T00:21:41.002499+00:00: pending checks none; failed checks none.

This remains a separate draft, preserving #314/#315 heads awaiting their own approvals. Main alerts remain open until a reviewed fix is merged and analyzed there. Full portfolio/application/latest-runtime/vendor SDK/native/database/operator acceptance remains incomplete. No merge, deployment, real documents/credentials/data access, account permission or billing change is included.

author: geiserx
body:
Following the self-hosting docs could leave you with a broken or data-losing install.

- The self-hosting page recommended pointing all four `DATABASE_URL_*` at one database and called that the compose default. It is not the compose default, and it destroys data: every start runs `prisma db push` once per schema, and each push drops the tables of the other schemas. `env.example` showed the same layout.
- The quick start wrote `NEXTAUTH_SECRET=$(openssl ...)` into `.env`. Compose stores that text as is, and the file also lacked `DB_PASSWORD`, which the compose file requires.
- The page named `GITHUB_ID`, `GITHUB_SECRET`, `EMAIL_SERVER` and `EMAIL_FROM`. The code reads `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` and `SMTP_*`, so GitHub login and sign-in mail failed with no warning. `ENABLE_STRIPE` and `SMTP_FROM_NAME` were documented too, and nothing reads them.
- The page said federation defaults to off. It defaults to on.
- The self-host compose file had no volume for `/data/uploads`, so moving to a new image tag deleted every avatar, team logo and blog image.
- The entrypoint built the database URL without encoding the user or password, so a password containing `@`, `:` or `/` broke the connection.
- The Mailpit try-out file published its inbox on every interface. That inbox holds working sign-in links.

## What changed

- `docker-compose.selfhost.yml` mounts an `uploads` volume at `/data/uploads`. `docker-compose.mailpit.yml` binds to `127.0.0.1`. `entrypoint.sh` percent-encodes the user and password, and passes them to node after `--` so a value that starts with `-` is kept.
- The self-hosting page now shows one server with four databases, a quick start that matches the README, the variable names the code reads, federation on by default and what it sends, the CLI's real default URL, and a healthcheck that works without curl.

That covers the unused variables, `APP_LOGO_URL` (it is not shown in the header), the contact form needing an SMTP login, `UPLOAD_DIR`, Gravatar requests, the MCP claim, and a dev setup that actually reaches its databases.
- The API blueprint reference now shows the real request and response shapes. The CLI auth page now has the real config paths, a 90-day token expiry, and no longer claims user-only file permissions. The wizard page lists the 12 steps the wizard has instead of 7. The FAQ no longer says every instance stores data in the EU.

## Testing

It checks every variable named on the self-hosting page, in `env.example` and in `docs/configuration.md` against what the code, the entrypoint and the compose files read. The wizard check also passes with the step metadata map from the wizard refactor, so it does not break whichever PR lands second. author: jespiron
body:
If we choose to pivot to spatial architecture, review all PRs from this stack and merge, starting from https://github.com/jespiron/protocol-emulator-compiler/pull/5

## Big picture

This stack introduces Spatial, a language for defining protocols on our spatial architecture chip, alongside some code examples for some protocols in this language (UART, SPI, I2C, USB)

Build system: User writes an `.spt` file, then they follow a workflow pretty similar to Rust, where they can
* `spatial check` to check whether their program can "compile" and fit on the chip
* `spatial build` to compile it into bytes that are loaded onto the chip
* `spatial run` - to build and run it

## Stack
| PR | Goal | 
| --- | --- | 
| this PR | deleetus |
| #5 | Spatial language, add UART protocol | 
| #6 | Add ability to run user-defined tests with `spatial run --test` |
| #7 | Enforce `always` keyword |
| #8 | Add SPI protocol  | 
| #9 | Add I2C protocol | 
| #16 | Fully implement `spatial run` | 
| #14 | Pretty colors for `.spt` in editors | 
| #15 | Pretty spinning Klein bottle in Spatial CLI | 
| #10 | Add USB protocol | 

## This PR

clears the original repo to make way for spatial compiler

author: d-sorgclaudeagent[bot]
body:
## Summary

Step 1 of #3279 (Barb's ruling): warn mode for Barb-seat writes that arrive without lease claim headers.

- New `claim_for_write(headers, principal, *, surface)` in `backend/staff/barb_lease_fence.py` wraps `parse_barb_claim` at every principal-bearing fenced write site: memory append and session digest, Barb turnover, inventory and handoff, and staff dispatch.
- A **Barb seat** is identified by the new shared predicate `is_barb_seat`. It matches a Grok-kind assistant, the ids `agent-grok`/`barb`, or the `barb` role/scope, which is the same rule as memory's `is_barb_principal` minus admins. `is_barb_principal` is now `is_barb_seat(p) or admin`, so the rule lives in one place.
- `DASHBOARD_BARB_FENCE_MODE` sets what happens to a Barb-seat write that carries neither `X-Barb-Scope` nor `X-Barb-Lease-Epoch`:
  - `off`: today's behaviour.
  - `warn` (default; an unknown value falls back to it): the write is allowed. It logs one warning on `dashboard.barb_fence` with the principal id, surface and mode, and never logs header values or credentials. It also increments the new Prometheus counter `dashboard_barb_unclaimed_writes_total{surface}`, served on the existing `/metrics`.
  - `enforce` (small and tested, so included): the write is counted and refused with the existing fence 409 `stale_barb_lease`, reason `claim_required`, and the refusal is audited through the existing `reject_stale`. `reject_stale` now takes `claimed_holder` instead of the whole claim.
- Non-Barb requests are unaffected in every mode. Writes that do carry the claim are fenced exactly as before.
- `PUT /api/priorities/directives` is left on `parse_barb_claim`. It authenticates a `Caller`, not a `Principal`, and `priorities.write` is held only by operators and admins, so a Barb bot seat cannot reach it.
- Module docstring and the #2734 contract section in `docs/operating-the-fleet-through-the-dashboard.md` now describe the modes. The change fragment `changes/3279-barb-fence-warn-mode.md` becomes the SPEC.md change-log row on collation, as AGENTS.md requires (no direct SPEC.md edit).

Refs #3279 (step 2, enforcing by default and fencing release, stays open)

## Validation

RED (new `tests/api/test_barb_fence_unclaimed_warn.py`, run on `origin/main` code):
- `test_barb_write_without_claim_is_logged_counted_and_allowed_in_warn_mode`: failed with `assert 0.0 == (0.0 + 1)`. The unclaimed Barb write was neither counted nor logged.
- `test_enforce_refuses_an_unclaimed_barb_write_with_the_fence_error`: failed with `assert 200 == 409`. The write ran unfenced.
- `test_unknown_mode_falls_back_to_warn` and `test_barb_seat_identity_excludes_admins`: failed with `ImportError` (`fence_mode` and `is_barb_seat` did not exist).
- `test_non_barb_write_without_claim_is_not_logged_or_counted`, `test_barb_write_with_claim_is_fenced_as_before` and `test_flag_off_behaves_like_before` passed on main as intended, because they pin behaviour that must not change.

GREEN:
- New file: 7 passed. Existing fence suites (`test_barb_lease_epoch_fence`, `test_barb_dispatch_fence`, `test_barb_seat_security`, `test_prometheus_metrics`) also pass: 55 passed in total.
- Full suite (`pytest -o addopts=""` with the default marker filter): 10240 passed, 42 failed, 18 errors. Every one of the 60 failing or erroring tests fails the same way on a clean `origin/main` (15b1146e) on this Windows host: 42 failed and 18 errors in the same set (symlinks, bash or actionlint, vault, deploy scripts). None of them touches the changed code.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy --explicit-package-bases` are clean on all changed files.

## Handoff

- Branch `claude/3279-barb-fence-warn-mode`.
- Rollout: the auto-deploy timer picks up main within about 10 minutes once main CI is green. Verify the `auto_deploy` section in `/api/fleet/status`. The default `warn` needs no env change. Watch `dashboard_barb_unclaimed_writes_total` on `/metrics` and the `barb fence: write by Barb principal` warnings to find seats or clients that drop the headers before step 2.
- Next step (step 2, #3279): once the counter stays at zero, flip the default to `enforce` and fence lease release.

author: verity-agents[bot]
body:
Lane vllm-leverf

VLLM-137 (lever F of VLLM-128), piece 1 of 3. Supersedes #5254, which is 1,714 commits behind main with 18 conflicting files.

## What changes

The required-value manifest stops requiring the FlashAttention M1 stream, the attention interiors nothing reads:

- `query.required` no longer puts a `fa2_hidden_m1_stream` / `fa3_hidden_m1_stream` row (`fa2.m1/L<k>`, `fa3.m1/L<k>`: each launch's scores, probabilities and every key block's running max, lane sums and accumulator) in a request manifest. The header loses `attention_hidden_family`, the query text loses its `hidden = ...` clause, and `populations` loses `attention_layers`.
- `query.compose` drops the per-engine-step merge of those rows.
- The guarded-max manifest policy (`query.guarded_max`, `manifest build|build-global|manifest-verify --guarded-max`) goes. It only lengthened those rows: ROW word 3 held `GuardNegInfZero(m)`, and the MS class held `max * scale`. The row stops passing the flag (`row_records.TAP_POLICIES`), and so do `compiled_commit.sh` and the regression's `POLICIES_OFF`.
- `hidden_source.attention_hidden` binds no hidden class for a manifest that names none. So the Commit, serve-openai and the TP ranks drop the class and attach no hidden source, even when given `--hidden-so`; this is the existing "hidden source NOT attached" path. `hidden_source` keeps the guarded-max check (`guarded_max_policy`, `TAP_ROW3`) for an older manifest built under that policy.

## Why nothing reads them

- **The window circuit.** An FA3 head is `Attention_v20`'s Calls, and `window_rows._heads` evaluates every key block's state from q, K and V by Definition. `Served` reads only node outputs. No window-circuit unit, wire, registered read or opening names an `fa*.m1` row.
- **`query.units`.** The rows are no Call's Value, so they're in no unit's boundary. Only the policy required them, and the canonical partition (`test_units_canonical`) doesn't contain them.
- **The word check.** It flags an attention interior only when a tap claims it (`interior-not-acquired` needs a nonzero tap count). No tap claims these, so the partition's checks are unchanged.
- **The replay and the protocols.** `check.replay.coverage` already says these rows are "COMMITTED (coverage + openings) and value-UNCHECKED". `oracle_compare` gives them no oracle family. `verity/core/protocols` and `Security/` don't reference them.

What the Program requires is unchanged. Every attention Call's output is still an `instance_outputs` row (`test_required_profile`).

## The saving

On the 4,32,4 window circuit (Llama-3.2-1B, FA3 on the H200; `window_cost.stream`, under either schedule; pinned in `benchmarks/prove_path/tests/test_window_cost.py`):

| | bytes a window circuit | SHA-512 compressions | ANDs | seal store |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| serving's stream now | 316,342,832 | 3,398,252 | 197.5 G | 0.98 s |
| without the M1 rows | 198,869,552 | 2,136,332 | 124.2 G | 0.61 s |
| saved | **117,473,280 (37%)** | 1,261,920 | **73.3 G** | **0.36 s** |

This PR stops requiring those bytes. A Commit over a manifest built with it doesn't stage, hash or seal them.

## Recorded values

A new manifest's identities lose the M1 rows, and the query text loses its `hidden =` clause, so every regression row's rebuilt `manifest_digest` and `identity_rows_sha256` move. `tests/regression/fixtures.toml` now has one `pending_review` `manifest_digest` decision for each of the nine rows the check rebuilds; the four others are TP rows, a row with no manifest of record, and #74's retired check.

- **Rebuilt at both ends.** `r20261028-033228-40d0` rebuilt all nine at this PR's base `a65dcb3980`, and every row reproduced its current contract (9 passed). `r20261028-031948-c13d` rebuilt them at `e09f3f818c`, and its recorded actuals are the decisions' `expected` values. `resolver.sanction` accepts all nine with the new decisions.
- **Only the M1 rows move.** On every row the `program_digest` is unchanged, and `identities` falls by exactly the base manifest's `fa2_hidden_m1_stream` rows (`fa3_hidden_m1_stream` on the H100 row): 512 to 14,336 a row. The M1 rows' distinct identity keys are the whole move in `removed_n` and `added_n` against v1. Where v1's manifest had those keys, `removed_n` rises; on the H100 row, where it had none, `added_n` falls by 396. Batched rows have fewer keys than rows: llama32-1b at batch 64 loses 2,048 rows but only 736 keys, matching its `removed_n` rise of 736.

## What doesn't change tonight

A manifest built before this, such as V2's row manifest, still names the stream, and the Commit still commits it as today. So `served_verdicts.sh`, serve-openai's defaults and `placement.toml` are untouched, and tonight's V2 run of record isn't affected.

- PR 2, after the freeze, removes the attach path and its flags (`--hidden-so`, `--tap-cap-mb`, `--retain-exclude`) and refuses a manifest that names the stream. It also rebuilds V2's row manifest and re-pins `known_roots.json`. Network-accounting's NET-83 passes `--retain-exclude hidden_m1`, so they hear before PR 2 lands.
- PR 3 removes the tap code.

No circuit changes, so no circuit-check is needed.

## Checks

- Locally, all passing:
  - `tests/query/test_required_profile.py`, `tests/query/test_compose_engine_steps.py`, `tests/query/test_norm_scales.py` and `tests/query/test_router_softmax.py`;
  - `tests/acquire/test_hidden_source_policy.py` and `tests/acquire/test_mla_attention_hidden.py`;
  - `tests/regression/test_harness_rules.py`;
  - `test_row.py`'s policy and query tests (its three tests that need stored workloads couldn't fetch them on the VM);
  - `benchmarks/prove_path/tests/test_window_cost.py -k "4_32_4 or serving_streams"`.
- Quick suites, `suites.py --changed origin/main --quick`, at `e09f3f818c` (`r20261028-031956-0b70`): 21 of 22 suites passed. `verity-vllm` failed 2 of 12,340 tests, both because of this change, and `b2e969f2e7` fixes both:
  - `test_narrowed_producers.py::test_the_last_layers_attention_launch_is_the_prompts_whole` read the geometry of the manifest's `fa2_hidden_m1_stream` rows, which it no longer has. The test is deleted.
  - `test_typed_records.py::test_allowlist_has_no_stale_entries`: `verity_vllm/query` lost one `.get(k) or []` site, so its allowance drops from 26 to 25.
  - Both files pass locally, as do `tests/regression/test_harness_rules.py`, `tests/regression/test_rebaseline.py` and `tests/lint/test_repo_lane_text.py`.
  - The rerun at this head is `r20261028-073212-2de9`.
- The head merges cleanly with `origin/next` (`git merge-tree`).

author: zanderofficial
body:
Closes #195

## Why

D40 promises that page text leaves the disk seven days after it was captured. When the full-text index has to start afresh, for example in the history repair added by #193, `CacheFolder::empty` (`crates/syrinx-platform/src/storage/cache.rs`) deletes every file in the index's folder. Until now it deleted them in whatever order Windows listed them. Suppose one deletion failed partway, leaving a segment that holds page text after the index's metadata was already gone. Nothing would ever remove that segment:

- Without `meta.json`, the next open creates a fresh index beside the leftover.
- Tantivy's garbage collection deletes only the files its managed list names, and that list was gone too.

The issue assumed this could not happen today, because NTFS lists hex-named segment files before `meta.json`. Writing the session-level test showed that it can. Tantivy's managed list is called **`.managed.json`**, with a leading dot (`MANAGED_FILEPATH` in tantivy 0.27.0, `src/core/mod.rs`), not `managed.json` as the issue says. Because of the dot, NTFS lists it first, before the lock files and every segment. So when a segment could not be deleted, the managed list was already gone. The retried repair then opened the old index and restarted its count, but it left the old segment's files on disk for good. This is exactly the D40 leak the issue describes, reached through the managed list instead of `meta.json`.

## What changed

- `empty()` deletes every other file first, in listing order. It then deletes `.managed.json`, and `meta.json` last of all. The files are matched by name, ignoring ASCII case as Windows does, not by listing order (`METADATA_DELETED_LAST`, `metadata_last` and `metadata_rank` in `cache.rs`).
- Which entries `empty()` may touch is unchanged. `plain_files` still checks every entry and refuses a link or a subfolder before anything is deleted.
- If a deletion fails partway, the old index survives with its metadata, so the next open finds it. The repair that failed is refused and offered again at the next start, and that retried repair empties the folder. An ordinary start does not empty it, because Tantivy reports a missing segment file as an I/O error rather than damage, and the doc comment says so.

## Tests

- `a_failed_empty_keeps_the_index_metadata_so_the_next_open_retries` (`crates/syrinx-platform/src/storage/tests.rs`). It holds a synthetic segment open with `FILE_SHARE_READ` only, so the segment cannot be deleted, and names it to list after the metadata. It checks that both metadata files survive the failed empty and that a second empty finishes once the segment is free. It failed before the change.
- `a_repair_whose_index_is_only_partly_emptied_is_refused_and_retried_until_it_is_gone` (`crates/syrinx-app/src/session/page_text_tests.rs`). It holds a real Tantivy segment so that a confirmed repair cannot empty the index. It checks that the repair is refused with `IndexNotEmptied` and that both metadata files are kept. It then checks that the retried repair leaves no page text and removes the old segment. It failed while `.managed.json` was still treated as an ordinary file, which is the old behaviour.
- `cargo xtask check` passes locally at 1f38004: dependency checks, formatting, Clippy, tests and the smoke run.

## Review

An independent opus reviewer (two-axis-review plus thermo-nuclear-review) approved the change with no blocking findings. Two of its nits are applied in 0864065: a more exact doc comment, and moving a test constant. The third nit is not applied. It suggested deleting `meta.json` before `.managed.json`, so that an ordinary start could recover by itself if only the last deletion failed. That gain is liveness only, not privacy, because every data file is already gone by then. This PR keeps the order the issue asked for.

## kickoff 0.9.0: clarity, not ceremony

A vague requirement should become, step by step, a decided solution, architecture, feature set and design, then a task breakdown and an effort estimate. 0.8 governed delivery (phase, gate, commit, evidence) more than it converged on clarity. Spec: `docs/plans/2026-10-28-kickoff-v0.9.0.md`. This PR also carries 0.8.1 (`kickoff init --nested`, commit 02604dd), which was never released on its own.

### Added
- `.kickoff/clarity.yaml` and `kickoff clarity [show|init|set]`: how settled each area is (problem, users, scope, solution, architecture, design, estimate); `kickoff status` and the session start show it and name the weakest area.
- Estimate ranges: package `min`/`max`/`confidence`/`basis`, feature-level `estimate`, `kickoff estimate [--json]`, generated `06-planning/estimate.md`, export columns `effort_min`, `effort_max`, `confidence`.
- `project.yaml`: `scheduling: "on"|"off"` (absent = on; new projects start off) and `estimate.overhead` (management share).
- `kickoff validate`: error for an ADR *Accepted* before C3 and C4 (not after a reopened sign-off); error for a malformed `clarity.yaml`; range checks.
- Plain words: a rule in `methods.md` that every question, option list and approval request is written in everyday words (no gate IDs, phase names, file names or plugin terms); every confirmation step names it, tests enforce it.

### Changed (behaviour)
- The pre-write hook allows `04-architecture/` files that carry `Status: Draft` in their first 20 lines before C3 and C4. Anything else is blocked as before.
- `--evidence` is optional for the lead's gates (C1, C2, C5, C6); still required for CD, C3, C4.
- `kickoff status` lists every phase in progress.
- Skills: clarity-first router, slim `init` (team and calendar are asked by `plan` when scheduling is turned on), estimate-first `plan`, an architecture sketch step in `research`, scheduling-off handling in `signoff` and `feedback`, team-only sections in the customer templates.

### Compatibility
A 0.8 project with none of the new keys behaves as before (schedule, workbook and golden schedule unchanged); new files are `estimate.md` (generated) and an optional `clarity.yaml`.

### Verification
- `uv run ruff check .`: clean; `uv run pytest -q`: 338 passed (262 before)
- `kickoff validate` on both examples: 0 errors; `kickoff docs --check` on `ai-minute`: up to date; golden schedule unchanged

- Reviewed by a Python reviewer and a skills/CLI consistency reviewer; one P1 (accepted ADRs flagged after a reopened sign-off) and six P2 fixed in cc8a694

author: steveash
body:
## Task

T-2948 (docs/tasks/M2/T-2948-export-writes-the-kept-whitespace-into-the-saved.md): the xlsx export writes the typed whitespace into `<f>`, as Excel saves it.

## What changed

- The export prints each formula's written tree (`ParsedFormula::written()`). For example, `=1 + 2` is saved as `<f>1 + 2</f>`, and `=SUM( 1 )` as `<f>SUM( 1 )</f>`. A line feed is written as `
`, which reads back as LF, the same as Excel's raw CR LF.
- `add_implicit_intersection` (import) and `remove_redundant_implicit_intersection` (export) now decide on the tree with no whitespace, using the new `Node::rewrite_as_unspaced`. The written tree keeps its whitespace only when its rewrite, stripped, equals the bare tree's rewrite. So a shape site that does not look past `Spaced` loses the whitespace, never a value. This also fixes import of an Excel `<f>N( IF(1,{2;3}) )</f>`: before, it got an `@` that the bare formula does not get.
- A LET name written with spaces (`LET( x, …)`) is now prefixed with `_xlpm.` on export (`Node::unwrap_spaced_mut`). Without this it would have been read back as a defined name.
- Docs: xlsx-storage.md "Typed whitespace is saved…" Ours line is updated, and SPEC-0023 has an implementation note.

## Evidence

- `make check`: pass
- Eval delta: 0 fixed / 0 new / 0 regressions (this changes the saved text, not values)
- Tests: `test_typed_whitespace_is_saved_in_the_formula_text` (xlsx round-trip) and `spaced_formulas_keep_their_whitespace_and_their_at` (engine). `test_array_formulas_keep_implicit_intersection` now round-trips its typed space (`=POWER(@A1:A3, 3)`).

## Agent review

| reviewer | verdict | notes |
|---|---|---|
| security | APPROVE | none |
| architecture | APPROVE | MINOR: stale spec lines and a duplicate criterion. Both fixed. |
| quality | APPROVE | MINOR: comment nits, fixed; triple clone acceptable |
| excel-fidelity | APPROVE | MINOR: the saved shapes beside `@`, LET and a sign, and the leading run, are derived, not probed. Filed as T-2971. |

## Follow-ups filed

- T-2970: the legacy `@` shape sites look past `Spaced`, so `N( IF(1,{2;3}) )` keeps its spaces
- T-2971: probe the saved `<f>` text for the derived whitespace shapes and the typed leading run

body:
## 요약

`apps/api` 단위 테스트 `test_kor_travel_weather_client.py::test_backoff_longer_than_remaining_stops_and_counts`가

필수 `lint-typecheck-test`를 막는다.

## 원인

- 테스트가 "backoff를 자지 않았다"를 **벽시계** `loop.time() - started < 0.1`로 단언했다. 실제로는 sleep이 없는데도
  CI 러너에서 MockTransport 호출 하나(두 번째 반복)가 0.17~0.26 s 걸려 실패한다.
- 같은 SHA가 16:39에는 통과, 재실행에서는 실패. 러너 이미지(20261012.163.1)는 같고, CI가 `pip install -e ".[dev]"`(락 없음)로
  해석하는 의존성 중 바뀐 것은 **pytest 9.1.1 → 9.2.0**(+ boto3 패치)뿐이다. 코드 회귀는 아니다 — 판정이 환경 시간에 결박돼 있었다.

## 수정

- client 모듈의 `asyncio` 이름만 `_SleepSpyAsyncio`로 바꿔 끼워(`monkeypatch`, 전역 `asyncio.sleep`은 건드리지 않음)
  sleep 요청을 기록하고 실제로는 자지 않는다.
- 단언: 호출마다 attempt 1회(재시도 없이 멈춤) + `spy.slept == []`(backoff를 자지 않음) + `DeadlineExhausted` 아님 + 3회 뒤 회로 열림.
- 예산 30 s / 첫 backoff 60 s — 러너 지연이 판정에 끼지 않는다.

## 검증 (n150, `python:3.12` 컨테이너, pytest 9.2.0)

- 새 테스트 단독 5회 통과, `ruff check .`·`ruff format --check` 통과, 전체 unit은 PR CI(pytest 9.2.0)에서 통과.
- 빨강 확인: client의 deadline 가드를 `if False:`로 지우면 `assert 3 == 1`로 실패.

author: cyangdev
body:
Adds a separately trained CPU neural model for paths/plazas, visible building roofs, car parks, landscaped/grass islands and other visible surfaces. RGB-only inference produces source-linked review polygons; desktop training/prediction jobs and persistent research-cycle checkpoints support reuse and weak-class research prioritization. Learned proposals respect protected plan coverage and remain unaccepted geometry.

Real training uses four Esri images from three parks and 89 provisional assistant visual annotations (153,915 labelled pixels). These are not independently verified human labels. Whole parks are held out together. Five-class mean IoU is 28.30% versus 17.93% for the RGB-centroid baseline, but paths/plazas score only 5.23% and islands 5.83%; roofs score 28.60% and car parks 38.23%. The other-visible class raises the mean. Only annotated pixels are scored, and the final all-data checkpoint has no untouched final test. This is a research model, not reliable autonomous reconstruction.

Validation: 62 tests passed, including real training, park separation, annotation/source integrity, saved-checkpoint tampering/reuse, protected-plan clipping, desktop workers and separate cycle training. Actual all-data weight-change L2 is 25.75. Checkpoint SHA256: e7df032eb29eab196e95913fc12a7dcd034fa863f2148f855dd71298d8ad0161. Evidence and detailed limitations are in evidence/aerial-semantic-training-validation.json and docs/aerial-semantic-training.md. No Windows EXE rebuilt and no world blocks generated.

Stacked on PR136.

## The batch

Group 3, batch C2 of `docs/review-checklist-2026-10-25.md`: the pending cite retargets (`cite-retargets-2026-10-15`, PR #178) whose family starts ח–נ, laid out for the maintainer's scan read in `admin/pipeline/patch/records/tranches/c2-rereads-2026-10-27/README.md`. It follows C1's README (#200) as it stood before the reads were applied.

**Predicate** (checklist Group 3), run on `reviewed/patches.jsonl` at `079ef2a2d`:

```bash
jq -c "$D select(retarget and fam >= \"ח\" and fam <= \"נ\")" $P
```

**39 records, 37 entries, 23 families**, as the checklist's table says. All 39 are `replace`s whose find/replace differ only in `href`/`data-ref`. `removes` is absent on all of them. The README's ids are the same as the predicate's output (diffed).

## What the maintainer does

There is one block per record, in family order and then rid order. Each block has the entry, a scan link (IIIF `$leaf+1`), the hOCR line copied verbatim from `leafLines` (Latin-only), the cite as Sefaria has it with Sefaria's target, the patch's target, and the collapsed proposal. Read the scan, tick **confirm** or **withdraw** (one box only), and write what print shows on the `Read:` line. A re-aim is a withdraw tick that names the new target, as in C1.

Two notes appear in the blocks for the read:
- **Numeral on a later form (34 of 39).** The target carries its numeral on a later form than the one the cite spells (e.g. H00701 `חִיזְרָא, חִזְ׳ I`). Under 10-05, the maintainer may want reforms like C1's P000940/P000941 (10-13 case 2). That would be a separate record.
- **`ch.` line (10-15).** Only one target, H01764 `חָרַר I`, is followed by a `ch.` line (H01765). Its citing line (H01653) is Hebrew. No target of an Aramaic citing entry has a `ch.` line after it.

No family has a reviewed patch (reform or other) on any member.

## hOCR

- An hOCR line was found for 37 of 39 records. On 14 of those lines the hOCR reads the numeral the cite names. On the other 23 the numeral is misread as `1`, `l`, `L` or `i`, is fused into the word, or is not read at all.
- No line was found for K00162 (P000632) or K00171 (P000633). Both are one-line cross-references on leaf 638, and the hOCR cannot tell those lines apart.

## Not in this PR yet

No record, entry or checklist change. The reads, the evidence updates (`maintainer-read`), any withdrawals or re-aims, and any reforms the reads call for will be applied in a later commit on this PR, after the maintainer's read. That is how C1 was done.

## Checks

- `bun qa` passes, including `docs:links` (0 dead links).
- All 41 quoted hOCR lines are verbatim from `leafLines`, checked by script.
- All 41 scan links match the page index's leaf and use `$leaf+1`. Two were spot-checked with `curl -sI` and both resolve to JPEGs.
- The local CodeRabbit review gave 1 finding. It said P000645's find and replace are identical. That is not right: they differ by the nun's vowel. The block now says so.

## What it does

- **"Ask chat" Shortcuts action** (iOS/macOS 27, `AskChatIntent`): a message, an optional chat (empty starts a new one) and optional saves to ask about. It waits for the reply and returns it as text, and Siri reads it out. Siri phrases: "Ask capystore", "Ask capystore chat", "Chat with capystore". It goes through `ChatStore.send`, so the reply also shows up in the chat tab.
- **Chat reply Live Activity** (Dynamic Island + Lock Screen, `CobaltWidgets/ChatLiveActivity.swift`): shows thinking, the tool the AI is using ("searching your library…"), writing, then the start of the reply when it's done, plus "2 tools · 3 files". Every message this device sends (chat tab or Shortcut) gets one. Tapping it opens the thread (`cobalt-apple://chat/<thread>`).
- **Mac → iPhone** (APP-API-CONTRACT 27.9, `src/chat-live.ts`): a chat sent from another device (the Mac app or a Mac Shortcut) push-starts the same activity on the iPhone through APNs and keeps it updated. The new pieces are `features.chat_live_push`, `PUT /live/chat-start-token` and `PUT /live/chats/<thread>`. The device that sent the message is never pushed, because it draws its own activity. The only change in `chat.ts` is a `liveFor` hook on `ChatDeps`, so the chat registry work (#54) can rebase over it easily.

This needs an API deploy (no migration) and an app build. If #54 merges first, its route snapshot test will need rows for the two new `/live` routes.

author: biwceni
body:
## Resumo

Fase 4: o **início guiado** e os **modelos**, no fluxo do protótipo navegável (`vOnboarding`, `PACKS`, `KPACKS` e `TPLS`). O leigo escolhe o tipo de site, o ramo (no site da empresa) e um de dois modelos com prévia ao vivo, digita nome, frase e WhatsApp, e o site fica pronto e no ar. A "Nova página" passa a oferecer modelos de página.

### Coleção Modelos (`templates`)

- Modelos de site (início guiado) e de página (Nova página), com versões. Leitura para quem está logado; criar, mudar e excluir só administrador, nas telas padrão em "Avançado".
- O conteúdo de cada página do modelo passa pelo **mesmo esquema Zod das páginas** (migrado para a versão atual ao salvar). Como as páginas, as fotos e os formulários ainda não existem, o conteúdo cita cada um pela **posição no modelo** (`{ mediaId: 2 }` é a 2ª foto do modelo); um gancho recusa posição que o modelo não tem.
- Menu, botão do topo, rodapé, cores, fontes, endereço e horário de exemplo e formulários (criados junto com o site) ficam no modelo.

### Os 26 modelos (`npm run modelos`)

- 22 de site: os 5 ramos do "Site da empresa" (café, clínica, serviços, loja, outro) e os outros 6 tipos (uma página só, landing page, evento, pessoal, links, em breve), com 2 variações de cores, fontes e banner cada. 4 de página: promoção, sobre, perguntas e contato.
- Lorem Ipsum no conteúdo; nomes de página, menu e botões legíveis. Sites de uma página só, evento e pessoal têm menu com links para seções; landing, links e "em breve" são páginas de campanha.
- O script cria só os que faltam (pelo identificador); `-- atualizar` regrava os existentes. Não pede `SEED_PERMITIDO`: modelo não é conteúdo de teste e não aparece no site até alguém aplicá-lo.

### Fotos dos modelos

- O modelo guarda só o **endereço da foto no Pexels ou no Unsplash** (nada no repositório). As fotos do Pexels foram conferidas uma a uma.
- A prévia mostra direto do banco de fotos (sem o otimizador de imagens do site, que só aceita o nosso Storage).
- Ao aplicar, cada foto **usada** é copiada uma vez para a biblioteca, com o texto alternativo do modelo. O campo escondido `sourceUrl` nas Fotos guarda a origem: aplicar de novo reaproveita a mesma foto. As páginas continuam com foto por relação.

### Aplicar um modelo (`src/lib/applyTemplate.ts`)

- **`POST /api/templates/:id/aplicar`** (só administrador): cria as páginas do modelo já no ar e os formulários, e publica Configurações, menu e rodapé.
  - Fotos copiadas antes, fora da transação; o resto numa **transação só**, com o usuário da requisição (`overrideAccess: false`).
  - Páginas antigas **saem do ar como rascunho** (com as mudanças não publicadas), depois de a página inicial já ser a nova.
  - Endereços livres (`inicio-2` se `inicio` já existe). Frase digitada vai no banner da primeira página; na página de links, o nome do site vai no título.
  - Contato só completado onde está vazio; o **e-mail nunca muda** (é para onde vão os avisos de mensagem); nenhum telefone ou WhatsApp de exemplo entra.
- **`POST /api/templates/:id/pagina`**: página nova em rascunho a partir de um modelo de página, com o nome no banner. Botões que levariam a outra página do modelo levam ao WhatsApp.

### Telas

- **`/admin/comecar`** (tela cheia): tipo → ramo → modelo (duas prévias com o site de verdade num iframe, "Ver maior") → nome, frase e WhatsApp opcional (número inválido trava o botão). Com páginas no site, aviso do que acontece e botão "Trocar meu site por este modelo"; editor vê só um aviso.
- **Meu site**: com o site vazio, o administrador vai para o início guiado ("Prefiro montar sozinho" pula); na volta, "Seu site está pronto e já está no ar".
- **Configurações**: cartão "Começar de novo com um modelo", só para administrador.
- **Nova página**: os 4 modelos de página antes de "Em branco" e "Copiar uma página".

### Banco

- Migração `modelos`, **só de acréscimo**: tabelas da coleção e das versões, coluna opcional `source_url` (com índice) em `media` e coluna em `payload_locked_documents_rels`. RLS ligado nas 12 tabelas novas. Já aplicada no Supabase, e os 26 modelos já gravados.

## Como foi testado

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npx prettier --check` nos arquivos alterados e `npm run build`.
- `npm run test:unit`: 67 testes, 10 novos: os 26 modelos passam pelo esquema, citam só o que têm e o menu aponta para seções que existem; endereços de foto aceitos; troca de posições por ids (incluindo o que falta); a rotina de aplicar com o Payload simulado (endereços, links entre páginas, Configurações, contato preservado, ordem de tirar do ar, formulário, página de links) e a de página.
- No computador, com navegador automático e a conta do Fábio, computador e celular, sem erros no console:
  - os passos do início guiado e as prévias de todos os grupos de modelos, com "Ver maior";
  - WhatsApp inválido e aviso de páginas existentes;
  - Nova página com "Promoção ou produto": rascunho com o nome no banner e as fotos copiadas (página e fotos apagadas depois).
  - Ajuste feito no teste: a prévia usava "#" como destino, e o site esconde link com endereço inseguro (sumiam menu e botões); agora usa destinos válidos.
- **"Criar meu site" de ponta a ponta testado pelo Fábio**, funcionando.

## Depois do merge

- [ ] Conferir no site no ar que o "Meu site" leva ao início guiado com o site sem páginas (não deu para ver com o site de teste cheio).
- [ ] Para um banco novo (fase 5): rodar `npm run modelos` depois das migrações.
