author: matilencina97
body:
## Summary
Until now the event's AAP tournament only changed what the app displayed. This PR makes it decide answers where tournaments really differ. With the AAP rules chosen, the Resolver gets a **"Tiempo, empates y desempates"** flow alongside the foul topics. Fouls themselves are unchanged, because no AAP tournament regulation changes how they are called.

| Situation | General rules (no tournament, opens, other) | Tournament-specific answers |
|---|---|---|
| **Last chukker level** | Asks whether it's a knockout match. Knockout → play on 30″, then extra chukkers to the first goal (10.c, 10.f). Otherwise → ends at the first bell (10.c). | LGS: golden-goal extra chukker · Interprovincial: 30″ then an extra chukker · Copa República: draw allowed (asks about the second leg of a two-match series → golden goal) · Liga Federal: no draws, broken under 10.f · Women's: adds its 30″, then the general rule |
| **Bell with ball in play** | Asks how the play ended: ball out → hit-in or boards · foul → penalty at the start of the next chukker · second bell → throw-in (10.a, b, d) | Women's / LGS: 7′ + 30″ timing; the women's regulation places the throw-in where the ball was when the bell rang |
| **Penalty in the last 5″** | 5 more seconds from when it is taken (10.g) | No regulation changes it (the answer says so) |
| **Mid-chukker horse change** | Asks if it's category B up to 14 goals → 1-minute change (10.e); otherwise none (10.e, 10.i) | Women's / LGS: general change mid-chukker, 1 minute, except in the 4 × 5′ format |
| **Teams level on points** | General rules don't cover it (the answer says so) | LGS: head-to-head, then penalties (2 from 40 yards, 2 from 60, then one each) · Copa República: head-to-head; three teams → goal difference, goals scored, then a draw by lot |
| **Match length** | Up to 6 chukkers × 7′, or up to 8 in opens (Rule 8) | Per regulation (women's by level, LGS 6 × 7′30″, Interprovincial 6, Federal League by category, amateur 4/5/6, Copa final 6) |

Every answer:
- says whether it comes from the **tournament regulation**, which prevails, or from the **general rule**. If no tournament is set in the event profile, it tells the user to set one;
- has a "Dónde lo dice" row of chips that open the AAP rule or the tournament regulation.

## How it works
- **`lib/aap-time-decision.ts`:**
  - `nextTimeQuestion` asks only what the tournament needs;
  - `decideAapTime` gives the answer;
  - `detectAapTimeSituation` recognises descriptions about time and draws.
- **`components/AapTimeFlow.tsx`:** the question and verdict cards, with "back one answer".
- **`MatchMode`:**
  - in AAP mode, a description about draws or time opens this flow. One that is mainly a foul (e.g. "cruzó justo cuando sonó la campana") stays a foul play;
  - the topic picker gets a "Tiempo, empates y desempates" button.
- Multiple-choice answers use neutral, left-aligned buttons (`.matchAnswers.isStacked`) instead of the green/red yes/no styling.
- App version 0.30.0.

## Reviewer notes
- Rule 10.c says the last chukker goes on when level only "en los partidos jugados por eliminación". That's why the general-rules path asks whether the match is a knockout one.
- The women's regulation adds 30 seconds when level but says nothing more. The answer then falls back to the general rule.

## Test plan
- [x] New tests:
  - a level last chukker under each tournament;
  - the follow-up questions asked per tournament;
  - every answer path, for every tournament and both languages, cites an existing rule and clause, or an existing regulation;
  - Rule 10.c still contains the knockout wording;
  - description detection, including that a crossing play is not taken as a time question.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test:rules` (166/166), `npm run test:sw`, `npm run test:match-ui`, `npm run build`
- [x] In the browser, with Copa República set in the profile:
  - "Terminó el último chukker empatado…" → second-leg question → "No" → *El partido termina empatado*, citing the regulation;
  - "Rojo cruzó a Azul justo cuando sonó la campana…" → still a crossing play;
  - the topic picker → teams level on points → three or more → goal difference, goals scored, then a draw by lot.

  Desktop, and mobile at 375px in dark mode.

author: runemark7
body: ## Summary Follow-up to #98. Paper only. No gate threshold, holdout, cost, graduation, or mint-ban change. `DISCOVERY_REFILL_BATCH_SIZE` stays 16. - **Buy-and-hold requeue.** The v4-only batch (`v4-bh-requeue-20261027`) matched a `gate_v4` tag and a prod dry-run found 1 name. The other discovery-window buy-and-hold misses are under `sltp_cap100_bhdsr_tiled87_20261008` (185) and `sltp_cap100_bhdsr_20261008` (156). New batch id `bh-only-requeue-20261027` and new file `discovery_bh_requeue.json`, so the unapplied v4 file is not this queue. One apply freezes all 342. Dry-run is still the default. Fail reasons must still be only discovery-window buy-and-hold comparisons, and the later checks must still be absent. The retest uses `n_backtested`, not `n_backtested + 1`. The holdout stays sealed. - **Lease expiry.** A claim used to set TTL to `2 × 600s × ceil(n / parallel)` (16 names at parallel 1 was 19200s, about 5.3h). It is now the heartbeat grace, `FARM_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECONDS` (900s). A running or idle heartbeat from that worker renews its discovery leases and its requalify leases. The first heartbeat that lists a name in `heartbeat.evaluating` records `started_at`, and that name is not renewed past `started_at + 2 ×` the eval timeout (1200s; timeout 0 still uses the 600s backstop). A paused heartbeat does not renew. Names not yet started stay leased while the worker heartbeats and return about 15 minutes after the last heartbeat. - **Throughput.** With `--workers 2`, the parent posted a result before submitting the next name, so one core sat idle for the POST. The next name is submitted first; the POST carries `heartbeat.evaluating` for the names already in flight. The buffer `mix_refill` (up to 64) runs outside `paper_state_lock`; the lock is taken again only to drop names that became taken and to append the rest. The shared tape was already reused until its sha256 changes. That path is unchanged. Qualify math is unchanged. ## Evidence Fixture shaped like the prod dry-run: 1 `gate_v4` + 185 tiled + 156 pre-tiled = 342. Decoys (other fail, mixed reasons, holdout, cost stress, v5 tag, qualified, ops park, a different old tag, book names) stay out. Dry-run writes nothing. Apply is idempotent. A leftover `discovery_v4_bh_requeue.json` does not short-circuit the new scan. `python3 -m pytest`: 736 passed, 11 skipped. `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) clean. ## Merge danger Do not apply until a prod dry-run of this batch reports about 1 + 185 + 156. The earlier v4 batch was not applied; applying this one is the single queue for all 342. A second apply does not move the timestamp. After the server rolls, an offline worker's names return about 15 minutes after its last heartbeat, including names it had not started. A live worker's heartbeats keep those unstarted names. A name it has actually started cannot be held past about 20 minutes from that start. Workers on the previous image still get the 15-minute grace (their result posts renew the lease) and do not send `evaluating`, so the per-name cap starts once this worker image is out. The overlap fix is in the worker process, so the farm hosts need this checkout for the second core to stay busy across the result POST.

author: cstheorist
body:
## What and why

Queries that look local can broadcast or add global-index participants without explaining why. Add `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` for physical SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE plans, `SHOW TARN PLAN FOR` for unbound prepared statements, and bounded `SHOW TARN QUERIES` observations. Closes #133.

Plans reuse the executor's coercion/routing and colocation guards and existing schema lint. They distinguish cached-map constraints and upper bounds from unknown parameters, dependent/global base-row lookups, conditional grouped reads, runtime alternatives and actual completed observations. Planning never materializes subqueries, reads user tuples, allocates IDs, takes locks or commits buffered writes. Unsupported formats/options/complex shapes fail explicitly. Text and binary MySQL result envelopes are covered.

Runtime observations retain at most 256 digests, 512-byte redacted samples and 4096 explicitly observed buckets per call. They separate routed targets/staged writes from commit cardinality, preserve errors and retries, exclude detached background work, and report coverage/cancellation/eviction. Complex queries and other administration remain untracked; bucket totals are partial and documented. No throughput/latency improvement is claimed.

The public test uses equivalent parent/child schemas and proves identical 16-row results while aligning shard keys changes observed fanout from two shards to one. Documentation describes semantics, bounds, exposure and proof limits.

## How it was tested

- Pinned Rust 1.98.1: rustfmt, workspace/all-target clippy with warnings denied, workspace unit/IPROTO tests (including 160 SQL tests).
- Native and Lua fallback storage protocol suites with yield/lock checks, including the existing engine/lazy crash and replication cases.
- New public MySQL suite in native memtx, Lua-only memtx and native vinyl: prepared/text/unbound plans, READ COMMITTED distinctions, unsupported subqueries with no reads, no IDs/implicit commits, schema lint/colocation, exact join results, redaction, errors, commit attribution and bounded eviction.
- MariaDB 10.11 differential suite: 1,014 cases per storage mode. Plan JSON fields are engine-specific; the result envelope and subsequent data/transaction behavior are checked separately.
- Transactions: 27 tests in each of the three modes; READ COMMITTED: 30 tests each on native memtx/vinyl; online DDL: 21 tests on native memtx. Lost-reply faults pass in all three modes, preserving 1180/unknown outcome and exactly one increment; RF3 failover passes with memtx and vinyl.
- TLA+: GroupedTables, GroupedRead, Local_ROValidate and Recov_GC pass; both grouped-read negative controls violate the expected invariants. Coordinator hooks only observe existing events; the model change is a proof-boundary comment, with no state/message/action change. Verus bodies are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` and native/Lua `lua/test/run.sh` pass
- [x] SQL/live-fault validation complete as listed above
- [x] Relevant TLA+ positive and sensitivity checks pass; no protocol behavior changes
- [x] Verified bodies unchanged
- [x] Docs, generators and `CHANGELOG.md` updated

## Summary

The transcript column sat 5px left of the composer column, and moved 5px whenever autoscroll ran (for example when the clarifying-question card opened). Enter in the question card did nothing.

- `src/renderer/src/index.css`: `scrollbar-app` now reserves its gutter on both edges (`scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges`) and always shows its thumb. ## Problem
`Create` → `CreateNode` → `resolveNodeClassFromNodeSpec` always loaded the NodeClass named `default`. Karpenter labels every NodeClaim with `karpenter.bizflycloud.com/bizflycloudnodeclass=<name>`, and those labels are copied onto the node spec. The NodeClass is now resolved from that label, falling back to `default` when it is missing.

author: shiba4life
body:
A normal clean shutdown updates the storage totals and flushes native files. An upgrade can therefore lose the exact match between its pre-stop snapshot and the final stopped CURRENT pair. This adds `cloud backup-v2 start-stopped` so the upgrade can make and verify a real final V2 backup before it selects the candidate program.

The command requires the exact clean session, flush receipt, existing account connection, automatic-off policy, and exclusive native owner locks. It uses the ordinary source, semantic/counter/file certification, transfer, inventory, and publication path. It retains original source metadata before release, reads every accepted provider object, and verifies each complete native file hash. Both CURRENT files must stay unchanged. A resume keeps the same request and admits only its exact retained marker link. Native encryption, file readers, and file format stay intact. Main files and metadata use R2; CAS runs use B2. The cloud service remains opaque.

Validation: [exact source CI](https://github.com/EdgeVector/lastdb/actions/runs/40636286104), [benchmark-complete](https://github.com/EdgeVector/lastdb/actions/runs/40635484496), and [exact Mac client](https://github.com/EdgeVector/lastdb/actions/runs/40635484329) pass. The actual DEV operation passes an automatic snapshot, two mutation-log checkpoints, same-cut log restart, a separate interval-triggered snapshot, an interrupted stopped-source resume, baseline reopen, and two source-free restores with two starts each. Reads verify 14 exact records, two deletions, and both complete 8 MiB files. All five backups pass independent full provider-byte and whole-account checks, with zero reservations and prior allocations unchanged. The exact restored client also passes native/persist health and the 60-second memory observation. All owned DEV nodes stop cleanly. Raw receipts remain outside Git.

All PR source checks pass, including the separate received-range operations. Primary activation uses the companion upgrade policy after the accepted-main CI and complete measurement uploads pass.

## 3. Shared script

`js/ts-tracking.js` loads with `defer` on pages that embed a GoHighLevel form or the LeadConnector chat widget, and on pages that received the Call Now button. It is wrapped in try/catch. A comment at the top states that name, email, phone, and message text are never pushed to `dataLayer`.

### Form success (the conversion)

Read from the production form app the live iframe loads (`https://stcdn.leadconnectorhq.com/_preview/cuexcqRf.js`, fetched 2026-10-28). After `submitRequest` resolves, helper `gd` posts:

- `["set-sticky-contacts", "_ud", JSON.stringify(contact), locationId, fingerprint]`

Only the `embedded_iframe_` message is treated as a confirmed submit. The `_ud` JSON holds contact fields and is also what a sticky-sync helper can send, so it is ignored and never copied. On that signal the script pushes once per submit (5 second dedupe per form id):

`{event:'ghl_form_submit', form_id, branch, lead_channel:'web-form'}`

Accepted origins: `*.leadconnectorhq.com`, `*.msgsndr.com`, `*.trushineservice.com`. The site's embeds use `https://api.leadconnectorhq.com`.

Confidence: moderate-high. The signal is in the current production bundle, on the success path only. It was not confirmed by submitting a live form, because that would create a real lead. Open any form page with `?ts_debug=1` and submit in GTM preview. The console logs message shape and redacts contact values. If GoHighLevel changes the bundle, this signal can stop.

`form_embed.js` on the parent page listens for `set-sticky-contacts`, `fetch-query-params`, and height messages. It does not itself emit a submit event.

About 105 pages also POST a custom HTML form to GoHighLevel with `mode: 'no-cors'`. That response is opaque, so it is not a confirmed success and this script does not count it. The same bundle sets an internal completed state after a widget submit and does not dispatch a parent event for the captured phone or email. `chat_lead` is not emitted. Configure that inside GoHighLevel (a workflow on the widget, or the widget's own settings). Do not expect it from the site.

On landing, `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_term`, `utm_content`, and `gclid` are stored first-touch for 90 days in `localStorage` and a first-party cookie, with `landing_page` set to the path. author: davidbagh22
body:
### Verified code-level vulnerability
`POST /telegram/webhook` currently checks `if expected_secret and ...`; when `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (default), it accepts forged `Update` JSON. This PR changes the handler to fail closed before JSON parsing. Three async regressions cover missing/wrong/correct secret.

### IMPORTANT DEPLOYMENT BLOCKER — DO NOT MERGE YET
Further review of `app/webapp.py:lifespan` found **the production webapp calls `bot.set_webhook(...)` whenever `effective_base_url` exists**, with `secret_token=settings.effective_webhook_secret or None`. It is **not safe to assume polling mode**. If the Render `WEBHOOK_SECRET` environment variable is currently empty, merging this fix would reject legitimate Telegram updates and cause an outage. The connection cannot read only the existence of this secret without exposing values; no secret was read or changed. User authorization is required for any secret/config change.

**Keep DRAFT** until the owner verifies (without disclosing value) that Render `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is configured and the Telegram webhook header is set accordingly, or explicitly authorizes a coordinated secure migration. Do not change secrets, call `set_webhook`, or trigger a deploy from this PR. CI success alone is not sufficient. Review how the webhook is configured, then approve release with exact HEAD CI and automatic Render deploy.

### Tests
`python -m pytest -q tests/test_telegram_webhook_secret.py tests/test_webapp_frontend_mount.py tests/test_stabilization_contracts.py`
`ruff check app/webapp.py tests/test_telegram_webhook_secret.py --select E9,F`

No live webhook requests, Telegram messages or production changes performed.

body:
## Summary

On Windows with psmux, a new Codex cell ended at once with `psmux: can't find session: mulmoterminal__mt-<id>` while a Claude cell on the same machine ran (#3201). The reporter's codex is the npm install — `codex`, `codex.cmd`, `codex.ps1`, no `codex.exe`; claude is the native `claude.exe`.

`ptySpawn`'s tmux branch handed the pane's program to `new-session -- <file> <args>` unresolved. psmux takes a `--` command as an argument vector and starts it with `CreateProcessW` itself, after resolving the bare name the way its `search_path` does: the first file on PATH spelled exactly like the name, then one per `PATHEXT` extension. For an npm install that is the extensionless shim or the `.cmd`, neither a PE image — the spawn fails, the fresh psmux server exits, and the attaching client reports the session it was told to create as missing. The direct (no-tmux) spawn has wrapped such a shim in `cmd.exe` since #798 / #801; the resolution never ran for the pane.

- `server/infra/process/resolve-bin.ts` — `resolveTmuxPaneLaunch` (+ `ForEnv`): the same decision as `resolvePtyLaunch` (the `.exe` by its absolute path; a batch shim through cmd.exe), carried the way a multiplexer can take it. The decision itself is now one shared `windowsProgram`.
- The batch case is `cmd.exe /d /e:ON /v:OFF /c %MULMOTERMINAL_BATCH_COMMAND_LINE%`, with the quoted command (`"C:\…\codex.cmd" "-c" "…"`, each word through `escapeBatchArgument`) set on the session with `new-session -e`. The direct route's raw `/d /s /c "…"` string cannot be used here: psmux quotes every argv word for the CRT, so the quotes inside would be re-escaped and cmd.exe would read a different line. No word in the argv holds a space or a quote, so that quoting leaves each one as written, and cmd.exe expands the variable once in its `/c` text before parsing. psmux's own master takes this exact route for a batch program (`batch_script_target` / `PSMUX_BATCH_LINE` in `src/pane.rs`, added after the 3.4.0 release of 2026-10-13 — the released 3.4.0 does not have it).
- `server/infra/process/cmd-escape.ts` — `batchCommand` (the quoted words) split out of `batchCommandLine`, which now wraps it.
- `server/session/pty/pty-spawn.ts` — the tmux branch asks the resolver against the pane's environment (the one the binary check uses) and merges its variable into the `-e` set. Off Windows the resolver is the identity, so the tmux branch is unchanged there.
- README: one bullet under "psmux on Windows". Plan: `plans/fix-3201-psmux-codex-cmd-shim.md`.

## Items to Confirm / Review

- **Not run on psmux.** No Windows machine here. psmux's side is read from its 3.4.0 source: `--` as an argument vector (`src/main.rs` `raw_cmd_after_dd` → `create_window_raw` → `build_raw_command`), `-e` reaching the raw pane (`merge_session_env_into_app` before `create_window_raw`, and `apply_user_environment` inside it), `search_path` taking the exact name before extensions (`crates/portable-pty-psmux/src/cmdbuilder.rs`), and `append_quoted` quoting a word only when it holds whitespace or a quote. The reporter can confirm on their machine; the pane's program after `--` should become `cmd.exe /d /e:ON /v:OFF /c %MULMOTERMINAL_BATCH_COMMAND_LINE%`.
- **The cmd.exe half is measured, in the Windows CI job**: `pty-spawn-win.spec.ts` spawns the new form through node-pty (which quotes argv under the same rule psmux does) against a `.cmd` shim and compares the child's argv — the same argument table the direct route is checked with, codex's TOML `-c key="value"` overrides included, plus the claim that a `%VAR%` inside an argument is NOT expanded a second time (the direct route's known limitation). That last assertion is my reading of cmd's single expansion pass; if `windows-pr` disagrees, the test is what is wrong, not the fix.
- **`.exe` resolution is applied to the pane too**, not only the batch wrapping: psmux takes the exact-name file first, which for an npm install is the extensionless shim beside the `.cmd`, so a user with a real `codex.exe` later on PATH would also have failed. Same rule as the direct spawn (#794).
- **Platform-gated, not psmux-gated.** The resolver runs for `win32`, like `resolvePtyLaunch`; the Windows tmux path is de facto psmux. PR #3133 gated its branches on psmux detection — say if that convention should hold here as well.
- **The `resolvePtyLaunch` refactor** (shared `windowsProgram`) was checked by running the old function verbatim beside the new one over generated inputs in a throwaway harness (not committed); the existing `resolve-bin.spec.ts` is unchanged and passes.
- **Out of scope**: the `unknown option 'terminal-features'` warning the same report shows. Cosmetic, on every psmux session; #3133 left the fork's conf filter out deliberately. A separate change if wanted.

## User Prompt

- https://github.com/receptron/mulmoterminal/issues/3201 — 直せる？
- pr → review まで進めて

## Implementation approach

- The rule stays a pure function in `resolve-bin.ts` with the platform, PATH, ComSpec and the existence probe as parameters, so it is checked from any host; the call site only wires it in.
- One `windowsProgram` decision, two carriers: `resolvePtyLaunch` (node-pty, raw string) and `resolveTmuxPaneLaunch` (argv + env). A spec pins that the two name the same file for every PATH layout the direct route is tested on, since the binary check follows the first and the pane runs the second.
- The pane is resolved against `ptyEnv(unset, env)` — the environment `refuseBeforeStart` already resolves against — so "can it launch" and "what launches" cannot disagree.

Closes #3201

author: upasanaajbani
body:
Closes #12.

## What's here

**20 cases** in `packages/evals/dataset/cases/<id>/`, across 6 categories:

| Category | Cases | | Outcome | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| images | 4 | | fix | 16 |
| names | 5 | | no_change_needed | 3 |
| forms | 5 | | unsure | 1 |
| aria | 3 | | | |
| contrast | 2 | | | |
| structure | 1 | | | |

- **Fix cases** each have a reference fix in `expected/` (for the judge in #15). The custom-checkbox reference fix switches to a native checkbox, in line with the "native over ARIA" rubric.
- **No-change cases** are stale reports on code that's already correct in ways an agent might try to "improve": a decorative `alt=""`, a visually hidden label, and an icon button with hidden text.
- **The unsure case** is an icon-only link in an order table where nothing says what it does.
- **Issue data is real axe output.** Every case was client-rendered with React in Chromium and run through axe 4.14 (WCAG 2.1 A/AA). Each fix and unsure input triggers exactly its target rule, each reference fix comes back with no violations, and each no-change input is clean while its older version reproduces the reported issue. That check was a one-off script and isn't in this PR.

**`npm run evals:validate`** (`src/dataset/validate.ts`) checks that:
- every `case.json` matches `EvalCase` and its `id` matches its folder
- `input/` holds only `filePath`, `allowedLines` stay inside the file, and the folder holds no unexpected or wrong-kind entries
- `expected/` is used only for fix cases, holds exactly the input file, differs from it, and every change stays within `allowedLines`
- `manifest.json` (`datasetVersion: 1`) lists exactly the case folders

A unit test validates the real dataset, so `npm run check` (and therefore CI) covers it.

**Type-checking:** `dataset/tsconfig.json` checks every input, reference fix and case test as part of `npm run typecheck`, so the bugs are accessibility bugs, not build errors. This adds `@types/react` to `@curbcut/evals`.

`src/dataset/lines.ts` holds the scope check that scorer (c) in #13 can reuse. When lines repeat, it picks the alignment with the fewest out-of-scope changes, and it ignores CRLF vs LF.

**Core schema:** `EvalCase` gains `version` and `framework: "react"`, and `EvalResult` records `datasetVersion` and `caseVersion`, as the project plan asks.

## Notes for #13 and #14

- The dataset README sets out the harness assumptions: each input default-exports a component that takes no props, styles are inline, and the page wrapper is `<html lang="en">` with a `<title>` and a `<main>`.
- With an iframe on the page (`frame-title-video-embed`), axe can't decide its page-level `bypass` rule and leaves it unresolved, so the "resolved" scorer should ignore that rule.
- `smoke` tags and `dataset/CHANGELOG.md` are left for #14.

## Testing

- `npm run check` passes (format, lint, typecheck, 113 tests).
- `npm run evals:validate` reports all 20 cases valid.

author: saikireeti2905
body:
## Summary — CRITICAL
Closes Rahul audit #1. Before this patch, any party could mint a fresh KERI AID, self-issue an ACDC claiming `role=admin` (or any other role in the policy engine), bind it to themselves, sign it with their own key, and present a grant whose KEL they also controlled. The grant was cryptographically internally consistent, the KEL verifier accepted it, and ds-login issued a JWT with admin claims. **End-to-end bypass of the entire login system.**

The fix is a policy gate, not a cryptographic one.

## Change
`AcdcVerifier` now holds a set of issuer AIDs it will accept grants from, loaded from `DS__TRUSTED_ISSUER_AIDS` (JSON list env var). Any grant whose issuer AID is not in the allowlist is rejected **before** KEL resolution — so an attacker can't even cause their malicious inline KEL to be parsed by our KERIpy.

**Gate placement — step 2 of `verify_grant`** (between envelope-parse and subject-binding). Running it this early avoids:
- parsing an attacker-controlled inline KEL with KERIpy (defence in depth against KERIpy parser bugs)
- any network round-trip to attacker-named OOBI URLs
- subject-binding leaking which login AID the server was expecting

## Fail-safe defaults
- Default = empty list = reject-all
- `environment=production` + empty list → lifespan refuses to start (loud misconfig beats silent reject-everything)
- Outside production, warning + continue — nonce-only challenge still works for dev/CI where no trusted issuer exists yet

## Deployer action required
Set `DS__TRUSTED_ISSUER_AIDS=["<AID>"]` on every ds-login deployment. In HUS this is the ds-credential-issuer's bootstrap AID — visible in its startup logs: `issuer identifier ready: alias=hus-issuer aid=…`.

The matching gitops PR against hus-services/login/values.yaml follows this one.

## Test plan
- [x] 3 new scenarios: empty-allowlist rejection, right-issuer-wrong-attacker rejection, legitimate-issuer passes the gate
- [x] New tests assert the KEL resolver is **never** consulted when the gate fails — closes the defence-in-depth concern
- [x] Existing grant tests updated to pass a trust-list fixture so their intended downstream paths still execute
- [x] Full suite: 44 passed, 1 skipped

author: yonghong-song
body:
If the result of __builtin_preserve_field_info(),
__builtin_preserve_type_info() or __builtin_preserve_enum_value() is not used, e.g., for bpf.c:
```
  enum E { A = 4 };
  void f(void) { (void)__builtin_preserve_enum_value(*(enum E *)A, 1); }
```
'clang --target=bpf -O2 -g -c bpf.c' crashed in BPFAbstractMemberAccess.

Such a call is collected for relocation through its users only, so a call whose result is not used is not relocated and is left for removePreserveAccessIndexIntrinsic(). There, it was handled as a preserve_struct_access_index() call and replaced with a GEP of its first argument, which is not a base pointer for these intrinsics.

These intrinsics have no side effects, so just remove such calls.

author: mathershifter
body:
Sets the package version to 0.8.1, the next version after `v0.8.0`. The release is everything merged since that tag: the `raw` step (#98) and the solicit-newline fix (#99), both merged. The schema gains the `raw` step additively and the format id stays `2026-10`.

- `pyproject.toml`: `version = "0.8.1"`
- `uv.lock`: the `autobot` entry, refreshed with `uv lock`

No other file carries the version (`grep -rn 0.8.0` outside `uv.lock` finds only `pyproject.toml`). SPEC.md and README.md are untouched.

Checked locally on this branch:

- `uv build --clear --no-create-gitignore` produces `autobot-0.8.1.tar.gz` and `autobot-0.8.1-py3-none-any.whl`. The sdist carries both `schemas/autobot.2026-10.json` and `src/autobot/autobot.2026-10.json`.
- The wheel installed into a fresh Python 3.12 venv: `autobot --help` works, `autobot validate` reports both `examples/*.autobot.yaml` valid, `autobot/autobot.2026-10.json` is present (`importlib.resources`) and has the `rawStep` definition, `importlib.metadata.version("autobot")` is `0.8.1`, and in a fresh `python -I` interpreter `Config.model_validate` accepts a `raw` step as a `RawStep`.
- `uv run --locked pytest -q -rs -m "not slow"` on this branch's base (`d96f043`, the only difference being the version string): 4397 passed, 34 skipped (the ksh, mksh and ksh93 tests, those shells being absent locally), 35 slow deselected, in 17:52; the `build`-marked tests ran. The full suite including the slow tests ran on #99's branch: 4432 passed, 34 skipped.

A draft GitHub release `Autobot 0.8.1` for the tag `v0.8.1` targets `main`; no tag exists yet. Its notes are below.

## Merge order

1. **This PR** (its CI run on `main` is the full suite that `release.yml` reuses).
2. **Tag the merge commit on `main`**, annotated, with the version `release.yml` checks against `pyproject.toml`:

   ```
   git fetch origin
   git tag -a v0.8.1 -m "Autobot 0.8.1" origin/main
   git push origin v0.8.1
   ```

   `origin/main` must be this PR's merge commit (check with `git log -1 origin/main`). The workflow's first guard compares the tag with `pyproject.toml` at the tagged commit: a tag pushed on a commit whose `pyproject.toml` isn't 0.8.1 fails there, so the tag goes on `main` only after this PR merges. The tag starts `release.yml`: it checks the tag against the version and that the commit is on `main`, waits for or reuses `main`'s `Tests` job for that commit, builds and smoke-tests the wheel, attaches the wheel and sdist to the draft, checks both are there, and publishes the draft with its notes and title unchanged, marked Latest.

## Release notes (as on the draft)

Autobot 0.8.1 covers everything merged since `v0.8.0` (PRs #98 to #100): a new built-in step, `raw`, that types keystrokes with no Return and no prompt wait, and a fix to the prompt wait's solicit newline so that a device which is printing, such as a boot loader counting down, never gets a Return pressed into it. Scripts still use the `2026-10` format, and the format id is unchanged; the schema gains the `raw` step additively (new `rawStep` and `rawPiece` definitions, `raw` in `step.oneOf`) and ships in the package as `autobot/autobot.2026-10.json`. Every 0.8.0 script is valid as it is. The progress lines, the error messages and the exit statuses are as in 0.8.0, with the additions below for `raw`.

## New: the `raw` step

`raw` types a list of pieces back to back, each at once, with no Return and no prompt wait (#98):

```yaml
- raw: ['^a', 'b']        # tmux/screen prefix: Ctrl+A then a plain b
- raw: ['^[', ':wq']      # Escape, then the text :wq (follow with `return: 1` to enter it)
```

- A piece of exactly `^` and one more character is a control key, from the same table as `control`, and sends the same byte; any other second character is the `control_char` validation error at the step's `raw`, with the `control` step's message. Every other piece is text: a Jinja2 template rendered like a `line` and sent verbatim with no line break. There is no escape for a literal `^x`: `^`, `^abc` and `a^b` are text, exactly `^a` as written is always Ctrl+A, and a template that renders to `^a` is text, since a piece is classified as written, before it is rendered (#98).
- An empty piece and an empty list send nothing and change nothing; a piece that isn't a string, and a bare string instead of a list, are validation errors (#98).
- No settle inside the step: the pieces go out in the same breath, even after a control key. After the step, the half-second settle applies to the next line only when the last piece was a control key; a text piece clears it, so a `line` after `['^[', ':wq']` is sent at once (#98).
- `raw` presses no Return, leaves the partial-line flag alone, never raises `PartialLine` and makes no canonical-mode length check. It ends the at-a-shell-prompt state and makes the next prompt wait solicit, as `control` does. A write that fails is bounded by the step's `timeout`; a send of which the pty took nothing leaves the session where it was (#98).
- Progress lines `>> raw sent: ^A` for a control key and `>> raw sent` for text, never the text; the error report names the step `(raw)`; a send that fails says `while sending raw text` (#98).
- Plugins: `session.send(text, timeout=...)`, on `SessionLike`, sends text verbatim with no line break; control keys go through `session.sendcontrol`. `raw` is a reserved step key, rejected for a plugin like the other built-in keys (#98).
- Docs: SPEC `### raw` after `control`, with a paragraph on Alt, arrow and function keys and why Cmd/Win have no syntax; `raw` added wherever the step types, the non-line sends, the settle, the send timeouts, the templated values, the output table and the error-report names are enumerated. README: step table row, examples next to `control`, plugin bullet for `session.send` (#98).

## Fixes

- A prompt wait's one solicit newline, the Return pressed for an idle console, is sent only at the end of a 5-second poll in which nothing at all arrived, not one in which nothing matched. A device that is printing is not idle: a boot loader's countdown with no line break (`Hit any key to stop autoboot: 8 7 6 ...`) used to get the Return after 5 seconds and take it for the interrupt key, so any script with a device reboot and an "any key" boot loader failed. A poll with unmatched bytes sends nothing and does not use up the one solicit; a later silent poll still gets it, once. A boot that is silent for over 5 seconds before it checks for a pending key still gets the newline: give the next `cmd` an `after` on something printed late in the boot, since a `cmd` with `after` never presses Return (#99).
- Docs: SPEC Prompt Handling step 3 and every statement of the rule say "silent" where they said "no match", with the reason, and `line` gets the note about `after` after a reboot. README: the `cmd` section says the same, and the reboot example uses `cmd: "true"` with `after: Debian GNU/Linux` and `timeout: 10m` instead of `delay_after: 10s` (#99).

## Tests

- New `tests/test_raw.py` (P8-61, 24 tests); the enumerations of the built-in steps and of `SessionLike` updated (#98). Fake device: `--countdown SECS` prints a countdown with no line break and logs `ABORT=<hex>` if any byte arrives; P4-47 in `test_get_prompt.py`, two slow tests: no Return during a countdown, and a countdown followed by silence still gets exactly one (#99).
- The suite without the `slow` tests, on the release branch: 4397 passed, 34 skipped locally (the ksh, mksh and ksh93 tests, those shells being absent), 35 slow deselected (0.8.0: 4295 passed, 34 skipped, 33 deselected). The full suite on #99's branch: 4432 passed, 34 skipped.
- Version 0.8.1 (#100).

**Full list of changes**: https://github.com/mathershifter/autobot/compare/v0.8.0...v0.8.1

_Requested by **Hawk** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011PDbJa1fiWQFWP9M4hX1Vw?thread=cmsg_011PDbJa1fiWQFWP9M4hX1Vw4kNhsheqTvfkz5scPziiEu)_

This is a follow-up to #272. The `panchang alarms: a switch changes only itself and no row moves` e2e test failed about once in every three runs. It showed up on #275's CI.

**Cause.** The test read all twelve switches right after the last click, before Angular had re-rendered. The failure snapshot shows Godhuli was switched on, so the app was right and the test read too early.

**Fix.** After each tap, the test now waits for that switch's `aria-checked` to update, then compares the whole row and the row positions. Only the test changes; app code is untouched.

**Check.** With `--repeat-each=15 --workers=4` on mobile-chrome-360, all 30 runs pass. Before the fix, the same command failed 3 of 6 alarm runs.

(The branch also merges its old, already squash-merged #272 head so the push did not need a force. The net diff against main is just this one test file.)

body:
dunk_core.list_panes() computes `agent_status_source` / `agent_status_reason` / `agent_status_inferred` (DS #46) and the desk projects them, but `dunk_api.h_list_panes()` **dropped all three** because its keep tuple did not name them. A restart could not fix it: the live daemon's core hash equals main's (`0b663c507626`), so the loss was **in the handler**, downstream of the core.

**Head `80a1d11` (2.70.76).**

## The fix
- the three keys are in the keep tuple;
- **contract unchanged**: a key is present only when the core supplies it, so a pane with no provenance gains **no null keys** (the `if key in pane` filter is untouched);

## Tests (`tests/test_dunk_list_panes_provenance.py`, 4)
True survives; **FALSE is a value, not a missing key** (a truthiness-based pass-through would keep the key and null the value — the same defect in different clothes); a pane with no provenance gains no null keys; and a key-set assertion so no other field is added or removed.

Reverting the keep tuple reds three of the four.

## Not verified
No live call after the fix (the daemon is still 2.70.59 in memory and a restart is not mine to take); no desk-side projection run (that is the desk lane's); no full suite.

Closes #99

### fix(checkout): price order lines from product price and link reservation
Every checkout failed with `null value in column "product_variant_id"`
and, had it got further, would have priced every line at LKR 0: the
service read `product.base_price`, `product.title` and
`variant.price_override`, none of which exist on the models.

- Unit price = products.price + product_variants.additional_price,
  rejected with 400 if not positive; the client never supplies a price
- Order items persist product_variant_id
- The stock reservation is linked to its order inside the order
  transaction so payment success can confirm it by order id (ADR-004)
- If the order insert fails the reservation is released immediately
  instead of holding stock for 15 minutes
- shipping_method is validated against [standard, pickup]
- Unit test mocks used the same non-existent columns; they now mirror
  the real models. New integration tests run against PostgreSQL.

Closes #102

_Requested by **team kami labs** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01UyU4t5ka28Pu8MGH8sVBZy?thread=cmsg_01UyU4t5ka28Pu8MGH8sVBZy4PPnkg5LhSNXdeC37BMmFy)_

## What this adds

T16, which unblocks T12: the registry entries Suhani's APP-03, 05, 07 and 08 modules read, and the selector that decides when they run.

- `registry/approaches/APP-01..08.json`: one entry per approach with its select and reject rules, fallback and triggers, budget targets from the plan, and dependency licences.
- `registry/selection-matrix.json`: default / optional / experimental / excluded per project type. APP-04 and APP-06 start experimental, as the plan says.
- `src/registry/condition.mjs`: the shared condition evaluator (T14 question rules and T17 design rules will reuse it).
- `src/registry/load.mjs`: `loadApproaches(root?)` validates every file and checks them against each other (all 8 present once, one registry version, no self-fallbacks).
- `src/registry/select.mjs`: `selectApproaches` as frozen in `docs/interfaces.md`. Every decision has a reason, every selection a fallback, and experimental selections carry `needsApproval` (B1 for APP-06, B2 otherwise).
- `forge select <brief.json> [--json]` prints the decision for a brief.
- `docs/registry.md` has the rules table and the matrix in plain words.

## Tests (A6)

`tests/decision/` holds 48 briefs, 3 qualifying and 3 non-qualifying per approach. Each negative case names the rule it exercises (matrix, selectWhen, rejectWhen or plugin) and the test checks the reason matches, so a case cannot pass for the wrong reason. APP-01 qualifies for every brief Forge accepts, so its negatives are briefs Forge refuses (two languages, a page without a CTA, an e-commerce type), where the selector throws `SchemaInvalid`. The suite also pins what each of the 7 sample briefs selects:

| Sample | Selected |
| --- | --- |
| business, portfolio | APP-01 |
| event | APP-01, APP-05 |
| launch | APP-01, APP-02 |
| showroom | APP-01, APP-03 |
| nonprofit | APP-01, APP-06 (needs B1) |
| flagship | APP-01, APP-02, APP-03, APP-04 (needs B2), APP-07 |

`npm test`: 233 pass, 0 fail.

## Needs both owners

- One additive interface change: `selectApproaches` takes an optional `opts.now` for `decidedAt`, so the selector stays deterministic in tests. `docs/interfaces.md` is updated.
- The rules and matrix are proposals from the plan's "Selected when" column. Worth a look for T12: APP-03, APP-07 and APP-08 reject a `low` device floor; APP-05 does not, because its quality ladder covers it. APP-07 needs flagship + tier L and motion 2 or more.

## Notes

- GSAP and the Spline runtime stay `licenceVerified: false` until someone reads their terms. The MIT/Apache/Unlicense entries are from npm metadata.
- Adds a `select` line to `src/cli/index.mjs` and the README, which may give a one-line conflict with #9 (`site`). Whichever merges second rebases.

author: f000nkkk
body:
Core backlog item 8: benchmarks for the `gac-wgpu` batch kernels and `BackgroundPool`, so the parallel cutoff and the pool are judged on numbers.

**What the bench found.** The four motor kernels locked their shared output once per item, so the parallel path was slower than sequential at every size (100k motors: 13 ms sequential, 21 ms parallel). 

**Fix.** `ComputeContext::parallel_ranges(count, |range| ...)` runs `work` over contiguous sub-ranges (one range below the cutoff, one per thread above it); `parallel_for` is now a thin wrapper over it. The kernels fill a local buffer per range and lock once. Results are unchanged (existing kernel tests pass).

| items | sequential | parallel before | parallel after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 000 | 117 us | 321 us | 273 us |
| 10 000 | 1.28 ms | 1.85 ms | 0.63 ms |
| 100 000 | 13.7 ms | 21.6 ms | 5.2 ms |

(`Motor3` transform kernel, 4-thread machine; the `Fixed` kernel is the same within noise.)

**Not changed, and why.**
- The default parallel cutoff of 1 024 items still loses at 1k (a thread spawn per dispatch costs about 150 us) and wins at 4k (350 us against 515 us). Raising it changes which path several physics tests exercise, so it goes through team/physics.
- `BackgroundPool`: ~43 us for one job, ~12 us per job for 1 000 tiny jobs on 4 threads. Asset loads are I/O bound, so no change.
- Scratch reuse for `FixedArithmeticKernels` (no caller outside tests) and the physics broad phase (team/physics, no per-frame caller) is left until a caller exists.

Also: `.clippy-backlog` 1295 -> 1286 (recorded), `docs/segments/core.md` item 8 updated, new tests for `parallel_ranges` (exactly-once coverage, zero items).

author: dipta007
body:
### Summary
- When a folder is renamed or deleted on the reMarkable tablet, `rmapi`'s local `tree.cache` can still list the old folder path, causing `rmapi mkdir` to no-op and `rmapi put` to fail with `Error: directory doesn't exist`.
- Add `refresh=True` support to `ensure_remote_folder` (which runs `rmapi refresh` and clears `_MADE_FOLDERS`) and automatically retry `ensure_remote_folder(..., refresh=True)` + `rmapi put` once when `put` fails with `directory doesn't exist`.

author: phanyen06ym-ien
body:
Summary

This PR introduces a structured documentation layout for DX-OS Open-Core, covering project context, system architecture, four reusable Core capabilities, applications, integration, testing, deployment, open-source compliance, architecture decisions, and verification evidence.

The documentation is based on the selected architecture direction:

  • Modular Monolith

  • Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters)

  • Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)

  • Four Core capabilities: Identity, Workflow, Data Management, and API Gateway

This is a documentation-only PR. No production implementation or existing Core contract is changed.

Changes

1. Documentation Structure

Introduces the numbered documentation sections:

Directory | Purpose -- | -- 00-project/ | Project overview, problem, vision, MVP, glossary 01-architecture/ | System architecture and dependency boundaries 02-core/ | Identity, Workflow, Data, Gateway architecture 03-applications/ | IT Helpdesk and Facility 04-integration/ | Cross-component integration contracts 05-testing/ | Test strategy and acceptance 06-deployment/ | Installation and operations 07-open-source/ | Licensing and release documentation 08-decisions/ | Architecture Decision Records 09-evidence/ | Verification evidence 10-reviews/ | Independent reviews 11-poc/ | Proof-of-concept documentation

These selections establish the design direction. They do not imply that all implementations or integration tests have been accepted.

Other architecture decisions remain proposed or subject to independent review.

Verification

Local checks reported:

  • Documentation scaffold committed separately

  • 106 Markdown files staged

  • 12 non-empty documentation drafts

  • 94 empty placeholders identified

  • git diff --cached --check PASS

  • No production code changes identified in the staged documentation diff

  • Markdown links independently validated

  • Cross-document consistency review completed

  • Business scope aligned with Issue #53

  • Architecture/Security/Application reviewer approval

  • CI results confirmed

Review Focus

Reviewers are requested to verify:

  1. Product and MVP scope: Ensure consistency with the approved Business Contract, including Helpdesk and Facility reuse scope.

  2. Core–Application boundaries: Ensure reusable Core contracts do not contain application-specific business rules.

  3. Dependency rules: Confirm consistency with the existing Java package structure and provider adapters.

  4. Security and authorization: Distinguish authenticated principals, operation authorities, resource policies, and database enforcement.

  5. Transaction consistency: Review the unresolved Helpdesk–Workflow atomicity boundary.

  6. Documentation governance: Ensure proposed designs and placeholder files are not represented as implemented or verified capabilities.

Out of Scope

  • Refactoring production code

  • Moving legacy documentation or SQL evidence

  • Changing existing API/Core contracts

  • Database migration changes

  • Merging unreviewed implementation PRs

  • Claiming release-level E2E verification

References

  • Repository: https://github.com/lexuanbao258-collab/dxos-open-core

  • Business Contract: Issue #53

  • Identity/Gateway handoff: PR #46

  • Authorized Workflow candidate: PR #47

  • Workflow authority candidate: PR #48

  • Helpdesk backend candidate: PR #63

  • Portal BFF candidate: PR #70

  • Portal UI candidate: PR #71

Review Status

PROPOSED — REVIEW REQUIRED

Requested review areas: Architecture, Application/Business Contract, and Identity/Security.

Merge gate: Required reviews, documentation consistency checks, and applicable CI checks must pass before merging into main.

author: kimjooyoon
body:
## Summary

A source-owned record list can run natively but `assembling` previously rejected its finite input cases with `collection elements must be scalar values`. Carry declared nominal records through the bounded evaluator, typed case decoding, ordered sequences, constructors, optional presence, reads, immutable value copies, equality and canonical output.

The carrier retains declared type/field layouts and strictly validates source type IDs, keys, presence, cardinality and text bounds. Shared zero defaults form a bounded type DAG; expanded field/index occurrences still pay the 8192-slot quota. The private cell layout fits within the previous scalar cell size. Existing flat scalar collection limits retain their behavior.

The public example `examples/record-collections/assembly.gooo` selects the declared sum among two alternatives. Existing model features decline unsupported nominal layouts and selection proceeds deterministically. Completeness scope reports the nominal limits and explicitly lists direct nested assignment, two-present-pointer identity, and full dynamic nested dependency provenance as remaining dimensions.

## Validation

- [x] Targets `dev`; includes accepted PR #1838 ancestry with identical source tree across that ancestry merge.
- [x] Fifteen independently expected program/input cases agree between the evaluator and separately compiled generated Go. These are the same cases in two paths, not thirty independent cases. Coverage includes ordered sums and integers beyond2^53, four record field shapes, optional presence, record copy/literals, indexed reads and required-child value equality.
- [x] Source-owned CLI example:4/4 declared cases, model calls0. Typed source, generated source and metadata are retained separately.
- [x] Targeted malformed-child, exact8192/8193, depth8/9, optional-cycle, scalar-impersonation, shared-default and legacy32x256 boundaries pass.
- [x] Complete bodycodegen package and the named rendered-helper capacity regressions pass before the generated registration repair; the capacity remains75.
- [x] The Gooo/native registration generator produced nine digest-verified members, including the new source case, syntax141 and denominatorv103. Syntax/semantic/metric packages and the correct inventory CLI regression pass after registration.
- [x] The native workspace-split consumer passes against the committed registered source. Its Git-tree snapshot correctly refused the earlier unregistered commit even while working files had been repaired.
- [ ] Complete frozen-source local checks are running; original exact-head PR CI owns repository-wide canonical acceptance.
- [x] No generated region was hand-edited.

The prior full local run at25cc9f6 failed because the new public source was unregistered; that failure is retained. Earlier7b6a6cd validation was intentionally stopped after actual CLI output exposed its stale scalar-only completeness description. Both findings are corrected in the submitted source.

## Deterministic CI boundary

- [x] Gooo declarations and stable field/type IDs own the domain.
- [x] The registration result remains `PROPOSAL_ONLY`/`UNASSESSED`; its output does not grant acceptance or promotion authority.
- [x] Acceptance uses the exact current PR tuple, its six canonical jobs and digest-bound proof/receipt.

Review cap exception: nominal carriers, the shared typed codec, finite evaluator/Go oracles and scoped completeness reporting form one cross-layer value contract. The generated registration members keep the source inventory and its denominators synchronized; the implementation uses the existing CLI and report families.

author: andrewgazelka
body:
Since #835, `windows x64 / tests` fails on every train (e.g. [40629346215](https://github.com/indexable-inc/blaze/actions/runs/40629346215), job 122621804414). The one failure outside OPEN is `ra_jit::cargo::plan::tests::headerpad_written_again_after_a_clean`, which got `None` where it expected `Some(2097152)` at plan.rs:946.

The test wrote its own link line with unquoted paths. `shlex::split` treats a Windows path's backslashes as escapes, so it never found the `.headerpad` file. Real commands quote every path with `shlex::try_quote` (`LinkLine::command`), which is why the first assertions, built through `command`, pass. The test now quotes its paths the same way. The code itself doesn't change: it is Apple-only.

Verification: train [40632235377](https://github.com/indexable-inc/blaze/actions/runs/40632235377) on this branch (windows, linux and macOS tests).

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

body: ## 做了什么 工具箱按已确认的设计稿改版（目录 = 设计稿 A，工具页 = 设计稿 B）。 - **地址**：`/tools` 是目录，`/tools/<工具>` 是工作台（尺寸调整为 `/tools/resize`）。每次切工具写一条历史，浏览器前进/后退可切回；未知工具名落回 `/tools`。Pages 重定向与 BFF 的 SPA fallback 都加了 `/tools/:tool`。 - **目录**：居中标题 + 说明；「全部 / 单张处理 / 多图合成」页签带件数，导入操作同行；4 列卡片（手机 2 列），4:3 效果示意图只用 `public/website-assets/v41/wall` 里的样图，不使用用户图片。 - **工作台**：左侧工具列表（窄屏横向滚动）· 中间舞台 · 右侧参数栏与汇总框。页头是「工具箱 › 工具名」面包屑加导入操作。导入的图存在工具箱 store 里，换工具不丢。 - **结果卡**：4:3 棋盘格底、`object-contain`；点击进入原图 / 处理后对比滑块（支持键盘方向键与 Esc）。 - **合成工具**：横向排序条（前移 / 后移 / 移除）+ 预览；汇总框显示输出尺寸、文件大小或切图张数。 - **旋转**：参数移入右侧参数栏，舞台保留原图 / 调整后与缩略条。 - **尺寸调整**：参数栏是原导出表单（自带导出按钮），因此不显示工作台底栏。 - author: ljchang
body:
## What it does

`vision.active-speaker` 1.1.0 keeps LR-ASD's full per-frame output and the word votes behind the voice links, as two side files beside the `speakers` layer. The layer points at them with `raw.scores` and `raw.votes`. With these files, candidate rankings, the vote's threshold (> 0) and the 0.3 voice-link gate can be revisited without rerunning the model.

- **`layers/speakers_scores.parquet`** (`bundle.speakers_scores@0.1`, kinds: transcript). One row for every 25 fps frame of every scored face track, in the faces layer's track order, then frame order. Columns:
  - `face`: the face track id.
  - `frame`: the 25 fps frame index, counted from the video's first frame.
  - `t`: frame / 25, to 3 places.
  - `score`: the per-frame score, float32. The layer reads it to 2 decimals.
  - `windows`: `fixed_size_list<float>[11]`, LR-ASD's float32 score in each window length (1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6 s). `score` is their mean.
  - Metadata: model, fps, the window lengths, and how `score` is taken from them.
- **`layers/speakers_votes.json`** (`bundle.speakers_votes@0.1`, kinds: transcript). Holds `max_word_seconds`, the `people` matched (the faces layer's order, which is the assignment's columns), and one entry per voice:
  - `visible`: how many of its words had a person's face on screen.
  - `votes`: votes per person.
  - `words`: for every word that can vote, `{word, face, person, score}`. `word` is the word's index in the transcript layer's words. `face` is the top visible face track, `person` is that track's person, and `score` is that face's mean score over the word, unrounded, and kept even when ≤ 0. The word votes when `score > 0`.
- **"Before and after the median filter."** LR-ASD's scores are never median-filtered or smoothed. The node's only median filter smooths the crop boxes. So the two forms worth keeping are the per-window scores (before the mean) and the mean (after). Both are stored.
  - The mean is stored, not just the windows, because it cannot be recomputed bit-for-bit in every order. On OOO, averaging the windows row by row differs from the node's `np.mean(windows, axis=0)` in 2621 of 9066 frames, by up to 9.5e-7.
- **The layer is made from the files**, so the files reproduce it exactly by construction:
  - The node writes the Parquet file, then reads its scored tracks back from it (`asd_raw.read_scores`, `scored_tracks`).
  - It records the votes per word (`speaker_links.voice_votes`) and makes the voice links from those records (`link_voices(voices, people, assign)`).
  - `voice_votes` counts exactly as 1.0.0's `votes_for` did. `test_the_word_records_count_the_votes_as_before` checks this against a copy of the 1.0.0 code on random tracks, with ties.
- **Layer content does not change**, apart from `producer.stage_version` (1.0.0 to 1.1.0) and `raw`. See the comparison below.
- **Kinds** (justified in the `artifacts.SIDE_FILES` comment):
  - Scores: `transcript`. Joined with the faces layer's track → person, they say who speaks when, frame by frame. `transcript_diarization` and the speakers layer count that as transcript. They hold no image, landmark, box, audio or words.
  - This changed after the first review's MEDIUM: the first commit gave them no kind. `test_the_speakers_side_files_count_as_transcript_as_the_layer_does` failed before the fix.
  - Votes: `transcript`, as the speakers layer. They hold voices and who speaks when, with no word text and no audio.

## Models and licences

No change: LR-ASD `finetuning_TalkSet` at commit `1b6dcd2d`, with the same https URL and sha256 in `manifest.yaml` and in `models.py` WEIGHTS.
- The code is MIT.
- The weights state no licence and are trained on AVA-ActiveSpeaker and TalkSet (VoxCeleb2 + LRS3): `needs-review`.
- The layer is academic-only overall, through the py-feat face tracks.
- No API, no secrets, no `privacy.external_upload`.

## Runners and environment

- Runners are unchanged: mps (darwin/arm64), cuda (linux/amd64), cpu. An unusable device still fails with `NodeError`.
- `envs/gaze` already pins `pyarrow==26.0.0` (for gaze's heatmaps), so the lock does not change.
- Writer options are fixed: zstd 9, row groups of 65,536, dictionary on `face`, statistics on face/frame/t, format 2.6, data page v1, no page index, no byte-stream split. The file carries no time.
- `test_the_same_scores_are_the_same_bytes` writes 72,000 rows (two row groups) twice and gets identical bytes.

## Side files: sizes (OOO clip 1, 119 s)

| file | rows | bytes | per hour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speakers_scores.parquet` | 9066 frames, 164 tracks | 171,248 | ~5.2 MB |
| `speakers_votes.json` | 5 voices, 328 words | 26,703 | ~0.8 MB |

The node holds every track's scores until the end, about 56 B per frame, roughly 30 MB for a two-hour film at OOO's density. It already held the per-frame means the layer needs.

## Comparison (real run, OOO clip 1, MPS)

I ran the node twice in the same store: `origin/main` (1.0.0, as a baseline) and this branch (1.1.0). Upstream nodes (decode, asr, diarize, faces) came from the cache for the second run.

**Against main's 1.0.0 layer:**
- The content is identical: utterances and voice_links are equal.
- The only producer difference is `stage_version` 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, plus the new `raw`.

**The layer from the side files alone** (Parquet + votes JSON, with the faces and transcript layers):
- Rebuilding the votes from the stored scores gives exactly the stored votes.
- `tally(words)` gives back each voice's stored `votes` and `visible`.
- `layer_content` from the stored scores and votes gives the layer's 86 utterances (candidates, margins, predictions) and its voice links exactly.
- Links from the votes JSON alone are SPEAKER_00 → E 0.12, 01 → G 0.43, 02 → F 0.66, 03 → B 0.67, 04 → C 0.38. These are the layer's.
- Gate sweep on the stored shares, as an example of what is now possible: 4 trusted links at 0.2, 0.25 and 0.3, 3 at 0.4, 2 at 0.5.

**Against the bake-off** (`asd_lrasd.json` and `bundle/layers/speakers.json`):

| | node 1.1.0 | bake-off |
|---|---|---|
| tracks scored | 164 (same set, starts, lengths) | 164 |
| frames | 9066, **0 differ** at the bake-off's 2 decimals | 9066 |
| utterances | 86 | 86 |
| `predicted` identical | **86/86** | |
| candidates identical | **86/86** | |
| margins identical | **86/86** | |
| via asd / voice_link / none | 67 / 13 / 6 | 67 / 13 / 6 |

Every difference is explained:
- **Voice-link word shares** (0.12/0.43/0.66/0.67/0.38 against 0.25/0.39/0.60/0.59/0.42). Same people, same trust. The bake-off linked voices on WhisperX's transcript; the node links on the diarize node's transcript, which is the transcript the layer describes. This was documented in #16 and is unchanged here.
- **`second_opinion_agrees`** is null for all 86 utterances, where the bake-off filled it. The bake-off's second opinion was TalkNet, which was rejected and not ported (#16).
- **Speaking frames: 3092 of 9066** have a score above 0 in the float32 file. #16 counted 3077 on the 2-decimal scores: 15 frames lie in (0, 0.005) and round to 0.00.

**Validation:**
- `artifacts._layer('speakers')`: no problems. The `bundle.speakers_votes@0.1` and `bundle.speakers_scores@0.1` validators: no problems.
- `pipeline/bundle/validate.py` on the export: valid, with the Parquet columns checked under pyarrow.

**Determinism:** `perception rerun --from speakers --no-cache` gave byte-identical outputs: speakers.json `76e2ad3c…`, speakers_scores.parquet `827f290d…`, speakers_votes.json `cc993453…`.

## Timing (M5 Max, MPS, OOO 119 s)

- 1.1.0: 83.5 s for the task (crop 9.5 s, load 5.1 s, score 66.6 s), and 76.2 s on the no-cache rerun.
- 1.0.0 baseline in the same session: 88.3 s (crop 10.1, load 4.9, score 73.3).
- Writing and reading back the side files takes a negligible share of that. The variation comes from load from other agents on the machine.

## Tests

- `nodes`, run as CI runs them (`uv run --no-project --with pytest --with numpy --with av==16.1.0 --with pillow --

author: zackees
body:
Fixes #4945. Part of #4949.

## Problem
ESP8266 had **no** `fl::RxChannel` backend — every backend (`gpio_isr_rx`, `i2s_rx`, `parlio_rx`, `rmt_rx`) lives under `esp/32/drivers/`, and the AutoResearch benches hand-rolled a GPIO poll instead.

## Design note (why I2S RX, not GPIO ISR)
The hand-rolled capture (`AutoResearchEsp8266.h::captureEdges`) is a **synchronous IRAM `rsr ccount` poll that also feeds the UART1 TX FIFO** — it's welded to the TX it measures and can't be a generic async device. A real per-edge GPIO **ISR** is also not feasible: ~1 µs interrupt latency ≫ the ~350 ns WS2812 T0H. So the one usable hardware receiver is the **I2S RX** path.

## Change
- **`rx_device_i2s_rx.{h,cpp.hpp}`** (new) — `Esp8266I2sRxDevice` implements the full `RxDevice` interface over the core's **verified `core_esp8266_i2s.h`** (`i2s_rxtxdrive_begin` RX-only, `i2s_set_rate(kI2sSlotHz)`, `i2s_read_sample`). It captures 16-bit samples at the WS2812 slot rate (the same rate the #4943 I2S engine emits), reconstructs the slot-level bit stream, converts runs to `EdgeTime`, and decodes via the shared `decodeWs2812Edges` path — so the **I2S output engine is validated by looping its output back into I2S RX**. `samplesToEdges` is pure math (host-testable).
- **`rx.cpp.hpp`** — ESP8266 branch in the `RxDevice` factory: `RxBackend::I2S_RX` + `PLATFORM_DEFAULT` → the I2S RX device; `ISR`/`RMT`/`FLEXPWM`/`FLEXIO`/`PARLIO_RX`/`LPC_SCT_CAPTURE` → `DummyRxDevice` with a clear message.
- **`_build.cpp.hpp`** — the device TU joins the ESP8266 unity build.

## Test plan / evidence
- `bash compile esp8266 --examples Blink,Esp8266Uart` → both succeed; images **unchanged from `master`** (264,671 / 264,199 B) — the RX device **dead-strips when unused**.
- `ci/lint.py --strict` clean (SpanFromPointer/Stdint fixed).
- **Remaining (needs a board):** on-device I2S TX→RX loopback capture + decode; the sample→edge reconstruction is pure math and host-testable.

body:
### Summary of Changes

1. **Bug Fix: Multi-Click Debrief Payouts Lock:**
   - Fixed the issue in Phase 4 HQ Downtime where repeatedly clicking `"Claim & Deposit Payouts into Vaults"` credited infinite currencies (`credits` and `pip`).
   - Added single-claim idempotency guard `state.payoutsClaimed` in `src/vtt/VirtualTabletop.tsx`. Once claimed, the button locks with `✅ Payouts Deposited into Vaults (Claimed)` and is disabled. State resets upon concluding HQ downtime for the next mission.

2. **Dual-Stream Payout Model (`BL-RULES-01`):**
   - Codified the canonical dual-stream payout model in `game/core/vault_economy.md`:
     - **Stream 1 (Guaranteed Operative Participation):** Each participating operative earns `+2 CR` base stipend; each participating faction earns `+1 PIP`. In 3P games, the Vanguard Slot operative's stipend flows to the Squad Leader.
     - **Stream 2 (Shared Clearance Pot):** Mission clearance bounty (`+6 CR` and `+1 PIP`) forms a shared pot negotiated at the table.
   - Built an interactive **Dual-Stream Payout Console** in the VTT with seat breakdowns, participation tallies, interactive negotiation steppers (`- / +`), total payout previews, and real-time unallocated pot alerts.

3. **Automated Test Coverage & Status Tracking:**
   - Added Test 10 in `tests/05-vtt-engine-and-simulator.test.js` validating dual-stream payouts, negotiated allocations, and multi-click claim locking (all 29 tests pass).
   - Documented Iteration 22 and ADR-15 in `PROJECT_STATUS.md` and updated `BACKLOG.md`.

…Pad (COM-1583)> Draft: merge only after COM-1582 (POST /api/waitlist) is merged; until then Send shows "Couldn't save".

## What changes
- Page 3 no longer embeds CryptPad. It renders our own form from `public/waitlist-form.json` (the CryptPad export the team provided): every question, option, note and show/hide section, in the same order.
- Everything after "I understand" stays hidden until it is ticked; "pick up to 3" disables further options at 3.
- Done → Send: checks required visible questions (marks them red, scrolls to the first), posts `{ answers: { <questionId>: string | string[] } }` to `/api/waitlist`, then returns to page 1. On failure shows "Couldn't save your answers. Please try again."

author: vito
body:
`python-sdk.dang`'s `onSdkRuntime` annotated `SdkHelpersModuleManifest!`. From v1.0.0-beta.22, a module is named by the rules of its own declared `engineVersion` (dagger/dagger#14810, #14891). Every sdk-helpers tag up to v1.0.7 declares a bare `v1.0.0`, and this module pins `sdk-helpers@v1.0.6` in `dagger-module.toml` (`@v1` in `dagger.json`). So on a beta.22 engine the dependency's type is `SDKHelpersModuleManifest`, and the annotation no longer resolves, even though python-sdk itself declares beta.18.

This PR inlines the call at its three sites, so the module spells neither name. It then loads on engines on both sides of the cut, whichever sdk-helpers tag it resolves to. Nothing else in the repo names an sdk-helpers type. (dagger/sdk-helpers#10, and a pre-cut tag after it, would fix the `@v1` case too, but not the `@v1.0.6` pin.)

Checks: on the session engine, the workspace loads the edited `python-sdk` module (generator `python-sdk/generate` is listed). I could not run it on a beta.22 engine here.

author: silkie86
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Silkie86"} -->
_Requested by **Solomon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Ci2bkvsAaQa1WvBQNPMQVi?thread=cmsg_01Ci2bkvsAaQa1WvBQNPMQViMeaaJSadCp7WYSPLB4jhmS)_

M6 part 2: a workspace can send its email from its own domain (for example bookings@youragency.com) instead of the platform's address.

## What it does

- **Adding a domain** (Settings → Email accounts → Your own domain). This is for owners and admins only. The domain is added at Resend, which gives the DKIM and SPF records. The page lists each record with copy buttons, plus a DMARC record when the domain has no policy. A workspace can have up to 5 domains and sends from one at a time. Mail-service domains (gmail.com and similar) and the platform's own domain are refused.
- **One-step DNS setup with Domain Connect.** OnHold looks up the domain's DNS provider through its `_domainconnect` record. If that provider has OnHold's template, a signed link sends the owner there to approve the records. Lookup only follows public https addresses. The template and setup steps are in `docs/domain-connect/`.
- **Checks.** The worker asks Resend about a pending domain every minute at first, slowing to every 6 hours, and asks Resend to start or retry its verification when it has stopped. A verified domain is checked daily, and "Check now" triggers a check straight away. The first domain verified becomes the sending domain. Resend's "temporary failure" leaves a verified domain verified.
- **What sends from the domain.** Invitations, quote, invoice and signature emails, rule emails, and inbox messages sent without a connected mailbox. The sender name and reply-to address are unchanged.
- **Domain ownership.**
  - A domain belongs to one workspace across the whole platform.
  - A domain whose records have not been found for 14 days (since they were last found, or since it was added) is released, both here and at Resend, so nobody can hold a domain they don't own. A never-verified domain Resend no longer knows is released at once.
  - Closing a workspace releases its domains. Released domains are kept as rows marked removed, since the app never hard-deletes.
- **Small footprint.** Each domain is one database row holding a handful of records, and nothing is stored on devices. No new crates were added: lookups use DNS over HTTPS, and signing uses `ring`, which is already compiled in.

## Configuration

- `RESEND_API_KEY` and `RESEND_REGION` (default `eu-west-1`). `SMTP_URL` must then be Resend's SMTP server on the same account.
- Optional: `DOMAIN_CONNECT_PROVIDER_ID` and `DOMAIN_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY` for the one-step setup.

## Tests

- `crates/core-worker/tests/domains.rs` runs end to end against stand-ins for Resend, a DNS-over-HTTPS resolver and a DNS provider with Domain Connect. It covers adding a domain, discovery, the signed setup link, verification, invitations sent from the domain, turning the domain off, removal, expiry, a domain the provider lost, and the permission checks.
- Unit tests cover domain cleaning, the check schedule, record naming for subdomains, TXT parsing and signing. The signing test checks the signature against the published key.
- `e2e/inbox.spec.ts` checks the page on a server without Resend set up.
- An ultracode review confirmed 21 findings (domains getting stuck or lapsing, races on the in-use choice and the 5-domain cap, record names for subdomains, page polling and wording); all are fixed in the last commit.

## Not yet

- The Domain Connect template hasn't been submitted. Until DNS providers adopt it, every domain is set up by hand.
- The link-signing format follows the reference libraries. It still needs checking with the Domain Connect signature checker before the template is submitted (step 4 in `docs/domain-connect/README.md`).

author: x7c1
body:
## Summary

The workspace now runs on MSW 3 (`^3.0.3`) instead of being held on MSW 2, and Dependabot no longer ignores MSW's major updates. The web tests wait until every request a test started has reached MSW before the next test installs its handlers, so a request left by one test is no longer answered by the next test's mock.

## Changes

- Bumped `msw` in `packages/apps/web` and `packages/testing/api-mocks`, regenerated `public/mockServiceWorker.js` with `msw init`, and renamed `onUnhandledRequest` to `onUnhandledFrame` (`test-setup.ts`, `api-mocks/src/browser.ts`).
- Removed the `msw` entry from `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: MSW 3 has no postinstall script. Removed the MSW ignore from `.github/dependabot.yml`.
- `test-setup.ts` wraps the global `fetch` and keeps each request pending until MSW emits `request:start` for it (by then MSW has chosen its handlers) or it settles. `afterEach` waits until none is pending, looping because an answer may make the app start another request. MSW 3 picks a request's handlers only when the request reaches its interceptor, a few turns after `fetch`, which is what let requests leak across tests.
- MSW 3 in Node cannot observe a request's `credentials`, so `RecordedRequest` no longer carries it and four web assertions on it were dropped. The gateway clients' own tests still check it (`session-api/src/client.test.ts` for `include`, `activity-api/src/client.test.ts` for `omit`).
- The sign-out test in `App.test.tsx` waited only until the cache had some key, and could sign out before the activity response was stored. It now waits for both keys.
- Only that one wait needed changing. Under load on a 4-CPU machine (web tests 4 in parallel × 10 rounds), the failures counted were:

  | Run | Failing runs |
  |---|---|
  | `main` (MSW 2) | 0/40 |
  | MSW 3 with only the `fetch` wrapper | 1/40 |
  | This branch | 0/40 |

  An earlier MSW 3 attempt without these changes failed widely at 8 in parallel on another machine. That load did not reproduce here, so this machine cannot tell the fix apart from the race just not showing.

## Review notes

The acceptance criteria live in the accompanying `docs/tasks/2026/1028-0325-upgrade-to-msw-3.md`. The automated items are ticked. The Before merge items are verified and ticked on this branch before merge:
- a load comparison with `main`, which is more meaningful at the higher parallelism where MSW 3 failed before
- the regenerated browser worker under `VITE_API_MOCK=1 make dev`

author: xiaofan-luan
body:
issue: #54706
pr: #54733

Backport to 3.0 of #54733 (master ea8c5096bb), together with #54707 (master 76c4dca597), which it builds on. Squashed into one commit. 3.0 had no `IsRetriableEtcdErr`, so that function and its tests are carried over in full. The rest of the change is identical to master line for line.

Why 3.0 needs it: a scheduled scale-down on a 3.0.4 instance restarted all etcd members. mixcoord panicked in `proxy_watcher.go startWatchEtcd` with `etcdserver: leader changed`, lost the in-memory node suspension, and the drain never converged. Three such panics in a week across two instances. With etcd auth enabled, any transient error returned while authenticating a new watch stream cancels the watch the same way: `server stopped`, `no leader`, request timeouts, and so on.

What it changes (see #54733 for the full description and the per-error reproduction):
- `IsRetriableEtcdErr` classifies transient etcd errors by code, and `IsRetriableWatchErr` reuses it.
- `etcdKV` / `EmbedEtcdKV` keep the driver error as the cause of `ErrIoFailed`, so callers can classify it.
- Session and proxy watchers re-watch until etcd recovers. Lease expiry still exits the process through the keepalive.
- The CDC controller retries transient list errors with a backoff, instead of every error in a tight loop.
- `ProcessActiveStandBy`, `ResourceManager.unassignNode`, `GoingStop` and the CDC replicate pchannel removal retry transient errors instead of panicking or Fatal-ing. `ProcessActiveStandBy` also recognizes an attempt that was applied despite the error.

A client-side request timeout (`context.DeadlineExceeded`) is never retried; it aborts. Server-side `etcdserver: request timed out` is `Unavailable` and is retried.

Tests (on dev, 3.0 headers): `pkg/util/{etcd,merr,retry}`, `internal/util/{sessionutil,proxyutil}`, `internal/cdc/{controller,replication/replicatestream}`, `internal/kv/etcd`, `internal/metastore/kv/querycoord` and `internal/querycoordv2/meta` pass, with and without `-race`. golangci-lint reports 0 issues on the touched packages.
