body:
## Why the demo stopped working

I can't reach mindform-ai.com from the sandbox, so I rebuilt production locally (gunicorn, `DEBUG=True` plus public hosts, collectstatic, an OpenAI-compatible stand-in for Gemini) and tried every way the demo can fail. Three causes reproduce, and the code on `main` handles all three badly:

1. **Database unreachable → `/demo/` returns 500.** Every first visit created a session row before the console could load. With the database down, `main` serves the homepage (200) but `/demo/` and its API answer 500, which is exactly "the demo stopped working while the rest of the site works". Neon's free plan suspends the database when the month's compute hours run out, and this is the end of the month. The demo no longer touches the database at all (verified: zero queries; full demo works with the database switched off).
2. **Gemini overloads → robotic replies.** Since the time-budget change, the OpenAI client's retries are off, so one "model overloaded" (503) or rate limit (429) dropped that step, often the reply, to the offline voice. Now each call gets one quick retry inside the budget. With a stand-in model failing one call in three, every reply still came from the model.
3. **One failed request → "Demo temporarily offline" until reload.** Any single 502/503/504/52x or network blip swapped the whole console for the offline card. Now a single failure shows a note in the chat and the next message works; reads retry once; only two failures in a row (or `DEMO_ENABLED=false`) show the card.

To see which cause hits production: after deploying, sign in at `/admin/` and open **`/demo/health/`** (staff only, 404 for everyone else). It makes a live call to the model and a real turn, and shows the exact error if the model fails (bad key, retired model, quota).

## Other bugs fixed

- **Security: demo cookie path traversal.** The demo named each visitor's folder after the raw session cookie, which Django passes through unchecked. A forged `sessionid=../../x` made the server write files outside the demo folder (reproduced). The folder is now a signed 32-hex id.
- **Contact link broken.** "Contact us" pointed at `mailto:hasangit @mindform-ai.com`. All mailto links use `CONTACT_EMAIL` again, which now defaults to hasan@mindform-ai.com (partners section too).
- **CVs disappeared.** They were saved to Render's disk, which is wiped on every deploy, restart and idle spin-down. CVs are now stored in the database, downloadable from the admin's Applications list (CV column). Migration 0007 copies any CV file still on disk. A 200 MB total cap (`RESUME_STORAGE_LIMIT_MB`) stops spam uploads from filling the database.
- **Log-in required "Confirm password"** although the page says to leave it blank. Fixed; new accounts must now pass Django's password validators.
- **Static files were never compressed**: `STATICFILES_STORAGE` was removed in Django 5.1 and silently ignored. Replaced with `STORAGES`.
- **Local dev broke with a production `.env`** (HTTPS redirect or HTTP 400 on 127.0.0.1). `manage.py runserver` outside Render now always works on localhost.
- **Stale database connections** after idle periods: `conn_health_checks=True`.
- **Render ignores the Procfile.** `gunicorn.conf.py` now gives 2 workers x 4 threads and one log line per request with its time, whatever the dashboard start command is.
- **Stale JS after deploys**: CSS/JS links carry a content fingerprint (`?v=`), so a deploy reaches visitors at once.
- PDFs with a few bytes before `%PDF-` are accepted; the "How it works" diagram quote no longer overflows its box; Escape closes both mobile menus.

## Team

Marc Mechkak (CEO & Co-founder), Hasan Mavlonov (CTO & Co-founder), Ray (CFO), François Mechkak (Founding AI Engineer / SWE Lead), Yifei (SWE, Math & Computing). Umar removed. No photos or initials: photos appear automatically once all five have one.

## NVIDIA wording

Kept "Member of NVIDIA Inception". Our signed trademark license, Section 2(c), forbids displaying the marks "in any way that implies that Licensee's ... goods or services are provided by NVIDIA, with NVIDIA's supervision, or endorsed by NVIDIA", and NVIDIA "may terminate the license granted above immediately upon Licensee's material breach". "Backed by" reads as investment or endorsement, and Inception doesn't invest, so it is not used.

## Verification

- `python manage.py test core`: 92 tests pass (57 on `main`). `validate_content` passes, no missing migrations.
- Production replica: full demo (3 turns, story character, manual character) at desktop and mobile; with a flaky model; with the database unreachable; 8 failure scenarios for the console (single 502/524/network error, two in a row, kill switch, engine error).
- Over real HTTPS (self-signed, browser origin `https://mindform-ai.com`): careers form with a real PDF, CV downloaded byte-for-byte from the admin, sign-up, log-out, log-in with blank confirm, health page.
- Every page at 375/768/1440 in light and dark: no console errors, failed requests, broken images, broken internal links or anchors, or sideways scrolling. Homepage scripted demo plays, pauses and restarts; mobile menus work.

## TODO (needs you)

- [ ] After deploy, open `/demo/health/` signed in as staff; if `model.status` is an error, it names the fix. Also check Neon's dashboard for a suspended database or used-up compute hours.
- [ ] **Privacy: this repository is public** and contains 8 applicants' CVs (`media/resumes/`) and `db.sqlite3`. Make the repo private now (Settings → General → Danger Zone). Removing them from history needs a force-push; tell me if you want that done.
- [ ] Team: Ray's surname and LinkedIn, Yifei's full name and profile link, and square photos (at least 160px) for all five.
- [ ] Confirm hasan@mindform-ai.com receives mail (Contact, Join, waitlist and Partners now go there). Set `PARTNERS_EMAIL` if there is a separate inbox.
- [ ] Content TODOs: Inception join year; Gemma hackathon event page; UzCombinator year and official site; 4 milestone dates and the Zenodo list link (`grep -rn TODO content/`).
- [ ] Optional settings: `LINKEDIN_URL`, `WECHAT_ID`, `DEMO_RECORDING_URL`. Make sure `SECRET_KEY` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` are set on Render.

author: qualified-opinion
body:
_Requested by **Jan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BWJe69EFV45RG5BssMr4Dx?thread=cmsg_01BWJe69EFV45RG5BssMr4DxLPoQAwFgv5KdG7YmFQqeoj)_

Stacked on PR #3 (base `feat/pr3-storage`), so the diff shows only PR4. When PR3 merges, retarget this to `main`.

## What was wrong
The vault could be created and unlocked, but there was no way to put anything in it. Two review findings also needed fixing before import could be safe:
- **F8**: a crash in the middle of saving could leave an encrypted data or thumbnail file with no metadata file. Nothing ever cleaned these up, so they wasted card space.
- **F9**: the startup clean-up could run while an import was writing, and delete a file that was still being saved.

## What changed
- **Import button** on the unlocked screen opens the system photo picker (photos and videos, no permission needed). It shows "Importing x of y…" with a progress bar, then a summary: how many were saved, skipped as not a photo or video, skipped for lack of space, or failed.
- Each item is encrypted straight from the original onto the card (data, then thumbnail, then metadata last). Nothing is written in plain form, and the 320 px thumbnail is made in memory.
- **Originals are not deleted.** The summary says they are still in the gallery.
- Before each item, a free-space check skips anything that would not fit (encrypted size + 16 MiB).
- **Locking stops the import.** The item being copied stops on its next read and its partial files are removed. Items already saved stay.
- A read-only card hides the Import button. If the card is removed or becomes read-only mid-run, the import stops and the summary says why.
- F8: startup clean-up now also removes data or thumbnail files with no metadata.
- F9: import and startup clean-up share one write lock.
- The placeholder `ImportModule` was removed.

**Defaults chosen without the planning pack (please confirm):** `docs/plans/pr4.md` has the table. Originals are kept; system picker; no duplicate detection; no FAT32 4 GiB pre-check (a too-big file just fails cleanly); one item at a time.

## How to test on your phone
After PR3's phone checks:
1. Unlock, tap **Import**, pick 3 photos and 1 video. The progress bar should move and the summary should say "4 imported". The item count goes up by 4.
2. Lock, then unlock again. The count should stay the same, which shows the metadata was saved and read back.
3. Pick a large video and tap **Lock** while it imports. On the next unlock the count should not include it, and the card's `staging/` folder should be empty.
4. Fill the card nearly full, then import a video bigger than the free space. The summary should say it was skipped for lack of space.
5. The originals should still be in the gallery.

## Risk
- Medium. New write path onto the card. It reuses PR3's `ItemRepository.create`, which already cleans up on failure.
- If an item finishes in the same instant the vault locks, it could reappear in the in-memory list. The controller locks again at the end to clear it. The files on the card are complete either way.
- HEIC thumbnails on Android 9 and older depend on the phone's decoder. If it fails, the item is still imported, just without a thumbnail.

## Not tested here
- No Android SDK in this session, so GitHub CI is the only build and test run.
- New JVM tests cover the import loop on a temp folder with real encryption: import and read back, skip unsupported, no space, an unreadable item, lock between items and mid-item, read-only folder, and date parsing. Orphan clean-up and free space are covered in `VaultFilesTest`.
- The picker, thumbnail and metadata reading (`MediaProbe`) use Android decoders and are not unit-tested. They need the phone checks above.

author: kashyab12
body:
## What the person saw

A running turn's work read as three things that didn't belong together: a "Ran a command ⌄" summary with a strip of glyphs, an indented hairline list, then a separate "⌄ Running … · no output for 5m" row with its own chevron, and a heartbeat glyph for "Working". Agents started together read "5 agents · 5 working" with a robot on each row, and three of the five rows said only "Agent" until opened.

## What T3 Code does that reads as polished

- Every work row is the same line: a 16px glyph column, then the words in one face and size (14px, secondary colour), 24px tall, no borders, no indentation.
- A finished group is one row: a single glyph for the kind of work (a hammer when mixed) and "Ran 3 commands and read 2 files". No chevron; hover shows it's pressable. Opened, its entries list in the same column in a capped scroller.
- A command's row is the command; a read is "Read guard.ts". The command face is not used in the row.
- While running, one row says what runs now ("Running npm") under a 4.5rem crest swept across the text, 2.2s, 30 steps, paused off screen and under reduced motion. Nothing else on the row moves; there is no spinner or orb.
- "Working for 1m 12s" at the head of the turn is text, with no icon; a settled turn folds behind "Worked for 3m 12s ›".

## What changed

- **One column.** The summary has one glyph (the kind's, or a stack for mixed work) in the column every row's glyph stands in, with no glyph strip and no trailing chevron. Its chevron replaces the glyph under the pointer, as on every row. Opened steps are listed in that column, not indented on a rail.
- **The running call is its own row.** A running call renders as `ToolRow`, its words under the sweep, so nothing is swapped when it returns. Live rows no longer toggle anything, so the "⌄ Running" chevron is gone.
- **One line of words.** A row's words are one face, one size and one truncating line. A command is its own words ("npm test", not "Shell npm test"); its code shows in the code face when the row opens. An agent row is what the agent was asked to do. A path inside the conversation's folder is shown relative to it.
- **How long, not "no output".** A call running for a minute or more says "for 4m" after its words, counted in minutes so it rarely repaints. "No output for…" was wrong for harnesses that don't stream a command's output: every long command read as silent. It stays only on waits and thoughts.
- **"Working" is an ellipsis.** `WorkingIcon` (lucide's ellipsis) is the one static mark for work in progress. It replaces the heartbeat in the live row and the bar meter in `ActivityMark`. An unfinished line reads "more to come"; the motion stays in the sweep over the word, not in the mark. The monitor glyph keeps the heartbeat, because there it means a monitor. A live thought sweeps "Thinking" and no longer has a mark at its end.
- **Agents.** The group's glyph is the mark of the harness running the agents. "Running 5 agents" sweeps while any agent works, and the counts say how the rest ended ("1 done"). After a minute it adds "for 2m". Marks follow the words only when the agents run on more than one harness. There is no end orb, and the opened rows are flat. Every subagent and background-agent glyph (transcript rows, the Agents panel, the background-work line, event lines) is the mark of the harness that runs it: the roster's harness first, then the transcript's own. So when cross-harness agents land, an agent shows its own harness.
- **Agents are named while they run (root cause).** The host's live history preview cut any call input over 2048 characters with a plain `slice`. That left JSON that no longer parsed, so an agent with a long prompt had no description, and its row read "Agent" until opened, when the whole input loaded. A reopened thread showed the name, so live and reopened disagreed. `previewInput` now keeps the input's JSON and cuts each long string to its head, falling back to the slice for non-JSON input. While the model is still streaming a call's input, the name is read from what has arrived so far (`argumentsSoFar`), and only for naming a running call.
- **Footer.** A running turn's footer no longer shows the newest step's time as if it were the answer's time.

The changes are CSS and markup only: no per-token renders, and the only clocks are the shared `Ticking`.

## Screenshots

`node scripts/work-log-screenshots.mjs <out> [--prefix …] [--cut slice]` renders seven scenes in dark and light against the mock bridge. The scenes are a quiet long command, several steps, parallel calls, five agents with long briefs (closed and open), the steps opened, and a settled turn (closed and opened). `--cut slice` previews long inputs the way the host did before this change.

## Checks

See the PR conversation for the run log.

author: muthu011
body:
## Summary
Levels are now data. A new **Game.Levels** assembly (`Assets/Scripts/Levels/`) reads level JSON with Newtonsoft, validates it against `docs/level-schema.md`, and builds a Core `Board`. **Game.Core is unchanged**: it has no JSON or Unity code.

- **Newtonsoft:** `com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json` 3.2.2 is now a direct dependency and is listed in `docs/approved-dependencies.md` as approved by Muthu. Before this, the project only had it through the editor-only MCP package.
- **Parsing:** done with `JsonTextReader`/`JToken`, never with reflection-based deserialisation, so IL2CPP stripping on Android is safe with no `link.xml`.
- `Game.Levels` has `noEngineReferences: true`. It takes a JSON string; reading the TextAsset is left to the view/bootstrap.
- API: `LevelLoader.Load(json, sourceName)` returns a `LevelLoadResult` holding `Success`, `Board`, `Level` and `Errors`, and never throws for bad content. `LevelParser` and `LevelValidator` can also be used on their own. All errors are collected, not just the first.
- Error format: `<levelId>: shelf <i> ("<id>"), layer <l>, slot <s>: <problem>`, plus line and position for JSON errors. For example: `sample_unknown_object: shelf 3 ("s4"), layer 1, slot 0: unknown object id "dabba"`

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Loads `Assets/Levels/World1/w1_l001.json` into a Board. Tests: `Load_World1Level1_BuildsBoard`, `Load_World1Level1_TumblerToShelf1Clears`

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zerojunz"} -->
_Requested by **Dan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01CxLicvn5y4tRRpJxVUdpgo?thread=cmsg_01CxLicvn5y4tRRpJxVUdpgo7ALFsYen3CQ1ayUrwv2Q6T)_

Before: a generated or imported model went into a game as it arrived. A CAD crate stayed in millimeters with z up, a generated boulder kept thousands of triangles more than its budget, and a mesh without texture coordinates couldn't take a texture. The storyboard caught the over-budget model but nothing fixed it.

After: one `model.cleanup` call makes a model game-ready and writes it as a `.glb` file that holds everything. This is most of milestone 7's "game-ready cleanup" item; delighting textures and collision hulls are left for later PRs.

How:
- **`scene3d::cleanup_model`** (new `src/cleanup.cpp`, `slash/scene3d/cleanup.hpp`) runs these steps in order:
  - turns the file's up axis to y;
  - simplifies each surface with meshoptimizer to its share of the triangle budget, as Godot's importer simplifies LODs, trying lower when the shares overshoot, then makes the LODs again;
  - sizes the model by a scale or a height in meters;
  - moves its origin to a pivot in its box (`[0.5, 0, 0.5]` stands it on the ground);
  - unwraps surfaces whose vertices share one texture coordinate with xatlas, as lightmap UVs are.
  It refuses skinned and animated models for now, since the writer leaves skins out. It also refuses a budget the simplifier can't reach.
- **`scene3d::write_glb`** writes a model as one binary glTF, as Godot's GLTFDocument does. Its buffer and every image go inside it: PNG and JPEG files as they are, anything else re-encoded as a PNG. `write_gltf` now shares its document code.
- **`model.cleanup`** (`engine/command/src/model_cleanup.cpp`):
  - Takes `path`, `out` (default: `path` as `.glb`), `up`, `scale` or `height`, `pivot`, `triangles` and `uvs`.
  - The budget defaults to the storyboard's tightest one covering `out` (`storyboard::budget_for`).
  - Returns the triangles before and after, the budget used, the size and pivot, and the number of surfaces unwrapped.
  - Stages the file with undo; a repeat call that writes the same bytes reports `unchanged`.
  - Errors point at `/up`, `/height`, `/triangles` or `/out`.
- **Tests.**
  - `tests/test_model.cpp` turns, simplifies, sizes and pivots a z-up recipe, reads the `.glb` back, unwraps a card and checks the refusals.
  - `tests/test_command.cpp` runs `model.cleanup` under a storyboard budget, then checks `model.inspect`, `storyboard.check`, repeat calls, undo and the error paths.
- **Example.** `examples/model-cleanup` cleans a CAD crate (OBJ, millimeters, z up, no UVs) and a 3968-triangle boulder down to its 600-triangle budget.
- **Docs.** `commands.md` (`model.cleanup`), AGENTS.md, the roadmap item's progress and `examples/README.md`.

author: stevenmih
body:
Redraws the stats page as the network over time. It keeps the page's rules: it reads only the repository's files, never adds rehearsal and live together, never draws a gap as zero, and every count says what it is out of.

**The page, top to bottom:**
1. **Today in words**, with denominators, above a **pulse band**. The band has one column per day for 30 days and one square per listed node, split per question and coloured in the six day states. Missed days are hatched, days with no file are dashed, and ticks mark joins and leaves. The band spans the content width; on a phone it scrolls in its box and opens on the newest day.
2. **Six small multiples on one day axis:** nodes answering, records sealed per day, book growth per node, asks by outcome, days missed, and nodes listed, joining and leaving. Each is an SVG with a `<title>`, a `<desc>`, a denominator-and-window caption, and a `<details>` table of its numbers.
3. **The loop as a strip:** twelve tiles per population, rehearsal above live. PASS, FAIL, MALFORMED and NOT_CHECKED are each told apart, a ring marks PASS with a gap, and a dashed border marks a held row. Below each strip is a sparkline of PASS steps per run.
4. **The five numbers as sparklines.** An unmeasured number is a dotted track labelled with its milestone and has no value drawn. The both-halves measure is a count, "x of y exchanges", well below the fold.
5. **The nodes, day by day** becomes a heatmap, with each node's table in a `<details>`.
6. **The prose** moves into one collapsed "How to read this page" section, with its words kept.

**Checks:**
- CI builds the page from committed fixtures and diffs it byte for byte against `tests/fixtures/stats/expected/index.html`. The output has no build time or other nondeterminism.
- A negative fixture (a missed day, and a node whose count fell) renders hatched gaps and no zeros.
- Every `<details>` table is reconciled with the values and geometry drawn in its SVG.
- A WCAG contrast check runs in CI without network: text is 12 px or larger at 4.5:1 or better in both colour schemes. The lowest pair is 5.13:1.
- No `<script>`, no external assets, and no `%` in the page.
- The neutrality scan and branding tests pass.
- Mutant checks (fallen count drawn as zero, missed day drawn as settled, table off by one, bars scaled wrong, a dropped band column, a low-contrast token) each fail a test.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests`: 384 tests OK (17 step tests skip, saying why, where the tools are not built).

**Existing tests:** tests in `tests/test_site.py` that pinned the old layout are rewritten for the new shapes. The branding tests are unchanged, byte for byte.

Spec impact: none.

body:
Closes hearsay-tools/cezarion#1992

Refs hearsay-tools/cezarion#1993

## Summary

The cockpit thread now shows peer task messages (`relationship: 'peer'`) as green cards with a "Peer" chip. They are never user messages, so they stay apart from the yellow human message and the blue and purple worker cards, including beside an open question. Each card names the peer by title and links its thread. A peer that the run list lacks is read from the server, and a deleted or unreadable peer shows "Deleted task" or "Task unavailable" with no link. The `deleted` request outcome reads "Recipient deleted".

## Evidence

- Screenshots at 360×640 and 1440×900, light and dark, are written by `packages/web/e2e/peer-conversation.e2e.ts` to `.ai/qa/artifacts_e2e/peer-conversation/`. The spec seeds a request, a reply, a progress message beside an open `cezar_ask`, and a request to a peer whose record is gone.
- Regression proof: `proof_base` = `645f36a0e` (`main` before this change). The new and changed tests (`peer-conversation.test.tsx`, `conversation-presentation.test.ts`, `thread-groups.test.ts`, `thread-state.test.ts`) were copied into a scratch worktree there: 22 tests fail. They pass on this head. Guard tests that pass both ways stay on purpose: the deleted-outcome fold, the fold-level R1 check, and "no lookup when the run list names the peer".
- R1 (the incident): a peer `agent-input` beside an open `ask.requested` yields one peer card, no `user-message`, and an ask that stays unresolved. Pinned in `thread-state.test.ts`, `peer-conversation.test.tsx` and the browser spec.

## Design decision

Design track, approved spec `.ai/specs/2026-10-27-task-communication-protocol.md` (F4). The fold carries `relationship` onto the card; a peer without a known title is read through `useRun`, because the run list holds only a window of projects' tasks and the contract carries no peer title (no server change).

## Experience

- States: peer request, reply, progress, outcome (`replied`, `deleted`), undelivered (peer wording: "Only its human can continue it"), loading, deleted and unreadable peer. Worker cards are unchanged.
- Peer hue is green (150), not rose: the rose first tried read as an error card in light mode. The "Peer" chip and the heading carry the meaning, so colour is not the only cue.
- Checked at 360×640 and 1440×900 in light and dark. The browser spec asserts AA contrast (≥ 4.5) for the heading, chip and outcome, no horizontal overflow, and interactive targets ≥ 44 px. Unit tests pin AA contrast of the peer tokens in both themes.
- Links keep `min-h-11`. The deleted peer renders plain text, not a link.

## Verification

- `npm test -- packages/web/src/routes/task-thread` → 56 files, 1692 tests passed
- `npm test -- packages/web/src/test packages/cezar/src/file-length.test.ts packages/cezar/src/contract-import-boundaries.test.ts packages/cezar/src/test-wait-discipline.test.ts` → 27 files, 503 tests passed (before the last refactor commits; the file-length test also passes in Squeal at this head)
- `npm run test:e2e -- worker-conversation.e2e.ts peer-conversation.e2e.ts` → 15 passed, `TEST_E2E_STATUS=passed`
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` in `packages/web` → no errors
- `node .github/scripts/check-citations.cjs` → no bare citation added
- `squeal status --wait 60000` on the 5 changed test files and `file-length.test.ts` → each has a current result, no known failures
- Complexity gate: `node .ai/skills/check-code-quality/scripts/complexity-gate.mjs --base origin/main --head HEAD` → none over 20 is new or worse
- Code quality (pre-PR, with coverage): PASS, 115/115 changed functions, max complexity 18, max CRAP 18. Report: published as a task artifact `code-quality.md` (local snapshot; the cockpit link is not a public GitHub URL).
- Reader sweep: `worker-conversation.e2e.ts` is the only browser spec that reads the conversation card and it passes. `index.css` selects every spec (85), so the rest are left to CI. The seeded e2e continuation text now names `worker resume`.
- Not run locally: the full unit suite and the other 83 browser specs (CI owns the final gate).

## Left undone

- Relationship views (the run activity dock and the relationships panel) do not list peers. Issue acceptance covers the thread only.
- Behavior beyond the issue: the seeded continuation text in `worker-conversation.e2e.ts` names `worker resume` (coordinator request; seeded data, so it does not depend on F3 merging). The card fallback text for an undelivered worker message still says `--resume`: F3 (hearsay-tools/cezarion#1991) owns changing it once the verb exists. The card moved from `thread-items.tsx` to `conversation-card.tsx`; that drops its file-length pin (1248 → under the limit).
- Docs: `AGENT_PROTOCOL.md` and `BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md` describe the cockpit rendering. The wider docs sweep stays with hearsay-tools/cezarion#1993.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Presentation only; no contract, stored record or API change.

**Blast Radius:** Cockpit task thread. Worker cards keep their code path; a peer card needs `relationship: 'peer'`.

author: cyberlife-coder
body:
## Summary

Recall always searched the vector index at the collection's runtime quality; `velesdb-memory` exposed no way to trade latency for recall. With the core now able to search `SemanticMemory` at an explicit `SearchQuality` (merged in the previous change), this adds the setting:

- `VELESDB_MEMORY_SEARCH_QUALITY` / `[search] quality` in `velesdb-memory.toml`: `fast`, `balanced`, `accurate`, `perfect`, `autotune` or `custom:<ef>`, parsed by the core's `parse_search_mode` so every surface speaks one grammar.
- Unset or blank keeps the collection's own quality, so nothing changes for a store that does not opt in. A value that is not a quality stops the daemon at startup, before the store lock is taken, naming the setting and the accepted forms.
- Library callers: `MemoryService::with_search_quality` / `NativeStore::with_search_quality`, `select_search_quality`, `resolve_search_quality` (explicit value, then the environment), `SettingError::InvalidSearchQuality`. `SearchQuality` is re-exported.
- Bindings: the Node `MemoryService.open(..., searchQuality)` and the Python `MemoryService(..., search_quality=...)` take it as a trailing optional argument; an explicit value wins over the variable, and an unknown one rejects the open. The LangGraph tools take a preconfigured `MemoryService`, so they inherit it. The WASM service has no vector index to tune and is unchanged.

author: lemmih
body:
## Summary

The desugarer gave each use of a class method its own dictionary term. Thus a function that used `>>=` of `TcM` (`ReaderT TcEnv (StateT TcState (Either TcAbort))`) at many sites built the transformer dictionary again at each site. At `-O0`, each such site gave two thunks, two continuation functions and four info tables. `aihc-tc-bench` was the only benchmark that was larger than the GHC program at `-O0`. This defect was the largest cause.

- The desugarer now gives each closed dictionary application of a module (no local variable and no type variable) one private top-level value, for example `$dMonad$1`. Each use names that value. GHC does the same at `-O0`. A dictionary that is not closed stays at its use, as before.
- The value is `INLINE`. The inliner first puts each such application back at its uses (`expandDictionaries`). Thus the optimizer gets the same input as on `main`, and the output of each optimization level that runs the inliner is the same as on `main`.
- `-O0` runs no System FC pass, so it keeps the shared values.

The desugarer output is the same at all optimization levels.

## Sizes

Stripped native executables (`strip`), `apple-arm64`, Apple M4 Pro. Each compiler used a new, empty store. The benchmarks are from `ai-haskell-compiler/benchmarks` `origin/main` (815c970). The `aihc-resolve` and `aihc-tc` dependencies are the pinned commit `6ceb5ca`. The `main` compiler is `2f3fcc261`.

| Benchmark | Level | main (bytes) | This PR (bytes) | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| aihc-tc-bench | -O0 | 43,821,760 | 37,317,664 | -14.84% |
| aihc-parser-stackage | -O0 | 15,745,952 | 14,564,880 | -7.50% |
| aihc-resolve-bench | -O0 | 18,721,376 | 17,489,120 | -6.58% |
| regex-log-extract | -O0 | 6,408,480 | 6,271,424 | -2.14% |
| microhs-self-compile | -O0 | 22,084,608 | 21,844,912 | -1.09% |
| string-metrics | -O0 | 3,120,000 | 3,103,024 | -0.54% |
| aihc-cpp-stackage | -O0 | 5,930,336 | 5,930,208 | -0.00% |
| arithmoi-factorise | -O0 | 7,186,512 | 7,185,920 | -0.01% |
| exact-convex-hull | -O0 | 2,599,200 | 2,599,168 | -0.00% |
| fgl-queries | -O0 | 6,923,744 | 6,923,696 | -0.00% |
| rsa-verify | -O0 | 1,475,952 | 1,475,888 | -0.00% |
| sha-digest | -O0 | 4,010,592 | 4,010,544 | -0.00% |
| snappy-roundtrip | -O0 | 2,069,840 | 2,069,792 | -0.00% |
| aihc-tc-bench | -O1 | 38,908,336 | 38,908,656 | +0.00% |
| aihc-tc-bench | -Os | 13,839,824 | 13,839,824 | 0 |
| all 13 benchmarks | -O2 | | | 0 (the same size for each one) |

The GHC 9.14.1 `-O0` executable of `aihc-tc-bench` on perf.aihc.app is 35.0 MB, and the AIHC one was 42.8 MB. Thus the gap is now about 2 MB, not 8 MB. The remaining part comes mostly from the generic `eval` and `apply` at each call of an imported function. That is a different change.

## Run time

`aihc-tc-bench -O0` on the frontend corpus (`O0 native` workload), one run each: `main` 45.3 s and 864 MB peak memory, this PR 42.6 s and 782 MB peak memory. Both print `ok`, so the checksum of the type checker output is the same.

## Tests

- New fixture `closed-dictionary-module-value.yaml` (FC golden, no pass). It shows one module value for a dictionary that two functions use. It fails on `main`, where each function builds `v$fFlagList @tBool v$fFlagBool`. Cost: about 0.01 s. It changes only when the desugaring of dictionaries changes.
- `specialise-top-compound-dictionary.yaml` and `super-specialise-top-dictionaries.yaml` run their specialiser alone, without the inliner. They now see the shared value `v$dFlag$1` or `v$dToggle$1` in place of a local `let` of the same application. The specialized code is the same. In `super-specialise`, the unique numbers of the copies changed.
- The four inliner fixtures (`inline-dictionary-context`, `inline-dictionary-function-stays-call`, `inline-local-dictionary-selection`, `inline-pragma-alias`) did not change. They fail without `expandDictionaries`, because a module value hides the dictionary function application from the method selection.

## Progress counts

No progress count changes.

author: teffluvium
body:
## Summary

Make alternative flocking algorithms usable through the existing stepper without changing its orchestration or sequential update model.

Closes #40

## Changes

- Add the structural `FlockingAlgorithm` protocol and default `ClassicFlocking` adapter, preserving public mathematical rule functions for experiments.
- Inject one algorithm at stepper construction while retaining existing `apply()` and `stats()` interfaces.
- Validate the declared interaction radius once per pass before mutation; support finite nonnegative radii and `None` for the whole flock.
- Supply exact, self-inclusive neighborhoods in original flock order across scan/grid backends, including coincident members at radius zero.
- Preserve sequential velocity updates and wrap visibility, predator reactions, speed-before-boundary ordering, and index maintenance.
- Document programmatic usage and controlled before/after benchmarks. No settings UI, plugin registry, or simultaneous mode is introduced.

## Validation

- `uv run ruff check .` passed.
- Changed Python files passed `uv run ruff format --check`.
- `uv run mypy src/my_boids tests` passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q`: **271 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Staged whitespace checks passed.
- Tests cover independent classic numerical expectations, strict thresholds, custom tuning, exact neighborhoods, invalid/zero/extreme/whole-flock radii, current options and population, sequential wraps, and multiframe backend parity.

## Performance

Median frame times in milliseconds from three interleaved before/after runs of the existing harness, 120 frames each, with both Python and NumPy generators reset to seed 40:

| Starting boids | Scan before | Scan after | Grid before | Grid after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 1.693 | 0.738 | 0.624 | 0.633 |
| 200 | 7.158 | 2.751 | 1.540 | 1.557 |

Scan mode filters the neighborhood once before the classic rules rather than traversing the entire flock three times. Grid timings are approximately 1-2% higher in these short runs. These are smoke measurements, not statistically significant performance guarantees; conditions and caveats are recorded in `PERFORMANCE_ANALYSIS.md`.

author: mitsuru
body:
## 概要

RAIKIRI-749: grid コンテナが、最初の行の item の first baseline を自分の first baseline として出すようにします。

baseline 揃えの flex / grid の中に grid を置くと、外側の item が Chromium とずれていました（再現: 外側の最初の item の y が Chromium 23、raikiri 40）。

## 原因

Taffy 0.15 の grid は、baseline を `item の y + (item.baseline があればそれ、なければ item の高さ)` で出します。`item.baseline` が入るのは、同じ行の 2 つ以上の item が baseline 揃えのときだけで、margin.top も二重に足されます。そのため、stretch の item、baseline 揃えが 1 つだけの item、margin のある item は、どれも border box の下端に倒れていました。また Taffy は source 順の最初の item を選びますが、Chromium は列順で選びます。

## 変更

- 新しい `layout/dispatch/grid_baseline.rs` の `with_first_baseline` を、grid アルゴリズムの直後（レイアウト軸のまま、縦書きの grid でも同じ）に呼びます。
- item の選び方は Chromium の実測に合わせました。最初の行だけを見て、列順で、baseline 揃えの item を優先し、なければ最初の item です。`position: relative` の offset は baseline を動かしません。`contain: layout` の item は border box の下端、スクロールコンテナは border box の中に収めます。`last baseline` の item でも first baseline を出します。入れ子の grid はそのまま上に渡します。
- item の baseline は、新しい `Node::exported_first_baseline`（`compute_child_layout_with_block_ctx` が PerformLayout ごとに記録）から読みます。
- `first_baseline_item` / `aligns_by_baseline` は、ページ分割側の `grid_first_line`（page_projection）と共有し、2 か所で選び方がずれないようにしました。
- `axis_adapter.rs` の合成 baseline を `synthesized_baseline` に切り出して再利用しています（挙動は変えていません）。

## 副作用（意図したもの）

行の中の `inline-grid` が、最初の行の item の first-line の baseline に乗るようになりました（Chromium も同じで、行の高さが変わります）。layout-diff で見えた差分は、すべてこの baseline の変更が原因です（生成ケース 275 件のうち inline-grid 247 件、baseline 揃えの item の中の grid 24 件、table cell の中の grid 4 件）。

## 検証

- Chromium（Playwright + Ahem）で実測した規則を、`grid_baseline_tests.rs` の 20 本余りのテストにしました。
- layout-diff: 6934 件中 291 件が差分、panic なし。WPT の差分は 16 件で、すべて今 PASS の inline-grid / subgrid 系です（grid-inline-*、subgrid/standalone-axis-size-008, 009 ほか）。ページの高さだけが動き、Chromium と一致することを確かめました（例: 200px の item があふれる subgrid の行は、Chromium も 202px になります）。
- strict WPT: PASS 4868 / XFAIL 119 / XPASS 0 / FAIL 0。
- `scripts/gate.sh` 通過、clippy / doc / fmt もクリーンです。

## 範囲外（M4 に起票済み）

- RAIKIRI-1004: 縦書き grid で、最初の行の item が grid と逆向きの writing-mode のとき（コンテナが後から動かす item）は、これまでどおり Taffy の値のままです。
- RAIKIRI-1005: `contain: layout` の block box は、flex / inline-block の baseline 揃えではまだ最初の行の baseline を出します（Chromium は border box の下端）。この PR は grid の item だけ直しています。

author: ideotion
body:
## What & why

Before: `import_due_feeds` (the scheduler's markets pass) and `POST /api/markets/feeds/import-all` ran every feed through `import_feed` and counted anything not imported as `failed`. `import_feed` already files a failure under an engaged kill switch as the `offline` verdict (R320), but both callers counted that verdict as the feed's own failure and walked every later feed through a refusal too, so one Stop became N failures in the scheduler tally and N `offline` results in the route response.

After: both callers read the switch at the top of each iteration, and read the `offline` verdict (or an exception raised with the switch engaged) after the check, and end the pass. The feed the Stop cut and the ones after it are neither checked nor failed; they stay exactly as due as they were. The route's response gains `skipped_offline`, present only when the kill switch caused it (the `verify_due_feeds` idiom), with the number of feeds not fetched. No new key in the pass tally: a Stop is not an outcome. The markets Load / Refresh / Retry verdict box draws that count.

Why `checked -= 1` after the fact: the cut feed is only known to be cut once `import_feed` returns, because the switch engages mid-fetch; a check before the call cannot see it. The counter is corrected rather than moved so that a feed that really completed is still counted where it always was.

Host answers keep their own verdict and stay failures: a robots disallow and an HTTP status are answers the host really gave, which a Stop (a cut connection) cannot produce.

## What the read found (folded in `7d4e5e939`)

- **The page follow-on became a must-fix.** The first head left the page untouched, on the reasoning that drawing `skipped_offline` could follow. The full read showed why it cannot: the cut and unasked feeds left `results`, so after a Stop the Load button read "Imported X point(s) across 2 feeds", the toast said "Market data loaded.", the verdict box was empty and Retry said "still failing: 0". A partial load read as complete, which regresses "partial says so" and the kill-switch corollary of invariant #14e (before, the user saw one `offline` warn pill per feed). `_renderFeedVerdicts` now draws one line, "{n} not fetched (airplane mode)", in the box all three handlers already call, with or without failures. It reuses the locale key the law tracker already has in all 12 locales, so there is no new string (`i18n_report.py --min 100` is unchanged at 100%).
- **Except order (a fix the read found).** The scheduler pass broke out of its `except` before `session.rollback()` and without `log_failure` under a Stop: a failed transaction could reach the lane's next step, and a real exception during a Stop left no log line. The order is now log, rollback, switch check, break (the route already had it); the test pins the rollback and the log line.
- Comment wording ("nothing was asked of the host", "the next pass asks it first") was inexact: a Stop inside a request may already have sent the GET, and catalogue order means an earlier feed that failed with a host answer is asked first. Now "the host did not answer" and "stays as due as it was". The except-branch test ran on a 5-feed catalogue, so deleting `checked -= 1` still passed; it now runs on one feed and asserts `checked == 0`. The control tests no longer pay about 15 s of real retry sleeps.
- A second, delta-sized read of the fold found nothing to fix.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Checklist

- [x] ruff and mypy clean on the touched sources; `node --check src/static/app-markets.js`; 412 tests green locally (the new tests, the market suites, the ledger and ratchet guards, `test_repo_invariants` minus the two stale-install version tests, the os-patch guard on this tree)
- [x] Added tests for the changed behaviour: `tests/test_markets_stop_in_flight.py` (11 tests; they drive the real `import_feed` with a fetcher that engages the switch and raises the raw `requests`/`AirplaneModeError` string) and `tests/markets_skipped_offline_node_test.js` (the real `_renderFeedVerdicts` extracted from `app-markets.js`, 4 English shapes and all 12 locales checked for the count, placeholders and English leaks; 3 mutants of the JS killed), run through `tests/test_markets_skipped_offline_ui.py`
- [x] **Red before, as run:** 7 of the first 9 tests fail on the old code (the two ordinary-failure controls pass on both). The 2 route tests added after the mutant round (host answer; the except branch) were not in that run.
- [x] **Mutants of the fix, all killed (11):** no top-of-loop check (pipeline 2 fail, route 2), offline verdict not read (1, 2), except branch not read (1, 1), verdict test widened to the switch so a host answer is swallowed (1, 1), cut feed still counted checked (1), `skipped_offline` always present (1), `skipped_offline` counting only the cut feed (2). Two mutants survived the first 9 tests (route except branch; route verdict widened); the 2 tests were added for them and all 11 re-run.
- [x] No number shown to a user comes from a constant; no new outbound traffic; no schema or chrome-string change
- [x] Docs: one shipped row

## Notes for reviewers

- **Stated limit (R320):** a genuine failure that coincides with a Stop reads as the Stop, because the two are not told apart; the feed is asked again on the next online pass.
- **Changed behaviour:** `import-all` under an already-engaged switch now returns `results: []` plus `skipped_offline: N` (it was N `offline` results). A release-notes line is pending with Plan (R319).
- **Not changed:** the single-feed routes (`/feeds/{key}/import`, one honest verdict) and `monitoring/field_test.py` (opt-in only). The toasts "Market data loaded." / "Indices updated." still fire after a partial load; the verdict box line is what says it was partial.
- **Carried wording limit:** when a real exception is raised outside the fetch during a Stop (a store error), the scheduler pass logs it with the line "market feed ... import failed" and then treats it as the Stop's. Under R317 a Stop is not a failure, so the label is imprecise; it is carried rather than reworded, because the point is that the exception is not lost. The route's except branch rolls back and ends the batch without logging that case (it never logged a non-Stop exception either); also carried.
- **Test hygiene, carried:** the sleep patch in `tests/test_markets_stop_in_flight.py` replaces `time.sleep` on the shared `time` module for the length of each test (`monkeypatch` undoes it). That is the class Q measured under R376 (a process-wide patch of a shared module, with no live reader in pytest 9.2.0; the lesson is in #1615). No test here needs a real sleep, so it is harmless today; scoping it to `csv_feeds` with `monkeypatch.setattr(csv_feeds, "time", stub)` rides this lane's next change.

author: realdecimalist
body:
## What failed

On Windows, a repair command that leaves a read-only file in its scratch tree breaks both repair helpers. The common case is a command that runs `git init`, because git writes every object file read-only.

- `repair-replay.py observe()` raises `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` from its `finally` block. The error replaces the replay's completed result, so a valid reproduction reads as a crash, and the scratch tree is left half-deleted.
- `repair-proof.py cleanup()` raises the same `PermissionError` before its own `snapshot cleanup could not be confirmed` check runs. The snapshot is left half-deleted, neither removed nor preserved, and every retry with the same token hits the same file.

## Cause

Each helper deletes its scratch tree with a bare `shutil.rmtree`, and on Windows `os.unlink` refuses a read-only file:

- `plugins/fluxpoint/scripts/repair-replay.py:104`, `shutil.rmtree(scratch)` in the `finally` of `observe()`
- `plugins/fluxpoint/scripts/repair-proof.py:78`, `shutil.rmtree(parent)` in `materialize()`'s failure path
- `plugins/fluxpoint/scripts/repair-proof.py:100`, `shutil.rmtree(path.parent)` in `cleanup()`

## Fix

- `process_tree.remove_tree(path)` is the shared removal for both helpers. When `os.unlink` or `os.rmdir` fails, it clears the read-only bit and retries once. It hooks in through `onexc` on Python 3.12+ and `onerror` before that. If anything is still present afterwards, it raises `CleanupPending` naming each leftover path and its error. Nothing is swallowed.
- In `repair-replay.py`, a scratch tree that still cannot be removed now ends the replay with that `CleanupPending`, naming the tree and each leftover. The replay already raises that error type when it preserves a snapshot.
- `repair-proof.py cleanup()` removes the snapshot tree first and the witness directory second. If removal is refused, the witness survives, the snapshot stays owned, and a later cleanup with the same token can retry. The `snapshot cleanup could not be confirmed` branch could no longer be reached, so it is removed.

New tests:

- `repair-origin-test.py`: `test_command_that_runs_git_init_keeps_its_result_and_removes_scratch` runs a command that commits in a fresh `git init` and exits 1. The replay must return `reproduces: true`, and the scratch tree must be gone.
- `repair-proof-test.py`: `test_cleanup_removes_git_objects_an_attack_left_behind` runs an `execute` whose attack runs `git init`, then expects `cleanup` to return `CLEANED` with the observation and no snapshot directory left.
- `repair-proof-test.py`: `test_cleanup_names_what_it_could_not_remove` makes `os.unlink` refuse one file. It expects a `CleanupPending` naming that file, with the file still present. A second cleanup with the same token must then return `CLEANED`.

## Windows evidence

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Git Bash, CPython 3.11.0. Paths are shortened to `<repo>` and `<tmp>`.

RED, with the tests on main's scripts:

```
$ python plugins/fluxpoint/tests/repair-origin-test.py RealReplay.test_command_that_runs_git_init_keeps_its_result_and_removes_scratch
  File "<repo>\plugins\fluxpoint\scripts\repair-replay.py", line 104, in observe
    shutil.rmtree(scratch)
PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied: '<tmp>\\git-init-snapshot\\.git\\objects\\4b\\825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904'
FAILED (errors=1)

$ python plugins/fluxpoint/tests/repair-proof-test.py RepairProof.test_cleanup_removes_git_objects_an_attack_left_behind RepairProof.test_cleanup_names_what_it_could_not_remove
  File "<repo>\plugins\fluxpoint\scripts\repair-proof.py", line 100, in cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(path.parent)
PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied: '<tmp>\\fluxpoint-repair-proof-8u1gc05m\\tree\\.git\\objects\\2a\\786cb7e410efef65fe4a63085ecc6999cd5826'
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Access is denied
FAILED (errors=2)
```

GREEN, with the change:

```
$ python plugins/fluxpoint/tests/repair-proof-test.py
Ran 20 tests in 383.100s
OK

$ python plugins/fluxpoint/tests/repair-origin-test.py
test_command_that_runs_git_init_keeps_its_result_and_removes_scratch ... ok
Ran 20 tests in 15.394s
FAILED (errors=3)

$ python plugins/fluxpoint/tests/longrun-test.py
Ran 26 tests in 9.751s
OK (skipped=4)
```

The three `repair-origin-test.py` errors also occur on main on this machine, in the same three tests with the same `patch failed: state.json:1`. They are not part of this change. The test writes its fixture patch with `write_text` (`tests/repair-origin-test.py:98`), so on Windows the patch has CRLF line endings and `git apply` rejects it against the LF base. #212 fixes that fixture. It changes a different place in the file from this PR's new test.

The proof suite also passes under CPython 3.12.10, which takes the `onexc` path, with `-W always`. No `onerror` deprecation warning is emitted. The three new tests pass under CPython 3.9.25, the Windows Actions job's version, which takes the `onerror` path.

`scripts/harness.sh --full` is RED on main on this machine, with 21 failing steps. With this change it fails the same 21 steps with the same sub-checks, and nothing else.

This changes the import block of `process_tree.py`, and so does #213. Whichever merges second needs a one-line rebase there.

## Linux CI

Linux CI cannot reproduce this. On POSIX, `unlink` of a read-only file succeeds when the directory is writable, so the bare `rmtree` already removes git's objects there. The Windows Actions job runs `repair-proof-test.py`, so it exercises the two proof tests. It does not run `repair-origin-test.py`.

Closes #196

author: brekkybot
body:
Closes #1116.

## What changed

`backlot diff --source github --update-baseline` acknowledges the sixteen new `missing_operation` gaps and drops the four `/agents/automations/...` entries the vendor's document no longer publishes. The notes are the ones the maintainer's `/decision gap` on #1116 supplied: one replaces the note on `GET /agents/automations`, and one is added for each of the agent-merge, issue-artifact and security-advisory-comment families.

No operation is served. The baseline changes, and so does what is refused ahead of the router, because `backlot.routers.github._PUBLISHED_NOT_SERVED` is built from it:

- All 16 new operations now get `refuse_an_unserved_operation`'s answers ahead of the router's 404, 14 of them for the first time: 401 "Requires authentication" with no credential, 401 "Bad credentials" for `Bearer nope`, and 400 for a token with `1999-01-01`. On the 12 operations real asks a credential for, that matches real for no credential and for `Bearer nope`, with and without `1999-01-01`, including which methods' 401 carries the five `x-ratelimit-*` (`GET` and `POST` do; `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` do not).
- The four `GET`s that real serves without a credential, the artifact list and get and the advisory-comment list and get, answer 401 "Requires authentication" here, where `main` answered 404. This is the choice `refuse_an_unserved_operation`'s docstring records for the ten operations in its sample that real answered without one.
- `GET /agents/automations/{}` and `GET /agents/automations/{}/tasks` leave the baseline, but api.github.com still routes both, so a second set, `_ROUTED_UNPUBLISHED`, keeps refusing them.
- Telemetry moves, because `backlot.telemetry.naming` reads the baseline: `GET …/issues/1/artifacts` and `PUT …/pulls/1/agent-merge` were `unmatched`/`unknown` and are now `issues/list-issue-artifacts` and `agent-merge/put-agent-merge-enrollment` with `missing`. The automation routes go the other way, from their ids with `missing` to `unmatched`/`unknown`.

## Why this is what the real API does

The decision measured each family against api.github.com on 2026-10-28:

| Family | Real answer | Backlot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/agents/automations` and per-repository routes | 401 with no credential; with a token `200 []` for the caller's list, 404 for the rest | not served |
| `.../pulls/{}/agent-merge` | 401 with no credential; with a token the `GET` is 404 with an empty body | not served |
| `.../issues/{}/artifacts` | with a token `200 []` on the list, 404 on a get | not served |
| `.../security-advisories/{}/comments` | `200 []` on the list, 404 on a get of comment 1 | not served |

The maintainer's measurement of the refused operations, 2026-10-28, from a machine with a direct credential:

| Request | Real | `main` | This head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /agents/automations/{available-tools,available-triggers,1}` and `…/1/tasks`, no credential | 401 Requires authentication, counted | 401 | 401 (`_ROUTED_UNPUBLISHED`) |
| the same, `Bearer nope` | 401 Bad credentials | 401 | 401 |
| the same, a token | 404, empty body | 404 | 404 |
| `/agents/automations/available-toolsx` | 401 with no credential | 401 | 401 |
| `/agents/automations/1/nosuch`, `/x/y/z` | 404 for every credential | 404 | 404 |
| `POST …/issues/1/artifacts`, `PUT …/agent-merge`, `POST …/security-advisories/{}/comments`, no credential | 401 Requires authentication, the five on `POST` only | 404 | 401 |
| the same, `Bearer nope` | 401 Bad credentials | 404 | 401 |
| `GET …/issues/{}/artifacts` and `…/{}`, advisory-comment `GET`s, no credential | 404 with the version echo; list `[]` 200 on comments, get 404 | 404 | 401 (not matched, see What changed) |

Two divergences the same measurements show, outside this change, are #1124.

`backlot diff --source github` now reports 1252 divergences, 1252 acknowledged, 0 new.

## Verification

- **Tests** — `pytest -q` on `tests/test_github.py`, `tests/test_fidelity.py` and `tests/test_docs.py` passes; new rows of `_UNSERVED_ROWS` pin the change, and the two `/agents/automations` rows fail without `_ROUTED_UNPUBLISHED`. The full run stops at `tests/test_mcp.py`, whose `MCPError(-32000, 'Conne...')` failures also occur on `main` in this session.
- **Optional surfaces that ran rather than skipped** — none.
- **Lint** — `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` clean. `scripts/prose_check.py` reports one finding in `tests/test_linear.py:3960`, which this change does not touch.

- [x] A test fails without this change: the rows added to `_UNSERVED_ROWS` in `tests/test_github.py`
- [ ] A new endpoint serving corpus content is ACL-scoped, proved for both an admin and a scoped token: this change serves no corpus content

body:
targum-internal#548. **Independent of #963 (#546).** It touches only `talk.js`, plus design.md and the CHANGELOG. It is based on master, so it can merge in either order.

## What changes
- **On a phone** (where `sheet()` draws the drawer as a sheet), opening Talk pushes **one** history entry at the same address, marked `{targumTalk: true}`.
  - The phone's Back (or the swipe) closes the sheet and the page stays. The next Back leaves.
  - ×, the scrim, the handle, Escape and the frame's `targum:close` all take the entry back (`history.back()`), so no dead entry is left.
  - A text opened from the conversation (`targum:open`) uses `location.replace` while on the sheet's entry. That way Back from the reader comes to the page, not to an entry that closes nothing.
  - Forward onto the entry reopens the sheet.
  - A page that loads onto the entry clears its mark rather than reopening, because the next page on a phone opens with the sheet shut (D7).
- **The palette fix (talk.js `open(id)`):** the frame's hash is now set with `contentWindow.location.replace(...)` instead of `location.hash =`, so naming a conversation adds no entry to the holding page's history. On a phone the sheet's own single entry is still there, which is the one the §12 entry allows.
- **The desk is unchanged:** no entry is pushed.
- design.md §12: David's approved entry, word for word.

## Tests
- New `tests/test_talk_back_browser.py`, covering:
  - Phone: open adds one entry; Back closes and stays on /library; Back again leaves.
  - Closing with ×, the scrim or Escape, then Back, leaves (no dead step).
  - Desk adds no entry.
  - Palette `TargumTalk.open('abc')` adds no entry of its own at 1440; at 390 it adds only the sheet's one, which Back then closes.

## Known edge
- The Library listens to `popstate`. Closing the sheet with Back sends it a same-address pop. That resets its page-of-results count only when a `?see=` view is open, and nothing else moves.

No new strings.

body:
## Summary

- The `LogEntry` resource (`/api/admin/log_entries`) now requires the permission `audit:read` (`AuditPermissions::READ`) instead of `ROLE_ADMIN`; the operations carry no security of their own.
- The bundle registers `audit:read` at the container tag `za7_core.permission` (plain string, inert without za7-core). No role map, no configuration node, no za7-core dependency.
- PHP >= 8.5 (composer, CI matrix, Compose runner); `symfony/yaml` declared as runtime dependency.
- README rewritten, CHANGELOG added (0.1.0 to 0.4.0).

## Breaking changes

1. PHP >= 8.5 is required.
2. Without a voter that grants `audit:read`, every request gets 403, administrators included (Symfony's default strategy denies when all voters abstain). Migration: use the za7-core release that ships the permission voter, map `audit:read` in `za7_core.permissions`, and roll out this bundle only together with that release.

## Tests

- `AuditReadPermissionTest`: reads the security expression by reflection and evaluates it with a test voter fixture and an example map (allowed for a mapped role; denied for a wrong role, empty map, empty role list, no token, and for a bare role attribute).
- `PermissionRegistrationTest`: exactly one `za7_core.permission` tag, value `audit:read`, matching the permission format and the resource's expression.

The suite was not run locally; this PR's GitHub Action on PHP 8.5 is the evidence.

Release plan: tag `0.4.0` (no `v`) on the merge commit after a green `master` run.

body:
Closes #99

## Summary

Who may see an event is now decided in one place, `EventService.findEvents`, whatever the query asks for. Before, a guard in the controller only reacted to the literal `pending` in `status`.

```diff
 GET /api/events
   EventController.list
-    if status contains "pending": 403 for anonymous/volunteer, force managerId for a manager
     EventService.findEvents(filters + viewer)
+      admin   → no extra condition
+      manager → status in (approved, finished) OR managerId = self
+      others  → status in (approved, finished)
-GET /api/events/all   (no auth, every row; unused by the frontend)
```

Asking for unpublished statuses as an outsider now returns an empty list (200) instead of 403. A manager asking for another manager's pending events still gets nothing.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on production without a token, `/api/events`, `?status=all` and `/api/events/all` each returned 13 events, including 1 `pending`, 1 `draft` and 1 `cancelled`.
  **After:** `check:events` asks for the pending test event with no status, `all`, `pending`, `approved,pending` and `draft,cancelled`, as an anonymous caller, a volunteer and another manager, and expects it in none of them. The manager who owns it and an admin still see it. `/api/events/all` answers 404. `check:authz` covers the anonymous status-list case.

Existing callers keep working: the events page asks for `approved,finished`, the feed asks a manager's own events with `status=all`, and the admin page is an admin.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No schema change; a revert restores the old behaviour.

**Blast Radius:** small

`/manage-events` still lists other managers' approved events, which is #100. `GET /api/events/:id` still returns a pending event to anyone who has its id; the id is no longer listed anywhere public.

body:
## Why

The owner asked (2026-10-28): can a ticket on GitHub fire an agent by itself, is there a shortcut inside Reef for it, why an API key when a Claude subscription exists, and does it need anything on GitHub's side. The factory (phase 7) answers the first, but it had no skill: its four setup steps lived only in the workflow's header comment, the token was named as an API key only, and the README, the site and the manual said "accept the file, then label" in one sentence each.

## What

- **`skills/reef-factory/SKILL.md`** (30 lines), the owner's side of the factory. Empty → status in five lines, each with its fix: the accepted workflow (`reef-init --accept`), the one secret (`gh secret list`: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; the owner sets it with `gh secret set`, never the agent), branch protection on the base, the labels, the last runs. _Requested by **Arya** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KbZCQujoBnjyWiKDhcnu5L?thread=cmsg_01KbZCQujoBnjyWiKDhcnu5L4dQGHnQZukUtvUhVhnKDKK)_

## Before

Since #92, sources with `browser-session` run four calls at once. A site block, such as comix's WAF answering `captcha_required`, can reach several of those calls together. Each call then started its own Chromium and solved the same check, so a single block could mean four CloakBrowsers running at the same time.

## After

Each source and user gets one browser session at a time.

- A call that needs the browser while another call has it open waits for it to close. It waits at most one browser lifetime (120 s), then fails with "another call is still using this source's browser; retry".
- By the time a waiting call gets the browser, it finds the cookies the first call earned.
- Calls that only make HTTP requests still run four at a time.

readchek/ext#34 completes the fix on the comix side. If comix sees that a fresh clearance arrived while it waited, it closes the browser and retries without solving the check again.

## How

- `calls::Browsers` is a gate on each `Context`. `browser_session::open` takes it, and `release_browser` gives it back. `release_browser` runs on `close`, on the next `open`, and when the call's `State` drops, so a call that fails still releases the gate.
- I added a unit test for taking turns at the gate.
- `docs/server.md` describes the new behavior.

Tested here: `cargo test -p chek-sources` passes, and `cargo clippy -p chek-sources --all-targets` reports no warnings.

## 为什么

`tests/unit/admin-contract-docs.test.mjs` 的 A–D 组只检查「描述里有该有的东西」（含自身 `x-scope`、状态码 ⊆ `responses`、声明了 `Idempotency-Key` 就必须写进描述）。它们**挡不住语义退化**：把一条已经被代码证伪的描述原句放回去，九道门禁依然全绿。

| 轮次 | 结论 | 关键发现 |
|---|---|---|
| 一 | 需修改 3 | 两条片段是**真话的子串** ⇒ 会把正确表述误红；`:684` 注释宣称堵住「先删登记再改回错话」，实测 `rotate-pin`（删真钉子 + 垃圾片段补足 12 条）⇒ **20/20 全绿**；E6 方向二恒真 |

author: macguard
lucagenchi
body:
Closes #158. [#161](https://github.com/LucaGenchi/opticalsetup/pull/161) fixed most of it — specimen two-beam signals moved to the crystal's `mixOverlap`, timed beam to beam — and left two pieces, which this PR finishes.

## What changes for the user
- **CARS fades sooner than SRS as the arms drift apart.** CARS goes as I<sub>p</sub>²I<sub>s</sub> (pump and probe are one beam), so its gate is the overlap of the squared pump envelope with the Stokes one, `exp(−4 ln2 Δt²/(τp²/2 + τs²))`. Sum frequency and stimulated Raman keep `exp(−4 ln2 Δt²/(τ₁² + τ₂²))`. Two 1 ps pulses 667 fs apart now keep 43.9 % of a CARS signal, where the shared rule gave 54 %.
- **The inspector agrees with the canvas.** The two-beam warning still used `pulseOverlap`, which treated unequal repetition rates as fully overlapping and used a different envelope. It now uses `mixOverlap` with the same photon counts and says *"CARS timing is not modelled between 80 and 40 MHz trains, so no signal is drawn. Run both lasers at one repetition rate."* `pulseOverlap` had no other caller and is removed.
- The Sample wiki article and the Coherent Raman example page said the I<sub>p</sub>²I<sub>s</sub> weighting was not modelled; both now describe what is.

## Physics limits
Instantaneous, non-resonant limit only: a resonant vibration's dephasing (which lets a delayed probe still read a coherence out) is not modelled. Gaussian envelopes; equal repetition rates only, as before.

## Saved scenes
No format change. Matched scenes read the same: every bundled golden snapshot is unchanged, and the Coherent Raman example still reads 100 % overlap. A hand-built scene with a partly mismatched CARS pair now shows a weaker CARS signal than before — a physics correction, not a conversion. The crystal and OPA call `mixOverlap` without photon counts and are unchanged.

## Implementation
- `mixOverlap(a, b, { orderA, orderB })` (`parametric.js`): n photons from a beam → width τ/√n, centre weighted by n/τ²; non-finite or < 1 counts fall back to 1.
- `twoBeamOrders(kind, wlA, wlB)` (`elements.js`): CARS counts the shorter wavelength twice.
- **Partner choice (review round 1, finding 1):** where a colour arrives on several paths, the partner a two-beam channel pairs with is chosen by that channel's own gate (`twoBeamPartner` in `raytrace.js`, shared with the inspector), so CARS no longer picks by the plain overlap and then gates the choice with its pump counted twice.
- **Timing warning per pair (review round 1, finding 2):** the inspector judges the pairs the tracer makes, not the shortest and longest beams. A pair at another repetition rate is named as not mixed (*The pair 800 nm at 37 MHz and 1040 nm at 80 MHz is not mixed: timing between different repetition rates is not modelled.*), and *so no signal is drawn* is said only when no pair can be timed.
- Offline cache v161 (main reached v160 with #277, #281, #283 and #282; #284 kept v160). Main merged in at `a2084ad5`. The Sample wiki article keeps this PR's gate text followed by #283's *Coherent Raman excitation* paragraph.

## Checks
- `npm test` (after merging main, round 1 fixes): 2,523 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped. New tests reproduce both review cases (a 200 fs pump with 400 fs/450 fs-late and 50 fs/200 fs-late Stokes beams; two 800 nm pumps at 37 and 80 MHz with an 80 MHz Stokes), and each fails with its fix removed. Earlier run: 2,520 pass (the Python checks; `python3 validation/run.py` is current). Browser on the merged branch: the Coherent Raman example with the Stokes arm 0.2 mm longer shows 43.9 % CARS overlap and its warning, and #283's readout unchanged; no console errors. `node --check` on `sketch/js/*.js` and `serve.mjs`; `git diff --check`.
- New tests in `test/specimen-types.test.js`: the closed form against a numerical integral of I<sub>a</sub>ᵐ I<sub>b</sub>ⁿ for four width/order pairs and four delays, plus invalid orders and the signal centre; CARS against sum frequency on a traced bench; unequal repetition rates traced (no anti-Stokes line, `unsupported` state, canvas text) and in the inspector warnings. One existing readout test changes 54 % → 43.9 %.
- Browser, Coherent Raman example served from this branch: matched → 100 %; retroreflector moved 0.1 mm → "667 fs apart (0.2 mm of path), 43.9% temporal overlap"; 1030 nm laser at 40 MHz → timing readout and both channel warnings shown; no console errors, no overflow at 1024 px.

## Known open point
The specimen's *Two-beam timing* readout shows one overlap figure per specimen. With CARS and SRS on one specimen the two now differ for the same mismatch, and the readout does not say which it shows.

body:
Slice: AUTH-LOGOUT-CSRF-1

Depends on #231, #254, #273 (branched from `integration/wave3-2026-10-28`; the diff against develop includes those trains until they land).

## Changes
- **`POST /auth/logout`** (`services/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts`): it reads and clears the `wrench_access` / `wrench_refresh` cookies only when the caller sends `x-client: wrench-web`, the same header the cookie refresh needs. A header-less form POST (cross-site or same-site) now does nothing to the cookies. Logging out with an `Authorization: Bearer` header still works without the header and still clears cookies, since a cross-origin page can't send a Bearer header without a preflight either. A body `refreshToken` still revokes on an exact hash match.
- **Login, signup, `2fa/verify`, `2fa/backup`**: if the caller sends `x-client: wrench-web` (cookie mode), the JSON no longer includes `refreshToken`. The HttpOnly cookie is still set. Callers that don't send `x-client` (header mode: Playwright API clients, scripts, mobile SDK) still get it.
- **Web** `clearSession()` logout fetch now sends `x-client: wrench-web`. Every other web call already does through `apiFetch`.
- Spec: `docs/product/slices/auth-logout-csrf-1.md`.

Callers checked: `setSession` in web ignores `refreshToken`. Desktop wraps the web app and has no auth client of its own. Admin login uses a raw fetch with no `x-client` and reads only `accessToken`. `packages/mobile-sdk` and marketplace read only `accessToken`.

Assurance trace: no role check (the route is public) → `@Public()` route → no guard/tenant (the service matches by refresh hash or by verified bearer sid) → no DTO → CSRF rule `isCookieClient` → no transaction → effects: cookie clear + session revoke → UI: `clearSession`.

## Tests (container `ww-baseline-dev`, git-archive copy in `/tmp/alc1`, node_modules symlinked from `/tmp/dev`)
- Test-first: `cd services/api && npx jest src/auth/auth-logout-csrf.spec.ts` failed **3 failed / 4 passed** before the fix. After the fix:
- `npx jest src/auth/auth-logout-csrf.spec.ts src/auth/auth.controller.spec.ts src/auth/auth-cookie.spec.ts src/auth/auth.logout.spec.ts` → **4 suites, 33 tests passed**
- `npx jest src/auth` → 29/31 suites, 341/345 tests. The 4 failures are in `route-inventory.spec.ts` (bullmq ESM parse) and `auth.controller.throttle.spec.ts` (throttler metadata). They fail the same way with the unmodified controller, so they come from the environment and existed before this change.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (api): no errors in `src/auth/` (17 errors elsewhere, outside this change).
- Web: `npx vitest run -c vitest.alc.config.ts src/lib/api-session.test.ts` → 11/11 pass. The new header assertion fails on the old `api.ts` (1 failed). The scratch config only drops the `vite-tsconfig-paths` plugin and PostCSS, which aren't installed in `/tmp/dev`, and aliases `@wrench/domain` to its source. `api-refresh.test.ts` has 2 failures (`OfflineSessionChangedError`) that are the same on the old `api.ts`.
- `prettier --check` passes on all changed files.

## Limitations
- **E2E follow-up needed (I can't edit `e2e/**`, which belongs to #231's CI-fix lane):** in `e2e/tests/session-lifecycle.spec.ts`, the test "logging out one session leaves an independent login active" does a cookie-only `a.post('/v1/auth/logout')` with no header. That is exactly the CSRF shape, so it will now get `/me` 200 instead of 401. Fix: add `headers: { 'x-client': 'wrench-web' }` to that call. The other two tests in the file use Bearer or the browser, so they're unaffected.
- No e2e or live-browser run. The CORS preflight rejection is assumed from the existing allowlist and was not re-tested here.
- Admin (`x-client: wrench-admin`) isn't treated as cookie mode. Its login is a credential-less raw fetch, so it gets no cookies anyway.

body:
I changed the OS label sent during linked-device registration from `Ubuntu` to `Home Assistant`. New pairings should display Google Chrome (Home Assistant); the final phone display and live approval still need device confirmation.

I preserved a canonical `Chrome (Ubuntu)` display for phone-code requests. The pinned Baileys 6.7.23 captures the browser tuple by reference and sends it directly in that IQ. [Upstream issue #2560](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/issues/2560) documents rejection of custom phone-code display labels. I switch only this socket's OS label during its serialized phone-code request, then restore it on success, failure, cancellation, or timeout. Normal registration keeps the Home Assistant label.

I aligned all release metadata to 3.3.1 and included the dedicated native Rust caches from #32 in both changelogs.

Validation:
- Passed the installed-Baileys loopback test for the actual registration payload and canonical phone-code IQ, without contacting WhatsApp.
- Passed the full Node suite: 495 passed, zero failed, two skipped.
- Passed JavaScript syntax, version metadata, Markdown, whitespace, and HACS release-package preflight checks.
- Reviewed browser ownership, concurrency, timeout, and restoration behavior independently.

I skipped branch CI while preparing the release. The merge into main will run the combined workflows and warm the Rust caches before v3.3.1 is tagged.

body:
## 요약

Windows 보안의 '제어된 폴더 액세스'(랜섬웨어 방지)가 `문서\IeumOffice`를 막은 PC에서 처음 켤 때 앱이 멈추던 문제를 고친다(결정 0078).

## 원인

기본 저장 폴더를 정하는 함수가 부를 때마다 폴더를 다시 만들고, 대체 폴더를 쓸 수 없으면 예외를 던졌다. 이 함수는 홈 화면의 폴더 나무, 폴더 감시, 검색 색인, 편집기의 첫 저장이 쉬지 않고 부르므로, 막힌 PC에서는 그때마다 동기 폴더 만들기가 막히고 예외가 났다. 0.12.4~0.12.6에서 "처음 켜면 응답없음", "환영 화면에서 멈춘다", "회색 화면" 신고가 열 건 넘게 들어왔고, 한 신고자가 앱을 허용 목록에 넣자 정상이 됐다고 알려 왔다.

## 바꾼 것

- 없는 폴더만 만들고, 있는 폴더는 쓰기 권한만 본다.
- 쓸 수 없던 폴더는 30초 동안 다시 시도하지 않는다(편집기 번들 사이에 `Symbol.for`로 공유).
- `문서\IeumOffice` → `<홈>\IeumOffice` → `<앱 데이터>\IeumOffice` 순서로 내려간다.
- 내려갔으면 실행마다 한 번, 어디에 저장되는지와 허용하는 방법을 알린다.

## 확인

- `packages/electron-utils/tests/default-save-dir.test.ts`
- 실제 '제어된 폴더 액세스'를 켠 PC에서의 확인은 시험 사용자·신고자에게 부탁한다.

0.12.8에 넣는다.

author: mapiolca
body:
The installer loads module activation for `$conf->entity`, but menu cleanup scans and deletes entries from every entity. A module disabled in entity 1 can therefore lose its menus in entity 2 even when it is enabled there.

Filter both the scan and deletion by the loaded entity. Preserve entries belonging to other entities and entity 0. This follows #42221's separation of operation scope: its entity selector continues to apply to ECM only, without changing the global configuration context.

Reproduction: add menus for the same module in entities 1 and 2, enable the module only in entity 2, then run `clean_menus` from the installer. Before this fix both entities lose their menus; afterward only entity 1 is cleaned.

Validation on PHP 8.4.22 / MariaDB 11.4.5, using the actual `repair.php` handler with an isolated database and CLI request variables:
- Reproduced the failure before the change and verified the same fixture afterward.
- Preview preserves all rows; confirmed cleanup preserves other entities, global entries, active modules, OR conditions and the legacy margins alias.
- Quoted module names and repeated cleanup verified.
- PHP lint, `git diff --check`, and targeted PHPStan level 10 passed with the repository bootstrap and installer paths explicitly included.

The full application suite and browser interaction were not run locally. No interface change.

author: z-brenner
body:
This adds the evaluation report and its lab scripts. It changes nothing in the app. The full report is `bench/reports/lfm3-d1-linux-cpu-2026-10-28/README.md`.

## Answer
- **LFM3-Omni-2B should not replace Qwen3.5-2B.** Neither should LFM3-1.7B, which is Omni's text backbone. Both ran on llama.cpp b11946 with the app's flags and current `main`:

  | Live InternBench, 77 docs | Names right | Wrong but ready | Trap dates filed | Median per doc |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Qwen3.5-2B (production) | **52** | 15 | 0 | **17.5 s** |
  | LFM3-Omni-2B, few-shot | 40 | 19 | **3** | 21.2 s |
  | LFM3-1.7B, few-shot | 45 | 7 | 0 | 22.7 s |

  - With Intern's own prompt, both LFM3 models copied the instructions into the answer. Omni's `document_type` was literally "what the document is". So they were also run with the few-shot profile built for Bonsai 2B; that's the table above.
  - LFM3's tokenizer needs about 46% more tokens for the same text, so it is slower even though it decodes faster.
- **d1-2B works as a check, not as a namer.** It answers one yes/no question per name Qwen marks ready: "Is ⟨party⟩ the main organization or person this document belongs to or comes from?" Thresholds were chosen by leave-one-out:
  - **Q8_0:** it holds **8 of 14** wrong names for 3 of 46 right ones.
  - **Q4_K_M, 2 threads, the shape it could ship in:** 8 of 14 for 5 of 46, at about 15 s per ready name and a 2.3 GB server.

  The errors it catches are the substantive ones: a signatory, chair or mechanic named instead of the organization. The ones it misses are relation-word slips ("to" vs "for").
- **Licence.** Both models are under the LFM Open License v1.0. Its §5 licenses commercial use only below **US$10M annual revenue**. Law firms above that would be unlicensed without a commercial licence from Liquid AI.

## Recommendation
- Keep Qwen.
- Pursue d1 only if Liquid AI licenses it for Intern's customers, and the question holds up on real documents.
- The cheaper next experiment: ask Qwen itself the main-party question as a constrained yes/no second turn.

## Scripts
- `scripts/lfm3-eval/run.sh` builds b11946 from source and runs the live runs and the d1 questions.
- `scripts/lfm3-eval/run-fewshot.sh` runs the few-shot passes.
- `scripts/lfm3-eval/run-d1-gate.sh` runs d1 in the shape it could ship in.

author: agentloopapp[bot]
body:
Write cards where the knowledge lives. A line `Question :: Answer` in any page becomes a flashcard when the page is saved:

```
Capital of France :: Paris
- Leitner boxes :: a ladder of review intervals
```

- **What changes a card:** changing the answer **updates** the card, and removing the line **deletes** it. Deleting the page deletes its cards, and restoring the page brings them back.
- **What counts as a card line:** list markers (`-`, `*`, `1.`, `- [ ]`) are fine. Lines inside fenced code are ignored, since C++ and Haskell use `::`. Both sides must be non-empty. A repeated question counts once.
- **Identity:** a page card's id is `nameBasedId('giki/page_card', [page, question])`, with case and spacing ignored. Fixing an answer or the capitalisation keeps the card **and its review schedule**. Two devices saving the same page write the same row, and Last-Write-Wins merges them.
- **Hand-made cards** (Study → New card) have random ids, so `syncPageCards` never touches them, even when they belong to the page.
- **Only changed cards are written.** Saving a page doesn't stamp its unchanged cards, which would otherwise beat an edit made elsewhere under LWW.
- **Local saves only.** A page that arrives by sync brings its cards as their own rows, written by the device that saved it.

**Review follow-up**
- **Diff-based.** Comparing cards to the current text undid Study-page edits and brought back deleted cards on every unrelated save. Now the page text **before and after** the save is compared, and only lines that were added, changed or removed touch their cards. A card edited or deleted on the Study page or on another device stays that way until someone edits its line.
- **Found by id.** A removed line's card is found by id, not by its current text, so a card whose question was rephrased on the Study page is still deleted with its line or its page.
- **Atomic.** The page, its links and its cards are written in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, so a closed tab can't leave a page synced without its cards.
- **Fences follow CommonMark:** same character, at least as long as the opener, no info string on the closing fence. Indented code and a `::` inside a code span aren't cards.
- **CI.** The native-SQLite test moved to `client/test_vm/`. The browser can't even compile it, and CI's VM step now runs `flutter test test test_vm`.
- The editor help text mentions the syntax.

Tests:
- `test/page_cards_test.dart`: the parser (list markers, fences, empty sides, duplicates), and `syncPageCards` against the real schema in an in-memory SQLite. It covers create, update, delete, no writes for unchanged text, hand-made cards left alone, and page delete and restore.
- An integration phase: a page line becomes a due card, the card reaches the server, editing the answer keeps the card, and removing the line removes it.
