body:
## Host load confirmation (revised after Aegis review)

Attach/rebind leave the host load **pending**; the first real host activity records a confirmation in `.mwf/local/integration.json`, and `status`/`doctor` show pending / confirmed (+ the hint 「可能未加载或未信任」 after 10 minutes).

### Design
- Record lives in the **free-form per-client `probe`**: `probe.host_confirmation.{hook|extension|mcp} = {time, host_version, host_name, trigger}` (+ `binding_generation`, `runtime_version`), mirrored as `probe.host_confirmed`. **No strict receipt schema change, `receipt_version` stays 3.**
- Shared pure helper `src/contracts/host-confirmation.ts` (`hostLoad`, `currentConfirmation`) is the single source of truth for both the probe mirror and status.
- Codex confirms only on a **hook**; Pi on the **extension** event; an MCP call is tracked as its own channel.

### Review items
1. **Receipt compatibility**: confirmation is stored inside `probe` (`Record<string, unknown>` for 0.3.x), so older runtimes' strict schema still parses it. Verified manually with a 0.3.1 (main e8efb23) build: `status`, `doctor`, `detach --apply` all succeed on a receipt containing a hook confirmation. Test: receipt stays v3 and parses under a copy of the 0.3.1 strict client schema.
2. **MCP ≠ hook loaded**: separate channels; Codex stays `pending` (`channels: {hook: pending, mcp: confirmed}`) until a hook fires; hint detail says "hook 未触发（MCP 已连接）". Test at the old host-confirm.test.ts:133 rewritten accordingly.
3. **Rebind/stale**: attach/rebind replace `probe` (confirmation cleared). A record with another generation or runtime_version is ignored by *both* probe mirror and status, and replaced (not extended) by the next trigger. Tested.
4. **Host version from hook**: read from the hook payload when present (`codex_version`/`client_version`/`version`). The documented Codex hook input has **no version field**, so otherwise status falls back to the same host's MCP clientInfo version (documented, tested).
5. **10-minute hint**: anchor = earliest valid of attach probe time and receipt file mtime (works without a probe), anchors in the future (clock set back) are ignored, `>=` boundary; if no usable anchor there is no false hint. Tested incl. future/absent probe time.
6. **Lock**: first confirmation waits ≤250 ms for the project lock (`withLockDeadline`), gives up silently (retried on next trigger), never throws; read-only fast path otherwise. Test with a lock-holder process.

Note: `withLockDeadline` + the `storage/index.ts` hunk are byte-identical to the one in #33 (clean merge in either order; nested budgets only shorten).

### Files
`src/contracts/host-confirmation.ts` (new), `src/integrations/shared/confirm.ts`, `src/core/diagnostics.ts`, hook/Pi/MCP call sites, `src/storage/index.ts` (lock deadline), `tests/host-confirm.test.ts` (9 tests), `tests/safety.test.ts`, docs/CHANGELOG/status skill.

### Tests
`npm run format:check`, `typecheck`, `npm test` (176 pass), `test:package` pass locally; CI green. Local trial merge #32+#33+#34: 198/198, codex-stop 15/15.

Real-host validation (Codex trust flow, 10 min timeout) is deferred to 1.0; the timeout value is provisional.

Closes #131

## What changed and why

From docs/astra-audit.md finding 9: an SEC size outside the standards was either not marked at all, or the mark was dropped before it reached the summary and the calibration figure.

All changes are in `hplc-figure-bench(WF1.13).html`:

1. **`secInfo`** (size exclusion section): a peak is now marked extrapolated (`extrap`) as soon as its Kav (or Ve) is outside the interval of the standards actually used in the fit. The unmarked 8% extension beyond the outermost standards is gone. A 1e-9 tolerance keeps a peak sitting exactly on a standard inside the range.
2. **`sumRows`**: the SEC size kept for the main pooled peak (`secMw`) now carries `extrap` as well as `{mw, ve}`.
3. **`renderSumTable`**: the summary note for that peak prints `apparent ~316 kDa` and adds "It elutes outside the range of the standards, so this size is extrapolated from the calibration." when the peak is extrapolated. Notes for peaks inside the range don't change.
4. **`buildCalSVG`**: sample labels on the SEC calibration figure get the same `~` prefix the peak table, overlay labels and CSV already use (for example `P1 ~316 kDa`).

No calculated value changes. Only the extrapolated/not extrapolated decision and the labels that show it change. **This needs the owner's OK** (the issue says so): taking out the 8% allowance means peaks that lie 0–8% of the standards' span beyond the outermost standard now show `~` where they didn't before. Source: the worked fit in the audit, and the fact that a calibration only holds over the interval its standards cover (Cytiva's SEC selection guide on the finite fractionation range, cited in docs/astra-audit.md).

Saved settings and projects are unaffected: `extrap` is worked out again each time and never saved.

## The new check (tests/suites/26_sec_calibration.js)

Two new UI-only cases (`extrapCase`), each in a fresh browser. Each case uses the synthetic `tests/data/science/sec_inject2.csv` (peaks at Ve 12.00 and 15.00 mL from injection), sets V0 8 and Vt 24, and types two standards (100 kDa and 10 kDa) into the SEC panel. It then clicks Detect peaks, pools with Suggest, reads the summary notes, and opens the SEC calibration figure tab in Quick mode, since project mode hides figure tabs. Nothing reaches into `window.__HFB`.

| Case | Standards | 12 mL peak (outside) | 15 mL peak (inside) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extrap_14_18` | 100 kDa @ 14 mL, 10 kDa @ 18 mL | log10 M = 5.5 − 0.25·Ve → **316.23 kDa**, must read `~316` | 56.23 kDa, no `~` |
| `extrap_12p2_18p2` | 100 kDa @ 12.2 mL, 10 kDa @ 18.2 mL | 10^(2 + 0.2/6) → **107.98 kDa**, must read `~108` | 34.15 kDa, no `~` |

Checks for each case: `fit_from_2`, `table_outside_marked`, `table_inside_unmarked`, `summary_note_marked`, `cal_figure_outside_marked`, `cal_figure_inside_unmarked`, `no page errors`. Numbers are compared within ±1 kDa of the displayed rounded value.

What should happen on main, worked out from the code (not run):
- `extrap_14_18.summary_note_marked` fails: main's note reads `apparent 316 kDa` with no `~` and no extrapolation wording.
- `extrap_14_18.cal_figure_outside_marked` fails: main's label reads `P1 316 kDa`.
- `extrap_12p2_18p2.table_outside_marked` fails: main shows `108` with no `~`, because the 8% allowance (0.48 mL) covers the 0.2 mL gap.
- `extrap_12p2_18p2.summary_note_marked` and `.cal_figure_outside_marked` fail for the same reasons.
- The `*_inside_unmarked` checks and `extrap_14_18.table_outside_marked` should pass on both main and this branch. They make sure inside-range peaks don't get flagged and that the peak table, which was already right for case A, stays right.

All existing checks are unchanged.

**Nothing. The suites were not run.** In this Claude Code session every `node` command needed an approval that can't be given non-interactively, and the PowerShell tool failed on every command ("The command line is too long"). So:

author: 294962silent
body:
## Summary

`WindowScheduler` derives its window start offsets from `init_timestep`, `window_size` and `num_timesteps`, but never checks that the last window actually fits inside the schedule. When `num_timesteps - window_size < init_timestep`, it returns SDE step indices at or beyond `num_timesteps`:

```python
>>> WindowScheduler(10, WindowConfig(strategy="progressive", window_size=4, init_timestep=10)).get_sde_indices(0)
{10, 11, 12, 13}      # schedule length is 10
>>> WindowScheduler(1, WindowConfig(strategy="random", window_size=4)).get_sde_indices(0)
{0, 1, 2, 3}
```

Downstream that lands in two different behaviours:

- `rollout/engine/fastvideo/engine.py:333` range-checks the indices (`bad = [i for i in sde_indices if i < 0 or i >= num_steps]`) and fails the rollout;
- the vLLM-Omni gate in `rollout/engine/vllm_omni/pipelines/_shared/flow_match_sde_scheduler.py:149-153` is a bare membership test (`step_is_sde = int(sigma_idx) in self._sde_indices_set`), so with `init_timestep >= num_timesteps` **no step ever matches**, SDE silently never fires, and the run degrades to deterministic ODE with no error or warning. Geometry that only partly overflows is likewise truncated silently (e.g. `init_timestep=9, window_size=4, num_timesteps=10` leaves exactly one usable SDE step).

This rejects the geometry at construction, the same fail-closed posture `AllSDEScheduler` already takes when `num_sde_steps` exceeds the pool size:

```
ValueError: WindowScheduler(progressive) needs num_timesteps - window_size >= init_timestep,
got num_timesteps=10, window_size=4, init_timestep=10.
```

The `all` strategy is exempt (it does not use windows). Every shipped recipe stays valid — `bagel_*` use `num_timesteps: 7` with `window_size: 3`, and `*_mixgrpo` use `num_timesteps: ${..num_inference_steps}` = 10 with `window_size: 4`.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Test Plan

Scheduler-only; no model, GPU, or dataset needed. Run from the repo root with a CPU environment.

```
$ python - <<'PY'
from unirl.sde.index_schedule import WindowConfig, WindowScheduler
# before this change these returned out-of-range indices
for T, strat, ws, init in [(10,"progressive",4,10), (10,"progressive",4,9),
                           (1,"random",4,0), (3,"decay",4,0)]:
    try:
        WindowScheduler(T, WindowConfig(strategy=strat, window_size=ws, init_timestep=init))
        print("ACCEPTED", T, strat, ws, init)
    except ValueError as e:
        print("REJECTED:", e)
PY
REJECTED: WindowScheduler(progressive) needs num_timesteps - window_size >= init_timestep, got num_timesteps=10, window_size=4, init_timestep=10.
REJECTED: WindowScheduler(progressive) needs num_timesteps - window_size >= init_timestep, got num_timesteps=10, window_size=4, init_timestep=9.
REJECTED: WindowScheduler(random) needs num_timesteps - window_size >= init_timestep, got num_timesteps=1, window_size=4, init_timestep=0.
REJECTED: WindowScheduler(decay) needs num_timesteps - window_size >= init_timestep, got num_timesteps=3, window_size=4, init_timestep=0.
```

Exhaustive bounds sweep over every accepted geometry (all five strategies, `num_timesteps` 1..24, `window_size` 1..7, all `init_timestep`, `overlap_size` 0..2, steps 0/1/2/3/7/25/100/999):

```
checked=22332 configs, rejected=8988 invalid configs, out-of-bounds=0
ALL IN BOUNDS
```

Shipped-recipe regression (constructed from the recipe values):

```
bagel  (num_timesteps=7,  window_size=3, random, roll_back=None): union of steps 0..49 has no index outside [0,7)
mixgrpo(num_timesteps=10, window_size=4, progressive, overlap_size=1, roll_back=True): step 0 -> [0,1,2,3], step 25 -> [3,4,5,6], no index outside [0,10)
roll_back=False still pins to the last window: step 999 -> [4,5,6,7]
```

`AllSDEScheduler` swept separately for the same class of defect (fraction in {0.0,0.1,0.5,0.9,1.0,(0,0),(0.3,0.3),(0.2,0.5),(1,1)} × `num_sde_steps` in {None,0,1,2,5}, `num_timesteps` 1..20): no out-of-range index, never returns more steps than requested, degenerate pools return `set()`.

Lint gates (what CI runs):

```
$ ruff check unirl/sde/index_schedule.py            -> All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check unirl/sde/index_schedule.py   -> 1 file already formatted
$ python lint/check_docstring_lines.py              -> check-docstring-lines: 3144 docstrings, all one line.
```

Not run; reason: reproducing the end-to-end symptom needs a GPU rollout (`vllm_omni` or `fastvideo` engine with a diffusion checkpoint), which is not available here. The defect and the fix are both confined to index computation, which the sweeps above cover directly.

## Compatibility / Risk

Config-only, fail-closed: recipes whose window geometry does not fit their schedule now raise at construction instead of silently running without SDE exploration. No shipped recipe is affected. No API, checkpoint, data-format, or resource requirement changes.

## Reviewer Notes

- Duplicate-work check: `gh search issues` / `gh search prs` for `sde_indices`, `window_size`, `WindowScheduler`, `index_schedule` in `Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL` return no issue or PR covering window bounds. #489 added the `decay`/`exp_decay` strategies and #376 moved the scheduler into `sde/`; neither addressed out-of-range geometry.
- The asymmetry between the two engines (hard range check vs. membership test) is what made this silent rather than loud — worth knowing if the gate is ever refactored.
- AI assistance: drafted with an AI coding agent; the submitter ran and read every command above, and an independent reviewer pass checked the diff before publication.

## Checklist

- [x] I reviewed the changed code and removed unrelated/generated artifacts.
- [x] I updated tests, docs, and configs where needed, or explained why not.

Local JSON/JSONL datasets can trigger a native Arrow failure during Dataset Preview or Token Preview and terminate the Unsloth backend. This change runs the shared local JSON preview read in a disposable, account-scoped process. A reader crash or parsing failure returns a controlled HTTP 400 while the backend remains available.

**Scope: crash containment and clear rejection.** The reporter's sample is valid JSON, but its incompatible nested tool-argument types still produce a dataset error. Supporting those types for preview, tokenization and training is a separate change. This PR adds no schema normalization, type coercion, dependency upgrade or Arrow patch.

Addresses #15681.

### Implementation

- Keep the existing datasets parser, row selection, conversion and Arrow validation inside the child; accept validated Arrow IPC only after a clean exit, preserving schema and Features.
- Preserve account ownership, cache settings, dataset security guards and native-path secret handling. Bound worker lifetime and clean up processes and temporary files on failure or timeout.
- Avoid optional Torch/TensorFlow imports for inferred plain-JSON columns. Explicit Features retain normal decoder behavior.
- Cover uploaded/local/cached JSON and JSONL reads shared by Dataset Preview, Token Preview and Start Training's format-check preflight. Remote Hugging Face streaming and the already-isolated training worker are unchanged.

### Validation

A/B tests used the supplied 679-record sample and the exact reported `unsloth/unsloth:v0.1.910-beta` image, pinned to digest `sha256:5570381e7bf7d68e65da0a702c324dcf80fd7514601e783b571928a2bc6432f2`: Python 3.12.3, datasets 4.3.0, PyArrow 23.0.1, pandas 2.3.3 and NumPy 2.5.2.

| Check | Upstream base | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dataset Preview / check-format | Backend SIGSEGV (-11); health unavailable | HTTP 400; same backend healthy |
| Token Preview | Backend SIGSEGV (-11); health unavailable | HTTP 400; same backend healthy |
| Valid JSONL and JSON-array preview after the failing request | Backend unavailable | HTTP 200; all test rows preserved |

- 10 focused tests passed: schema/Features and nested-tool preservation, large IPC output, child-only optional imports, parsing errors, worker-death recovery, timeout/reaping and temporary-file cleanup.
- 172 existing regression tests passed across dataset schema drift, account access, missing-file handling, token previews, Arrow validation, CSV cells and role aliases. One Hub-dependent tiny-tokenizer test was skipped with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Canonical formatting, targeted Ruff lint and `git diff --check` passed.

### Tradeoffs and limits

A disposable worker adds startup overhead: small valid previews took 2.63–2.71 seconds in the Docker test. Concurrent-preview throughput has not been benchmarked. Live validation was on Linux/WSL Docker without a GPU or loaded model; browser UI, actual training and supervisor restart behavior were not exercised. This prevents the reported backend shutdown; it does not make the supplied dataset trainable.

author: praetoros
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two confirmed findings from the security audit, both in the Better Auth config.

```diff
 betterAuth({
   basePath: "/auth",
+  disabledPaths: ["/list-sessions"],
   emailAndPassword: {
     enabled: true,
     requireEmailVerification: true,
+    revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset: true,
```

- **Password reset kept old sessions alive.** A completed `/auth/reset-password` changed the password but left every existing session and bearer token valid, so whoever held one kept access after the owner recovered the account.
- **`/auth/list-sessions` returned other sessions' raw tokens.** `bearer()` accepts a raw token as a credential, so one fresh session could copy the account's others and keep access after it was signed out. No client calls this endpoint.

`requireSignature` on `bearer()` would not fix the second issue alone: the native app stores and sends the raw token.

## Evidence

New `apps/api/test/auth-sessions.test.ts`:

```text
reset: auth.$context.options.emailAndPassword.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset === true
list-sessions: GET /auth/list-sessions (Bearer token) -> 404
```

- **Before:** both tests fail (`expected undefined to be true`; list-sessions not 404).
  **After:** both pass. The full API suite passes (216 tests in 29 files), and so do `types:tsc`, `biome:ci` and `vp fmt --check`.

The audit also reproduced both behaviours end to end, in a sandbox running the installed Better Auth 1.7.13 with a memory adapter:

- **Reset:** a pre-reset bearer token returned `VALID` and could still update the user. With the option set, it returned `null` and got 401.
- **list-sessions:** the copied token stayed `VALID` after the original session signed out. With `disabledPaths`, the endpoint returned 404.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Both are config lines and revert cleanly. Sessions revoked by a reset after deploy do not come back on revert, which is the intended effect.

**Blast Radius:** small

- After a password reset, users are signed out on every device and extension, and must sign in again.
- Any external caller of `/auth/list-sessions` gets 404. Nothing in this repository calls it.
- Sessions that leaked before this deploy are not revoked by it.

author: kitokoh
body:
## Probleme

Deux fichiers sans rapport avec le produit vivaient a la **racine de `main`**, et aucun diff API ne les montrait.

**1. `CHANGELOG entry present on main? ==="`** — 150 lignes de la sortie paginee de `man`, ajoutees par `e355952` (#8973).

Le nom est la signature de la panne : une substitution de commande **non quotee** du type `git commit -m "... $(man git-commit)"`. La sortie a ete decoupee en arguments ; un `?`, un `=` et un `"` ont survecu et le shell a cree un fichier dont le **nom** est la question.

**2. `RAPPORT_FINAL_MISSION.md`** — le rapport de session d'un agent (`8802dfb`), commite dans l'arbre de `main`. Un rapport de mission est une piece jointe de conversation, pas un livrable du produit : dans l'historique il devient un fichier que personne ne met a jour et qui contredit le code au bout d'une semaine.

## Pourquoi personne ne l'a vu

La revue porte sur le diff de `api/`. Un fichier ajoute a la racine n'apparait dans aucun diff qu'on regarde, et `git status` reste propre. Il faut une verification dediee — c'est tout l'objet de ce lot.

## Correctif

- Suppression des deux fichiers.
- `dev-hub/tools/check-root-hygiene.sh` : refuse tout fichier racine hors **liste blanche explicite** (30 entrees, chacune justifiee), et signale specifiquement les noms contenant espace / `?` / `=` / `"` / `$` comme residus probables de substitution non quotee.
- Ajouter un fichier racine redevient un choix conscient : il faut l'inscrire dans la liste, dans le meme commit.

## Verification

- La garde **echoue** sur `origin/main`, en nommant les deux fichiers et la cause du nom suspect.
- La garde **passe** sur ce commit : `Racine du depot propre (HEAD) : 0 fichier inattendu.`
- `dev-hub/` n'est pas dans `criticalPattern` de `check-governance.ps1` : aucune entree CHANGELOG requise (verifie).
- Aucun code applicatif touche — `api/` est intact, donc aucune regression possible sur la suite de tests.

## Typage `chore:`

Le job `Check PR/issue governance` exige un `Closes #XXX` pour les PR `fix:`/`feat:`. Cette PR ne ferme aucune issue : c'est de la maintenance d'arbre (deux fichiers parasites + une garde), et inventer une fermeture pour satisfaire le linter serait pire que le linter. Le typage `chore:` est celui que la regle prevoit pour ce cas.

Lite needs a useful view of mesh devices and services without forcing every board to keep every full record in memory. This adds readers and bounded directories for the new signed binary device manifests, including their embedded service descriptions.

Larger devices can retain complete records, while constrained consumers can extract compact endpoint information for browsing and connecting. Certificate storage and record ownership live in RAM with explicit lifetimes, giving later routing and service code a common source of verified information rather than separate overlapping caches.

Depends on [#104](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/wendy-lite/pull/104). This draft targets its prerequisite branch; retarget to `main` after the dependencies merge.

Validation: Combined-stack smoke passed on C5/C6 and four Linux lab devices, including real CLI routing and desktop topology.

body:
Part of #629 — foundation for the worker-record migration (goal-agent decision: **option 2**, Rust owns the Worker record).

## What this does
- Defines the full `swoole::Worker` layout as a `#[repr(C)]` `WorkerRecord` in `crates/process/src/worker_record.rs`, mirrored by `swr_v1_worker_record` in `native/process/swoole_rs_process.h` (every field; pointer/atomic fields are opaque storage, methods stay C++).
- **Locks** `swoole::Worker` to that layout with `static_assert`s in `process.cc`: `sizeof` plus `offsetof` of the migrating fields (pid/id/status/type). A layout drift now fails the build, not the `sw_shm`-backed worker array at runtime — the safety mechanism the decision called for.
- Adds the first accessors (`swr_v1_worker_status`/`_set_status`); later slices convert each scalar field's C++ readers to accessors and delete the field from the header, smallest blast radius first (`status`→`type`→`pid`→`id`).

- `cargo test -p swoole-rs-process` (layout/accessor tests) + `cargo clippy -p swoole-rs-process --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `build_hybrid --module process` compiles with the `static_assert`s holding — i.e. the Rust mirror is byte-exact with the pinned `swoole::Worker` (if it weren't, the build fails).

Part of #629; the claim stays open for the field-migration slices.

author: lonnieezell
body:
Closes #640, #641, #642, #643, #644. Part of #639 (#645 and #646 follow in batch 2).

## What
Each admin can arrange their own dashboard. **Customize** enters edit mode, where they can:
- drag widgets into a new order and into titled sections, managed from each section's ⋯ menu;
- size widgets ¼ / ⅓ / ½ / ⅔ / Full from a floating toolbar or by dragging the card's corner (within each widget's allowed range);
- remove widgets, open a widget's settings, and add others from a slide-in widget library.

Every change can be undone and redone (edit bar, Ctrl/⌘Z, or Undo on the toast). Every edit also works from the keyboard: arrows move the focused card, Shift+←/→ resizes it, Delete removes it. Screen readers hear each change announced. **Save layout** stores the layout for that user only, and **Cancel** restores the page in place. **Reset** restores the default in the editor, and saving a layout that equals the default forgets the user's own.

The UI follows the Dashboard Editor design from Claude Design.

A fresh install's default dashboard is Quick Links, then a **Users** section (Users by Group and Users in Recycler, ½ each), then a **Monitoring** section (Log activity).

## How it plugs in
- **Widget contract and registry:** `Bonfire\Dashboard\DashboardWidget` plus `service('dashboard')`. Modules call `register()` from `initAdmin()`. Existing stats, charts, Log activity and `Dashboard.cells` entries become widgets through adapters (`stats:`, `charts:`, `logs:` and `cell:` ids), so no module changes are needed.
- **Layout resolution:** `LayoutResolver` uses the user's own `Dashboard.layout` (user-scoped setting, v1 JSON format) if there is one. Otherwise it uses the site default: the global `Dashboard.layout`, configured in `Config\Dashboard::$layout`, or the plain cells when that is `null`. `LayoutValidator` checks every layout, stored or posted:
  - wrong shape or version is rejected;
  - unknown, unavailable, unpermitted and duplicate widgets are dropped;
  - sizes are clamped to the widget's range;
  - titles are trimmed to 100 characters;
  - empty sections are dropped, and more than 20 sections is rejected.
- **Endpoint:** `POST admin/dashboard/layout` (JSON), behind the `csrf` filter.
- **Widget settings:** `DashboardWidget::settingsUrl()` links stats, chart and Log activity widgets to their Settings → Widgets tab, for users with `widgets.settings`.
- **Lazy queries:** a stats or chart item runs its query only when it is in the viewer's resolved layout (`DashboardContext::shows()`).
- **Editor:** `themes/Admin/js/dashboard.js` (Alpine + SortableJS 1.15.6 from jsDelivr with SRI).

## Decisions worth a look
- **Widgets settings switches** now mean "available" and are on by default. Being switched on no longer puts a widget on the dashboard: the site default layout decides that. This changes epic stories 2 and 15; see the decision comment on #639.
- **Deleting a section deletes its widgets** (as in the design), and Undo brings them back.
- **No new `<x-dashboard-…>` theme components.** The editor markup lives in `src/Dashboard/Views` so an older published theme can't break rendering.
- **Permission filtering in the registry was pulled forward from #645.** Log activity declares `logs.view`.
- **`CellManager` no longer has any callers.** It's kept because it's public API.

## Upgrade notes (in the changelog, marked breaking)
- Re-publish the Admin theme to get the new `admin/js/dashboard.js` and `admin.css` rules. With an older copy, widgets stack in one column and Customize does nothing.
- The default dashboard is now the configured `Dashboard.layout`. Installs with their own `Config\Dashboard` and no `$layout` property get the plain cells instead.

## Testing
- The dashboard tests check the registry, adapters, resolver, validator, endpoint, per-user isolation, lazy queries, the default layout, palette contents and editor markup hooks. The full suite passes (493 tests), and the 2 deprecations already exist on `develop`.
- `composer style`, `rector` and `inspect` are clean. phpcpd was not run locally.
- **Browser:** I checked the editor by hand in Chrome against a local install (bftest). That covered adding from the library, keyboard move/resize/remove, corner resize, drag to move, the section menu, undo/redo, toast Undo, reset, cancel, save and reload, and reset-then-save forgetting the user's layout. Drag from the library onto a section was not exercised by hand. The editor JS has no automated tests, because the repo has no JS test runner.

body:
## Summary

Implements Plan 14 "Vui học" (Fun learning) — a comprehensive entertainment system featuring a rank quiz game, sticker collections, daily check-ins, and a social explore feed. This is a major feature addition spanning backend services, frontend pages, admin management tools, and database migrations.

## Key Changes

### Backend Services (Java/Spring Boot)
- **Quiz Game System**: `QuizGameService`, `QuizBankService`, `QuizGameSettings`, `QuizRules` — server-side question selection, shuffling, timing, and grading with server-side answer validation
- **Sticker System**: `StickerService`, `StickerTradeService`, `WelcomePackService`, `StickerSettings`, `StickerRules` — sticker collections, trading between friends, rarity tiers (common/rare/epic)
- **Game Currency**: `CoinService`, `FunSettings` — separate "Leo Xu" game currency independent from anyPoint
- **Daily Check-in**: `CheckinService` — streak tracking and daily gift rewards
- **Achievements**: `AchievementService`, `AchievementRules` — shareable achievement banners
- **Explore/Social**: `ExploreService`, `ExploreRules` — posts with photos/clips, likes, comments
- **Access Control**: `FunAccessInterceptor`, `FunAccessRules`, `FunAccessSettings` — feature rollout and access management
- **Referral System**: `ReferralService`, `ReferralRules`, `ReferralEvent` entity — track who invited new users via `/ref/{phone}` links

### Frontend (Next.js/React)
- **Quiz Pages**: `/today/fun/quiz`, `/today/fun/quiz/board` — rank quiz gameplay with helper items (lifelines), leaderboards
- **Sticker Pages**: `/today/fun/sticker` — collection management, trading UI
- **Explore Pages**: `/today/fun/explore` — social feed with posts, comments, shares
- **Coins Page**: `/today/fun/coins` — game currency wallet and transaction history
- **Components**: `Leo` mascot, `FunScene`, `QuestionView`, `ResultView`, `RankCard`, `StarBurst` animations, `ItemShop`, `TradePanel`
- **Utilities**: Quiz rules, sticker rules, referral store, achievement sharing, check-in logic

### Admin Panel (React/antd)
- **Quiz Management**: `QuizGame.jsx`, `QuizBank.jsx` — configure game settings, manage question bank with AI generation matrix

## What this changes

Core 0.9.5 releases the Launcher steps L09 to L12, moved from NFC, together with the two API clean-ups that followed them (#259) and the flatter LogConsole header (#251). NFC and NFH can then pin these packages before 1.0.0. NFC's `core-packages.json` is on `core-v0.5.0` today.

Decisions behind the scope:

- Owner, 2026-10-28: accepted that the focus ring of the two LogConsole header buttons overflows the 32 DIP header by 4 DIP (#251, section "Owner decision on the focus ring"). Commander, 2026-10-28 18:32: 0.9.5 is `main` plus #251.

## Changes

- `Directory.Build.props`: `0.9.4` to `0.9.5`.
- `tools/core-packages/README.md` and `README.zh-TW.md`: the sample package versions use `0.9.5`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`:
  - The `Unreleased` entries move to a `0.9.5 - 2026-10-28` section. The L10 entry (#250) was missing from `main` and is added; its text is the one in the 1.0.0 draft (#234).
  - The section also lists the two API adjustments of #259 under `Changed`: the `VersionManagementExperience` constructor lost `packagePolicy` and `admissionCodec`, and `ManagedSetupRecoveryAction` now has `ConvergeReady = 0` and `RemoveIncompleteInstallation = 1`. Both types are new in 0.9.5 (neither is in the 0.9.4 `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt`), so no 0.9.4 code is affected.
  - The #251 entry moves from `Unreleased` into the 0.9.5 section.
  - The `Nvt.Core.Fonts` 0.1.2 entry stays under `Unreleased`, because Fonts is a separate release line that this version does not publish.
- `ROADMAP.md`: a `0.9.5` row dated 2026-10-28. It stays `Planned` until the tag exists, like 0.9.4 did.
- This branch contains a merge of `main` (`b367bdd`, after #260 and #251 merged). The merge conflicted in `CHANGELOG.md` only, because #251 added its entry to the `Unreleased` list that this pull request restructures.
- No C# change. `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` and `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` do not change.

## What is in the release

Everything on `main` since `core-v0.9.4`:

- Launcher entry and first-install use cases (L09, #243), recovery diagnosis (L10, #250), recovery execution (L11, #255), engine composition and version management (L12, #256 and #257).
- Two clean-ups of unshipped API shapes before the freeze (#259) and one documentation correction (#258).
- The LogConsole header is one 32 DIP row (it was 40 DIP), and the toolbar's zoom group has no border (#251). No public C# API, resource key or token changes.
- The licensing changes already listed in the changelog (SPDX headers, the package `LICENSE`).
- A tools-only change to the codex queue wrapper (#260). It is not part of the packages.

It does not contain Fonts 0.1.2 (a separate release line) or the 1.0.0 draft (#234, which stays a Draft).

## The Unshipped entries are not moved

`docs/core/releasing.md` step 1 and `docs/core/api-inventory.md` say the release moves the approved entries from `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` to `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt`. This release does not. The 673 entries of `Nvt.Core` stay in `Unshipped`. `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` of every published project keeps all of its 0.9.4 entries.

Why: this version is a step before the 1.0.0 freeze. NFC's real Launcher composition has not been built yet, and it may still need a change in the shape of a public type (for example `FileSystemManagedFirstInstallationRootMaterializer.MaterializeAsync`, which returns `SourceChanged` for a payload capture that Core did not produce). Entries in `Shipped` could only be changed by a breaking edit.

What it costs: `.editorconfig` sets RS0016, RS0017, RS0024 and RS0025 to error for the projects that reference the PublicApiAnalyzers, and the analyzers read `Shipped` and `Unshipped` together. So the build still fails when a public member is missing from the two files, when a listed member no longer exists, when a file is invalid, or when a symbol is listed twice. Changing the signature of an entry in `Unshipped` therefore still shows up in the diff. The difference is the baseline:

- A changed `Shipped` entry must be written as a `*REMOVED*` line plus the new line (`docs/core/api-inventory.md`), and the old line stays as the record of the released shape.
- An `Unshipped` line is edited in place, with no marker and no record of the earlier shape. After 0.9.5, only review notices that a shape changed after a version was published. A changed shape needs a new version, because tags and Releases cannot be replaced.

author: humblewriter01
body:
## What this branch is

Two increments, one experiment.

1. `2cb5c3a` built a second Telegram driver on `@mtcute/node`, behind a new `TELEGRAM_DRIVER` switch, with a Postgres storage provider so its `Sqlite`-shaped storage contract could be met.
2. `1cb4f42` **replaces that candidate with `teleproto`** — the maintained fork of GramJS — and retires the parts of increment 1 that only existed to serve mtcute.

The verdict that caused the swap, all of it measured against the installed packages rather than a README:

| | `@mtcute/node` | `teleproto@1.232.0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transport over 443 | no websocket transport in the package at all | `transport: new WebSocketTransport()`, which builds `wss://<ip>:443/apiws` from `globalThis.WebSocket` |
| Session login | `importSession`, ordering-sensitive, needed a translator | `StringSession` is a 36-line diff from GramJS's; loads our stored string and re-saves it **byte-identical** |
| Install cost | pulls `better-sqlite3`, a native build, which fails in this sandbox and would fail a Render preflight | zero native modules, zero install hooks, MIT, `engines.node >=18` |
| Maintenance | active | active: 61 releases since the 2026-07-14 fork, `1.232.0` on 2026-10-22 |
| Touchpoints we use | a rewrite | **35 of 46 present verbatim; only `useWSS` is gone**, and that is the documented migration |

Risks worth naming in the same breath: 423 of the fork's 426 commits are by one author, its root `package.json` has no `test` script, and its CI is docs-only. It is a fork of a package we already trust, not a package we have independently audited.

## What is safe here, and what is not claimed

- **`TELEGRAM_DRIVER` defaults to `gramjs` and `server/services/telegram-adapter.js` is byte-identical to `main`** — this PR touches 0 lines of it, of `index.js`'s code (3 comment lines only), of `db.js`, of `telegram-listener.js`, and of `client/**`. Behavior is unchanged; that is a claim about the deployment, not about the new file.
- **Nothing imports the switch yet.** The four files that talk to Telegram still import the GramJS adapter directly. Making the switch live is deliberately not in this PR: doing it needs either a static `.ts` import (raising the Node floor of the *whole* service, gramjs path included) or adapter injection through four files, and either would be a second unproven change in the deployment that is supposed to be measuring one.
- **The heartbeat rules are untouched.** `pingMay`/`pingMust`/`pingDisconnect` were not re-derived on purpose. The only keep-alive change is vocabulary: the timeout matcher now recognises the fork's `Ping timeout of Ns expired` / `Read timeout of Ns expired` **in addition to** `Error: TIMEOUT`, in its own test file so a future re-swap cannot quietly lose the suppression.

## Gates

| gate | status |
| --- | --- |
| Full server suite on `TELEGRAM_DRIVER=gramjs` | **861 / 861** ✅ |
| Full server suite on `TELEGRAM_DRIVER=teleproto` | **861 / 861** ✅ |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json` and `tsc -p tsconfig.strict.json` | clean in both runs ✅ |
| Client suite | 238 / 238 (unchanged; no client file touched) |
| Adapter parity, 45 operations | ✅ `test/telegram-driver-parity.test.js` — same method, same args, same return value; handler-pair add/remove on two real clients; TL constructor ids equal |
| Session loads in the fork with no re-login | ✅ `test/telegram-session-bridge.test.js` — 3-way byte identity (GramJS class, fork class, our reader) |
| Visible 443 fallback kept | ✅ gramjs keeps `useWSS: true`; teleproto keeps `transport: new WebSocketTransport()`; `test/telegram-adapter.test.js` still pins the flag, and the transport options differ by **exactly one key** |
| **Capture latency < 1 s on live signals, 5–10 in a row; any single capture over 5 s fails the pilot** | ⏳ **not run — needs a Preview environment with a live authorized session.** `scripts/telegram-latency-pilot.mjs` is the harness; it exits 0 only on a pass. No numbers are reported for it in this PR, and there will be none until a real run produces them. |

The pilot also runs the `addEventHandler(NewMessage)` path and `.watch()` side by side in one process, because the fork's [issue #36](https://github.com/teleproto/teleproto/issues/36) reports 10–20 s delays receiving `NewMessage` from some large channels and the maintainer's answer is to use `.watch()`. We will not depend on either path until the comparison has run against the channels this workspace actually monitors.

## Rollback

`TELEGRAM_DRIVER=gramjs` on the environment, no redeploy of code. Because the GramJS file is untouched, that is the same string of characters that is running today.

## Merge condition

Do not merge to `main` until the latency gate above has passed on Preview with live signals, with the numbers reported. Merging this PR as-is would still be safe-but-pointless: the switch is not consulted by any running file.

author: luqman-v1
body:
Closes #768.

## The bug

A custom `openai-compatible` node pointed at `https://developer.amd.com.cn/radeon/api/v1` received the POST at that exact path, and the upstream answered 404. The issue's own log line names the lane the gateway dialled:

```
forward to https://developer.amd.com.cn/radeon/api/v1: upstream returned 404
```

Reproduced live against the host in the report:

```
POST https://developer.amd.com.cn/radeon/api/v1                  -> 307
POST https://developer.amd.com.cn/radeon/api/v1/chat/completions -> 401
GET  https://developer.amd.com.cn/radeon/api/v1/models           -> 401
```

The route exists and only the key is missing, so `/chat/completions` is the lane that answers.

## Why it happened

`chatCompletionsURL` completes a configured endpoint to a chat route, and it deliberately leaves a multi-segment path alone: that is correct for the Ollama Local host field, an endpoint the operator typed. A node's `baseUrl` is a **prefix** by contract — upstream appends the lane unconditionally (`open-sse/executors/base.js` `buildUrl`: `` `${normalized}${path}` ``, path chosen by `resolveOpenAICompatibleApiType`). The two shapes need two rules, and only one existed.

## The fix

`compatibleNodeLaneURL` completes a node's base URL by the node's own contract, and the shared helper keeps its shape rule for registry and Ollama Local overrides:

- `anthropic-compatible-*` -> `/messages`
- `openai-compatible-*` -> `/responses` when its stored `apiType` is `responses`, else `/chat/completions`
- `custom-embedding-*` -> `/chat/completions`, deliberately: the embeddings handler derives its own URL from this one (`buildEmbeddingsURL` swaps `/chat/completions` for `/embeddings`), so giving it an `/embeddings` lane here appended it twice — `/proxy/v1/embeddings/embeddings`. Caught and corrected before this PR left draft.

A base URL that already names a lane is used as-is, and a bare host or a `/v1` root resolves exactly as it did before, so a node that already worked keeps its URL. Both config branches use it — the connection's `providerSpecificData.baseUrl` and the node row's `baseUrl` fallback each carried their own copy of the completion.

## Verification

`go test ./internal/handlers/chat/ ./internal/handlers/media/ ./internal/proxy/... ./internal/handlers/dashboard/` green.

The new `compatible_node_lane_test.go` covers the URL mapping across all three node shapes and both `apiType` lanes, the resolution through `getProviderConfig` on both branches, and a request through the real handler whose fake upstream asserts the path it was dialled on.

Replayed on the pre-fix tree, the end-to-end case fails with the reported symptom:

```
upstream saw path "/radeon/api/v1", want "/radeon/api/v1/chat/completions"
```

and passes after. The anthropic-compatible lane was checked the same way, on both a bare-prefix and an already-full stored URL.

`go test ./internal/handlers/ ./web/...` fails 15 times on both trees identically — the `web/dist` placeholder this worktree carries has no `/sw.js`, no `/manifest.webmanifest` and no pre-compressed siblings. Pre-existing, not this diff; CI builds the real SPA.

`.changes/768-compatible-node-baseurl-lane.md` added. `CHANGELOG.md` untouched.

## What changes
- `StealthSettingsStore`: per-account switches (typing, read marks, media open, online, story views, risk warnings) and per-chat exceptions (Inherit / Allow / Block). One SharedPreferences file per account, synchronous `commit()`. Unreadable data while protection was on (or with no readable "off" flag) fails closed: every signal is refused. A failed write still enforces a stricter value in memory, never a looser one.
- `StealthInteractionPolicy` is now the default policy of both the legacy and secondary repositories. The store is created before the repository, so it applies from the first authorization. The online status stays account-wide; chat exceptions never touch it.
- `TdConversationEffects`: `ViewMessages` is decided and sent under one lock on every attempt (also on retry). A policy change stops typing indicators right away. New `markRead(consent)` and `contentOpenedWithConsent` (for view-once, package C).

author: thombles
body:
A user's CLI can join Wendy Net under its own operator identity and participate in routing alongside enrolled devices. Each installation gets an independent, stable router identity and address, allowing multiple installations or operator profiles to coexist without impersonating a device or colliding with another router.

Operator certificates now authorize ordinary mesh origins and authenticated application and management connections. Certificate lookup is tied to the exact signer, and bounded output handling prevents one slow connection from blocking shared routing work. This extends the full-router design adapted from Joannis's [#2466](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/WendyOS/pull/2466) with operator identities and the current binary protocol.

Depends on [#2578](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/WendyOS/pull/2578), [#2577](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/WendyOS/pull/2577). This draft targets its prerequisite branch; retarget to `main` after the dependencies merge.

author: calgooon
body:
Closes #374 (the CLI's reading of 2026-10-28 on the published 0.14.0-beta.2: a forged signature and a field above the 1 MiB bound were stored as given).

**What moves.** Between the direct acquire's argument checks (#311) and the store, the wallet builds bsv-rs's `MasterCertificate` from the normalized arguments, refuses when `verify()` is false, then proves the keyring with `MasterCertificate::decrypt_fields(self, ...)` as the reference does at `Wallet.ts:705-728` (edf6e03). The stored row is unchanged: the encrypted fields and the keyring as they came. The decryption is a proof, not a transformation.

**The refusal** is the reference's `WERR_INVALID_PARAMETER('args', ...)` in the port's form: `Validation error: The args parameter must be valid encrypted and signed certificate and keyring from revealer. <name>: <message>`. A false signature ends in `WERR_UNKNOWN: Certificate verification failed` (the reference's own words); an undecryptable keyring in `CertificateValidationError: Failed to decrypt all master certificate fields.` (bsv-rs's error name where the reference has a JavaScript one: the divergence is named in the CHANGELOG line and `src/wallet/CLAUDE.md`). bsv-rs's `to_binary` bounds (a field over 1 MiB, a signature over 72 bytes) travel with the verify step.

**Tests.** Red on base: a forged signature, an undecryptable keyring and a 1,048,577-byte field (3 of 3 red on ff0444b); a positive case the test signs itself with a keyring built for the test wallet's identity key (`MasterCertificate::issue_for_subject`). Plants: the `verify()` check removed and the decrypt step removed, each red on its test; restored. The busy-door fixture (a placeholder-signed certificate, outside the lane's bounds) now takes the signed arguments; the captain applied the lane's proposed change and ran the library gate (fourth commit).

**Sequencing.** PR #407 (typed refusals at the boundary) touches `direct_acquire_tests.rs` too: when it lands, this branch rebases onto it and the new refusal travels as `WalletRefusal { class: InvalidParameter, .. }` with the same text; the cold review reads the rebased tip.

Gates on the lane's tree rebased onto ff0444b: fmt, both clippy runs, `cargo test --lib` 1,425 passed, fixtures 29, storage wire 42, network isolation 11, ratchet green, arch-doc 321 rows 0 failed.

Lane report: `/Volumes/Lanes/out/bsv-wallet-toolbox-rs/p1-374-direct-acquire-verify/` (studio).

body:
## Summary

Steps 1, 2 and 4 of the UI revamp plan (`docs/plans/ui-revamp.md`), plus the tempo-first Library pages from the mockups. Mostly frontend; one small additive backend change.

- **Navigation (step 1):** the sidebar and mobile menu are grouped by intent: **Play** (Home, Run, Listen), **Library**, **Maintain** (BPM Review, Duplicates, Stats), **System**. Same routes and icons.
- **Home (step 2):** a new `/home` page and the new landing page. A card per run preset with its ready count that opens Run already set to it (`/run?bpm=N`), a Custom card, a **Needs attention** list (review count, decode problems, a running scan) that hides when empty, and a scan prompt for an empty library. The last-page restore and the PWA `start_url` (`/run`) are unchanged; the player kiosk is untouched.
- **Library Tracks:** a **Tempo strip** (the library's BPM histogram with the current window lit; click a bar, tap a run preset, or type a BPM) replaces the loose BPM/± inputs, using the same `bpm` / `bpm_tol` / `bpm_cadence` URL params. The table drops the detector column and the "ok" badge, shows a dash for zero plays, and reveals queue / play-next / add-to-playlist on hover. Four filters stay on the toolbar; the rest are under **More filters**.
- **Artists:** a per-artist tempo mix, "N of M" fit counts, the shared strip, a sort menu and an A–Z rail.
- **Albums:** a cover grid with "N of M fit" / "N half-time" badges and a fit bar, the shared strip, a fit filter and a sort menu.
- The tempo filter follows you between Tracks, Artists and Albums (`LibraryTabs`).

## Backend

`GET /api/artists` gains `mix` and `mix_range`, and `GET /api/artists` / `GET /api/albums` accept `bpm`, `bpm_tol`, `bpm_cadence` and then add `fit` (and `fit_folded` for albums). Existing fields are unchanged. The window rule is one shared helper (`bpm_in_window`) with tests asserting it agrees with the track listing's SQL filter.

## Also fixed

- The Plays and Rating cells were in the opposite order to their headers.
- On phones the rating cell's inline `display:flex` beat the rule that hides it, wrapping the status onto a second line.

## Not in this PR

Plan steps 3 (readiness on Run, Home v1), 5 (Settings regroup) and 6 (merge Run and Listen); the Artists/Albums mockups' per-row play and shuffle buttons; Albums' "Has starred" / "Needs review" chips. The optional detector toggle from step 4 is not built; the column is simply removed (it's on the track page).

author: blakehastings
body:
Closes #637

Two `add_book` calls for one ISBN at the same moment now add one book: the second answers the first's with `added: false`. `POST /api/books` still adds a second copy, which is what it did before and what the review pane tells the person it will do. No migration, no unique index, no response shape changed.

## What changed

- **`isbn:<isbn13>` lock**, built by `isbnLock` in `web/application/locks.ts` from the resolved thirteen digit form, so `0441013597` and `9780441013593` are one lock. A value that is no ISBN gets none (`null`).
- **`LOCK_ORDER` is now `isbn:`, `book:`, `shelf:`, `furniture`.** `isbn:` is first because a new book has no id until its row is written, so the number is the only thing two saves of it can meet on. It is also known before anything is read, so it can always be taken at the start. The refusal message now says "the order is isbn, book, shelf, furniture".
- **`CatalogueBookHandler` takes `isbn:` for any book carrying an ISBN, whoever the caller.** It is named in the unit of work's opening locks beside `book:<scanId>`, never mid-work. A book with no ISBN takes no `isbn:` lock.
- **`CatalogueBook.ifCatalogued: 'add-a-copy' | 'answer-it'`**, required and not defaulted (the `theAreaGoes` precedent: a caller that says nothing is a caller nobody asked). With `'answer-it'` the handler's first statement under the lock is `BookRepository.cataloguedWith(isbn13)`, which runs the same `catalogued_books` predicate as `findByIsbn`. If it finds a book, the handler writes nothing, starts no background work and answers `{ added: false, id }`. Overloads type a `'add-a-copy'` caller's answer as `Catalogued`, so the route needs no narrowing.
- `add_book` passes `'answer-it'` and answers `added: false, record_from: 'existing'` from either check. It keeps the lookup's early check, which spares a save when the book is already there. `POST /api/books`, `seed-world.ts` and `testBooks` pass `'add-a-copy'`.

## What POST /api/books does on a duplicate, before and after

**Before:** it adds a second copy. The route has no duplicate check. The client's review pane draws a quiet card titled "Saving adds a second copy" (`web/src/components/BookFields.tsx`, with the comment "this is a thing to know, not a refusal, since saving a genuine second copy is allowed").
**After:** the same, stated explicitly as `'add-a-copy'`. The test "still adds a second copy of an ISBN already catalogued, at once or one after the other" covers it: two concurrent POSTs plus a third by the ISBN-10 form give three distinct ids.

The route still takes the `isbn:` lock. It only waits for a concurrent save of the same number, and it means an `add_book` asking at the same moment sees the app's book once it has committed, rather than adding past it.

## The confirm path (scanId)

**`isbn:` is taken first in both paths.** A save out of the queue asks for `[isbn:<n>, book:<scanId>]` at the start, and `PgDb` takes them in `LOCK_ORDER`. Taking `isbn:` mid-work, behind `book:`, would be refused by the order check. The test "waits for whoever holds its number, a save out of the queue as well as a new one" holds `isbn:9780441013593` in another unit of work while a queued scan is confirmed. It sees `['number held', 'number let go', 'catalogued']`, not a refusal. A queued scan of the number is not "catalogued" (it is in `queued_books`, not `catalogued_books`), so it never counts as a duplicate of itself. The test "does not count a scan of the number still in the queue as catalogued" covers that.

**The capture queue's duplicate warning is untouched.** `CaptureQueue` still asks `Store.findByIsbn` and warns. Nothing on that path changed.

## Functionality

Not driven under Aspire. The evidence is the real `createApp` over HTTP and MCP against a scratch Postgres, in `write-tools.routes.test.ts`:

- **The race test flipped** to "is serialised: two adds of one ISBN racing past the lookup add it once (#637)". Both lookups are held until both calls arrive, as before. Now one call answers `added: true`, the other `added: false, record_from: 'existing'`, both carry the same `book_id`, and there is 1 book.
- **New:** "answers the book the app saved after its lookup and before its save". A spy on `findByIsbn` lets the lookup's check find nothing and then fires a real `POST /api/books` before `add_book` reaches the handler. `add_book` answers the app's book, and the count is 1.
- **New:** the `POST /api/books` second-copy test above.

Handler tests in `web/infrastructure/books/save-commands.test.ts` (+6): answers an existing book found by its ISBN-10 and writes, tags and starts nothing; `'add-a-copy'` adds a second; a queued scan is not a duplicate; two concurrent `'answer-it'` saves give `[false, true]` with one id and 1 row; waits on a held number in the confirm path; locks the 13-digit form for a 10-digit input and asks for no lock for an ISBN-less book or a non-ISBN string. That last one is read from a recording `UnitOfWork`.

`web/application/locks.test.ts` (+3): one lock for both forms and none for a non-number; `isbn:` sorts before `book:`, `shelf:` and `furniture`; taking `isbn:` while holding a book, a range or the furniture is refused, with the message quoted.

### Reverted, in the runner's words

With the lock removed (`const locks = [null, scanId …]`), the in-handler check still in place:

```
× a book whose ISBN is already catalogued (#637) > two saves of one ISBN at once take turns, so the second finds the first
  → expected [ true, true ] to deeply equal [ false, true ]
× a book whose ISBN is already catalogued (#637) > waits for whoever holds its number, a save out of the queue as well as a new one
  → expected [ 'number held', 'catalogued', …(1) ] to deeply equal [ Array(3) ]
× a book whose ISBN is already catalogued (#637) > locks the thirteen digit form of a number typed as ten, and no number for a book without one
  → expected [ undefined, undefined, undefined ] to deeply equal [ [ 'isbn:9780441013593' ], …(2) ]
× add_book > is serialised: two adds of one ISBN racing past the lookup add it once (#637)
  → expected [ true, true ] to deeply equal [ false, true ]
Tests  4 failed | 37 passed (41)
```

With the lock in place and the in-handler check disabled:

```
× a book whose ISBN is already catalogued (#637) > answers that book, writing and starting nothing, when the caller asks to be answered
  → expected { added: true, id: 2, …(2) } to deeply equal { added: false, id: 1 }
× a book whose ISBN is already catalogued (#637) > two saves of one ISBN at once take turns, so the second finds the first
  → expected [ true, true ] to deeply equal [ false, true ]
× add_book > is serialised: two adds of one ISBN racing past the lookup add it once (#637)
  → expected [ true, true ] to deeply equal [ false, true ]
× add_book > answers the book the app saved after its lookup and before its save
  → expected { added: true, …(4) } to match object { added: false, …(1) }
Tests  4 failed | 37 passed (41)
```

The "app saved in the gap" test passes with the lock removed, because that save has committed before `add_book` asks. It proves the check and not the lock. The two race tests prove the lock.

**Suite:** 3214 tests in 167 files before (master `7abd4e4`), 3225 in 167 after: +3 locks, +6 handler, +2 route, and the race test changed in place. None removed. `npm run typecheck`, `tsc -p tsconfig.domain.json` and `npm run lint:layers` (518 modules, 2653 dependencies, no violations) are clean.

## Code

- `web/application/locks.ts`: `isbnLock`, `LOCK_ORDER` with `isbn:` first, and the reason in its comment.
- `web/application/books/ports.ts` + `web/infrastructure/books/book-repository.ts`: `BookRepository.cataloguedWith(isbn13)`. It sits on the repository rather than the read model because a command must not read through a read model, and the read must run on the unit of work's transaction.
- `web/application/books/commands/catalogue-book.ts`: the lock, the check, `IfCatalogued`, `AlreadyCatalogu

body:
## Phase / module

Phase: `4` · Step: `4.1b orders-refund` (refunds: the orders and stock side, and the per-product refund settings) · Branch: `phase-4/orders-refund`

## What this PR builds

Refunds on Ramin's answer to R-C (2026-10-28): the admin decides per product, the till does not. Catalog gains two settings per item, `refundable` and `refund_restock`, set on `POST` and `PATCH /items` (a migration with a one-time backfill: products sold from stock or bought in go back into stock, products made to order do not, ingredients are not refundable). `refund_restock = true` is refused where nothing can go back into stock (`422 catalog.item.restock_not_stocked`). `Catalog\Contracts\RefundPolicy::for(ids)` is how Orders reads them; Orders reads no Catalog table for this.

`Orders::refund(orderId, reason, approver, lines, clientUuid)` is the stock and order side that step 4.3d's `Payments::refund` and its endpoint will call:
- each refunded line takes its disposition from its product's settings at that moment: `restock` writes one reversing `return` per movement of the product itself, through `Inventory\Contracts\Reversals` (M6 `stock_movement_reversals`, unique on the original), inside the Ledger with its lock order and shift rule; `waste` writes nothing;
- the money back is the lines' `line_total`;
- M7 `order_refunds` and `order_refund_lines` (append-only, the disposition kept as written), M8 `refunded_total` and `refunded_at`, and a new migration for the refund half of M9;
- `line.refunded` and `order.refunded` go on the timeline, `OrderRefunded` follows the commit (Analytics touches the refund's day), `Orders::totals` adds `refunded` and `net_paid`, and `OrderResource` adds `refunded_total` and `refunds`;
- `OrderStatus` does not change: a refunded order stays `closed`.

## Dependencies proven first

- [x] Contract tests committed red before the provider and consumer code (02b8eac): `payments->orders` cases 5 to 9, 11 and 13 rewritten for the rule, plus three cases of it; `orders->inventory` cases 13 to 15; one `orders->catalog` case for `RefundPolicy`
- [ ] `gate_check.py --mode entry`: not re-run in this step (phase 4 is in progress; the entry gate's red line was `analytics->facts`, green since 4.1c)

## Tests added

- Feature: `RefundOrderTest` (whole and partial refunds, the timeline, replay, the 72 h window, R-D, `refunded_total <= paid_total`, each line once, a station-made stocked product, the fallback to waste, a deleted product, the PIN rules), `ItemRefundSettingsTest` (defaults, validation, the restock refusal, audit, the backfill)
- Schema: `OrderRefundsSchemaTest`, `StockMovementReversalsSchemaTest`; `OrdersSchemaTest`, `CatalogSchemaTest` and `AppendOnlyTest` extended
- Property: `orders->inventory` case 15 (50 seeded sale and reversal steps, with the ledger oracle after each)
- Playwright: none (the refund screens are a later step)
- Registries: no new route in this step (the endpoint is 4.3d)

## Invariants

- [x] NUMERIC scales (12,2 money / 14,4 qty), no floats
- [x] `branch_id`, actor stamp, append-only triggers on the three new tables
- [x] bilingual `_en` / `_am` on every new refusal
- [ ] `make ci`: CI is the gate; the touched files were run locally in Docker

## Decisions and assumptions

ADR 0016 (refunds, voids and the cash drawer) is updated with Ramin's rule and stays `proposed` until 4.3d. The plan's As built note of 4.1b lists the decisions the brief left open.

## Gate impact

- `payment_refunds.order_refund_id` gets its foreign key. The live table has no row yet: it is written from 4.3d.
- The test helpers that wrote payment_refunds rows with a made-up `order_refund_id` now point at real `order_refunds` rows.
- Phase 1 state machines are unchanged, and `VoidOrderTest` still refuses a paid order.

author: peacock0803sz
body:
Closes #139

## Summary
- A new switch, `appIconBadges`, off by default and shared by both switchers. It lives in the config file (`ConfigSchema.pkl`, `config-schema.json`) and in the Panel section of the Appearance tab.
- With it on, each panel appearance reads the Dock's application tiles over the accessibility API (`AXStatusLabel`, `AXURL`) just before the panel goes up, and draws each app's badge at the top corner of the icon on every row of that app: window rows, rows of apps without windows, and rows in subgroups alike. The badges stay as they were when the panel opened; changes show on the next opening.
- The read runs inside the press-to-panel time with a 32 ms deadline, shrunk to what is left of the 100 ms budget (an appearance shown after the show delay gets the whole deadline). Messaging timeouts are per element, so each element is given the remaining time right before it is asked. A read that runs out of time or fails draws no badges at all rather than a partial set.
- Counts above 999 read `999+`; wording is cut short to stay beside the icon; a blank label draws a dot. Copies of one app launched from the same place get no badge, since nothing on a Dock tile says which copy it is.
- The panel line gains `badges` (`read` / `late` / `failed` / `noDock`) and `badgeMs` columns when the switch is on. A Dock that cannot be read gets one warning line per changed reason. With the switch off, the line is unchanged.
- The settings preview shows a fixed example, and `--sample-count` uses a fixed table instead of the live Dock.
- The usage and features pages (en/ja) describe the switch.

## Motivation
People who hide the Dock or switch without looking at it could not tell from the list which apps had something waiting. Contexts offers the same option (App icon badges). Part of #77; like its siblings it sits behind a switch that is off by default.

No new permission is needed: the badges are read with the Accessibility permission Lanterna already has.

## Behavior change
None unless the switch is turned on.

## Testing

- [x] `bash scripts/test.sh` passes (1664 tests)
- [x] Checked by hand on a debug build (if the change is visible to users)
- Before implementing, a spike on macOS 27.2 (26B123) with a positive-control app that sets its own `dockTile.badgeLabel` confirmed the labels read back as set, that no other permission prompt appears, the read time (p95 about 16 ms with reads 1 s apart), and that a 20 ms timeout returns within 25 ms against a Dock stopped with `SIGSTOP`.
- By hand: badges on Slack/Discord and a control app, `1234` and long wording at all five text sizes, all rows of one app and subgroups, All displays, the parallel switcher, a stopped Dock (`late`, panel not held up), `killall Dock`, the config key absent and invalid, and `--sample-count`. Not checked on the macOS 26 minimum.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: everything passes except `pinact`, which fails because pinact v5 rejects the `-fix=false` flag; this branch does not touch its config.

author: vvchldmsdn
body:
The original service and beta were deployed from separate release branches, allowing production behavior to diverge from master and duplicated backend code. This integrates the released features into current master and makes both frontends use its canonical tenant, ledger, lifecycle, financial and research paths.

Includes balance-photo onboarding and first-day analysis, trade-photo import, equal-condition ratio/MA120/FX contribution comparisons, and saved contribution effects linked to actual trades. Shared Cairn UI primitives now cover standalone screens and legacy forms. Unknown historical foreign-currency cost remains unavailable rather than being recalculated from current FX. Existing trade and cash records are preserved; this PR applies no production data repairs.

Registers four already deployed writers in the approved audit inventory without changing production grants or login policy. Removes unused backend source copies; preserves historical beta test files in the release branch and local worktree, with 39 beta-specific saved-plan/session tests included in the canonical suite. Fixes heatmap cell hit areas after shared-button adoption and aligns disposable integration rehearsals with deployed instrument-catalog DDL.

Validation:
- Local canonical suite: 3,259 tests passed, zero failures and process exit 0.
- Final-head GitHub CI passed all five gates: unit tests, production build, lint/type, PostgreSQL integration and browser journeys.
- Real Next production-build browser journeys cover fractional execution/cash separation, duplicate-save recovery, historical corrections, heatmap selection, target editing, and Korean/English desktop/mobile contribution flows.
- Shared-domain manifests, shared UI consumers and close-gap synthetic regressions passed.
- Desktop/mobile original and beta design-fixture rendering checked. Live production verification follows deployment.

Release switches /beta and /cairn-v2 to the same verified master deployment after Ready, retaining the beta-assets compatibility route, existing protection, separate aliases and cron schedules.

author: juwan-hwang
body:
## **User description** Scan for short-id keys directly instead of running the regex engine over subscription bodies, with the same edge-case fixes carried over from the earlier rounds. Round 20 changes: - Block scalar headers after an anchor of any length are now recognised: the 256-character name walk stays bounded for general node tracking, but header recognition uses an unbounded walk, since each header lookup covers only its own token and stays linear. Missing the header rewrote literal block content, which is worse than the benign miss the bound was kept for. - A quote directly after the colon of a quoted key now starts the value in flow context (`{"note":"x, short-id: 34010e92"}`): the colon closes a quoted key, so the quoted text is a value, not scalar key text. Over-accepting here only ever skips text, while missing a real quoted value let its content be rewritten. Both quoted-key cases join the parse-equivalence corpus. - Continuation values may start with an anchor: `short-id:\n &a 34010e92` and the anchor-alone form `short-id:\n &a\n 34010e92` are now quoted, in block and flow context alike; an anchor before an alias is still left alone, as inline. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** **Quote short-id values safely across YAML formats and speed up large subscription imports** ### What Changed - Quotes unquoted `short-id` values in inline, flow, sequence, and indented continuation forms, including values after anchors. - Leaves comments, quoted text, aliases, tags, block scalars, nested mappings, and multiword values unchanged. - Speeds up processing of large subscriptions by scanning for `short-id` keys directly. ### Impact `✅ Fewer short-id parsing errors` `✅ Preserved YAML comments and block-scalar content` `✅ Faster processing of large subscriptions`

author: ischarles
body:
## Why
Ardor stores one instant per calendar entry (`dueAt`) and has no duration column, so nothing in the product could answer "does 14:00 clash with what I already have?" or "when am I actually free?". The agent therefore invented alternative times instead of offering a real slot, which cost it the scheduling cases in the same-model comparison against Claude Code.

## Changes
- `CalendarAvailabilityTypes`: `BusyItem`, `Slot` and `Window` value records for the availability result.
- `CalendarTaskService.findFreeSlots(...)` and `conflictsFor(...)`: read-only, scoped to the calling user's own entries, with an explicit `assumedEventMinutes` because durations are not stored. Entries that start before the window but still overlap it are counted; `COMPLETED`/`CANCELLED` entries and `excludeTaskId` (so an update can ignore itself) are not. Window order, positive durations and a 31-day cap are validated instead of guessing.
- Two new READ tools, `find_available_slots` and `check_calendar_conflict`, registered under `ToolModule.CALENDAR`, plus a `create_calendar_task` description that tells the model to check conflicts first. No approval flow, no writes: the user still confirms a created entry in the UI.

## Verified
- `CalendarAvailabilityTests` (7): free slots around a fixed series, the 组会-collision regression, completed/cancelled entries not blocking, self-exclusion, ownership, validation, window-edge clamping.
- `ModularAgentToolsTests` 24/24 with the two new tools in the pinned catalogue; full backend suite `Tests run: 945` with the earlier single failure resolved.
- Not yet run against a live model: whether the agent actually calls the new tools in the comparison tasks. That needs the post-cache re-run.

author: thombles
body:
Lite can now combine authenticated device information, route selection and update propagation into an ordinary Wendy Net node. Capable devices can forward traffic and full records; constrained single-carrier devices can use their authenticated neighbour as their gateway while retaining the endpoint information they need.

This joins signed manifests, Babel and bounded gossip into one session model. Service and routing updates share the complete manifest, changes coalesce, and a route is not exported before its signed proof is available. Received records and certificate state stay within bounded RAM ownership, so ordinary mesh activity does not depend on writing peers' changing data to flash.

Depends on [#107](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/wendy-lite/pull/107), [#106](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/wendy-lite/pull/106), [#102](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/wendy-lite/pull/102), [#103](https://github.com/wendylabsinc/wendy-lite/pull/103). This draft targets its prerequisite branch; retarget to `main` after the dependencies merge.

Validation: Combined-stack smoke passed on C5/C6 and four Linux lab devices, including real CLI routing and desktop topology.

author: clawd20130
body:
WeChat may sign with a new platform certificate while the previous certificate is still valid. Single-PEM verification cannot handle that overlap. This adds exact `Wechatpay-Serial` selection for asynchronous notification and API-response verification, plus explicitly configured `PUB_KEY_ID_*` RSA public keys.

- Parse certificate serials and validity with Swift Certificates, retain unexpired old certificates during rotation, and share unknown-serial refreshes with a cooldown. Failed downloads or persistence keep existing valid certificates. Unknown public-key IDs fail without fetching certificates.
- Keep certificate bootstrap inside a fixed HTTPS certificate downloader. Authenticate AES-GCM entries, check X.509 serial/validity metadata, and verify the original response signature. Persist/reverify the original encrypted envelope rather than trusting arbitrary cached PEM files.
- Require all four single signature headers on ordinary API responses. Preserve existing public constructors and synchronous verification APIs; the new asynchronous notification method supports rotation. Handle malformed RSA input without force-unwrapping, and remove request-body printing.
- Reject non-decimal/overflowing or stale/future timestamps before any key lookup, using an injected clock and a strict five-minute window. Decrypt notification resources with redacted typed errors rather than force-unwrapping remote input. Remove the new PEM-list persistence hook; cache only authenticated encrypted envelopes. The legacy synchronous verifier is deprecated, and configured public keys explicitly require SPKI PEM.

[API and integration guidance](https://github.com/clawd20130/wechatpay-swift/blob/f6a720dafee72910518a0eaadeb6769b9cc3b698/PlatformCertificates.md) explains merchant scoping, refresh, cache trust, and public-key-only/hybrid configurations. The committed PEM files are generated offline test fixtures only; `.gitignore` exceptions name those exact fixtures.

Validation: `swift test --filter PlatformCertificateTests` passed **32 tests**, including real A/B RSA signatures, old/new coexistence, forgery and unknown IDs, validity, strict headers, concurrent refresh/failure behavior, encrypted-cache reload, expired cache signer, pure public-key/hybrid verification, authenticated certificate bootstrap, strict timestamp rejection before key lookup, the ±300-second boundary, cooldown expiry, the public notification entry, and typed malformed-resource failures. These tests use injected transport and generated keys; no live merchant API or transaction was exercised.

Compatibility: the package manifest declares Swift tools **5.8** and adds Swift Certificates **1.6.1**. The 17 public dependency pins used for validation include tools **5.9** requirements. The actual test run used **Swift 6.1.3 on Linux x86_64**; the minimum toolchain and other platforms were not tested. The older full test suite requires merchant environment configuration and was not run. No Actions workflows currently exist in the upstream repository, and this PR does not add one.

This is a draft for review; it does not publish a release or tag.

author: jstet
body:
Two fixes to how the imported questionnaires look in qwac.

### 1. Rating scales as grids, not sections

qwac showed ATTARI-12 (and the other scales) as separate single-choice questions instead of a matrix. The cause is my survey-import plan: it told agents to use `appearance: field-list` for item batteries, which formtransform emits as `varGrp type="section"`. `table-list` makes `type="grid"`.

This switches every group whose rows are all `select_one` on one shared list to `table-list`:

| Study | Grids |
|---|---|
| ATTARI-12, MAILS, SNAIL, GAAIS, TEI | 1 each (the whole scale) |
| EU ICT 2025 AI module | E1, E2, E3, E5 |
| CVTS7 | F2.3, F2.8, F3.3, F3.3 Anteil, F3.7, F5.1, F5.2, F6, F7.2 |
| EU AES 2022 | NFE activity types |

TEI's instruction note moved before its group so the group holds only items. Groups with mixed types stay sections. PLAN.md now says `table-list`; the ICT `gen-form.mjs` gets the license prefix that had been added to its `form.json` by hand.

### 2. CVTS7 table rows keep only their printed label

The CVTS7 transcription glued question text, row label and sometimes column into one label with " — " (e.g. "Wie viele … insgesamt? — Beschäftigte am 31.12.2025 insgesamt"), a string the questionnaire never prints. Now (29 items):
- each row's label is its printed row label;
- the question text above a table and the "davon: Geschlecht (nach Geburtenregister)" sub-heading are note rows, so formtransform puts them in the next row's `preQTxt`;
- column headings (Anzahl, Personen / Teilnehmenden-Fälle, …) go to the hint;
- amount boxes on "Ja" take the printed "Falls „Ja“ …" line (3.6) or their category text (4.6).

Known gap: a note only reaches the first row after it, so e.g. "Weiblich" has no stem. A numeric table/section text for all rows would need formtransform support.

Unrelated to this PR but found alongside: concepts equal to the question text are tracked in CorrelAid/formtransform#173 (make `concept` optional) and CorrelAid/qwac#68 (hide it).

Checks: all 8 codebooks rebuilt (round trip keeps every row), valid against the pinned schematron worker v0.7.1; `go test ./...` passes.

body:
Milestone: M2/M3 (built-in value semantics across GLSL, HLSL, Metal and SPIR-V; fail closed instead of emitting `gl_` names as user varyings).

Follows #3508 (built-in name registry). Four commits:

- **Stage and direction validity** (`semantics/builtin_stages.py`): a `gl_` built-in used in a stage or direction GLSL 4.60 section 7.1 does not declare it for is refused with a typed diagnostic, keeping the CrossGL conventions (vertex/fragment input `gl_Position`, fragment input `gl_PointSize`/`gl_FragColor`/`gl_FragData`/`gl_SampleMask`).
- **SPIR-V** (`codegen/spirv_extension_builtins.py`): maps HelperInvocation, FullyCoveredEXT, AMD barycentrics, DeviceIndex, NV shader-SM built-ins and BaryCoordNV->KHR with their capabilities and extensions; any other `gl_` value at the user-location path is refused.
- **HLSL** (`codegen/hlsl_extension_builtins.py`): `gl_SampleID`->`SV_SampleIndex`, NV barycentrics->`SV_Barycentrics`, shading rates->`uint SV_ShadingRate`, fragment subgroup/helper/sample-count reads->intrinsics; remaining `gl_` semantics are refused instead of emitted as `: gl_X`.
- **GLSL** (`codegen/glsl_stage_builtin_members.py`): vertex/tess-eval `gl_Layer`/`gl_ViewportIndex` outputs write the built-ins and require `GL_ARB_shader_viewport_layer_array`; fragment input-struct members read every fragment built-in; NV per-view and other unmapped vertex outputs are refused.

Measured delta (probe of every known `gl_` built-in in each stage/direction through each generator):
- built-ins silently emitted as user varyings: 523 -> 98 (stage validity), Vulkan 37 -> 0, HLSL 50 -> 0 (19 mapped, all DXC-valid; 31 refused), GLSL 46 -> 1 (the CrossGL `gl_PointSize` member convention);
- glslang compile failures of the GLSL probe outputs: 43 -> 0.

Tests: new `tests/test_translator/test_builtin_stages.py`, `test_spirv_extension_builtins.py` (spirv-val), `test_hlsl_extension_builtins.py` (DXC when available), `test_glsl_stage_builtin_members.py` (glslang when available). Tier 1 locally (`tests/test_translator tests/test_backend`): 40768 passed; `tests/coverage`: 577 passed after rebasing on #3507.

author: medboy224
body:
## Constat (WP-B.8, point 6)

Lors des essais réels, la fin d'un transfert repris attendait **5 à 8 s après 100 %** sur le téléphone.

En fin de transfert, le récepteur demande l'empreinte du fichier (`DIGEST`, le hash des hash de chunks). L'envoyeur garde le hash des chunks qu'il a servis ; mais après une reprise, les chunks que le récepteur avait déjà (avant la reprise), il ne les a pas servis. Il les **relisait et les hachait à ce moment-là**, après 100 % : environ 500 Mo pour 1 Go repris à 48 %.

## Correction (`pkg/transfer/sender.go`)

- Le premier chunk demandé pour un élément n'est pas le premier : c'est une reprise, le récepteur a ceux d'avant.
- L'envoyeur hache alors ces chunks **pendant que le reste passe** : une goroutine, un tampon. Le réseau est plus lent qu'une lecture plus un hash.
- Le `DIGEST` utilise ces hash. S'ils ne sont pas encore prêts, il attend la fin du calcul en cours plutôt que de tout relire.
- La garantie XFER-07 ne change pas : la taille et la date du fichier sont revérifiées avant et après le `DIGEST`, comme pour les chunks servis.
- Bible §8.3 mise à jour.

## Tests

- `TestSenderLearnsTheEndAfterAResume` (deux envoyeurs, reprise à mi-chemin) vérifie aussi que le `DIGEST` n'a relu **aucun** chunk lui-même. Sans la correction, il en relit 3 et le test échoue.
- `go test ./...` et `go test -tags diag ./pkg/api ./pkg/transfer` : OK.

À confirmer par un essai réel : reprise d'un gros fichier, puis temps entre 100 % et « terminé ».
