author: rocksbrothers-png
body:
## O que muda
Corrige o campo **Situação** (ativa/inativa) do formulário de Empresas. Este PR é independente da UBX-V5 e do SECURITY-LOGO-XSS-V1. Detalhes em `docs/FIX_EMPRESAS_ACTIVE_V1.md`.

**Reprodução:** o defeito foi reproduzido no Chromium contra a `main`; os 25 cenários falham, nos 5 idiomas.

**Causa 1: o valor era trocado pela tradução**
- As opções do `<select name="active">` usavam `data-i18n-value`, e o `i18n.js` troca o `value` (`1`/`0`) pelo texto traduzido.
- O seletor ficava vazio e o formulário enviava `active: ''`.
- O backend recusa ("Campo obrigatório: active"), então **cadastrar e editar Empresa pelo web falhava em todos os idiomas**.
- O texto visível também não era traduzido.

**Causa 2: o estado carregava errado**
- `startEditCompany` usava `company.active || 1`, e uma empresa **inativa abria como Ativa**.
- Com a causa 1 corrigida, gravar a edição a reativaria em silêncio.

**Correção**
- As opções passam a usar `data-i18n`, que traduz só o texto, e mantêm `value="1"`/`"0"`.
- `startEditCompany` usa `company.active ?? 1`, a mesma regra que `saveCompany` já usava.
- Backend, autorização (`companies:create`/`companies:update`), regras de negócio e ativar/inativar pela lista **não mudam**.

### Testes
| Teste | `main` | Este PR |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/browser/fix_empresas_active.py` (Chromium, 5 idiomas): opções traduzidas com value 1/0; cadastro ativa (padrão) e inativa; editar ativa mantém 1; editar inativa abre e grava 0; trocar o estado nos dois sentidos | 25/25 falham | **25/25** |
| `static/js/test/empresas-active-runtime.js` (3): opções do select; nenhuma `<option>` das views com `data-i18n-value`; edição carrega 0/1 | 3 falham | 3/3 |
| `scripts/browser/ubx_companies.py`: o `KNOWN-DEFECT` (`active == ''`) passa a exigir `'1'` | — | 20/20 |

A caracterização da UBX-V5 (`companies-view-runtime.js`) detectou a mudança no cenário `editar:inativa`. A referência congelada recebeu a mesma correção, com um comentário.

**Suítes**
- JS: 653 testes.
- pytest: 4.486 passaram, com 1 falha só do ambiente local (`odf` ausente; falha igual na `main`).
- Guarda UBX, ESLint, ruff e `build_index check`: OK.
- **Paridade:** arquivos idênticos ao PR gêmeo no SaaS.

- [x] fix (correção de bug)
- [ ] refactor / chore
- [x] docs

author: topherhindman
body:
Fixes [DEVX-889](https://linear.app/livekit/issue/DEVX-889)

`TestCredentialResolution` let `room list` fall back to the only configured project in every API-key case. That allowance dates from when a `--project` or `--subdomain` that didn't resolve fell back to the only project. #1076 made that an error, and #1084 made `--dev` with an API key or secret an error too. Since then, lk falls back only when no project is named on the command line and a `livekit.toml` names a project that isn't configured. That fallback is on purpose: an agent repo still gets a project to choose. Allowing the fallback anywhere else would hide the #1076 bug if it came back.

**What changed**
- The allowance now covers only the case where `livekit.toml` names an unconfigured project and nothing earlier in the resolution order (`--project`, `--subdomain`, a full inline key pair, `--dev`) has picked a project.
- The temporary allowance for `--dev` with an inline key or secret is removed. With #1084 merged, `mustFail` covers that case.

**How tested**
- `go test ./cmd/lk -run '^TestCredentialResolution$' -rapid.checks=1000 -rapid.seed={1,42,20261027}` passes.
- With the #1076 fix reverted in `requireProjectWithOpts`, the property fails on all three seeds. The counterexamples are `lk --subdomain one room list` and `lk --project one room list` with only `two` configured. With the old allowance, the same revert passes on all three seeds.
- With the `livekit.toml` allowance removed, the property fails on two of the three seeds (42 and 20261027), with `lk room list` and a `livekit.toml` naming `one` while only `two` is configured. So the allowance is still needed.
- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `golangci-lint run` all pass.

author: puthrayaharness
body:
## Problem
Creating an FME flag that a governance policy blocks returned an MCP error cut off at `"errors":`, with no policy name or deny message. The FME API replies with RFC 7807 `problem+json` (`title`, `detail`, `errors[]`) and no `message` field, so the client fell back to the first 200 characters of the raw JSON.

## Fix
New `src/client/error-parsers.ts` holds a small registry of API-specific error parsers. Each parser has a `match({ path, status })` and a `parse(body)`.

| Piece | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `fmeUnprocessableEntityParser` | Matches only `/fme/` paths with status **422**. Message = `detail`, else `title` (400-char cap). Each `errors[]` entry is appended as `title: detail` (2000-char cap, surrogate-safe) |
| `runErrorParsers` | First matching parser that returns a result wins |
| `harness-client.ts` | `enrichErrorMessage` takes the HTTP status and tries the registry first. The parser message is used only when the body has no usable `message` (HTML/JS junk is still rejected). Generic enrichments (`details`, `detailedMessage`, `responseMessages`, `ERROR_FIELD_ENRICHMENTS`) still run on top |
| `docs/coding-standards.md` | File-organization table says to register an `ErrorParser` for new API error shapes |

Example: `Governance error — FME Flag 2 owners min: Feature flags must have at least 2 owners. Current user owner count: 0`

author: marcio-w-alves
body:
## O que muda

Atende à sua reclamação de textos escritos à mão e repetidos, com o seu nome espalhado pelo código:

- **As respostas rápidas leem os fatos do seu registro.** Antes, números como "50%", "30%", "de um para quatro", "mais de 10 anos", datas e nomes de empresa estavam escritos dentro das respostas. Agora vêm do currículo: se um fato mudar no perfil, todas as respostas mudam juntas. Um teste troca datas e números de propósito e confere que as respostas reais acompanham.
- **Os seus textos foram para o perfil.** O texto das respostas rápidas, as páginas de tema, as perguntas sugeridas e as palavras só suas (HRIS, UFPB, o prêmio de 2019…) agora ficam em `src/profile/copy`. O núcleo do assistente é genérico e recebe esses textos prontos.
- **O núcleo não tem mais nenhum dado seu.** Testes automáticos falham se aparecer no núcleo o seu nome, o nome de uma empresa sua, um número do seu currículo ou uma palavra do seu vocabulário. Todos os testes do núcleo rodam com o perfil fictício (Ada Rivera).
- **O seu nome com acento ("Márcio") passa a ser reconhecido** em todas as perguntas, não só em algumas.
- **As respostas não mudaram.** Antes de remover o teste que gravava todas as respostas rápidas, conferi que todas saíam idênticas, inclusive as mudanças recentes das páginas de tema (POR-76).

## Como testar no ambiente online

Nada deve mudar. Em https://marciomariani.dev, faça as perguntas sugeridas e abra as páginas de tema: os textos e números continuam os mesmos.

author: anurag629
body:
The docs bot on chat.codercops.com used to answer from an 8-question FAQ. Now it answers from the docs pages themselves, through hybrid search, and cites the page each answer comes from. This is the groundwork for the second half of E5, the citation eval.

## How it works

- **`npm run docs-index`** (in `website/`) runs `@chatcops/ingest` over `src/content/docs` with OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` at 512 dimensions. It writes two files to `public/docs-index/`:
  - `chunks.json`: the text, sources, embedder id and a hash per page, 289 KB
  - `vectors.bin`: float32 embeddings in chunk order, 528 KB

  27 pages make 258 chunks. URLs get a trailing slash, the way Starlight serves them.
- **`src/lib/docs-index.ts`** turns those files into `memoryVectors` plus `hybridRetriever`, wrapped in `retrieverKnowledge`.
  - **Loading:** once per Worker instance, on the first question. The vectors are read as a typed array, so they need no parsing, and a failed load is retried on the next question.
  - **Checks:** it refuses an index built with another embedder, and an index whose vector count doesn't match its chunks.
  - **Querying:** questions are embedded with the same model through the Worker's existing `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- **The chat endpoint** reads the two files from the `ASSETS` binding. The knowledge is the docs index first, then the FAQ.
- **The evals config** reads the same files from disk, so the evals test what's deployed.

I chose this over Vectorize:
- It needs no new Cloudflare resources and no new secrets.
- No Worker request has to run a long ingest.
- 258 chunks are well within what an in-memory index handles.

Vectorize is worth it once the index is too big to load per instance.

## Keeping it current

- `npm run docs-index:check` compares each docs page's hash with what the index was built from.
- CI runs it as a new step that only warns (`::warning::`). Rebuilding needs a key that contributors don't have, so a docs PR mustn't fail over it.
- CONTRIBUTING.md says a maintainer rebuilds the index before a release.

## The evals caught a change

With the docs in context, "hi" got a long list of everything the bot can do, so the "stays on topic and short" test failed (judge 0.50, passes at 0.6). I added one line to the system prompt: "Answer greetings and small talk in one or two sentences, without listing everything you can help with." With that, all 9 tests pass again.

The recordings are redone, and replies now cite real pages: `/core/providers/` for the providers question, quick start and installation for the install question, `/widget/i18n/` for languages, and so on. Once `cites` lands (#424), the 50-question citation eval can build on this.

## Checks

- **Website:** the build passes, and the index is copied into `dist/client/docs-index/`.
- **Evals:** 9 replayed, nothing spent. The index check reports it's up to date.
- **Lint and docs:** `pnpm lint` is at 39 warnings and 6 infos, same as dev, and `docs:check` passes.
- **Keys:** the key check on the recordings is clean. The index has the docs' own `sk-ant-...` placeholders, and that check doesn't scan it.
- **The live endpoint** only runs once deployed. I'll ask the bot a few questions on the site after the next deploy.

author: admin-wekruit
body:
## Why
Repeating a contact lookup could spend credits again on people who had already been searched, including people for whom nothing was found. Avoiding that was left to the agent. It now has to be a product guarantee that every lookup path enforces.

## What changed
- Before calling any provider, the lookup service reads every earlier lookup this account ran, across all roles and all agents:
  - Saved emails are reused at no cost.
  - A source that already searched a person and found nothing is not charged for them again.
  - A source that only failed (for example, because it was out of credits) can still run later.
- The result summary has a new `already_looked_up` count for people skipped this way.
- A new `recheck` input searches those people again. It is meant only for when the recruiter explicitly asks.
- On the lookup connection, the raw `enrich_bulk` tool is hidden from discovery and refused at execution, so every lookup goes through this service.

No user-facing copy added.

## Testing
The adapters unit suite and typecheck pass. New tests show that:
- No source is charged for a person it already searched.
- Only the source that has not searched a person runs.
- The skipped count is reported.
- `recheck` runs the lookup again.
- Saved receipts are read into found emails and per-source "already searched" sets, and a failed source does not count as searched.

body:
## Why

Records containing `DateTime` fail to derive `ToSchema`, so applications cannot expose timestamp fields in read models. The existing JSON encoding is a string, and `SText` matches that wire form.

## What changed

- Add `ToSchema DateTime = SText` and cover direct, optional, and record fields through core schema, OpenAPI, JSON Schema, and JSON wire assertions.
- Add the runnable `nhtestbed-datetime-schema` shipment example and its exact README command.
- Add a release fragment that tells applications to remove an orphan `ToSchema DateTime` workaround.

## Scope

- Covers issue #729 only. Timestamp encoding and schema constructors stay as they are.
- OpenAPI does not add a `date-time` format in this change.

## Blast Radius

Applications with timestamped read models gain schema derivation. Applications with an orphan `ToSchema DateTime` instance must remove that instance to avoid a duplicate-instance compiler error.

- Red on old code. `nix develop --command .agents/skills/tdd/scripts/test-match 'DateTime' nhcore-test-core` and `nix develop --command cabal test nhtestbed:nhtestbed-datetime-schema --test-show-details=direct` both produced `No instance for ‘ToSchema DateTime’`.

author: perrinshanks-cogito
body:
## Summary
Closes the remaining items from the OWASP ASVS Level 1 record and adds the record to the repo.

### 1. Size limits on files people open (ASVS file handling)
Project files, data sheets and A3 pictures had no size limit. They're only read in the browser, so a huge file could only slow the person's own tab, but ASVS expects a limit.

| What is opened | Limit | Why this size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project file (.json) | 50 MB | A3 report files carry their pictures, so they can be large; other tools' files are a few KB |
| Data sheet (.xlsx) | 10 MB | A filled-in sheet is usually under 100 KB |
| A3 picture (chosen or pasted) | 25 MB | Covers phone photos; the report shrinks anything over 2400px |
| Each part inside a data sheet, unzipped | 100 MB | An .xlsx is a zip, so a small file could unpack into gigabytes |

- **`assets/js/focus-actions.js`**: `LIMITS` and `tooBig()`, used by the shared Open and data sheet import. The xlsx inflate reads the stream in chunks and stops once a part passes 100 MB.
- **Process map, driver diagram and fishbone diagram:** their own Open uses the project-file limit.
- **A3 report:** pictures use the picture limit.
- **README:** documents the limits.

### 2. Error reports send only the error type (ASVS logging and data protection)
Application Insights error reports carried the error message in four places: the message, the stack trace, and two copies in the properties. A message can quote what someone pasted.
- A telemetry initializer in `assets/js/analytics.js` now replaces them with the error type (`TypeError`, `RangeError` and so on) and keeps only where in the code it happened (line, column, page).
- The SDK's own `typeName` for these reports is just `String`, so the type is read from the stack or message.

### 3. SDK update cadence
The update note in `assets/js/analytics.js` now says to check for a new SDK version once a year, or sooner for a security fix.

### 4. The ASVS Level 1 record, as a draft
- Adds `docs/security/asvs-level-1.md`, a copy of the record under review: scope, a data-flow diagram (Mermaid, so GitHub draws it), the assessment by chapter, tests, accepted risks, open actions and review triggers.
- It's marked as a draft until it's signed off, then updated to match the approved version.
- `docs/` is excluded in `_config.yml`, so the record isn't published on the site; the README points to it.

## Testing
Built with Jekyll and served with the live security headers.
- **Size limits:**
  - Refused: 51 MB project file (SPC tool and process map), 11 MB .xlsx, 26 MB A3 picture.
  - Zip bomb (153 KB unpacking to 150 MB): stopped in under a second.
  - A downloaded data sheet and a saved project still open normally.
- **Error reports:** requests to Application Insights captured while two uncaught errors were thrown with marker text in their messages.
  - Before the change, the marker text appeared in the payload.
  - After it, each report holds only `TypeError` or `Error` plus line and column, and the marker appears nowhere in anything sent.
- **All pages:** all 31 pages and their exports run with no console errors or CSP violations, and the SDK still loads.
- **ASVS record:** the Mermaid diagram validates; a Jekyll build with the change has no `docs/` in `_site`.
- `node --test tests/stats/stats.test.js`: 111 pass.

## CI note
**Build and deploy** fails because the Static Web App has reached its maximum number of preview environments (see comment). It will keep failing until old preview environments are deleted in the Azure portal. The build and tests themselves pass.

author: brianduff
body:
## Summary

Merge controls in the review guide and board now immediately display a disabled “Requesting merge…” spinner after confirmation. The observable request state prevents duplicate sends and clears on engine acceptance, rejection, disconnect, or a visible 60-second timeout. Waiting for revision consent pauses the request timeout. Only an engine acceptance produces the “Merge requested” banner.

The engine previously recorded GitHub acceptance, then awaited `publish_work_item_changed`, which refreshes the global decision feed under its shared lock before publishing board invalidation, and only then sent the acceptance reply. Both GitHub and Trunk paths now send acceptance before that publication. The GitHub path still checks the exact PR head, executes the merge command, and commits the durable intent before acknowledging.

Timing logs cover the app click and RPC scheduling/write, engine socket receipt and preflight, GitHub head probe and merge command, durable write, acknowledgement enqueue/socket write, board publication, and application of the acknowledgement to the banner. The banner is driven by the direct reply; it does not require a later board patch. No progress-stage events currently exist on this RPC, so the in-flight label stays “Requesting merge…” until the terminal response.

## Evidence

The controlled baseline held the decision-feed publication lock for 300 ms, using the existing isolated engine test fixture and fake GitHub executor. The unchanged handler acknowledged after **303.814458 ms**. After the fix, acknowledgement arrived in **6.879125 ms while that lock remained held**. One measured run per version; the baseline test also passed once with output capture enabled. The regression holds the lock until after acknowledgement, with a two-second deadlock guard, and still verifies the subsequent board invalidation and durable intent. This isolates the avoidable publication dependency from GitHub network time.

The production incident was not sampled: these are isolated fixture measurements, not live click-to-pixel timings. No production engine/app was launched and no live PR was merged. The new per-hop logs make remaining network, socket, or main-thread delays observable on deployment.

- `bazel build //tools/boss/engine/core:engine //tools/boss/app-macos:Boss //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard3 //tools/boss/engine/core:engine_lib_test` — passed. An initial attempt aborted because a Swift source was edited during compilation; the stable rerun passed.
- `bazel test //tools/boss/engine/core:engine_lib_test --test_filter=direct_merge_request_marks_task_queued_and_broadcasts --test_arg=--nocapture --test_output=all` — passed on both the instrumented baseline and fixed handler; measurements above.

- `bazel build //tools/boss/cli/... //tools/boss/bossctl/...` — all 27 consumer targets passed.
- `bazel test //tools/boss/engine/... //tools/boss/app-macos/... --test_output=errors --keep_going` — 86 of 89 targets passed initially. Three existing confirmation tests needed connected-client fixtures now that disconnected confirmations correctly fail; those fixtures were corrected without changing their successful-send assertions.
- Final `bazel build //tools/boss/app-macos:Boss //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard3` and `bazel test //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard3 --test_output=errors` — passed after the fixture corrections and reconnect fix; all 31 merge-feedback tests passed, covering immediate observable progress, duplicate suppression, acceptance, rejection, timeout/retry, disconnect/reconnect, confirmation waiting, and card redraw equality.
- The broad run timed out `BossTestsShard4` during its unchanged portrait connected-component test at 60.4 seconds. `bazel test //tools/boss/app-macos:BossTestsShard4 --test_output=errors` passed alone in 48.6 seconds. Classified as unrelated environmental contention: that test only processes portrait pixels and does not execute merge-request code.

- The engine target's scale-test shard timed out at 300.4 seconds in the broad run and 300.2 seconds when the target was rerun alone. `bazel test //tools/boss/engine/core:engine_lib_test --test_filter=work_tree_production_scale_measurement --test_arg=--nocapture --test_output=errors` then passed in 271.0 seconds. Classified as an unrelated, non-trivial suite-composition/performance issue: the unchanged test seeds 10,030 tasks and benchmarks work-tree projections without calling merge-request handlers. The other ten engine shards passed. Validation uses the passing isolated test as evidence; the full engine shard did not finish within its deadline.

- Final serial `checkleft run` — passed: no findings, 22 checks in 210 seconds. The earlier concurrent invocation hit its Rust-lint subprocess wall-clock limit while the broad Bazel validation was active; the serial rerun completed normally.

author: prince22466
body:
## Goal: built-in grouped paged-KV optimization for standard vLLM serving

Bring the grouped page-table lookup kernel previously tested in `Optimization/v4_preplay` into `Optimization/v4`, **automatically active on eligible BI-V150 prefill** without requiring `FLAGGEMS_ILUVATAR_PAGED_KV=grouped` or `VLLM_FL_USE_FLAGGEMS_ATTN=1` at launch.

### Implementation

- `FlagGems/src/flag_gems/ops/flash_kernel.py` — the **same validated Triton kernel** from v4_preplay: load one physical page ID per KV page in an aligned tile, expand with `tl.gather`, and reuse the existing attention computation. Source bytes are identical to tested v4_preplay.
- `FlagGems/src/flag_gems/ops/flash_api.py` — connects grouped page addressing in both existing varlen launch sites; no tile/warp/stage heuristic changes.
- `FlagGems/src/flag_gems/ops/iluvatar_grouped_paged_kv.py` — grouped lookup now **defaults ON** for eligible Iluvatar paged-KV prefill (Q≥128, KV≥8192, aligned power-of-two pages/tiles, no dropout/local attention). Decode/short/unsupported cases retain original lookup. Optional `FLAGGEMS_ILUVATAR_PAGED_KV=baseline` remains for A/B/rollback.
- `vllm-plugin-FL/vllm_fl/dispatch/backends/flaggems/flaggems.py` — **on Iluvatar only**, the existing FlagOS attention dispatch hook now prefers the optimized FlagGems attention backend by default. The dispatcher and fallback policy are not removed, and the existing explicit backend override still works. Other vendors unchanged.
- `readme.md` — records algorithm, automatic activation, existing controls and official evaluation command.

There are no new profiling/benchmark/test scripts and no unrelated code changes.

### Previous GPU evidence from v4_preplay (not newly verified on v4)

| Attention workload | Baseline GPU-event median | Grouped median | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K / 16K | 114.5281 ms | 97.5166 ms | 1.1744× |
| 2K / 16K | 27.898 ms | 23.417 ms | 1.1914× |

Four previous grouped kernel GPU correctness tests passed. The old GPU results validate the *in-kernel* idea, **not the new automatic vLLM backend integration**.

### Official gating / risks

- [ ] Confirm a standard, installed-plugin `vllm serve` on BI-V150 now selects `AttentionFLBackend` and invokes FlagGems **Triton** varlen attention (not `TRITON_ATTN` or a FlagGems C-extension bypass).
- [ ] Run the **unmodified** official 4K/16K served-throughput benchmark with this automatic default, comparing the **previous standard TRITON backend** for total competition outcome.
- [ ] Independently compare grouped vs `FLAGGEMS_ILUVATAR_PAGED_KV=baseline` with **FlagGems held fixed** for fair kernel-level speedup attribution.
- [ ] Run the official `math_500` accuracy evaluation before adoption.

**Important:** selecting FlagGems by default on Iluvatar changes the attention backend for *both* 4K and 16K requests. The grouped optimization itself only activates for eligible long contexts, so 4K could regress. No end-to-end throughput or math_500 pass is claimed.

Competition compliance: a real attention-kernel memory-access optimization, no quantization, speculative decoding, hyperparameter changes, competition benchmark modifications, upstream FlagOS merges or deletion of the dispatcher logic.

**Status: Draft, pending BI-V150 validation.**

author: juvndvv
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **Juanda** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01XomVTRnqagBg2LUjhgv2Mt?thread=cmsg_01XomVTRnqagBg2LUjhgv2MtExH4tLGHiQtnfTnqsBdPzW)_

## Problem
Since the Lock Screen widgets (#15), every `Transaction::saved` dispatches `RefreshWidgets`, a `ShouldBeUnique` job. Its unique lock is acquired at dispatch time (even with `afterCommit()`), and with `CACHE_STORE=database` that is an `INSERT` into `cache_locks` inside `BankSyncService::store()`'s `DB::transaction`. From the second new movement on, the insert collides, Postgres aborts the transaction, and `DatabaseLock`'s fallback `UPDATE` fails with `SQLSTATE[25P02]`. The whole BBVA sync rolls back (`last_error = "Error inesperado al sincronizar."`). Revolut kept working only because it brought 0–1 new movements.

## Fix
- Dispatch `RefreshWidgets` through `DB::afterCommit(...)`, so the lock is taken outside the transaction and nothing is pushed on rollback.
- Give database cache locks their own connection (`pgsql_locks`, same settings as `pgsql`) via `DB_CACHE_LOCK_CONNECTION` in `compose.yaml`, `.env.example` and `phpunit.xml`, so a lock collision can never poison an open transaction (nested transactions and tests included).
- `SyncBankConnection` (the other `ShouldBeUnique`) is only dispatched outside transactions; unchanged.

## Tests
- Bank sync with 3 new movements on the `database` cache store imports all 3 and queues `RefreshWidgets` once (fails with the production 25P02 without the fix).
- A save that rolls back does not queue the job.
- Full Pest suite (570), Larastan and Pint green.

## After deploy
Containers must be recreated with the new `compose.yaml` to pick up `DB_CACHE_LOCK_CONNECTION`. Then trigger a manual BBVA sync to recover the missing movements.

author: blackie365
body:
A skip was previously final — a skipped row stayed skipped forever. This adds an undo in both places a decision can be made.

## What changed

**Email confirmation page** (`/api/social/approve`)

- After clicking **Skip**, the page now offers *"Changed your mind? Put it back in the queue"*.
- After undoing, it offers **"Approve & post now"**, so the whole loop works from the inbox without a trip to the admin screen.

**Admin Social screen** (`/admin/social`)

- Skipped rows now show an **Un-skip** button, alongside the existing Post now / Skip on pending rows.

## Safety

- Undo is signed as its own token action (`SocialLinkAction = 'approved' | 'skipped' | 'unskip'`), so a skip token can never be replayed as an un-skip, or an approve token as anything else. The payload is still `${id}:${action}`.
- `unskipQueuedPost` only updates `WHERE status = 'skipped'`, and `reopenQueuedPost` refuses anything else with a clear message.
- **Only a skip can be undone.** An `approved` row has already been published, so reversing it would mean deleting a live Facebook/Instagram post — a different and riskier operation that this deliberately does not do. Attempting it returns *"Already posted — this cannot unpublish it."*

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` clean, `pnpm lint` 0 errors.

author: justinchuby
body:
### Motivation and Context

Represent recent mixture-of-experts feed-forward blocks with portable opset-29 graphs built around `GroupedMatMul`. Add an executable model generator, reusable model-local functions, and a technical guide showing how routing, selected-expert SwiGLU, mixture reduction, and shared experts fit together.

| Composition | Role in real models |
|---|---|
| `SoftmaxRouter` and `MixingWeights` | Softmax top-k selection and selected-probability normalization for [Qwen3Next](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_next/modeling_qwen3_next.py#L782-L860). |
| `GroupedRouter` | Sigmoid scores, selection-only correction bias, sum-of-top-two group ranking, group/expert top-k, and unbiased mixture weights for [GLM-5 / GLM-MoE-DSA](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/glm_moe_dsa/modeling_glm_moe_dsa.py#L453-L505), [GLM-4-MoE](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/glm4_moe/modeling_glm4_moe.py#L268-L304), and the directly verified [Kimi Linear routing family](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/kimi_linear/modeling_kimi_linear.py#L718-L802). Normalization epsilon and routed scaling remain explicit inputs. |
| `SelectedSwiGLU` | Three `GroupedMatMul` calls evaluate gate/up/down projections for selected experts. Flattening only selected activations and IDs connects the down projection; weighted reduction returns one hidden vector per token. This represents the expert FFN used by these model families without graph-level copies of expert weights or one-hot dispatch. |
| Explicit shared-expert graphs | Dense SwiGLU plus a sigmoid gate for Qwen; dense SwiGLU added directly for GLM and Kimi. Shared intermediate width remains independent of routed expert width. |

The softmax composition also represents the newer **Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B** and **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** MoE FFNs:

- [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B's pinned configuration](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) selects `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, with 512 experts, 10 routes, hidden width 8192, and routed/shared intermediate width 2048. Its [router/expert/shared implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen3_5_moe/modeling_qwen3_5_moe.py#L832-L910) uses normalized softmax top-k and a sigmoid-gated shared expert.
- [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's pinned configuration](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/blob/de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540/config.json) has 512 experts, 10 routes, hidden width 2560, and routed/shared intermediate width 640. Its [`Qwen4Exp` implementation directly reuses the Qwen3Next router, experts and sparse block](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/c27795950091cdaf1b0e32c4aed58618fb41ffa0/src/transformers/models/qwen4_exp/modular_qwen4_exp.py#L511-L528); the [official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) describes this as a preview of the architecture underpinning Qwen4.

The generator writes complete softmax and grouped-sigmoid ONNX models carrying their local function definitions. The guide specifies float32 execution, cast placement when adapting mixed-precision models, tie ordering, duplicate-route behavior, valid routing bounds, and empty-token shapes. Attention, embeddings, normalization, and residual paths compose outside the MoE feed-forward block.

### Checklist

- [ ] The human author has reviewed this PR in full and takes responsibility for its content.

author: 7duckie
body:
## Overview

A site with an ordinary absolute symbolic link under `wp-content` — `wp-content/uploads/media` pointing at `/mnt/shared/media`, a common hosting arrangement — could not be recovered after a failed restore, and the remedy the failure message named failed for exactly the same reason. The symlink confinement rule exists to stop a backup from somewhere else planting a link outside the site, and it refuses any absolute target; it was also being applied to safety archives, which are Pontifex's own snapshot of *this* site taken minutes earlier. Such a site therefore held safety archives that none of its own recovery paths could replay: the operator was told automatic recovery had also failed, `wp pontifex rollback` failed identically, and the admin screens offered no override at all. Replaying a safety archive now skips a link whose recorded target is absolute, finishes the rest of the recovery, and names every link it skipped. Nothing about an ordinary forward restore changes.

---

## Changes

### Recovery — a safety-archive replay skips an absolute link target

`FileWriter` gained a `$replaying_safety_archive` flag, false by default so an ordinary restore behaves exactly as before. When it is true, the two places that would otherwise refuse an absolute target — the whole-archive confinement preflight and the per-entry write — record the link as skipped and carry on, and the two stay in agreement so a link the preflight decided to skip is never created later by the walk. The flag is set at the three places that replay this site's own prior state: automatic recovery after a failed restore or import, `wp pontifex rollback`, and the admin Rollback button. A relative target that resolves outside the site is still refused even during a replay; only an absolute target is skipped, because a restore is purely additive and such a link is almost always still on disk untouched.

### Reporting — a merge now names which cause applied

A recovery that skipped a link reports having merged rather than having put the site back exactly, because it cannot prove the second — the same distinction recovery already drew when it could not account for everything it created. A merge now has two possible causes, so they are kept apart rather than collapsed: an unconfirmed file cleanup keeps its own message, which sends the operator to the log for stray paths, while a skipped link over a provably complete cleanup gets a message saying the cleanup finished and naming the link. Reporting the first when only the second had happened sent the operator looking for files that were never left behind — which is what a real run of this branch did before the message was split.

### Surfaces — what an operator actually sees

The CLI prints one warning naming each skipped link and then a summary, mirroring the two-tier shape `ExportCommand` already uses for its changed-file list, because an operator watching a terminal must see this without going to the log. The admin Rollback success message carries the same information, appended to the message the screen shows verbatim. `wp pontifex rollback` draws no precise/merge verdict to downgrade, since it is deliberately additive with no creation ledger of its own, so its only obligation is naming what it could not re-create.

### Documentation and the decision record

ADR 0021 said "Absolute targets stay refused, unchanged", which is true of every forward restore and was false the moment this behaviour landed, so it carries an amendment recording why the original rule was written about a different input and what did not change. `docs/threat-model.md` carried the same claim in a form that was literally true — nothing in the admin UI can *waive* the target check, and still cannot — but which a reader would take to mean an absolute target is always refused in the browser; that section now separates the two cases. The ADR index is untouched, because its one-line summary for 0021 describes what a restore does and is still accurate.

`docs/when-pontifex-refuses.md` gains an entry for the new message and corrects the claim that `--allow-unsafe-symlinks` is needed to un-stick a recovery — it is not, and reaching for it there is neither necessary nor safe. The changelog entry records what changed and, explicitly, what did not.

---

## Decisions recorded

| ADR | Decision |
|-----|----------|
| 0021 | Amended: replaying this site's own safety archive skips an absolute link target rather than refusing it. A forward restore, a relative escaping target, and `--allow-unsafe-symlinks` are all unchanged. |

---

## Verification

Proven on a throwaway site carrying a real absolute symlink, because the project's own dev site is over the safety-archive entry ceiling and so refuses every restore before doing anything. The browser gate drove a successful restore followed by Rollback; the CLI gate drove a failed import through automatic recovery. Both named the skipped link, and the canary post, site URL and the link itself survived intact.

```
composer lint                              → 0 errors
composer analyse                           → no errors
composer test                              → 2095 tests, 17484 assertions, OK
PHP 8.2 in Docker, non-root                → 2095 OK, 38 skipped (ext-zstd / hardware AES absent)
```

Eight of those tests are new: four pinning the recovery outcome and the skipped-link list handed back to the caller, and four pinning the messages, including one asserting the unconfirmed-cleanup wording is byte-identical to what it was.

author: undecuple
body:
## Why

- On the first start of a level with an empty shader cache, the game's window stopped answering for up to about 8 seconds, long enough for Windows to mark it as not responding.
- A coding agent working from AGENTS.md on native Windows stalled on steps that only fit the maintainers' Linux and Nix setup. This was reported on Project Helghast (issue #10, by @Tzeentchnet), whose AGENTS.md ours is adapted from.
- The public host-test list left out every shell-script test, so the runtime and SPU tests in `tools/runtime/` and `tools/spu/` did not run in CI. The previous change's description said they were listed; they were not.

## Change

- Patch 2124 and `port/kz2/main.cpp`: the game window gets a thread of its own. It handles window messages only and wakes at least every 50 ms. Swap-chain calls stay on the frame thread. `KZ2_WINDOW_THREAD=0` restores the old behaviour. New test: `tools/runtime/test_window_thread.sh`.
- AGENTS.md is split into three parts:
  - rules for everyone (unchanged);
  - the maintainers' setup (Nix, the sandbox and Proton), labelled as not a requirement;
  - a "Without Nix (for example native Windows)" part. Native builds go through the installer.
- `tools/host-tests.txt` now lists the 19 exported shell-script tests (runtime and SPU). `test_spu_xr.sh` and `test_spu_fastcg.sh` print SKIP without a patched toolkit, like the other SPU tests.
- A CHANGELOG [Unreleased] line for the window fix.

## Size

About 540 changed lines, 330 of them in patch 2124. The window thread, the swap-chain hand-off it needs and its test only work together, so they go in one change; the AGENTS.md split and the test-list fix are small and independent.

## Tests

- On a clean clone of this tree with the toolkit submodule, run as CI runs it (patched toolkit built first, then `ci_host_tests.sh --no-sandbox`): 47 of 47 host tests pass, none skipped.
- The new test, `test_window_thread`, makes 15 checks. With the guard removed it fails the 2 checks that cover that guard.

## Evidence

Linux under Proton, 240 seconds each, from the menu into the first level:

| Shader cache | Longest window message gap, before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Empty | 7937 ms | 50 ms |
| Warm | 154 ms | 51 ms |

- Flips and level-start time stayed within run-to-run noise.
- The 8-second first-play pipeline build itself is unchanged.
- The display modes (fullscreen, windowed, Alt+Enter, resize, borderless) and closing the window were checked in a separate 60-second run.

Not tested: native Windows, and the AGENTS.md "Without Nix" steps on Windows (the Python tests were run with plain `python3` on Linux outside Nix).

## Overlap

None known. Patch 2124 changes only the port's own window code (`port/kz2/main.cpp`) and the display-mode helper from patch 2095.

author: cntent
body:
Each person connects their own Readwise Reader token in Settings › Integrations.

**Read only**
- Orbit only ever sends GET requests to Readwise. A test checks every request.

**Knowledge**
- Only documents tagged `orbit` reach Orbit. Their text and highlights are filed in Knowledge and kept up to date.
- Each document goes under the company whose name or domain matches one of its other tags, otherwise under Eclipse.
- Untagging or deleting a document in Reader archives the Knowledge item.
- Nothing untagged is stored.

**Assistant and MCP**
- `reader_list`, `reader_read` and `reader_highlights` read the whole library live, with the caller's own token.
- They are marked as outside content.
- In MCP they are registered only for personal tokens.

**Sync**
- A `readwise` step in the 10-minute cron: 12 seconds and 15 requests per run, within Readwise's 20 a minute.
- It resumes from a page cursor.
- A full pass runs daily and on Sync now.

**Storage**
- Tokens are encrypted, with only a four-character hint kept.
- `crm.readwise_keys` and `crm.readwise_documents` are owner-only.
- Removing a member deletes their token.

**Needs**
- Migration `20261208150000_readwise.sql` before deploy. It:
  - adds the two tables;
  - adds Knowledge kind `reader`;
  - adds `private.readwise_key_members`;
  - recreates `private.team_remove` with one extra delete. The production body matched the repo before the change.

**Checks**

- readwise (14), knowledge and team tests pass.

body:
# PR Details

Saving in the Avalonia Game Studio, as in the WPF editor. Stacked on #3723.

- File > Save (Ctrl+S) saves the session, and File > Reload project opens it again.
- Closing the window, File > Close, Exit, opening another project and Reload ask once whether to save (Save / Don't save / Cancel).
- Assets, solution explorer items, editor tabs and the window title are marked with `*` while they have unsaved changes.
- Before saving, a property grid text box with the focus commits its edit.
- Save errors stay in the progress window, and the session stays dirty.

The script editor keeps its own Save. Its unsaved edits make the script dirty, and the session save writes them through the editor (overwrite check, byte order mark kept). Ctrl+S in a script is File > Save, as in WPF.

Ctrl+S is a key binding of the main window, as in WPF, rather than the menu item's hot key: Avalonia evaluates a closed menu's items only when the menu opens. For the same reason, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y did nothing until the Edit menu had been opened once; they are now handled by the main window too.

The WPF editor is unchanged.

## Related Issue

Part of the Avalonia Game Studio port; stack overview in #3707.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

author: serhiimazurok
body:
On every spec change `Ready` left `True` for about 2.5 seconds while the tenant served: a writer whose input condition described an older generation wrote `False`, `WaitingFor<X>`, at the new one, and Lifecycle turned `Ready` `Unknown` as soon as any input lagged.

A readiness condition now keeps its availability while the controllers take a change up (`docs/decisions/independent-controllers.md`, carried to controller code by `.claude/rules/conditions.md`):

- A writer that waits for another condition at a new generation leaves its own at the generation it last described: PKI's `AccessReady`, Tenant's `AddonsApplied` and `AddonsAvailable`. Health waits for `AccessReady` at any generation, writes its conditions at the object's generation, and counts a failed probe only once its pass has applied them.
- A writer that decides from its own condition while it waits, or keeps one while its calls to the tenant fail, reads it live (`internal/live`) and compares its status apply with that copy, so a cache that lacks its own last write can neither write an older condition back nor skip a write; the ClusterRoles of Workloads, PKI, Tenant and Health get `get` on `controlplanes` for it.
- Workloads counts the Deployments it controls, at the generation `APIServerReady` names, through its waits for the certificates and the datastore, only while it reports their availability, so a wait never turns a refusal into `True`.
- Lifecycle builds `Ready` from the statuses, gives it the oldest generation of its inputs, so `Ready` `True` at the object's generation still means every change is taken up, and names the lag in `Progressing`, `LatestGenerationNotObserved`.
- The nightly HA toggle wants `Ready` and every condition it is built from `True` throughout adding `highAvailability`.

Refusals of a new generation (`Unsupported`, `Refused`, `ObjectsControlledElsewhere`) still drop `Ready`; `todo.md` takes them, and the one failed `e2e-ha` run on this pull request: a 500 in each loop as the etcd leader's pod went away.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Intent

Let automations (package jobs, webhooks, subscriptions, package workflow steps) and ad hoc `execute` say where they run: one named execution context, or their own ordered chain, with `requires`, the same no-fallback default, and an opt-in bounded queue for an offline context. All behind the `execution-contexts` flag.

**Door:** `one-way` (new `automation_execution_settings` table and manifest `execution` shape; flag-gated)

**Cleanup:** `none`

## Why

Automations always ran on Kody cloud, so an automation that only works on a specific machine had no way to say so (Execution Contexts PR 4).

## Summary

- **Shared setting** (`execution-contexts/automation-execution-schema.ts`): `{ context?, fallback?: "chain", chain?, requires?: ["fs"|"lan"], whenOffline?: "fail"|"queue", queueMinutes? }`. Chain rules live in `chain-rules.ts`: up to 3 contexts, `"cloud"` only last, no duplicates, cloud omitted = strict.
- **Per-run chain for execute**: `chain` on MCP/API `execute` and `kody execute --chain a,b,cloud` (plus `--context/--fallback/--requires`). It replaces the default chain. Entries are tried in order and skipped when they fail `requires` or are offline, busy, unusable, or inaccessible. If nothing qualifies, the error lists every entry (Kody cloud included) with its reason and is recorded in run history. A cloud fallback keeps the skipped entries in run metadata.
- **Automations**: manifest `kody.jobs.<name>.execution`, `kody.webhooks[].execution`, `kody.subscriptions.<topic>.execution`, and `workflows.create({ execution })` for workflow steps. An org override set from the API/MCP/UI (`automation_execution_settings`, migration 0200) wins over the manifest. `{ context: "cloud" }` pins an automation to cloud, and clearing the override (`null`) restores the manifest. With `fallback: "chain"`, a removed named context is recorded as skipped and the chain is followed. Routing happens in `runBundledModuleWithRegistry` before the hosted sandbox. The handler must be a package export, and it fails clearly otherwise.
- **Offline**: fails by default with a clear reason. `whenOffline: "queue"` parks the run in the context's session DO when no chain entry can take it, whether the context is offline or busy (default 60 min, max 24 h). The drain runs on reconnect, on daemon status updates, and every 30 s. Before each dispatch it re-checks the context, the actor's org membership and flag, context access, and the grant version. Revoking a context fails its queue at once. The alarm expires the run with `execution_context_queue_expired`, and the queued attempt is recorded as `expired`, or as `ran` once the context takes it.
- **Workflow steps** need a result before the next step runs. They reject `whenOffline: "queue"`, and when the context run outlives the wait the step fails (`execution_context_result_pending`) and the context run is cancelled, so a retry never runs alongside it. Jobs, webhooks and subscriptions hand off instead, and their child record owns the outcome.
- **Who it runs as**: the automation's billed actor (`callerContext.request.actor`: the enabler for triggers, same as background-run billing and lineage), re-checked on every hop. Credential values never reach a context (ADR 0083). The context run is a child run record (`parentRunId`) under the job, trigger or workflow-step record. It carries no `jobId`, so job counters count each run once.
- **Flag**: settings are read only after the run's actor passes `isExecutionContextsEnabledFor`. With the flag off, management answers `feature_disabled` and automations behave exactly as before, with no extra reads.
- **Management**: MCP `automationExecutionGet`/`automationExecutionSet`, Open API `GET|PUT /v1/automation-execution`, `kody api automationExecution{Get,Set}`, and a "Where this runs" section on the job detail page and on editable webhook/subscription triggers (package Triggers tab). Save refuses an incomplete selection. Workflow steps take their setting from `workflows.create` in package code, since workflows have no settings UI.
- Org hard purge covers `automation_execution_settings`; account deletion anonymizes `updated_by_user_id`.
- Docs: ADR 0086 (`0086-automation-execution-contexts.md`), architecture doc rules, CLI help.

## Referenced issues and PRs

Related to #4433 (PR 2), #4432 (PR 3) and #4489.

## Testing

- **`npm run validate`** at `52e4dca49`: typecheck, lint, docs, migrations, test-node (1735 files / 7663 tests), test-workers (128 / 604), test-mcp and e2e (34) all pass. The only failure is the final `worker-startup-time:check`, which hits "Worker startup profiling timed out after 10 seconds" on the Devin VM. That is a known VM-load issue, and CI runs the check.
- **Later review rounds**: after those rounds, the worker typecheck plus the targeted execution-context, MCP, package-runtime, invocation and CLI node suites pass, and so do the session-DO worker tests. That includes new tests for revoke failing the queue and for queued → ran/expired attempt labels.
- **Local** (dev worker + local API worker, real `kody` CLI):
  - `kody execute --context laptop` against an offline context fails with `laptop: offline` and no cloud fallback.
  - `--chain laptop,cloud --requires fs` fails and lists `laptop` and `Kody cloud` with their reasons.
- **Preview** (`kody-pr-4474`, deploy `7761d7dee`, `preview-flag:execution-contexts`), driven through the UI and API:
  - The contexts page shows the registered `laptop` as offline.
  - A manifest job's `execution` selects `laptop`. Run now fails with `laptop: offline` (no cloud) and is recorded in run history.
  - A 1-minute queue override persists across reload. Run now says the run is queued for `laptop` and shows the expiry. The child record starts as Running, and the real Workers alarm turns it into Error after about 60 s with `execution_context_queue_expired`. `runGet` shows the parent/child `parentRunId` link.
  - A `laptop, cloud` chain with `requires: ["fs"]` fails with both targets `skipped (no_fs)`.
  - A webhook override (laptop, queue, 7 min) persists across reload.
  - Preview found the expired child still labeling its attempt `ran`. That is fixed and covered by node tests.
- **Not exercised end to end**:
  - Live reconnect-and-drain: local and preview have no ECP frame-signing keys, and no secrets were created. The session-DO worker tests cover it.
  - Subscription and workflow-step runs on a real context.
  - Flag-off preview: the flag tests cover it.
  - No org has the flag on.

  - `PfSenseConfig`: `host` (SSRF-checked on save), `port` (default 9273), `scheme`. No secrets.

  - `test_connection()`: a single guarded `GET /metrics` (TLS verified, 10 s limit, body capped at 8 MiB). It passes if the page carries any of the Telegraf metrics the cards read, and reports only counts of interfaces and gateways. It never quotes device text.
  - Cards `pfsense-overview` (CPU, RAM, states, interface traffic) and `pfsense-gateways` (latency, loss). One TCP firewall hint.
- Registered in `registry.py`. Indexed in `docs/INTEGRATIONS.md`. New `docs/integrations/pfsense.md`.
- Hand-written fixture `telegraf_pfsense.prom` (documentation addresses only).
- `tests/integrations/netfake.py`: added the fake DNS entry `fw.example.internal → 10.0.0.1` (test helper only).

## How it was tested
`tests/integrations/builtin/test_pfsense.py` covers:
- schema defaults and rejections
- no secrets, and the host is found by the save-time check
- scrape targets (IPv4, DNS name, IPv6, https), and that the integration is scrape-only
- parsing, including counters (the parser renames counter samples to `*_total`, so matching is on the family name)
- connection test: OK, https with TLS verification, a non-Telegraf page, HTTP errors, an oversized body, connect timeout and refusal (each with a firewall hint), its own timeout, and a refusal by the guard (no hint, no connect)
- device label text never appears in the result
- only `GET /metrics` is ever sent, with no auth header
- end to end, API → `/sd/targets`; denied hosts (loopback, metadata, rebinding name) get 422

`python scripts/check.py`: ruff, mypy, pytest (1000 passed, 1 skipped: ICMP sysctl), bandit and pip-audit all pass. The frontend step was skipped because Node isn't installed locally, and this PR has no frontend changes. gitleaks runs in CI.

## Contract questions
None.

## New dependencies
None. The page parser is `prometheus_client`'s, already in the stack.

## TODO(maintainer)
None in code. Note for the real-lab test: gateway latency and loss come from Telegraf's `ping` input, so you need one ping target per gateway. pfSense's dpinger data isn't exported by Telegraf by default. Custom Telegraf name prefixes would hide the metrics. Both are documented in `docs/integrations/pfsense.md`.

body:
## Problem

Any error establishing the first persistent session pinned the client to the slow one-shot transport for life: a dial timeout, a dropped connection, a cancelled `ctx`, or a handshake stall on the very first call meant every later call paid a fresh SSH connection plus a cold `powershell.exe` start, silently and with no log. The original error was also discarded.

Closes #170.

## Implementation

- New `replHandshakeError` type returned by `readReplReady`: a healthy SSH connection whose remote end does not speak the REPL bootstrap positively indicates a host without `pwsh.exe`.
- `Client.run` falls back to one-shot (with a `tflog` warning recording the reason) only for that error kind with a live context; dial/handshake/context errors are returned as-is, so the next call still establishes the persistent session.
- CHANGELOG entry.

## Tests

- New `TestFirstCallDialErrorDoesNotPinOneShot` (closed port: error surfaces, `oneShot` stays false), `TestFirstCallCancelledCtxDoesNotPinOneShot` (cancelled first call, then two live calls share exactly 1 connection), `TestOneShotFallbackIsLogged` (`tflogtest`-captured warn entry on the no-pwsh path).
- Negative check: all three fail on the pre-fix code, pass with the fix.
- Pre-existing `TestFallbackToOneShotWhenPwshMissing` and `TestTransportRecoversFromDroppedSession` still pass unchanged; full `go test -short ./...` green; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.
- Not run locally: `-race` (container TSan limitation) — covered by CI.

author: kcheng486
body:
## Summary

The driver logs through the root logger (`logging.info(...)`, 51 calls in `connection.py` and `driver.py`). An app that keeps root at WARNING, as the Wherobots MCP server does, can't see the driver's INFO lines without raising every library's logs to INFO. Those lines include `Reconnected to SQL session …; re-attaching N pending queries.` and `Attached to execution ….`. So today the MCP server's logs show a lost connection but never the reconnect or the re-attach (DB-760).

Each module now logs on `logging.getLogger(__name__)`. An app can then enable `wherobots.db.connection` alone. The messages, their levels and the redaction are unchanged.

What changes for callers:

- **Logger name.** Records carry `wherobots.db.connection` or `wherobots.db.driver` instead of `root`. A log pipeline that matches the driver's lines by `logger == "root"` would need updating.
- **No implicit `basicConfig()`.** The module-level `logging.info()` calls `basicConfig()` when root has no handlers. So until now the driver's first log line quietly configured root logging for any app that hadn't, which also changed how other libraries' logs printed. A named logger doesn't do that. In an app with no logging set up, the driver's warnings still reach stderr through Python's last-resort handler, but without the `WARNING:root:` prefix.

The `isEnabledFor(DEBUG)` guard on request redaction now checks the module logger, so enabling DEBUG on `wherobots.db.connection` alone turns it on.

The README gains a short Logging section that names the two loggers and shows how to enable the reconnect lines.

## Related Issues

DB-760. A follow-up in studio-backend enables `wherobots.db.connection` at INFO in the MCP server once this is released.

---

body:
## Nopen VRAM SWAP v0.7.0-dev — Real Linux GPU-backed swap pilot and Bannerlord measurement

### Implemented

- Linux `ublk` block target selects real AMD OpenCL GPU-backed worker with **explicit physical-host risk opt-in**, rooted device ownership and configurable 64/256/1024/2048/4096 MiB capacity. No silent RAM mock on the real host.
- Reuses fully checksummed 4KiB I/O, process-isolated GPU worker, per-request deadline, fail-closed recovery semantics from v0.6.
- Operator controller `v070/tools/vram_swap_lab.sh start/stop/status`: verifies actual GPU raw read/write, then executes `mkswap` and `swapon -p 200` on **only `/dev/ublkb23`**; preserves existing zram; `swapoff` must succeed before removing device.
- One-click reproducible `v070/tools/build_ublk.sh` uses upstream pinned `libublksrv` SHA and builds actual runnable target, controller and worker; no swap activation at build time.
- Game telemetry: `game_probe.py --mode off|on` records Bannerlord process-tree RSS, GPU VRAM/GTT, and **actual system-wide Nopen `/proc/swaps` USED KiB**, guarding against falsely claiming the game's private pages were identified; `compare_game.py` evaluates captured runs and optional plain frametime files.

### Real Linux kernel evidence (disposable GitHub virtual machine, MOCK backing)

- Real `/dev/ublkb24` created; O_DIRECT 4KiB write/read verified; `mkswap`, kernel `swapon -p 200`, and `swapoff` succeeded.
- cgroup pressure yielded **37,986,304 bytes** actual kernel swap usage; `V070_VM_PAGING_PASS` and `V070_VM_SWAP_PASS` recorded in CI run [40741992707](https://github.com/nopenstudio/nopen-vram-swap/actions/runs/40741992707).
- Regression, sanitizer and toolchain tests run under CI, with the v0.6 inherited suite.

### Not yet verified

- GPU-backed physical host `swapon` on user's RX 9060 XT, true AMDGPU reset survival, actual Bannerlord physical RAM savings, FPS/1% low and net system RAM savings.
- Huge memory pressure might deadlock OpenCL/AMDGPU in kernel reclaim; a forced PC reboot may be required. The user explicitly accepted this experimental risk. **Do not call this a stable SWAP feature**; first stable release is v1.0.

User guide: [v070/README_TR.md](v070/README_TR.md).
### v0.7 current tested head

- [**CI 40742658263: 3/3 successful**](https://github.com/nopenstudio/nopen-vram-swap/actions/runs/40742658263): unit regression (35/35), ASan/UBSan, and actual Linux kernel ublk swap activation/pressure/swapoff on disposable VM, MOCK GPU backend. 
- Linux cgroup memory pressure genuinely allocated >35MiB of swap on `/dev/ublkb24`; compare log `V070_VM_PAGING_PASS` and `V070_VM_SWAP_PASS`.
- On physical host script, backend is OpenCL-only, explicit consent and selected VRAM capacity required. `swapon -p 200` does **not** disable zram. RX 9060 XT physical acceptance still needed before game results can be asserted.
- Added best-effort -900 OOM adjustment and `mlock` of 64KiB staging in isolated GPU worker; neither protects AMDGPU driver itself against kernel reclaim deadlock.

### Host test commands

```bash
cd ~
git clone --branch develop/v0.7.0 --single-branch https://github.com/nopenstudio/nopen-vram-swap.git nopen-v070
cd ~/nopen-v070
bash v070/tools/build_ublk.sh
ctest --test-dir build-v070 --output-on-failure
sudo bash v070/tools/vram_swap_lab.sh start 256
bash v070/tools/vram_swap_lab.sh status
# AFTER TEST:
sudo bash v070/tools/vram_swap_lab.sh stop
```

See [v070/README_TR.md](v070/README_TR.md) for Bannerlord OFF/ON comparison workflow and hardware acceptance limitations.
## 28 Oct 2026 — real crash follow-up implementation (v0.7.0-dev)

After a real RX 9060 XT kernel swap WRITE timeout (~21:25:14 TRT), mass swap WRITE/READ failures and user-session teardown, code on this branch has been changed substantially:

- **Detached from user login**: the physical ublk daemon is now launched as a root `systemd-run --system` transient service, running under `system.slice` with OOM protections, rather than tied to `user@1000.service`. The disposable VM test created a real kernel block device in a root system service and checked the cgroup.
- **Durable disk authority**: a full, upfront initialized independent NVMe/SSD shadow file is created exclusively with `O_DIRECT | O_DSYNC`. All pages are written through SSD **before** GPU write ACK. On worker timeout, crash, GPU checksum mismatch or simulated loss, kernel I/O reads from verified shadow instead of returning unreadable swap pages; subsequent writes continue to shadow. Physical start requires this file and accepts only ext4/XFS in launcher.
- **Failure injection**: mock test forces 500ms worker hang, verifies 1024/1024 pages after failover, then corrupts on-disk backup and verifies fail-closed/unchanged caller output. Separate disposable Linux VM creates a real `ublk` block device, SIGKILLs GPU worker, verifies previously acknowledged 4KiB pages and new reads/writes via disk shadow.
- **Explicit physical test safeguard**: `v070/tools/vram_swap_lab.sh start` remains blocked, pending actual RX 9060 XT non-swap hardware shadow smoke and independent low-memory analysis. `stop` and `status` remain available.
- **Safe real-hardware acceptance CLI**: `nopen-shadow-smoke` tests OpenCL GPU worker + SSD write-through, intentionally terminates only worker (NOT physical GPU reset), verifies every page, and never registers kernel swap.
- **Cost**: disk write-through changes the architecture and will cost SSD capacity/write latency, so the GPU isn't proven faster than NVMe and full Linux reclaim deadlock-freedom is not proven. No claim that the physical incident is completely solved.

CI: 38/38 regressions and ASan/UBSan passed on [run 40750274103](https://github.com/nopenstudio/nopen-vram-swap/actions/runs/40750274103); disposable kernel VM job being verified for this exact commit. Prior [run 40749560758](https://github.com/nopenstudio/nopen-vram-swap/actions/runs/40749560758) succeeded 3/3 and recorded `SYSTEM_UNIT_VM_PASS`, `V070_SHADOW_VM_PASS` and actual mock-backed Linux `swapon/swapoff` + paging.

Incident and technical limitations: [Issue #7](https://github.com/nopenstudio/nopen-vram-swap/issues/7). Source and safe hardware commands: [v070/README_TR.md](v070/README_TR.md).

## Actual RX 9060 XT non-swap shadow acceptance (user log, 28 Oct 2026)

Host: Garuda Linux 7.2.11-zen1-1-zen, gfx1200 RX 9060 XT. Real OpenCL+SSD shadow run:

```text
Nopen v0.12 selected discrete GPU: gfx1200; GPU reservation=64 MiB
V070_SHADOW_HARDWARE_RESULT backend=opencl capacity_mib=64 operations=1000 writes=485 reads=515 verified_pages=16384 shadow_fallback_reads=16638 gpu_failures=1 disk_failures=0 elapsed_s=1.024885 parent_maxrss_kib=67860 forced_worker_loss=YES real_gpu_reset=NO kernel_swap=NO
V070_SHADOW_HARDWARE_PASS all_pages_verified=YES read_after_worker_loss=YES write_after_worker_loss=YES no_global_swap=YES no_physical_gpu_reset=YES
```

**Hardware GPU-worker-loss + independent SSD fallback confirmed.** This is not physical GPU reset and not kernel SWAP.

Local CTest on Garuda initially got **37/38**, only `v070_durable_disk_shadow_survives_gpu_worker_timeout` failed during `nopen_shadow_open()`. Source inspection found test fixture incorrectly hardcoded `/tmp/nopen-shadow-ci-XXXXXX`; Nopen explicitly rejects tmpfs backing (common Garuda `/tmp`) and did so before test I/O. The *actual GPU hardware test* using `$HOME` SSD directory passed. Regression corrected in commits `d93e9b7b`, `ae013b01`: fixture is created inside the actual absolute CMake build directory rather than `/tmp`; added explicit tmpfs rejection diagnostic + preserved `posix_fallocate` error reporting in `7675326b`.

Hardware re-test needed ONLY for the corrected mock CTest; real OpenCL shadow acceptance already passed. Still keep physical kernel `swapon` activation blocked pending crash-resilience/reclaim validation.

author: pablopunk
body:
### Why

Users on a normal (non-tiling) macOS desktop have no keyboard way to move focus to the neighbouring window. Tiling window managers give this for free.

### What this PR does

- Adds Focus Window Left, Right, Up and Down as built-in commands.
- Adds a neighbour engine with soft-cone scoring (ideas from Hammerspoon, Navigation2D and sway), coincident-stack cycling, nested and occluded window handling, display preference and optional wrap.
- Adds a host `focusNeighbor` service and the OS-neutral extension API method `ctx.desktop.windowManagement.focusNeighbor`.
- Adds a macOS helper `window all` that lists every window in one call with z-order, and maps sheets to their parent window origin.

### How to test it

No local runtime verification was done (CI-only repo rule), so there are no screenshots. Unit tests cover the engine, listing, display preference, host service and commands.

Manual check on macOS: open several windows side by side, run each command, and confirm focus moves to the expected neighbour.

Known unverified: raise reliability on macOS 14+, other Spaces, minimized windows and Stage Manager, and helper latency with many windows.

### How are we measuring impact?

- Success signal: the commands run without window-management errors.
- Failure signal: `focusNeighbor` failure logs, or reports of focus not moving.

### Potential risk for production

New macOS-only behavior, not exercised locally; edge setups above may focus the wrong window or be slow. It runs only on user invocation, and the API method is additive.

author: joshmiles
body:
## Changelog
Audience: admin
Title: Twitch events in TCG Bridge
Tags: new
- TCG Bridge now listens to the connected Twitch channel's events (channel points, cheers, gifted subs, raids, stream online and offline) and the Mix It Up page lists the latest ones. It only records them for now; nothing is awarded.

## Summary

ROADMAP 58.2. When the site has a Twitch channel connected (58.1), TCG Bridge opens Twitch's EventSub WebSocket, creates six Helix subscriptions for each new session and hands every notification to the site. The site records the event and awards nothing; Mix It Up event handling is untouched.

**App** (`bridge/src/eventsub.ts`, a new `EventSubClient` owned by `BridgeService`):
- "Connected" is `POST /api/bridge/twitch-token` answering 200. 404 = none connected (quiet), 409 = Twitch ended it, 403 = this PC may not listen.
- Handles welcome, keepalive (Twitch's timeout plus 10 s, then the socket is dropped and reopened), reconnect (old socket kept until the new welcome, no duplicate subscriptions), revocation and notification.
- The token is renewed before it expires and after a Helix 401, and is never logged.
- Notifications go to the site in order, three tries each.
- State shows on the Connections page (Twitch channel row and detail with numbered fix steps), the status pill, a Home chip, and is reported to the site. A spare account shows "Testing on <login>, not the live channel".
- Alerts when EventSub drops while live and when it returns, with the same rules as the other parts.

**Site**:
- `POST /api/bridge/twitch-event` (admin PC only) records the event, dedupes the message id for 10 minutes (`SET NX EX 600`) and keeps a capped list of the last 30.
- `stream.online` and `stream.offline` feed `setLiveFromBridge`.
- `POST /api/bridge/report` takes `type: 'twitch'` (admin PC only).
- The token route also returns `clientId` and `testing`.

**Decisions**
- `stream.online` and `stream.offline` do not feed the live state when the connected account is a test account (not `CHANNEL_LOGIN`), so a spare account's stream cannot mark the real channel live.
- The "feed" is the Connection tab's recent-events list; the app's own event feed is 58.5.
- Events for a channel other than the connected one are ignored.
- The Twitch row and Home chip stay quiet while no channel is connected. "Not allowed on this PC" shows on the row but not in the pill.
- The pill only reports a red or subscription problem, and only while the site link is up.
- The same message id is deduped in the app and again on the site.
- The recheck of the site doubles as the token renewal (every 5 minutes, or earlier before expiry).

## TCG Bridge
- The app now listens to Twitch events for the channel connected on the site: channel point redemptions, cheers, gifted subs, raids, and the stream going online or offline. It passes them to the site, which records them; nothing is awarded yet.
- Setup > Connections has a new Twitch channel connection with its state in words and numbered fix steps, the status pill and Home show when Twitch events need attention, and a spare Twitch account shows "Testing on <login>, not the live channel".
- You get a Windows notification when the Twitch event link drops while you are live, and another when it is back.

## Docs

body:
Step 3 of the October 27 code review (`docs/CODE_REVIEW_OCTOBER_27_2026.md`): it closes two gaps in the release gate.

## Changes

- **Required CI jobs (#29).** `release-check` now requires each job in the new `RELEASE_REQUIRED_JOBS` in the `Makefile` to have run for the release commit and passed. The list covers CI's `build`, `tla`, `rules`, and `helm`; the container tests and `helm-smoke`; both image scans; `codeql`; and zizmor's `code-scanning`. The check reads HEAD's workflow runs and their jobs from the Actions API and names each job by workflow file as well as job name, because `ci.yml` and `docs.yml` both have a job called `build`. Before this change, any non-empty list of passing checks was enough. With `[skip ci]` or a disabled workflow, a single third-party check such as Codacy could make up that whole list. The rule that every check must pass still applies.
- **Complete version bumps (#30).** A bumped file now fails if it still has the previous release's version, read from the `CHANGELOG.md` section below the new one, in a place step 2 of `docs/RELEASE.md` bumps. Those places are image tags and the Maven coordinate, `<version>`, a chart's `version` and `appVersion`, and the backticked examples. Historical mentions such as "Version 4.3.0 (released …)" don't count. Until now, a file passed if the new version appeared anywhere in it, so a chart with the new `version` but the old `appVersion` passed and would have deployed the old image. `RELEASE_VERSION_FILES` now also lists `docs/RELEASE.md` and the release skill, which step 2 bumps.
- **Docs.** `docs/RELEASE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the release skill, the `build.gradle.kts` comment, and both changelogs describe the new checks. The review marks #29, #30, and step 3 done, and its plan table gains a Status column.

## Verification

`release-check` itself runs only on a clean `master` with the GPG setup in place, so I ran its new parts on their own:

- **Required jobs:**
  - `master`'s HEAD (`c4a2303`), where every workflow passed: the check passes.
  - `778f2df`, a commit CI never ran on: the check fails and lists all ten jobs.
  - An invalid `GH_TOKEN`: the check fails with "could not read HEAD's workflow runs".
- **Stale versions,** tested on a scratch copy of the bumped files:
  - Unbumped, with `VERSION=4.4.0`: the check flags exactly the 49 lines the release bump changes, and no historical mention.
  - After a full bump: the check passes.
  - With one chart's `appVersion` and one README tag left at 4.3.0: the check reports both lines.
- `make -n release-check` parses, and `./gradlew detekt lintKotlinMain build -x test` passes.

body:
This fixes a flake from #304 in `src/main/org/org-session.test.ts` that hit class 1a runs on master. The change touches tests only.

The failure was in run 40740419061: "logs each attempt's start and its end, a cancel included…" expected `attempt 1: cancelled at approval` and received `attempt 1: cancelled at checking`.

## Cause

The test waited for the hub's pending count to rise, then cancelled straight away. But the session posts the device's entry before it moves to the approval step: `postPending` resolves, then `await pairingFingerprint(...)` runs, and only then does `step({step: 'approval'})` (`org-session.ts:747-750`). Under load, the cancel landed while the step still read `checking`.

## Fix

Both cancels in that test now wait for the session's status to read the approval step, as the neighbouring test already does.

reviewer-low found the same early-cancel shape in "cancel stops the wait for approval…" (line 502). That test passed either way but did not guarantee the coverage its name promises, so it gets the same wait.

## Validation Evidence

- `npx vitest run --project node src/main/org/org-session.test.ts`: 59 passed (59).

## Give bare literals their units (EarthSciDiscretizations)

> **Updated:** angle literals (deg↔rad factors, 2π, radius per radian) now carry rad.

Generated by EarthSciAST's `scripts/codemod-dimensionless-literals.py` (EarthSciAST PRs #575, #584, #586). At the next major esm version a bare numeric literal is dimensionless (esm-spec §4.8.6). This PR writes the unit each literal carries as `const(value, units "U")`, raises files that gain one to esm 1.2.0, and gives genuine angle literals their `rad`. A site where an angular quantity such as `rad/s` meets a quantity without the angle (the Coriolis pattern) is left for the model author and listed under Unresolved. No value changes and no file changes validity.

**Review the suspicious rewrites and the declaration changes first.** A suspicious rewrite such as `const(-1, units "1/cm^3")` usually hides a real unit error in the model (a missing variable or a wrong declaration): it makes the site check, but it should be reviewed rather than merged blind.

- .esm files scanned: 829
- files with `units_dimensionless_literal_mismatch` warnings: 233 (484 warning sites)
- files with a proposed patch: 195 (esm bumped to 1.2.0 in 0)
