author: gonandrap
body:
## Summary

A pending assumption on a project with auto-review off rendered as its text and an age,
and nothing else. That project writes no `autoreview_*` event at all, so every sentence
the card can show came from a ruling that does not exist — the reader could not tell
that nobody had looked at it yet, and the feedback placeholder's "teaches Neo" read as
"Neo already ruled here". The worker's reasoning was only findable by scrolling the
Conversation tab.

The card now says why the assumption is with the user, links the worker turn that raised
it, and `jarvis wo show` prints the same sentence.

Fixes issue #1265.

## Implementation notes

- **The routing line fires only when `assumption_ruling_line` is empty.** Escalated,
  held and asked-Neo already have sentences with question links; the gap was a pending
  row with no ruling at all. Rejected adding a fourth phrasing beside them — it would
  have put two "who looked at this" lines on every escalated row.
- **`ops.autoreview_off_because` names the switch that is actually off**, and
  `auto_review_at` is now its negation. The issue asked for the fixed text
  "validation.enabled / validation.auto_review", which points at the wrong knob when
  `os.neo.enabled` is what is off — a line sending the reader to the wrong setting is
  the same defect being fixed here. One function, so the boolean and the prose cannot
  drift.
- **The source link needs no schema column.** `jarvis wo assume` cannot know a message
  id: the turn-ending reply is written afterwards, by `record_agent_reply` in
  `worker_session.py`. So the first agent reply an assumption precedes *is* the turn
  that raised it, and `ops.assumption_source_ref` resolves it to the `#msg-…` anchor the
  Conversation tab and the timeline refs already use. Rejected scanning message bodies
  for "assumption #N" — that matches a later turn discussing an older assumption.
- **Both facts are attached in `assumptions_with_rulings`**, the single enrichment point
  all three callers read, so the CLI and the page agree by construction rather than by
  assertion. The catalog is read only when a pending row actually lacks a ruling.
- **`assumption_routing_line` distinguishes an absent key from an empty one.** A row
  that never went through `assumptions_with_rulings` (a legacy row, a hand-built dict)
  gets `""`, because defaulting would word the commonest case backwards. Start reading
  there if anything looks wrong.
- **The placeholder claim was checked, not assumed.** `ops.review_work_order` calls
  `_teach_assumption_rules` unconditionally — gated on neither `validation.auto_review`
  nor `os.neo.enabled` — so feedback does become a Neo rule on every project. Hiding the
  phrase when auto-review is off, as the issue asked, would have made the UI assert
  something false. Reworded instead to drop the implication that Neo had already ruled.
- **Risk:** two tests that pinned the old silence now pin the new line, and
  `test_an_assumption_in_an_auto_review_off_project_grows_no_lines` is renamed
  `..._grows_only_its_routing_line`. That is the behaviour change the issue asked for,
  but it is a changed string on a surface other tests read.

## Questions asked to Neo

- Whether to implement the issue's item 3 literally, given that its premise (feedback
  teaches Neo only when auto-review is on) is false in the code —
  http://localhost:8787/neo/question/10. Answer: reword to keep the true claim and let
  the new routing line carry the correction.

## Alarms raised

- None. `jarvis alarms --wo wo-b551682a` reports `no cost alarm has ever been raised
  against wo-b551682a`.

## Learnings

- `kn-fdd11961` — user feedback on an assumption review ALWAYS becomes a Neo rule;
  "Neo reviews assumptions" and "feedback teaches Neo" are independent facts, and the
  issue conflated them.
- `kn-5c355230` — `ops.assumptions_with_rulings` is the one place an assumption row is
  enriched, and a renderer fed an un-enriched row must tell an absent key from an empty
  one.

## Test evidence

| Kind | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit / integration | `uv run pytest tests/test_ui.py tests/test_validation_surfaces.py tests/test_autoreview.py tests/test_autoreview_confirm.py tests/test_assumption_objection_view.py tests/test_assumption_early_state.py tests/test_repair_resettle.py tests/test_feature_orders.py tests/test_schema_upgrade.py tests/test_neo_stats_rows.py -q` | 784 passed. Full suite on CI. |
| UI | `uv run pytest tests/test_ui.py tests/test_validation_surfaces.py tests/test_assumption_objection_view.py` | 304 passed, including the new `test_a_pending_assumption_says_who_it_waits_on_and_links_its_turn`, which asserts the routing line, the `#msg-N` link resolving to an anchor on the same page, and the absence of "teaches Neo". |
| Eval | not run locally — `pytest evals -q` on CI | see checks |
| A/B | n/a — no prompt, contract or heuristic changed. The one new sentence is rendered text pinned by the tests above, not model input. |

Also run: `uv run python scripts/trim_comments.py --check` reports
`0 file(s) would change, 0 refused`.

## How to validate in production

The routing line appears on any `needs_review` order with a pending assumption, which
this project produces routinely.

- After the next work order reaches `needs_review` with an assumption,
  `jarvis wo show <wo-id>` prints the pending row with a `With you because …` clause
  naming a setting, instead of the bare `#1 pending your review: <text>` it printed
  before.
- The same order's page at `/wo/<project>/<wo-id>` shows that clause under the
  assumption plus a `the turn that raised it →` link, and the link's `#msg-N` target is
  an `id` on the same page.
- The string `teaches Neo` no longer appears anywhere in a work order page's HTML;
  `recorded as a rule for Neo` does.
- A count that should move: orders sitting in `needs_review` with pending assumptions
  should not grow — the line exists so the user can decide rather than go looking for a
  Neo verdict that was never asked for.

## Screenshots

![The assumptions card: the routing line, the source link and the reworded placeholder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gonandrap/agentic_os/d8efdbccd2e2ea4aee7cba168b9b35ddf648f22d/docs/screenshots/wo-1265-assumption-routing.png)

body:
> Depends on #8. This branch includes #8's commit, because GitHub cannot stack PRs from a fork. Review #8 first; the diff here gets smaller once it merges.

## Problem and resulting behavior

The public skills were adapted from the Creator skill library at revision `811c78c` on Oct 16. The library has improved since then, so the public skills are behind. This PR adapts every change from `811c78c` to `da3aa8b` for agents that only have the Voiceflow MCP, the `vf` CLI and the docs MCP. Only behavior that holds for any MCP or CLI client was carried over.

It is the first run of a scheduled sync. `docs/creator-sync.json` records the synced revision and date, so the next run applies only what changed after it, and does nothing when nothing did.

| Skill | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [Build](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-build/SKILL.md) | Adds the Initialization workflow read and set, launch values in `last_event`, one place for the greeting, the four ways a workflow runs, and a link to the working-environment rule. |
| [Debug](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-debug/SKILL.md) | Adds targeted log queries for transcripts and test runs, turn numbering, and links to two new references. |
| [Environments](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-environments/SKILL.md) | Adds where to make a change (propose a working environment for a live project, clone only after the user agrees), publish then merge, and what to do when Main moved. |
| [Evaluations](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-evaluations/SKILL.md) | Adds the scripted conversation run, rules for writing tests, bounded run reads, cancelling runs, and the tool-call audit before reporting. |
| [Functions](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-functions/SKILL.md) | Adds checking a function on boundary cases with expected outputs, only for self-contained code, and links to two new references. |
| [Integrations](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-integrations/SKILL.md) | Integration tools are now added over the MCP before they are attached. Credentials go to the shared CLI handoffs, OAuth to the UI. |
| [Knowledge](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-knowledge/SKILL.md) | Adds managed sitemap import and how to replace a text document's content. |
| [Messages](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-messages/SKILL.md) | Adds the project text search, finding every owner of a message or prompt, and safe deletion. |
| [Phone numbers](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-phone-numbers/SKILL.md) | New skill: which side a number uses, adding a number through the CLI handoff or the UI, and assigning, moving, renaming and deleting numbers over the MCP. |
| [Prompting](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-prompting/SKILL.md) | Unchanged: the only change was about loading another skill in the app. |
| [Transcripts](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-transcripts/SKILL.md) | Adds targeted log queries and turn numbering. |
| [Voice](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-voice/SKILL.md) | Adds the pronunciation dictionary and its patch, that the voice reads screen symbols aloud, and a link to Phone numbers. |
| [Wiring](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-wiring/SKILL.md) | Adds merge-by-key attachment updates, removing phantom inputs, progress counters, a full wiring check, and links to two new references. |
| [Workflows](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow-workflows/SKILL.md) | Adds the raw read, End step rules, batch block and link writes, action replace, arranging, duplicating, and global workflow tools. |
| Shared | New [CLI handoffs](voiceflow/skills/voiceflow/references/cli-handoffs.md): when the MCP refuses an action, such as setting a secret value, the agent gives the user a `vf` command to run in their own terminal, with the value read from a hidden prompt. The operation contract now proposes a working environment for live projects. The index routes to Phone numbers. |
| References | Ported in full: Debug `bulk-analysis.md` and `failure-patterns.md`, Functions `sensitive-inputs.md` and `custom-traces.md`, Wiring `patterns.md` and `anti-patterns.md`. |

**Not ported:**

- Coach: it runs only inside a scheduled in-app review routine.
- In-app cards, approval modes, question pickers, display widgets and plan tools. Public agents ask in plain text and use host approvals.
- Results produced by the in-app merge approval, such as a refused merge after the approval was shown. The product facts behind them were kept.

author: diegopereiran
body:
## Thinking Path

> - AlpacaBridge is the open source server that runs native ASCOM Alpaca drivers on a single-board computer at the telescope
> - The web UI Wi-Fi manager edits NetworkManager profiles through `WifiManager::save_profile`
> - NetworkManager `Update` replaces the whole profile with the settings it receives
> - For an existing profile, `save_profile` sent a small rebuilt profile, so static IP, BSSID lock and 802.1x settings were lost and `key-mgmt` became `wpa-psk`
> - A board that lost its static address comes back on a DHCP address, and a WPA3 or enterprise network stops working
> - This pull request reads the stored settings back and changes only the keys that the request sets
> - The benefit is that a change of priority or autoconnect no longer damages a profile made with `nmcli`

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Fixes #1690

## What Changed

- `AlpacaHTTP/src/util/wifi_manager.cpp`: new `WifiProfileBackend::patch_connection`. It reads the stored settings, applies the given keys and sends the result to `Update`. It generalises the copy that `pin_interface_name` did. `save_profile` uses it for an existing profile, and `connect_profile` uses it for the interface pin.
- `save_profile` changes only `autoconnect`, `autoconnect-priority`, `interface-name` and a given `psk`. It keeps the stored `key-mgmt` and writes `wpa-psk` only when the profile has no security section. It writes `id` only when the stored profile has none.
- `AlpacaHTTP/include/alpacahttp/wifi_manager.h`: declares `patch_connection` on the backend interface.
- `AlpacaHTTP/tests/test_wifi_manager.cpp`: the fake backend applies a patch to its stored settings, and two new cases check what survives.
- `changelog.d/`: one fragment.
- New profiles and the hotspot path (`set_ap`) work as before.

## Falsified by

- "WifiManager keeps every stored setting when it edits an existing profile": AlpacaHTTP/src/util/wifi_manager.cpp:1202 call `update_connection` with the rebuilt settings instead of `patch_connection`
- "WifiManager sets a new passphrase on an existing profile and keeps its other sections": AlpacaHTTP/src/util/wifi_manager.cpp:1197 always add `key-mgmt` `wpa-psk` when a passphrase is given

## Decision records

- None. Checked against 0007 (Wi-Fi API surface) and 0013.

## Verification

- `test_wifi_manager`: the new "keeps every stored setting" case fails on the base source (the `ipv4` section is dropped) and passes with the fix. The target passes with 11 cases.
- `clang-format-18 --dry-run --Werror` is clean on the changed source files. The quick pre-flight passes.
- Not tested on hardware or against a real NetworkManager: only the fake backend runs the merge. The real sd-bus copy is the code that `connect_profile` used before this change. Full ctest, sanitizers and the arm64 build run in pull request CI.

## Risks

- Low risk. A saved passphrase on a stored WEP, OWE or `wpa-eap` profile keeps that security type, so the new passphrase has no effect there. Before this change the profile switched to `wpa-psk`.
- The sibling hotspot path `set_ap` still rebuilds its profile and is not changed here.

## Model Used

Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5.5, `claude-sonnet-5-5`), with shell, file edits and test runs.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have specified the model used (with version and capability details)
- [x] I have searched GitHub for duplicate or related issues and pull requests and linked them above

- [x] I have not referenced private or internal tracker ids or links (only public GitHub `#NNN` / `github.com/open-astro/AlpacaBridge` URLs)
- [x] My branch name describes the change (e.g. `docs/...`, `fix/...`) and contains no private tracker id

- [x] I have run the targeted tests locally and they pass

author: ceendi
body:
## Problem i zachowanie po zmianie

Po #274 Alloy i SeaweedFS nadal miały blokujące podatności, a cache warstw obrazu pomijał kolejne poprawki dystrybucji. Aktualizacja SeaweedFS ujawniła również błędne kryterium gotowości: listowanie S3 i tworzenie bucketów działa przed pełną gotowością zapisu. Powodowało to timeout pierwszego PUT w teście orchestratora oraz PUT po restarcie w teście uprawnień S3.

Bootstrap kończy się teraz dopiero po rzeczywistym zapisie i usunięciu małego obiektu w każdym buckecie. Usługi zależne czekają więc na działającą ścieżkę zapisu, a nie tylko odpowiedź API metadanych.

## Zmiany

- Alloy v1.20.1 → v1.21.3, z przypiętym digestem; istniejąca łatka OpenSSL pozostaje.
- SeaweedFS 4.48 → 4.51 w Compose i teście integracyjnym orchestratora.
- AWS CLI w `seaweedfs-bucket-init`: **2.38.1 → 2.38.6**, wyłącznie zmiana tagu w Compose. Skan oficjalnego obrazu Trivy 0.75.0: **15 HIGH → 0 HIGH i 0 CRITICAL**. Bez własnego obrazu, nowych zależności ani zmian skryptu bootstrapu z powodu tego podbicia.
- Grafana pozostaje na 13.2.5. Wycofano nieskuteczne podbicie do 13.3.0: oba obrazy zawierają pluginy z Go 1.26.7 i CVE-2026-56857. Najnowszym oficjalnym wydaniem podczas weryfikacji nadal było 13.3.0.
- Właściciel repozytorium 2026-10-29 wyraźnie zaakceptował czasowy wyjątek dla CVE-2026-56857 w Grafanie **do końca 12 listopada 2026, Europe/Warsaw**. `infra/security/accepted-risks.json` dopasowuje dokładny tag i digest obrazu, `stdlib v1.26.7` oraz sześć ścieżek binarek pluginów. Wygasa automatycznie o `2026-11-13T00:00:00+01:00`. Zmiana digestu, inna ścieżka/paczka lub nowy CRITICAL nadal blokują job.
- Akceptacja zmienia tylko wynik bramki skanu Compose: pełne JSON/SARIF/Code Scanning nadal zawierają podatność, summary liczy rzeczywiste CRITICAL i pokazuje liczbę zaakceptowanych, a job emituje ostrzeżenie. Nie ma `.trivyignore`, `continue-on-error` ani wyjątku w bramce publikacji obrazów. Po wygaśnięciu CVE ponownie blokuje job. Testy sprawdzają też dokładną granicę daty i brak filtrowania raportu.
- `seaweedfs-bucket-init` wykonuje podpisany PUT/DELETE obiektu `.bootstrap/<hostname>` w obu bucketach. Test S3 dodatkowo sprawdza brak pozostawionych obiektów diagnostycznych. Po celowo nieudanym renderowaniu konfiguracji i restarcie ponownie wykonuje ten sam bootstrap przed niezmienionymi asercjami uprawnień.
- `ArtifactCleanupSeaweedIntegrationTest` sprawdza zapis w fazie gotowości. Klient tej fazy korzysta z dotychczasowego budżetu startu 90 s; żądania właściwego scenariusza nadal mają limity 5 s / 2 s. Próba gotowości nie jest przedwcześnie przerywana, aby opóźniony PUT nie odtworzył już usuniętego obiektu. Asercje sprzątania i uprawnień pozostają bez osłabienia.
- `build-push.yml`: cotygodniowy rebuild w poniedziałek o 03:23 UTC oraz ręczne `no-cache`. Skanowany build używa `no-cache` i `pull`, a publikacja nie importuje starych warstw GHA. Publikacja ręczna tylko z `main`; bramka Trivy, model smoke, attestacje i tagi `sha-<commit>` / `latest` pozostają.
- Dokumentacja gotowości storage i przebudowy obrazów oraz test strażnik cotygodniowego rebuilda.

## Przyczyna i odtworzenie

- Przed poprawką lokalny `test_bootstrap_restart_atomic_failure_and_real_signed_scopes` kończył się timeoutem admin PUT po restarcie na 4.51; porównanie z 4.50 odtworzyło ten sam błąd. Po dodatkowych 15 s ten sam zapis kończył się 200. Master miał już lidera i zapisywalne wolumeny, lecz wcześniejsza odpowiedź listowania nie gwarantowała jeszcze gotowości całej ścieżki zapisu.
- Przed poprawką `ArtifactCleanupSeaweedIntegrationTest` padał na pierwszym zapisie po 5 s. Ten sam scenariusz po poprawce przeszedł bez zwiększania timeoutów jego właściwych żądań.
- Upstream opisuje zmianę gotowości pierwszego zapisu w [zgłoszeniu #12058](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/issues/12058) i [poprawce #12059](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/pull/12059). Nie wyłączamy zabezpieczenia topologii ani nie zmieniamy jego progów.

## Dotknięte obszary

Infra: Alloy, SeaweedFS, bootstrap S3, publikacja obrazów i dokumentacja. Orchestrator: wyłącznie konfiguracja i gotowość rzeczywistego storage w teście integracyjnym. Zmiana zachowania startu storage — do przeglądu przez Osobę 1.

## Weryfikacja

- Odtworzenie obu czerwonych scenariuszy przed poprawką: potwierdzone lokalnie.
- `mvnw.cmd -B -ntp verify -Dtest=ArtifactCleanupSeaweedIntegrationTest -Dsurefire.rerunFailingTestsCount=0`: PASS.
- `python infra/tests/test_security_configuration.py`, `test_ci_reliability.py`, `test_e2e_ml.py`: 32 testy PASS.
- `python infra/tests/test_s3_configuration.py`: PASS (4 scenariusze S3 i 6 testów renderera, w tym restarty, izolacja wewnętrznych API i sprzątanie po timeoutcie uploadu).
- CI dla `b969d9a`: wszystkie 8 wymaganych checków PASS, w tym pełne `mvnw verify` orchestratora (502 testy), SonarCloud Quality Gate i Playwright. Infrastructure smoke i Security scan PASS. Brak oczekujących lub nieudanych checków.
- `python infra/tests/test_security_report.py`: 10 testów PASS, w tym dokładna granica wygaśnięcia, wszystkie ograniczenia zakresu, nowe CRITICAL jako blokujące i niezmieniony surowy raport. Na rzeczywistym raporcie Grafany: `CRITICAL: 6`, `Accepted CRITICAL: 6; blocking CRITICAL: 0`, ostrzeżenie z datą i przesłany pełny SARIF.
- Pełne lokalne `mvnw.cmd -B -ntp verify`: PASS, z `PYTHONUTF8=1` i `DETECTOR_TEST_PYTHON` wskazującym izolowane środowisko z `audio-detector/tests/requirements-light.txt` (domyślny `python3` na tym Windowsie jest aliasem Windows Store).
- `git diff --check`: PASS.

## Wyniki skanów per obraz

Końcowe wyniki CI dla `b969d9a`:

| Obraz | Build + bramka Trivy | Skan Compose |
|---|---|---|
| gateway | PASS | PASS |
| eureka-server | PASS | PASS |
| orchestrator | PASS | PASS |
| file-service | PASS | PASS |
| video-detector | PASS | PASS |
| audio-detector | PASS | PASS |
| keycloak | PASS | PASS |
| frontend | PASS | PASS |
| postgres (keycloak-db) | PASS | PASS |
| keycloak-config-cli | PASS | PASS |
| alloy (v1.21.3) | PASS | PASS |
| seaweedfs (4.51) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| grafana (13.2.5) | obraz upstream | PASS z ostrzeżeniem: 6 wystąpień CVE-2026-56857 czasowo zaakceptowanych do końca 12.11.2026 |
| loki (3.7.9) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| prometheus (v3.15.1) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| tempo (3.1.1) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| rabbitmq (4.3.6-management-alpine) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| rabbitmq-init (Python 3.14.10 Alpine) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| redis (8.10.2-alpine) | obraz upstream | PASS |
| seaweedfs-bucket-init (AWS CLI 2.38.6) | obraz upstream | PASS: 0 HIGH, 0 CRITICAL (poprzednio 15 HIGH) |

Łącznie: 11/11 buildów z bramką Trivy PASS i 20/20 bramek skanów Compose PASS. Grafana nadal ma 6 CRITICAL i 35 HIGH w pełnym raporcie; znane CRITICAL są objęte wyraźnie zatwierdzoną, wygasającą akceptacją. PASS oznacza brak niezaakceptowanego blokującego wyniku, a nie brak podatności.

## Ograniczenia

- Grafana 13.2.5 nadal ma wskazane CVE w sześciu dołączonych pluginach; główna binarka Grafany używa już Go 1.26.10. Weryfikacja najnowszych oficjalnych pluginów wykazała poprawione Loki 13.2.4, Jaeger 13.0.7 i MSSQL 13.0.9, ale nadal podatne PostgreSQL 13.0.4, InfluxDB 13.1.7 i MySQL 13.1.4. Właściciel wybrał pozostanie przy oficjalnym obrazie oraz czasową, wąsko ograniczoną akceptację do 12 listopada. Podatność pozostaje widoczna; nie dodano wyjątków Sonara. Po poprawce upstream należy usunąć akceptację, a jej przedłużenie wymaga ponownej zgody.

author: aletuan
body:
The owner asked on 28 Oct 2026 whether Explore's date and weather refresh when the city changes. Both refresh, and both have a fault, fixed here.

## Weather (`lib/sky.tsx`)

When the city changed and the new city had no cached reading yet, the hook kept the previous city's state:
- While the request was in flight, Đà Lạt showed Sài Gòn's 30°.
- If the request failed or hit the 6-second cap, that 30° stayed indefinitely.

Now a place with no reading of its own shows nothing until its reading arrives. A city's own stale reading is still shown while it refreshes, as before, so switching back to a city does not flicker.

## Date (`lib/format.ts` → `dayline`)

The hero line ("WEDNESDAY 28") was built from the phone's clock (`getDay` / `getDate`).
- This is invisible for the nine Vietnamese cities, which share Vietnam's time zone.
- Melbourne runs 3–4 hours ahead of Vietnam. From 20:00 or 21:00 Vietnam time, the hero showed yesterday for Melbourne.

`dayline` now takes the city's zone and reads the day from `wallClock`. That is the same reading opening hours already use; `Hero` passes `city.tz`, which defaults to Vietnam.

## Tests

- `sky.ui.test`: a new city shows nothing while its request is in flight, and still nothing when that request fails. Both new tests fail against the old code.
- `format.test`:
  - Every `dayline` call now passes a zone.
  - A new Melbourne case: 14:00 UTC is "Wednesday 28" in Vietnam and "Thursday 29" in Melbourne.
  - Two deliberately broken versions each turn the suite red: one without the Monday→Sunday shift, one that reads the phone's clock.

## Gates

- typecheck and lint pass.
- test, test:tz and coverage each pass 5,871/5,871.

author: joshualeestone
body:
## Why

The 0.7.73 staging cut stopped at step 4b on 2026-10-28 at 17:03 CDT (kosmos#1050). The sandboxed install passed (165 passed, 0 failed). Then the bundle-against-tree check refused with:

> not in the tree: app/release-notes.json

`tools/build-kosmos-bundle.sh` writes that file (kosmos#7411 step 1, merged that morning), so the tree has no file of that name to compare with. Nothing was served; staging still serves 0.7.72. This unblocks the re-cut.

## Change

`tools/lib/release-freeze.sh`, `release_bundle_matches_tree`: for `app/release-notes.json`, it makes the notes again from the frozen tree with the build's own command (`whats-new-pool.js notes <version> --platform=mac`, the tree's pool) and requires them byte-identical.
- A tree without the tool refuses: it cannot vouch for notes.
- A tool that fails refuses with its own reason.
- A stale or hand-edited notes file is still caught. The check is not skipped and the file is not allowlisted.

The inputs are the build's: the same frozen tree (`REPO=$BUILD`), the version from the same package.json, the same platform, the same pool. `notesFor` is deterministic. Both call sites in release.sh (steps 4b and the post-serve check) look only at the Mac tarball; Linux and Windows build their own notes and do not pass through here.

## Tests

`tools/test-release-detached.sh` (in test:shell) gains:
- a matching bundle passes
- edited notes are caught and named
- a tool that fails (a pool that is not JSON) refuses with its reason
- a tree without the tool refuses
- a control that the fixture's notes were made by the real tool

Shown able to fail: on the unfixed check the matching case fails with the cut's exact error, and removing the failing-tool refusal turns that case red.

Full suite: 25538 tests, 0 failed. Challenge loop converged at round 2 (opus, then sonnet).

Addresses kosmos#7411 (a follow-up to step 1) and the 0.7.73 cut on kosmos#1050.

body:
[32-frontend-2] What the tenant web shows when its plan closes something.

The API is the guard. The tenant web now closes what the plan does not allow and says why. Work is in `apps/web` and `docs/frontend/` only (plus the lockfile line of the new workspace dependency).

## What changed, item by item

**The helper.** `apps/web/src/shared/plan.ts`: `usePlan()` reads `GetMyTenant.entitlements` and `GetMyTenant.usage` and answers, for a key: on or off; the limit (`null` is unlimited); the count; `atLimit`; `overLimit`; `full` (at or over). A missing key is closed: a feature off, a limit 0. No screen compares numbers itself. `use-plan-reason.ts` holds the texts; `plan-banner.tsx` is the over-limit banner with its one link, "Contact us", to `brand.supportUrl` (`@repo/brand`).

1. **Roles.** The count comes from `usage["roles.custom.max"]` ("15 of 20 custom roles"); unlimited shows no count. At the limit "Create role" is disabled with the reason in place of the count. Over it, the count, the banner, and "Create role" names the banner as its reason. With `roles.custom` off: the custom roles stay listed; "Create role" shows the reason in place of "0 of 0" (gap 1); "Edit role" is disabled with the reason; "Delete role" keeps its own rules. A custom role opens read-only with the reason. The new-role page shows the reason and "Back to Roles" in place of the editor, with `roles.custom` off or at the limit.
2. **Change role and Invite member.** With `roles.custom` off, each custom role stays in the choice, disabled, with the reason. A built-in role is always given.
3. **Members.** The count includes the invitations and says so. At the limit "Invite member" is disabled with the reason (the empty state's button too). Over it, the banner: "Remove members or cancel invitations…" for a viewer with `tenant.members.delete`, "Someone who can remove members…" for one without. A viewer who cannot invite sees no count and no banner (`MembersPlanMember`).
4. **Errors.** 403 `plan.feature_unavailable` and 409 `plan.limit_reached` show the text of their `entitlement` in the dialog where they failed, the same text as the disabled action: the invite and change-role dialogs and the role editor (gap 2). An unknown key shows `errors.plan.<code>`. `afterRefusal` then reads `GetMyTenant` again. Every command that adds or removes a member or an invitation now reads it again too, so the counts follow.
5. **Plan's name.** A read-only "Plan" row in Settings › General, for everyone who can see General.
6. **Activity.** `tenant.plan_changed`, `tenant.entitlement_override_set` and `tenant.entitlement_override_removed` with the boards' sentences, the Platform badge and no person. The override's reason never shows. `tenant.created` names its plan ("The platform created this organisation on Pro."), from the same Plans section; an entry without details keeps the old sentence.

author: alex-denisov
body:
## Problem

Block A recheck (28.10), open item 1: profile edits (`SqliteManualExperienceFactRepository.add`) and source connections («Подключено: LinkedIn» from `nativeImportMode`) are stored in `messages` with `role='user'`. The consultant panel on «Сегодня» and «Профиль» showed them as the candidate's own bubbles, e.g. «Образование / Учебное заведение: … / Начало: 2008-09». Approved mockups 1 and 2 show only the real dialogue.

## Chosen path: no schema change

The prod DB is 3.8 GB and an `ALTER TABLE` before `listen()` already broke a deploy once, so this PR changes no schema and runs no migration or backfill.

A message's kind is **read from data that already exists**:

- `messageKind` (`server/data/store/messageKind.ts`): `assistant` → `dialogue`; a `user` row → `dialogue` only if a turn owns it (`turns.user_message_id`), otherwise `service`.
- Every candidate line is written in the same transaction as its turn (`insertPendingTurn` → `recordUserMessage`). Manual facts, import announcements and «Подключено: …» never get a turn. Deleting a consultant conversation removes its turns and messages together. So the rule is exact, and it marks **new and existing rows the same way** without rewriting anything.
- One `SELECT user_message_id FROM turns WHERE candidate_id = ?` per feed read (covered by the `turns` PK prefix), then a filter in memory.

## What changes

- `getMessages` (the panel feed, `GET /api/v1/candidate/me/messages`) and the **staged** snapshot return only dialogue. This covers 1440 and 390, which use the same endpoint, and the bundled .app frontend too, because the filtering happens on the server.
- The **unstaged** snapshot (export, command dispatcher) still keeps every row. No data is lost, and fact provenance (`sourceMessageIds`) still resolves.
- Model input is unchanged: facts still reach the consultant through `knowledgeContext.confirmedFacts`, which a test covers.

## Tests (written first, RED → GREEN)

- `server/data/store/conversationController.serviceMessages.test.ts`: the kind rule; the today/profile feeds and the staged snapshot without the manual fact and «Подключено: LinkedIn»; the unstaged snapshot still holds them; the fact is still in the model's knowledge context.
- `server/resumeStudioRoute.test.ts`: the provenance check now reads the full snapshot and asserts that the profile feed is empty.

## Test plan

- [x] Impact set locally: `server/data/store/**`, the resume studio, structured import, coach routes, STAR stories, app, `src/features/journey`. The only failures were 5 s timeouts at load average 240–450 (`applicationsRoute` 1,000-row perf tests, which don't touch messages); rerun with a longer timeout.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the changed files.
- [ ] Full CI.
- [ ] After deploy: on adenisov.test, the «Сегодня» and «Профиль» panel at 1440 and 390 has no «Образование / …» or «Подключено: …» bubbles.

Follow-up worth considering (not in scope): the model's `messages` history still contains these service rows as `user` turns, as it does today. Excluding them would be a model-input change of its own.

## Proof: the rule hides no candidate messages (CPO request, 29.10)

### 1. Every writer of `role='user'` rows, current and historical

`git log -S"INSERT INTO messages"` / `-S"insertMessage("` over `server/`:

| Writer | Since | Kind | Has a turn |
|---|---|---|---|
| `insertPendingTurn` → `recordUserMessage` (every candidate line, typed or quick button) | 6b8e70c8, 31.07 (B083) | dialogue | yes, same transaction |
| `importResumeEvidence(InTransaction)`: «Импорт: …» and, for connect-only, «Подключено: …» | 1000b650, 20.08 (B148) | service | no |
| `SqliteManualExperienceFactRepository.add`: profile fact | d434c935, 28.09 (C66) | service | no |

- The `turns` and `messages` tables were created in the same migration, `MIGRATION_1` (B083). No dialogue predates `turns`.
- No migration or script ever inserted into `messages`.
- Intake, quick buttons and quiz answers have no server path of their own. They all go through `startTurn`.
- Service turns (`isService`, since B340 on 01.10) write no user row at all.
- The only deletion (`consultantHistoryStore.delete`, B436) removes a conversation's turns and its messages together.

### 2. The 69 turnless rows on prod, decrypted on the host

Read-only: `DatabaseSync(..., { readOnly: true })`, key from `/etc/openqareer/openqareer.env`. The script printed counts only and was removed afterwards. Of 145 `user` rows, 69 have no turn:

| Category | How identified | Count | Dates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Import announcement | id `resume-import:` or text «Импорт: » | 50 | 25.08 to 27.10 (all of the August and September rows) |
| Source connection | text «Подключено: » | 1 | 23.10 |
| Manual profile fact | the `memory` source with `confidence='candidate-confirmed'` | 18 | 25.10 1, 27.10 16, 28.10 1 |
| **Unexplained** | none of the above | **0** | none |

All 69 rows are service records, and none is real dialogue.

### 3. Why not a content signature

A signature cannot catch manual facts. Their text is whatever the candidate entered, e.g. «Образование / …» or a free-form bullet, with no fixed prefix. The turn-ownership rule covers all three categories exactly, so the rule stays as it is.

author: mgwedd
body:
## Summary

Makes distributed pretraining worker membership elastic and resilient so workers can join mid-run, even if they failed to join earlier, were offline when the run started, or encountered failed member jobs.

### Key Changes
1. **Dynamic Lease Epoch in Member Invites**:
   - `invite()` now reads and forwards the active slot lease epoch (`machine.epoch`) instead of hardcoding `0`, preventing `Stale lease epoch` rejections when slots are re-granted.
2. **Re-inviting Missed / Unplaced Workers**:
   - `reinvite()` now checks both `unreachable` and `unplaced` machines (or those whose `peer_job` cleared), allowing machines that were offline at gang placement or dropped to be re-invited when their slot becomes available.
   - Fixed `invite()` filter when `only` is specified so re-offered machines are not skipped if they previously had an invite state.
3. **Immediate Member Failure Detection**:
   - `_tick_gangs()` checks `studio_facts.member_failures` before assuming nodes are healthy, immediately dropping the failed member slot and notifying coordinator (`lose(node)`).
   - Exempts chosen machines from the 120s `_lost` ban so they are immediately eligible to be re-offered a slot once free.
4. **Clean Slot Lifecycle in `offer()`**:
   - Filters out down/offline nodes during candidate selection.
   - Clears stale `invite_id` and records the newly granted `slot.epoch` on the machine before dispatching invitations.
5. **Testing**:
   - Added `test_a_chosen_machine_offline_at_start_is_reinvited_and_joins_on_later_round` and `test_a_failed_member_job_is_detected_immediately_and_reoffered_a_slot` to `tests/test_late_join.py`.
   - Verified with all 224 cluster tests and full distributed test suite.

author: mikev10
body:
## Scope

R6 serves an `https` endpoint that takes a credential. A local open-weight
model is usually neither: it listens over `http` on the host, with no key.
This unit lets the R6 driver reach one, which needs three things R6 does not
do: a relay upstream over `http`, allowed only for an address the operator
names as local and never inferred from the URL; a relay with no credential,
declared as such rather than read from an absent value; and a route from the
relay's outbound network to the host, which changes the sandbox's network
posture the way P10 did. Each loosens a rule the relay fails closed on today
(I5), so each is specified, reviewed, and asserted on its own. Metering, the
budget, and the family declaration are unchanged: a local endpoint reports
its own usage, and cost recorded for it is zero only where its declared
prices are.

Spec: `docs/plan/R21-local-endpoint.md`. The maintainer chose the Docker host
as the only local address, and a keyless relay for a local upstream only
(D-R21-02).

## Delivered

- `RelaySpec.upstream` takes `{ local: 'docker-host', port }`. This is the
  relay's only way to speak `http`, to `model-host:<port>`. The name is added
  with `--add-host model-host:host-gateway` to the relay container alone
  (A-R21-01).
- `RelaySpec.credential` takes `null` with the new `'none'` scheme, for a
  local upstream only. The relay writes no key and deletes the client's value
  in its header (A-R21-02).
- `LocalDockerOptions.dockerHostPorts`: a local upstream on a port the
  provider was not given is refused (A-R21-03).
- The relay's own start checks refuse each of these again.
- The OpenAI-compatible driver's config takes the local upstream and
  `'none'`. The host reads a `'none'` endpoint file without
  `FACTORY_ENDPOINT_KEY`, refuses a key given beside it, and hands the local
  port to the provider through `endpointGrants` (A-R21-04).

## Out of scope for this unit

- any address but the Docker host: a LAN machine, a named Docker network, a container's name, or an `http` URL of any kind
- an `https` endpoint with no credential
- starting, stopping, pulling, or health-checking the local model server
- binding the host's server for the operator, or detecting one bound to loopback on a Linux engine; the relay's call fails, and the run says why
- a price inferred from the endpoint being local. Its prices are the operator's table; zero is a price the operator writes
- any change to the sandbox's egress, the proxy, or the allowlist
- a paid suite. Every assertion runs against a listener the test owns

## Acceptance criteria

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`: pass.
- `pnpm -r --workspace-concurrency=1 --filter '!@olympus-ai/driver-claude-code' --filter '!@olympus-ai/conformance' test`:
  all ten packages pass (D-R21-07).
- Conformance package `vitest`: 316 passed, 16 failed, and every failure is in the set ship-unit exempts: the Claude Code driver's externals (12), the api `test/paid/` externals (2), and the two meta-tests that count them. No other problem line.
- `I4.model-relay-reaches-the-docker-host-only-as-declared` and
  `I5.model-relay-refuses-an-undeclared-local-endpoint` pass against a real
  daemon. Both fail with `packages/sandbox/src` reverted. Each new unit test in
  sandbox, the driver, and api also fails against the old source.
- Changesets: `r21-local-relay.md` (sandbox, conformance) and
  `r21-local-endpoint.md` (driver, api).
- `git ls-files -- .plan/`: prints nothing.
- **Pending CI, not marked passed:** the Claude Code driver's paid suite and
  `pnpm conformance`. `sandbox` is in that driver's tree, so they need the
  `run-driver` label (D-A-CI-05).

## Decisions

- D-R21-01: the boundary, the assumptions, and the places where the code
  differs from the entry.
- D-R21-02: the three choices the maintainer took.
- D-R21-03: a local upstream is a structure, never a URL.
- D-R21-04: no credential is `null` and `'none'` together; `RelaySpec` stays
  one interface.
- D-R21-05: the provider holds the host route as it holds a credential.
- D-R21-06: what the build decided. A key to a local endpoint is allowed;
  `model-host` is the upstream host for the allowlist check; the test
  listener binds every interface.
- D-R21-07: the local acceptance run.
- A-R21-01 to A-R21-04: the amendments.

## Registry delta

- Added live, none pending:
  - `I4.model-relay-reaches-the-docker-host-only-as-declared`, runtime, in
    `packages/conformance/src/registry/local-endpoint.ts`;
  - `I5.model-relay-refuses-an-undeclared-local-endpoint`, runtime, same file.
- `pending-baseline.json` is unchanged.

## Review notes

- **Gate paths:** `packages/sandbox/src/types.ts` and `packages/conformance/`.
  This pull request needs the `gate-change` label, and the squash body needs
  `Gate-Change: acknowledged`.
- **The entry is wrong about posture.** It says the route changes the
  sandbox's network posture "the way P10 did". It does not. The sandbox stays
  on an `--internal` network, and the I4 assertion shows it cannot reach the
  endpoint by `model-host`, by `host.docker.internal`, or by the gateway's
  address.
- **Linux engines:** `host-gateway` is the bridge's address there, so a model
  server bound only to `127.0.0.1` cannot be reached. This was verified only on
  Docker Desktop. CI's Linux runner is the first run on a Linux engine.

body:
Closes #256

## What

One coding agent per workspace, selected with `agent`:

```toml
[workspaces.my-project-claude]
paths = ["~/projects/my-project"]
agent = "claude"            # opencode (default), claude, copilot, omo

[workspaces.my-project-claude.agents.claude]
args = ["--model", "sonnet"]  # appended to every session
# version = "2.1.400"         # instead of the pinned version
# install = false             # provide the binary yourself
```

Custom agents are built-in agents under another name with their own settings:

```toml
[defaults.agents.claude-opus]
from = "claude"
args = ["--model", "opus"]

[workspaces.my-project-opus]
paths = ["~/projects/my-project"]
agent = "claude-opus"
```

- New `internal/agent` package holds the built-in harness definitions: pinned npm package, continue/resume flags, unattended flags, env (auto-update off), persisted state dirs, default mounts, TUI plugin env.
- Image: OpenCode removed from the embedded Dockerfile. jailoc builds a `jailoc-agent-<name>:<hash>` layer (`npm install -g --allow-scripts=<pkg>`) on top of the images it builds (embedded / `[base] dockerfile` / `defaults.image` + workspace `dockerfile`), before the workspace overlay. Directly used images are untouched and must contain the binary.
- Sessions: command line from the harness; before a new session jailoc checks the binary is on `PATH` and that the running VM was started with the configured agent (otherwise asks for `jailoc restart`). Exit message names the agent binary.
- Guest: shares and internal binds are mounted in one parent-first order (internal share first), so a mount inside a persistent agent directory (e.g. `~/.claude/skills`) is not hidden. Only the selected agent's state dirs are persisted (OpenCode keeps `opencode-data`/`opencode-state`, no migration); TUI plugin bind + `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG` only for OpenCode; `vm.Spec.Agent` recorded, `reload` reports agent changes as restart-only.
- Config: `agent`, `agents.<name>.{from,install,version,args}` in `[defaults]` and workspaces, validated. A non-built-in `agents` key with `from` defines a custom agent (no chains); `version` must be an exact npm version. Each setting comes from the agent's workspace table, its defaults table, then (custom agents) the tables of the built-in it derives from; agent env keys are reserved; `~/.claude/transcripts` default mount dropped; the "path in multiple workspaces" warning dropped.
- CWD resolution: equal-depth match of several workspaces errors with `choose one with -w`.
- Docs: new how-to `coding-agents.md`, configuration reference (Coding agents section), image resolution (agent layer), default image, sessions, CLI, overlay compatibility, README, llms.txt.

| agent | session command | continue / resume | persisted |
|---|---|---|---|
| opencode | `opencode` | `--continue` / `--session` | `~/.local/share/opencode`, `~/.local/state/opencode` |
| claude | `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` | `--continue` / `--resume` | `~/.claude` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) |
| copilot | `copilot --allow-all` | `--continue` / `--resume` | `~/.copilot` |
| omo | `omo --permission-preset full-access` | `--continue` / `--session` | `~/.omo` |

## Breaking

- OpenCode is not in the base image any more; a `[base] dockerfile` needs `npm` on `PATH`, and directly used images must contain the agent binary.
- `~/.claude/transcripts` is no longer mounted by default.

## Testing

- `go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` (1010 passed), `golangci-lint run` clean.
- Manual QA on macOS/arm64 with real VMs: claude (session, detach/reattach, `args`, state in persisted home), copilot, omo (`--continue`), opencode (TUI plugin, no update prompt); agent switch on running VM → restart hint; direct image without the binary → actionable error; ambiguous directory → `-w` error; `down --purge` removes agent state; `~/.claude/skills` mount visible over the persisted `~/.claude`; custom agent `copilot-old` (`from = "copilot"`, `version = "1.0.104"`, `args`) installs 1.0.104 and starts `copilot --allow-all --banner`.

## Also in this PR

- `chore(ci)`: CI on Go 1.27.x and golangci-lint v2.15.0; `dev/Dockerfile.jailoc` copies Go 1.27.3 from the official `golang` image, gopls v0.24.0, checksum-verified golangci-lint v2.15.0.

## Known gaps

Not verified:
- OmO RPC daemon lifetime after the session that started it ends.
- Copilot CLI login without a keyring (fallback to `~/.copilot` config).
- Whether `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` stops Claude Code self-updates.
- `dev/Dockerfile.jailoc` with the upgraded versions has not been built end to end yet (only the previous pins were).

Limitations:
- Copilot CLI still shows its folder-trust prompt despite `--allow-all`.
- No VM integration test boots Claude Code, Copilot or OmO; they were tested manually on macOS/arm64 only. Unit tests cover config, resolution, command lines and the agent layer Dockerfile.
- `agents.<name>.args` in a workspace replaces the `[defaults]` list instead of extending it.
- Agent versions are pinned in `internal/agent/agent.go` and bumped by hand; no Renovate/Dependabot rule yet.
- `omo-ai` pulls `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, whose platform package bundles a 277 MB `claude` binary: the OmO layer is ~600 MB.
- Go module downloads (`~/go/pkg/mod`) are not persisted across restarts in the dev overlay; `GOMODCACHE` under `~/.cache` would fix it.

author: jstar269
body:
The launcher showed full user paths again: the disc picker's chosen file, the disc checking card and error cards printed `C:\Users\<name>\...`, which puts the account name in screenshots and videos. This PR groups four player changes:

- full user paths on screen, and a "Starting <game>..." card for the seconds before a game's window opens (both from the showcase prep);
- a problem report that showed another game's boot events, and a Factory reset in Settings (both owner requests from 2026-10-29).

## Path privacy

**Root cause.** The old SDL renderer passed every string it drew through `player_display_text` (`ui_renderer.c`, `draw_text`), which shows the profile folder as `~`. The nk_ui launcher screens draw through nk_ui and Clay and never got that step.

**Fix.** The display rule moves to the one place all launcher text passes through:

- `NkUiConfig` gains `display_text`, the host's display rule. It must never grow its input.
- nk_ui applies it to frame text (`nk_ui_frame_text`, so `nk_ui_text`, buttons, eyebrows and prompt legends), to `nk_ui_label`, and to `nk_ui_text_clamp`. The clamp measures and cuts the rewritten text, so an ellipsis can never keep part of the profile folder (for example `C:\Users\Jas…`).
- The launcher sets it to `player_display_text`, the existing rule with its whole-component, case-insensitive matching and tests in `test_player_state.c`. The in-game overlay leaves it `NULL`.
- Stored paths, logs and copied error details are unchanged. Only what is drawn changes.

A disc under the profile folder now shows as `~\Downloads\game.iso`. A disc elsewhere (`D:\PSP\game.iso`) shows as before; it carries no account name. The Windows file dialog itself is drawn by Windows and still shows its own location bar.

## Starting card

**What was wrong.** The v0.0.1 final walkthrough timed 7 s (HST) and 9 s (LocoRoco) from PLAY to the game window on the first start of a new package. The launcher stayed on the title page the whole time, and since #1311 the launch runs off the UI thread. But the only sign of the wait was a Starting chip and one grey line at the bottom of the package card, which is easy to miss on screen or on video.

**Fix.** While the game starts, the title page shows a card under the action buttons:
- "Starting <game>...";
- the sentence "Its window opens when it is ready. The first start can take several seconds.";
- an indeterminate bar, which holds still with Reduce motion.

The card sits below the buttons so they don't move when the window opens. `PlayerUiTitleModel` gains `now_s` for the bar. The card goes away as soon as the game reports its window. The cause of the 7 to 9 s wait itself is not measured here.

## Problem report: another game's boot events

**What was wrong.** The owner's ModNation Racers (UCUS98741) report listed "Last boot events" with `entry=0x08a9c92c`, which is LocoRoco 2's entry. ModNation's own run log says `entry=0x08804000`.

**Root cause.** `player_app_format_error_report` took the last eight `BOOT_EVENT` lines from the developer log. That log has two problems for this:
- it spans every launch of the session;
- on exit it copies only the first 48 lines of each run's output.

So when a run's boot events came after its first 48 lines, none of them reached the developer log, and the report showed the previous game's instead.

**Fix.** The report reads the boot events from the error's own run log, `logs/game-<disc>-last.txt` (#1303), and lists the last eight in order. A report without a run log lists none. The UI test view's synthetic stop now keeps a run log the same way a real stop does.

## Factory reset

**What it does.** Settings gains a **Factory reset** button, in the danger style, at the end of the bottom row. It opens a check that:
- says what moves (library, saves, imported PSP fonts, keys, settings, built games, downloaded build tools) and what stays (disc images, logs);
- lists the folders;
- says how to undo it.

**Keep everything** has the focus. Esc also goes back.

**Reset** never deletes anything:
- It renames the config, data, cache and saves folders, plus the runtime root when one is set, to `<folder>-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>` in place. That is a rename on the same disk, and the user can name a folder back.
- Only the outermost folders move. On Linux, `saves` is inside `data` and moves with it.
- Logs stay, because the player has `player-output.txt` open.
- If any folder can't be moved, the earlier ones are put back and the card names the folder and the OS reason.
- It waits, with a card, while a game, launch, build, tool download, update or background check is running.
- After the move, the player saves nothing and quits. On the way out it starts a fresh copy of itself with SDL's background process, which outlives the parent (`nk_platform_spawn_process` would put the copy in a kill-on-close job). The copy finds no user data and opens on a first run. If the copy can't start, a message says to start the player again.

The folder list and the Updates page's folder now get the `~` rule before the page shortens them from the middle, so a cut can never keep part of the user name.

## Tests

- New `test_display_text_rules` in `tests/native/test_nk_ui_core.c` checks frame text, a clamp that fits, a clamp that cuts, a label and styled text, and that no drawn run in the frame dump carries the profile folder.
  - Failing before: with the old `nk_ui.c`, the test fails with `FAIL: frame text shows the profile as ~`.
  - Passing after: `mingw32-make --no-print-directory nk-ui-core-selftest` passes.
- `tests/native/test_player_screens.c`:
  - Starting state: the card names the game and carries the sentence.
  - Running state: no starting card.
  - `fixtures/nk_ui/title.golden` is regenerated. The only change is the `title-game-starting` case, where the card is added and the compatibility card moves down.
  - A new `title-game-starting` capture is added to `nk-ui-player-screens-capture`.
- Boot events (`tests/native/test_player_state.c`):
  - The stop card's report ignores an earlier run's event in the developer log. Failing before: with the old `player_state.c`, the assertion at line 2230 fails.
  - Subtest 20 launches two titles in a row: `synthetic-allegrex-v1` (TEST00001), then `synthetic-title2-v1` (TEST00002), whose boot event comes after 60 lines of output. The second report lists only its own events.
- Factory reset:
  - Subtest 24 checks that a busy player refuses, that a file held open on Windows triggers the rollback, that the folders are renamed, that a second reset in the same second gets a `-2` name, and that logs stay.
  - `test_settings_factory_reset_asks_then_moves_the_data_aside` checks the focus, Keep everything, Esc, and that Reset moves the folders and quits.
  - `test_every_view_is_drawn_by_the_launcher` covers the new view.
- After merging main: native-core-tests exit 0; player-ui-tests and nk-ui-core-selftest exit 0; player-ui-regressions: 117 of 119 passed in the run.
  - The stop-card test was fixed by the synthetic run log and passes on rerun.
  - `test_update_check_finds_downloads_and_installs_a_newer_release` fails only under MSYS2's `python`, where `os.sep` is `/`. It passes with the native CPython 3.15 that hosted CI uses.
- `tools.test_workspace_paths` passes. It was the cause of the 01:13Z deferral: the new nk_ui test spelled a `C:\Users\` path.
- Controls: `ci_controls.sh --adopt` gives `verdict: PASS (0 fatal finding(s))`.

## Provenance

No new paths. Changed files keep their headers.

author: gregyuzik
body:
"Show options" now reads at 4.5:1 on the settings card and on the quota banner. The quota's reset is told by the day it falls on. The evaluation row no longer starts over when it comes back into view. The tier caption leading an iPad's bar is capped, with the Large Content Viewer above the cap.

H8. Both "Show options" buttons drew their words in the accent tint. The card's `.bordered` button put system blue on the style's gray, the same pairing "Not now" measured at 2.67:1 light and 3.78:1 dark. The banner's button put footnote blue on glass: 3.52:1 on the estimated light ground and 4.31:1 on the dark one, under the 4.5:1 its sentence is held to. Both now take `.tint(.primary)`, as "Not now" does. The banner's button has no fill, so once it is the same hue as its sentence only its position marks it a button; it is semibold as well, to tell the two apart.

L41. The reset read as a bare time of day whatever day it fell on, and it still read that way once the reset had passed. `AskQuotaBanner.line(resetDate:now:calendar:)` is now the one line for the banner, its VoiceOver announcement and the card's `.limitReached` message, which used to keep a copy of its own:
- a reset later today keeps "It resets at 5:00 PM.";
- a reset on a later day reads "It resets on Friday, Oct 30 at 5:00 AM.";
- a reset already past adds nothing to the limit's sentence.

The line names a day rather than "tomorrow" because it is worked out when it is drawn, and a banner still showing after midnight would keep a "tomorrow" that had become today. The new key, "It resets on %@.", is translated into all 24 locales. Its placeholder is the weekday, date and time, formatted by the system. One translation was changed after the translator: Czech is "Obnoví se: %@.", not "Obnoví se v %@.". The system's weekday phrase is in the nominative case, so "v" would give "v sobota" and "v středa" where Czech needs "v sobotu" and "ve středu". Polish, Russian and Ukrainian use the same colon form for the same reason. The day is formatted into a local before the literal, because the catalog-completeness check can't read a key through an interpolation that chains calls.

L40. The evaluation row ran in a `.task(id: evalRun)` attached to the row. If the row scrolled out of a Form, or a page was pushed over Settings, the task was cancelled while `evalRun` stayed set. When the row came back, the task ran again and started a second evaluation, spending Private Cloud Compute's quota again. The run now lives in `AskEvalRun`, an `@Observable` object held in the card's `@State`. The row's appearing and disappearing never starts or stops it. A second `start` while a run is under way does nothing. The object's deinit cancels the task, so the run still ends when the card goes. The task holds the object weakly, so a run in progress can't keep the card's state alive.

M41. Where the caption leads the bar (an iPad under a top tab bar) it now stops growing at extra-extra-extra-large and shows the Large Content Viewer above that, as the face in the tab bar's slot does. Letting it wrap to two lines would not fit: the bar's row keeps its height at every text size, and at the largest size `.caption` is 40 pt, so two lines would be about twice the row's height. One line of "Private Cloud Compute" would be about 420 pt wide next to the centered tab bar. The visionOS ornament's caption is unchanged.

M62 and M60 (the words in these files only). The card's doc comment no longer uses "settled" to mean decided: the engine "decides on every turn", in house rule 1's words. The banner's accessibility comment uses "joined to" where it said "merged into".

Tests: `AskPrivateCloudCardTests` replaces `theResetTimeIsAppendedOnlyWhenThereIsOne`, which passed a 2001 date and so would now be a stale reset. In its place are `aResetLaterTodayReadsAsItsTime`, `aResetOnALaterDayNamesItsDay`, `aResetAlreadyPastLeavesTheLimitSentenceAlone` and `theCardAtTheLimitSaysWhatTheBannerSays`. A new suite, `AskEvalRunTests`, has `aRunAskedForWhileOneIsUnderWayIsThatRun`, `aFinishedRunCanBeAskedForAgain` and `theRunEndsWithTheCard`. Against a stub that behaved like the old row and the old line, the later-day, stale, second-run and cancellation tests failed. M41's cap and Large Content Viewer, and H8's tint, are view modifiers that `swift test` can't see, so neither has a unit test.

Hands-on checks still open:
- An iPad at regular width with a top tab bar, at AX5: the caption stops at extra-extra-extra-large without clipping, and a long press shows the Large Content Viewer.
- The banner's semibold `.primary` "Show options" on glass, light and dark: it still reads as a button.
- In Settings with diagnostics on: start the eval, scroll the card out of the Form and back (or push and pop a page). The spinner is still running, the report arrives once, and dismissing Settings stops the run.
- Whether SwiftUI installs the Large Content Viewer's long press on a non-interactive `Text` in a toolbar item. The slot's precedent is buttons.
- Apple's accessibility audit, contrast check, on the card with "Show options" showing (needs a spent quota with a limit-increase suggestion, which the demo can't produce).

author: miguel645
body:
Fixes from a review of everything that sends SMS or creates vales (no database change):

- **Interrupted first sends now finish by themselves.** The daily 10:00 job used to send only to clients added after the first send, so clients a send didn't reach in time (35 s limit) waited for "Continuar envio" forever. It now also includes them, still leaving out older clients who switched messages on later (`inLiveAudience`, uses `consent_at`, with tests).
- **No client missed during "Enviar campanha".** `first_sent_at` is now taken before the client list is read.
- **Daily job is sturdier.** One campaign failing (e.g. a database read error) no longer stops the rest; a scheduled campaign that sent nothing goes back to `scheduled` and is tried the next day.
- **"Não enviada"** for a scheduled campaign whose Início–Fim passed without the 10:00 run happening, with a message asking for new dates.
